species.name: Venado bura
species.short_description: Large western deer with outsized mule-like ears and a bounding, all-four-feet gait called stotting.
species.en_short_description: Large western deer with outsized mule-like ears and a bounding, all-four-feet gait called stotting.
species.description: The default deer of the Rocky Mountain West and the Baja peninsula. Told from White-tailed Deer by the enormous ears, the black-tipped white tail it carries down rather than raised, and antlers that fork evenly instead of branching from one beam. Browses sagebrush and mountain shrubs; drops to lower valleys in winter.
species.en_description: The default deer of the Rocky Mountain West and the Baja peninsula. Told from White-tailed Deer by the enormous ears, the black-tipped white tail it carries down rather than raised, and antlers that fork evenly instead of branching from one beam. Browses sagebrush and mountain shrubs; drops to lower valleys in winter.

species.name: Venado de cola blanca
species.short_description: Eastern deer that flags a broad white tail as it flees; antlers branch from a single forward-curving beam.
species.en_short_description: Eastern deer that flags a broad white tail as it flees; antlers branch from a single forward-curving beam.
species.description: The common deer of New York and the eastern slope, expanding west along river corridors. The raised tail flashing white is the field mark that settles it against Mule Deer. Fawns keep their spots through a first summer. Edge habitat suits it best, which is why suburbs hold such high densities.
species.en_description: The common deer of New York and the eastern slope, expanding west along river corridors. The raised tail flashing white is the field mark that settles it against Mule Deer. Fawns keep their spots through a first summer. Edge habitat suits it best, which is why suburbs hold such high densities.

species.name: Uapití
species.short_description: Also called Elk. Very large, pale-rumped deer; bulls bugle a rising whistle through the autumn rut.
species.en_short_description: Also called Elk. Very large, pale-rumped deer; bulls bugle a rising whistle through the autumn rut.
species.description: Second only to Moose among North American deer. Tan body against a dark neck mane and a pale cream rump patch make it unmistakable at distance. Herds graze montane meadows at dawn and dusk. The September and October bugling is the signature sound of the Colorado high country.
species.en_description: Second only to Moose among North American deer. Tan body against a dark neck mane and a pale cream rump patch make it unmistakable at distance. Herds graze montane meadows at dawn and dusk. The September and October bugling is the signature sound of the Colorado high country.

species.name: Alce
species.short_description: The largest deer on earth: dark, humped, long-nosed, with a dangling throat bell and palmate antlers.
species.en_short_description: The largest deer on earth: dark, humped, long-nosed, with a dangling throat bell and palmate antlers.
species.description: A willow-and-pond animal rather than a meadow one, found in Colorado's high basins, the North Cascades, and the Adirondacks. Bulls carry broad flattened antlers unlike any other deer. Frequently feeds belly-deep in water on aquatic plants. Give it distance; a cow with a calf is genuinely dangerous.
species.en_description: A willow-and-pond animal rather than a meadow one, found in Colorado's high basins, the North Cascades, and the Adirondacks. Bulls carry broad flattened antlers unlike any other deer. Frequently feeds belly-deep in water on aquatic plants. Give it distance; a cow with a calf is genuinely dangerous.

species.name: Ardilla gris de las Carolinas
species.short_description: Grey tree squirrel with a white-edged bushy tail; the default city-park squirrel.
species.en_short_description: Grey tree squirrel with a white-edged bushy tail; the default city-park squirrel.
species.description: Native to New York and introduced across the West, now abundant in Denver, Seattle and Bay Area parks. Grizzled grey with a pale belly; black individuals are common in some cities.
species.en_description: Native to New York and introduced across the West, now abundant in Denver, Seattle and Bay Area parks. Grizzled grey with a pale belly; black individuals are common in some cities.

species.name: Ardilla zorra
species.short_description: Large rusty-orange tree squirrel with a cinnamon belly and orange-washed tail.
species.en_short_description: Large rusty-orange tree squirrel with a cinnamon belly and orange-washed tail.
species.description: Bigger and much warmer-toned than the Eastern Gray. Introduced widely in western cities, where it dominates street trees and lawns. Prefers open woodland with scattered large trees.
species.en_description: Bigger and much warmer-toned than the Eastern Gray. Introduced widely in western cities, where it dominates street trees and lawns. Prefers open woodland with scattered large trees.

species.name: marmota de vientre amarillo
species.short_description: Stout ground-dwelling rodent of rockslides, with a yellow belly and buff neck patches.
species.en_short_description: Stout ground-dwelling rodent of rockslides, with a yellow belly and buff neck patches.
species.description: The whistling marmot of Colorado and Cascade talus fields, often seen flat on a boulder in morning sun. Hibernates up to eight months. A sharp alarm chirp gives it the name whistle-pig.
species.en_description: The whistling marmot of Colorado and Cascade talus fields, often seen flat on a boulder in morning sun. Hibernates up to eight months. A sharp alarm chirp gives it the name whistle-pig.

species.name: Ardilla de Manto Dorado
species.short_description: Chipmunk-patterned ground squirrel with a coppery head and no facial stripes.
species.en_short_description: Chipmunk-patterned ground squirrel with a coppery head and no facial stripes.
species.description: Looks like an oversized chipmunk but the stripes stop at the neck — no lines across the face. Common at Colorado and Sierra trailheads, where it begs boldly at picnic tables.
species.en_description: Looks like an oversized chipmunk but the stripes stop at the neck — no lines across the face. Common at Colorado and Sierra trailheads, where it begs boldly at picnic tables.

species.name: Juancito
species.short_description: Small desert ground squirrel that runs with its white tail flipped flat over its back.
species.en_short_description: Small desert ground squirrel that runs with its white tail flipped flat over its back.
species.description: A Colorado Plateau and Baja desert animal. The single white side stripe and the tail carried as a parasol over the back are conclusive. Active in full midday heat when other rodents shelter.
species.en_description: A Colorado Plateau and Baja desert animal. The single white side stripe and the tail carried as a parasol over the back are conclusive. Active in full midday heat when other rodents shelter.

species.name: Ardillón de California
species.short_description: Mottled grey-brown ground squirrel with pale shoulder flecking and a moderately bushy tail.
species.en_short_description: Mottled grey-brown ground squirrel with pale shoulder flecking and a moderately bushy tail.
species.description: Colonial burrower of California grassland and the Baja peninsula, common on roadsides and park edges. Stands upright at burrow mouths to scan. Alarm whistle brings the whole colony to attention.
species.en_description: Colonial burrower of California grassland and the Baja peninsula, common on roadsides and park edges. Stands upright at burrow mouths to scan. Alarm whistle brings the whole colony to attention.

species.name: Ardilla vientre rojo
species.short_description: Grey tree squirrel with a rich rusty-red belly and flanks.
species.en_short_description: Grey tree squirrel with a rich rusty-red belly and flanks.
species.description: The common squirrel of Mexico City's parks and gardens, including Chapultepec. Highly variable: some animals are almost wholly dark. The red underside separates it from any introduced grey.
species.en_description: The common squirrel of Mexico City's parks and gardens, including Chapultepec. Highly variable: some animals are almost wholly dark. The red underside separates it from any introduced grey.

species.name: Perrito llanero cola negra
species.short_description: Tan colonial ground squirrel with a short black-tipped tail, living in open burrow towns.
species.en_short_description: Tan colonial ground squirrel with a short black-tipped tail, living in open burrow towns.
species.description: Eastern Colorado shortgrass prairie. Towns are conspicuous mounds of bare earth with sentries barking a two-note alarm. A keystone species: burrows shelter Burrowing Owls and Black-footed Ferrets.
species.en_description: Eastern Colorado shortgrass prairie. Towns are conspicuous mounds of bare earth with sentries barking a two-note alarm. A keystone species: burrows shelter Burrowing Owls and Black-footed Ferrets.

species.name: ardilla de Douglas
species.short_description: Small dark conifer squirrel with an orange belly and a chattering, scolding call.
species.en_short_description: Small dark conifer squirrel with an orange belly and a chattering, scolding call.
species.description: The Pacific Northwest and Sierra pine squirrel, replacing the American Red Squirrel west of the Cascade crest. Leaves middens of stripped cone scales at the base of favourite trees.
species.en_description: The Pacific Northwest and Sierra pine squirrel, replacing the American Red Squirrel west of the Cascade crest. Leaves middens of stripped cone scales at the base of favourite trees.

species.name: marmota canosa
species.short_description: Large silver-and-black marmot of high alpine talus with a piercing whistle.
species.en_short_description: Large silver-and-black marmot of high alpine talus with a piercing whistle.
species.description: North Cascades and Olympic high country above treeline. Frosted silvery shoulders and a black bar across the face separate it from the Yellow-bellied Marmot of lower elevations.
species.en_description: North Cascades and Olympic high country above treeline. Frosted silvery shoulders and a black bar across the face separate it from the Yellow-bellied Marmot of lower elevations.

species.name: Ardilla de las montañas de las Cascadas
species.short_description: Cascade-endemic ground squirrel with a copper head and faint body stripes.
species.en_short_description: Cascade-endemic ground squirrel with a copper head and faint body stripes.
species.description: Restricted to the Washington Cascades, where it replaces the Common Golden-mantled form. Duller and less boldly striped. Common at subalpine campgrounds and huckleberry meadows.
species.en_description: Restricted to the Washington Cascades, where it replaces the Common Golden-mantled form. Duller and less boldly striped. Common at subalpine campgrounds and huckleberry meadows.

species.name: Ardilla Listada del Este Americano
species.short_description: Small striped chipmunk with a rusty rump and stripes that stop before the tail.
species.en_short_description: Small striped chipmunk with a rusty rump and stripes that stop before the tail.
species.description: The only chipmunk in New York. Larger than western chipmunks, with bolder white-and-black flank stripes. Gives a repetitive chip call from a log for minutes at a stretch.
species.en_description: The only chipmunk in New York. Larger than western chipmunks, with bolder white-and-black flank stripes. Gives a repetitive chip call from a log for minutes at a stretch.

species.name: Ardilla gris
species.short_description: Large, clean silver-grey tree squirrel with a pure white belly and very full tail.
species.en_short_description: Large, clean silver-grey tree squirrel with a pure white belly and very full tail.
species.description: Oak and pine woodland of California and Washington, declining where Eastern Grays have moved in. Noticeably more elegant and whiter-bellied than the introduced species. Shy of open lawns.
species.en_description: Oak and pine woodland of California and Washington, declining where Eastern Grays have moved in. Noticeably more elegant and whiter-bellied than the introduced species. Shy of open lawns.

species.name: Ardillón de Rocas
species.short_description: Large mottled grey-brown ground squirrel with a long bushy tail, on rock and canyon walls.
species.en_short_description: Large mottled grey-brown ground squirrel with a long bushy tail, on rock and canyon walls.
species.description: Present in Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. The biggest of the ground squirrels, and squirrel-like enough in the tail to be mistaken for a tree squirrel. Favours boulder piles and masonry.
species.en_description: Present in Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. The biggest of the ground squirrels, and squirrel-like enough in the tail to be mistaken for a tree squirrel. Favours boulder piles and masonry.

species.name: ardilla listada de Townsend
species.short_description: Large dark chipmunk with dull, indistinct stripes, in damp coastal forest.
species.en_short_description: Large dark chipmunk with dull, indistinct stripes, in damp coastal forest.
species.description: Western Washington and northern California rainforest. Duskier and less contrasty than any interior chipmunk. Forages in salal and sword-fern understorey rather than open ground.
species.en_description: Western Washington and northern California rainforest. Duskier and less contrasty than any interior chipmunk. Forages in salal and sword-fern understorey rather than open ground.

species.name: marmota canadiense
species.short_description: Heavy brown burrowing rodent of field edges; also called Woodchuck.
species.en_short_description: Heavy brown burrowing rodent of field edges; also called Woodchuck.
species.description: The eastern marmot, common on New York roadsides and pasture margins. Squat, grizzled brown, with a short dark tail. Digs extensive burrows under hedgerows and hibernates through the winter.
species.en_description: The eastern marmot, common on New York roadsides and pasture margins. Squat, grizzled brown, with a short dark tail. Digs extensive burrows under hedgerows and hibernates through the winter.

species.name: Ardilla roja americana
species.short_description: Small rusty conifer squirrel with a white eye-ring and a loud rattling scold.
species.en_short_description: Small rusty conifer squirrel with a white eye-ring and a loud rattling scold.
species.description: Spruce and fir forest in Colorado, the Adirondacks and eastern Washington. Territorial and vocal; announces any intruder from a branch. Caches cones in large middens it defends year-round.
species.en_description: Spruce and fir forest in Colorado, the Adirondacks and eastern Washington. Territorial and vocal; announces any intruder from a branch. Caches cones in large middens it defends year-round.

species.name: Ardilla roja del suroeste
species.short_description: Southern Rockies pine squirrel, greyer than the American Red Squirrel with a paler belly.
species.en_short_description: Southern Rockies pine squirrel, greyer than the American Red Squirrel with a paler belly.
species.description: Split from the American Red Squirrel and restricted to Colorado's southern mountains and the Southwest. Greyer-backed with a less rusty tail. Behaviour and midden-building are identical.
species.en_description: Split from the American Red Squirrel and restricted to Colorado's southern mountains and the Southwest. Greyer-backed with a less rusty tail. Behaviour and midden-building are identical.

species.name: Wyoming Ground Squirrel
species.short_description: Plain buff-grey ground squirrel of high mountain parks, with a short pale-edged tail.
species.en_short_description: Plain buff-grey ground squirrel of high mountain parks, with a short pale-edged tail.
species.description: Colorado's mountain valleys and sagebrush parks. Unstriped and unspotted, which separates it from every chipmunk and antelope squirrel. Colonies riddle meadow soils with small round holes.
species.en_description: Colorado's mountain valleys and sagebrush parks. Unstriped and unspotted, which separates it from every chipmunk and antelope squirrel. Colonies riddle meadow soils with small round holes.

species.name: Ardilla de Abert
species.short_description: Dark tassel-eared tree squirrel of ponderosa pine, with long winter ear tufts.
species.en_short_description: Dark tassel-eared tree squirrel of ponderosa pine, with long winter ear tufts.
species.description: A Colorado Front Range specialty, tied closely to ponderosa pine. Grizzled grey above with a white belly and a broad white-edged tail. The long ear tassels appear in winter coat.
species.en_description: A Colorado Front Range specialty, tied closely to ponderosa pine. Grizzled grey above with a white belly and a broad white-edged tail. The long ear tassels appear in winter coat.

species.name: Ardilla rayada
species.short_description: The smallest chipmunk: tiny, brightly striped, with a long tail held upright when running.
species.en_short_description: The smallest chipmunk: tiny, brightly striped, with a long tail held upright when running.
species.description: Widespread in Colorado, the eastern Sierra and eastern Washington. Stripes are crisp and continue onto the rump. Runs with the tail vertical, a useful cue where several chipmunks overlap.
species.en_description: Widespread in Colorado, the eastern Sierra and eastern Washington. Stripes are crisp and continue onto the rump. Runs with the tail vertical, a useful cue where several chipmunks overlap.

species.name: marmota olímpica
species.short_description: Endemic Olympic Peninsula marmot, brown fading to yellowish, in subalpine meadow.
species.en_short_description: Endemic Olympic Peninsula marmot, brown fading to yellowish, in subalpine meadow.
species.description: Found nowhere but Washington's Olympic Mountains. Browner and less silvered than the Hoary Marmot, which it replaces there. Colonies occupy flowery meadows just above the forest edge.
species.en_description: Found nowhere but Washington's Olympic Mountains. Browner and less silvered than the Hoary Marmot, which it replaces there. Colonies occupy flowery meadows just above the forest edge.

species.name: Ardilla de Pino Amarillo
species.short_description: Bright orange-toned chipmunk with contrasting stripes, in open montane pine.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange-toned chipmunk with contrasting stripes, in open montane pine.
species.description: Cascades and eastern Washington into the Sierra. Warmer and more richly coloured than the Least Chipmunk, with which it overlaps. Favours open sunny pine forest and shrubby burns.
species.en_description: Cascades and eastern Washington into the Sierra. Warmer and more richly coloured than the Least Chipmunk, with which it overlaps. Favours open sunny pine forest and shrubby burns.

species.name: Ardilla Terrestre de Douglas
species.short_description: Pacific coastal form of the California Ground Squirrel, mottled grey with pale flecks.
species.en_short_description: Pacific coastal form of the California Ground Squirrel, mottled grey with pale flecks.
species.description: Recently split from the California Ground Squirrel and found from northern California into Washington. Field-identical in practice; range and locality are what separate the two.
species.en_description: Recently split from the California Ground Squirrel and found from northern California into Washington. Field-identical in practice; range and locality are what separate the two.

species.name: Perrito llanero de Gunnison
species.short_description: Small pale prairie dog with a short white-tipped tail, in high mountain grassland.
species.en_short_description: Small pale prairie dog with a short white-tipped tail, in high mountain grassland.
species.description: Colorado's western valleys and the Four Corners. Smaller than the Black-tailed Prairie Dog, with a white rather than black tail tip, and colonies are looser and less mounded.
species.en_description: Colorado's western valleys and the Four Corners. Smaller than the Black-tailed Prairie Dog, with a white rather than black tail tip, and colonies are looser and less mounded.

species.name: Perrito llanero de cola blanca
species.short_description: Buff prairie dog with dark cheek patches above and below the eye and a white tail tip.
species.en_short_description: Buff prairie dog with dark cheek patches above and below the eye and a white tail tip.
species.description: Northwestern Colorado sagebrush basins at higher elevation than the Black-tailed. The dark eyebrow-and-cheek marks are the quickest field mark. Colonies are widely spaced and low-density.
species.en_description: Northwestern Colorado sagebrush basins at higher elevation than the Black-tailed. The dark eyebrow-and-cheek marks are the quickest field mark. Colonies are widely spaced and low-density.

species.name: Chichimoco de Merriam
species.short_description: Large, dull grey-brown chipmunk with weak stripes, in southern California chaparral.
species.en_short_description: Large, dull grey-brown chipmunk with weak stripes, in southern California chaparral.
species.description: Oak woodland and chaparral of central and southern California. Big, long-tailed and drab, without the crisp striping of montane species. Often heard rustling in leaf litter before it is seen.
species.en_description: Oak woodland and chaparral of central and southern California. Big, long-tailed and drab, without the crisp striping of montane species. Often heard rustling in leaf litter before it is seen.

species.name: Ardilla Terrestre de Columbia
species.short_description: Rich rusty-faced ground squirrel with mottled grey back, in eastern Washington meadows.
species.en_short_description: Rich rusty-faced ground squirrel with mottled grey back, in eastern Washington meadows.
species.description: Colonial burrower of northeastern Washington grassland and mountain meadow. The cinnamon face and forelegs against a speckled grey back are distinctive. Hibernates from late summer.
species.en_description: Colonial burrower of northeastern Washington grassland and mountain meadow. The cinnamon face and forelegs against a speckled grey back are distinctive. Hibernates from late summer.

species.name: Colorado Chipmunk
species.short_description: Bright chipmunk of Colorado's rocky pine and pinyon slopes, with contrasting flank stripes.
species.en_short_description: Bright chipmunk of Colorado's rocky pine and pinyon slopes, with contrasting flank stripes.
species.description: A southern Rockies endemic in ponderosa, pinyon and juniper country. Intermediate in size between Least and Uinta Chipmunks. Frequents rock outcrops rather than dense forest floor.
species.en_description: A southern Rockies endemic in ponderosa, pinyon and juniper country. Intermediate in size between Least and Uinta Chipmunks. Frequents rock outcrops rather than dense forest floor.

species.name: Ardilla de tierra de trece rayas
species.short_description: Slim ground squirrel patterned with thirteen alternating dark and pale lines and rows of spots.
species.en_short_description: Slim ground squirrel patterned with thirteen alternating dark and pale lines and rows of spots.
species.description: Eastern Colorado plains and mown grassland. The precise line-and-spot pattern is unlike any chipmunk. Nicknamed the striped gopher. Freezes upright when alarmed before dashing to a burrow.
species.en_description: Eastern Colorado plains and mown grassland. The precise line-and-spot pattern is unlike any chipmunk. Nicknamed the striped gopher. Freezes upright when alarmed before dashing to a burrow.

species.name: Ardilla de Tierra de Belding
species.short_description: Plain brown ground squirrel with a dark dorsal band, in eastern Sierra meadows.
species.en_short_description: Plain brown ground squirrel with a dark dorsal band, in eastern Sierra meadows.
species.description: High meadows and pastures of eastern California. Unstriped apart from a broad brownish back stripe. Stands very upright at burrow entrances, earning the local name picket-pin.
species.en_description: High meadows and pastures of eastern California. Unstriped apart from a broad brownish back stripe. Stands very upright at burrow entrances, earning the local name picket-pin.

species.name: Sonoma Chipmunk
species.short_description: Long-tailed coastal chipmunk with rusty flanks, in northern California scrub.
species.en_short_description: Long-tailed coastal chipmunk with rusty flanks, in northern California scrub.
species.description: Restricted to northern coastal California, in chaparral, brushy clearings and forest edge. Brighter and longer-tailed than Merriam's Chipmunk, whose range lies to the south.
species.en_description: Restricted to northern coastal California, in chaparral, brushy clearings and forest edge. Brighter and longer-tailed than Merriam's Chipmunk, whose range lies to the south.

species.name: Ardilla de San Bernardino
species.short_description: Brightly contrasted chipmunk with white-bordered dark stripes, in Sierra conifer forest.
species.en_short_description: Brightly contrasted chipmunk with white-bordered dark stripes, in Sierra conifer forest.
species.description: Sierra Nevada and southern California mountains, tied to lodgepole and Jeffrey pine. The boldest striping of the California chipmunks, with clean white stripes on a rufous ground.
species.en_description: Sierra Nevada and southern California mountains, tied to lodgepole and Jeffrey pine. The boldest striping of the California chipmunks, with clean white stripes on a rufous ground.

species.name: Nelson's Antelope Squirrel
species.short_description: Pale sandy antelope squirrel of the San Joaquin Valley, with a white-underside tail.
species.en_short_description: Pale sandy antelope squirrel of the San Joaquin Valley, with a white-underside tail.
species.description: A threatened California endemic of alkali scrub and remnant valley grassland. Paler and larger than the White-tailed Antelope Squirrel, and its range does not overlap. Carries the tail flat over the back.
species.en_description: A threatened California endemic of alkali scrub and remnant valley grassland. Paler and larger than the White-tailed Antelope Squirrel, and its range does not overlap. Carries the tail flat over the back.

species.name: Uinta Chipmunk
species.short_description: Greyish chipmunk with bold black-and-white head stripes, in high conifer forest.
species.en_short_description: Greyish chipmunk with bold black-and-white head stripes, in high conifer forest.
species.description: Colorado and eastern California high country, usually in spruce, fir and limber pine near treeline. Greyer-bodied than the Least Chipmunk, with strikingly crisp facial striping.
species.en_description: Colorado and eastern California high country, usually in spruce, fir and limber pine near treeline. Greyer-bodied than the Least Chipmunk, with strikingly crisp facial striping.

species.name: Ardilla voladora norteña
species.short_description: Soft grey-brown nocturnal squirrel with a loose skin membrane and a flat tail.
species.en_short_description: Soft grey-brown nocturnal squirrel with a loose skin membrane and a flat tail.
species.description: Old conifer and mixed forest in New York and Washington. Glides between trunks at night, so it is far more common than sightings suggest. Very large dark eyes; belly fur grey at the base.
species.en_description: Old conifer and mixed forest in New York and Washington. Glides between trunks at night, so it is far more common than sightings suggest. Very large dark eyes; belly fur grey at the base.

species.name: Hopi Chipmunk
species.short_description: Pale orange-toned chipmunk of Colorado Plateau pinyon-juniper, without dark facial stripes.
species.en_short_description: Pale orange-toned chipmunk of Colorado Plateau pinyon-juniper, without dark facial stripes.
species.description: Western Colorado slickrock and pinyon country. Warm buff overall with faint side stripes and no black through the face, which separates it from the Colorado Chipmunk it borders.
species.en_description: Western Colorado slickrock and pinyon country. Warm buff overall with faint side stripes and no black through the face, which separates it from the Colorado Chipmunk it borders.

species.name: Ardilla voladora sureña
species.short_description: Small nocturnal glider, greyer and smaller than its northern counterpart, with white belly fur.
species.en_short_description: Small nocturnal glider, greyer and smaller than its northern counterpart, with white belly fur.
species.description: Deciduous woodland in New York. Belly hairs are white to the base, unlike the Northern Flying Squirrel's grey-based fur. Often detected by soft chirping calls from oak canopy at night.
species.en_description: Deciduous woodland in New York. Belly hairs are white to the base, unlike the Northern Flying Squirrel's grey-based fur. Often detected by soft chirping calls from oak canopy at night.

species.name: Ardillón punteado
species.short_description: Small sandy ground squirrel scattered with pale squarish spots, on loose soils.
species.en_short_description: Small sandy ground squirrel scattered with pale squarish spots, on loose soils.
species.description: Sandhills and sandy grassland of eastern Colorado. Neither striped nor mottled but distinctly spotted, and smaller than the Thirteen-lined. Prefers open sand with sparse vegetation.
species.en_description: Sandhills and sandy grassland of eastern Colorado. Neither striped nor mottled but distinctly spotted, and smaller than the Thirteen-lined. Prefers open sand with sparse vegetation.

species.name: Ardillón cola redonda
species.short_description: Plain pale desert ground squirrel with an unmarked coat and a slim round tail.
species.en_short_description: Plain pale desert ground squirrel with an unmarked coat and a slim round tail.
species.description: Low deserts of southeastern California. Wholly unpatterned sandy-grey, which alone separates it from the antelope squirrels sharing its range. Aestivates through the hottest late summer weeks.
species.en_description: Low deserts of southeastern California. Wholly unpatterned sandy-grey, which alone separates it from the antelope squirrels sharing its range. Aestivates through the hottest late summer weeks.

species.name: Castor americano
species.short_description: Large aquatic rodent with a flat scaly paddle tail; the animal whose dams reshape whole valleys.
species.en_short_description: Large aquatic rodent with a flat scaly paddle tail; the animal whose dams reshape whole valleys.
species.description: Look for gnawed willow stumps, mud-and-stick lodges and flooded meadow before looking for the animal itself, which is mostly crepuscular. Slaps its tail on water as an alarm. Present on streams in all four US regions here.
species.en_description: Look for gnawed willow stumps, mud-and-stick lodges and flooded meadow before looking for the animal itself, which is mostly crepuscular. Slaps its tail on water as an alarm. Present on streams in all four US regions here.

species.name: Rata almizclera
species.short_description: Rat-sized marsh rodent with a thin vertically flattened tail, swimming with its back exposed.
species.en_short_description: Rat-sized marsh rodent with a thin vertically flattened tail, swimming with its back exposed.
species.description: Far smaller than a Beaver and with a rope-like rather than paddle tail — the quickest separation when only a swimming animal is visible. Builds cattail push-ups in shallow marsh. Common in city ponds.
species.en_description: Far smaller than a Beaver and with a rope-like rather than paddle tail — the quickest separation when only a swimming animal is visible. Builds cattail push-ups in shallow marsh. Common in city ponds.

species.name: Rata gris asiática
species.short_description: Heavy grey-brown rat with small ears and a tail shorter than its body; the sewer rat.
species.en_short_description: Heavy grey-brown rat with small ears and a tail shorter than its body; the sewer rat.
species.description: The commonest urban mammal in all six regions. Blunter-nosed and heavier than the Black Rat, with proportionally smaller ears and a shorter, thicker tail. Ground- and burrow-dwelling rather than climbing.
species.en_description: The commonest urban mammal in all six regions. Blunter-nosed and heavier than the Black Rat, with proportionally smaller ears and a shorter, thicker tail. Ground- and burrow-dwelling rather than climbing.

species.name: Puercoespín norteamericano
species.short_description: Slow, hunched, quill-covered rodent often found high in a tree.
species.en_short_description: Slow, hunched, quill-covered rodent often found high in a tree.
species.description: Cannot throw its quills, contrary to the story. Feeds on inner bark, leaving pale patches on conifer trunks. Waddles on the ground but climbs well. Present in Colorado, the Cascades and the Adirondacks.
species.en_description: Cannot throw its quills, contrary to the story. Feeds on inner bark, leaving pale patches on conifer trunks. Waddles on the ground but climbs well. Present in Colorado, the Cascades and the Adirondacks.

species.name: Tuza de Baja California
species.short_description: Burrowing rodent known mainly by its fan-shaped soil mounds; dark-coated.
species.en_short_description: Burrowing rodent known mainly by its fan-shaped soil mounds; dark-coated.
species.description: Almost never seen above ground. The crescent mounds with a plugged side entrance are the record most observers make. Ranges from southern California into the Baja peninsula.
species.en_description: Almost never seen above ground. The crescent mounds with a plugged side entrance are the record most observers make. Ranges from southern California into the Baja peninsula.

species.name: Tuza norteña
species.short_description: Highly variable California pocket gopher with large clawed forefeet and loose skin pockets.
species.en_short_description: Highly variable California pocket gopher with large clawed forefeet and loose skin pockets.
species.description: The widespread valley and foothill gopher of California, with dozens of local colour forms. Pushes up soil mounds in lawns and meadows year-round. Solitary and fiercely territorial underground.
species.en_description: The widespread valley and foothill gopher of California, with dozens of local colour forms. Pushes up soil mounds in lawns and meadows year-round. Solitary and fiercely territorial underground.

species.name: Tuza de la Cuenca de México
species.short_description: Large dark gopher of the Basin of Mexico, with prominent orange incisors.
species.en_short_description: Large dark gopher of the Basin of Mexico, with prominent orange incisors.
species.description: The gopher of Mexico City's remaining grasslands and volcanic soils, including the Pedregal. Bigger than the US species and endemic to central Mexico. Mounds are conspicuous in park lawns.
species.en_description: The gopher of Mexico City's remaining grasslands and volcanic soils, including the Pedregal. Bigger than the US species and endemic to central Mexico. Mounds are conspicuous in park lawns.

species.name: Ratón de abazones de Baja California
species.short_description: Small desert mouse with stiff spiny rump hairs and a long tufted tail.
species.en_short_description: Small desert mouse with stiff spiny rump hairs and a long tufted tail.
species.description: Rocky desert slopes of southern California and throughout Baja California Sur. The bristly rump is felt more than seen. Gathers seeds into fur-lined cheek pouches and caches them in burrows.
species.en_description: Rocky desert slopes of southern California and throughout Baja California Sur. The bristly rump is felt more than seen. Gathers seeds into fur-lined cheek pouches and caches them in burrows.

species.name: Rata cambalachera de las Californias
species.short_description: Medium woodrat with a furred tail and large ears, building stick nests in cactus and scrub.
species.en_short_description: Medium woodrat with a furred tail and large ears, building stick nests in cactus and scrub.
species.description: Coastal southern California and the Baja peninsula. The bulky stick-and-debris houses, often wedged into cholla or under boulders, are what most observers actually find and photograph.
species.en_description: Coastal southern California and the Baja peninsula. The bulky stick-and-debris houses, often wedged into cholla or under boulders, are what most observers actually find and photograph.

species.name: Rata negra
species.short_description: Slender dark rat with large thin ears and a tail longer than its body; the roof rat.
species.en_short_description: Slender dark rat with large thin ears and a tail longer than its body; the roof rat.
species.description: Climbs far better than the Brown Rat, so attics, palms and vine-covered walls are its habitat. Present in five of the six regions, and abundant in Mexico City and Baja ports.
species.en_description: Climbs far better than the Brown Rat, so attics, palms and vine-covered walls are its habitat. Present in five of the six regions, and abundant in Mexico City and Baja ports.

species.name: Ratón Meteoro de California
species.short_description: Chunky short-tailed grassland rodent with small ears buried in fur.
species.en_short_description: Chunky short-tailed grassland rodent with small ears buried in fur.
species.description: Cuts distinct surface runways through dense California grassland, which are easier to find than the animal. Tail is under a third of body length, separating voles from all mice at a glance.
species.en_description: Cuts distinct surface runways through dense California grassland, which are easier to find than the animal. Tail is under a third of body length, separating voles from all mice at a glance.

species.name: Ratón casero eurasiático
species.short_description: Small grey-brown mouse with a nearly naked scaly tail and a musky smell.
species.en_short_description: Small grey-brown mouse with a nearly naked scaly tail and a musky smell.
species.description: Present in all six regions and the mouse most likely to be indoors. Duller and smaller-eyed than any native deer mouse, with a uniformly grey rather than bicoloured tail.
species.en_description: Present in all six regions and the mouse most likely to be indoors. Duller and smaller-eyed than any native deer mouse, with a uniformly grey rather than bicoloured tail.

species.name: Rata-cambalachera patas oscuras
species.short_description: Large woodrat with dark feet and a well-furred tail, building tall stick lodges.
species.en_short_description: Large woodrat with dark feet and a well-furred tail, building tall stick lodges.
species.description: California oak woodland and chaparral. Its metre-high stick houses at the base of trees are landmarks that persist for generations of occupants. Strictly nocturnal.
species.en_description: California oak woodland and chaparral. Its metre-high stick houses at the base of trees are landmarks that persist for generations of occupants. Strictly nocturnal.

species.name: Rata canguro de Merriam
species.short_description: Small sandy kangaroo rat with huge hind feet and a long white-tipped tufted tail.
species.en_short_description: Small sandy kangaroo rat with huge hind feet and a long white-tipped tufted tail.
species.description: Open desert sand in southern California and Baja California Sur. Hops bipedally, leaving paired tracks and a tail drag. Never drinks; extracts all its water from dry seeds.
species.en_description: Open desert sand in southern California and Baja California Sur. Hops bipedally, leaving paired tracks and a tail drag. Never drinks; extracts all its water from dry seeds.

species.name: Ratón de Baja California Sur
species.short_description: Small buff deer mouse endemic to the Baja California peninsula's cape region.
species.en_short_description: Small buff deer mouse endemic to the Baja California peninsula's cape region.
species.description: A Baja California Sur endemic of rocky arroyos and thornscrub. Large-eyed and bicoloured like other deer mice, so locality is the practical identification. Nocturnal and seed-eating.
species.en_description: A Baja California Sur endemic of rocky arroyos and thornscrub. Large-eyed and bicoloured like other deer mice, so locality is the practical identification. Nocturnal and seed-eating.

species.name: Western Deer Mouse
species.short_description: Big-eyed grey-brown mouse with a sharply bicoloured tail, white below.
species.en_short_description: Big-eyed grey-brown mouse with a sharply bicoloured tail, white below.
species.description: The default wild mouse of Colorado, California and Washington uplands. The clean two-tone tail and white feet separate it from the House Mouse instantly. Occupies almost every dry habitat.
species.en_description: The default wild mouse of Colorado, California and Washington uplands. The clean two-tone tail and white feet separate it from the House Mouse instantly. Occupies almost every dry habitat.

species.name: Ratón de abazones de Baja California
species.short_description: Coarse-furred pocket mouse of Baja desert scrub, with a long tufted tail.
species.en_short_description: Coarse-furred pocket mouse of Baja desert scrub, with a long tufted tail.
species.description: Rocky and gravelly desert from southern California through the peninsula. Less spiny than the Spiny Pocket Mouse it overlaps with. Fills cheek pouches with seeds on brief nocturnal runs.
species.en_description: Rocky and gravelly desert from southern California through the peninsula. Less spiny than the Spiny Pocket Mouse it overlaps with. Fills cheek pouches with seeds on brief nocturnal runs.

species.name: Ratón de abazones del Cabo
species.short_description: Pale sandy pocket mouse restricted to the southern Baja peninsula.
species.en_short_description: Pale sandy pocket mouse restricted to the southern Baja peninsula.
species.description: A Baja California Sur endemic of coastal dunes and sandy flats. Paler than its relatives, matching the substrate it lives on. Known from relatively few records, so sightings have value.
species.en_description: A Baja California Sur endemic of coastal dunes and sandy flats. Paler than its relatives, matching the substrate it lives on. Known from relatively few records, so sightings have value.

species.name: Coipú
species.short_description: Large brown semi-aquatic rodent with orange incisors, white muzzle and a round rat-like tail.
species.en_short_description: Large brown semi-aquatic rodent with orange incisors, white muzzle and a round rat-like tail.
species.description: Introduced from South America and established in California and Washington wetlands. Beaver-sized but with a round, not flattened, tail. Grazes marsh vegetation to bare mud where numerous.
species.en_description: Introduced from South America and established in California and Washington wetlands. Beaver-sized but with a round, not flattened, tail. Grazes marsh vegetation to bare mud where numerous.

species.name: ratón de Baja California
species.short_description: Slim deer mouse with large ears, on the arid Pacific slope of the peninsula.
species.en_short_description: Slim deer mouse with large ears, on the arid Pacific slope of the peninsula.
species.description: Southern California and Baja California Sur. One of several near-identical peninsular deer mice; larger-eared than most. Rocky slopes and desert scrub, strictly at night.
species.en_description: Southern California and Baja California Sur. One of several near-identical peninsular deer mice; larger-eared than most. Rocky slopes and desert scrub, strictly at night.

species.name: Ratón cosechero común
species.short_description: Tiny grassland mouse with a grooved upper incisor and a faintly bicoloured tail.
species.en_short_description: Tiny grassland mouse with a grooved upper incisor and a faintly bicoloured tail.
species.description: Weedy fields and marsh edges in Colorado, California, Washington and central Mexico. Smaller than a deer mouse. Weaves a ball-shaped grass nest above ground, unlike burrowing mice.
species.en_description: Weedy fields and marsh edges in Colorado, California, Washington and central Mexico. Smaller than a deer mouse. Weaves a ball-shaped grass nest above ground, unlike burrowing mice.

species.name: Gambel's Deer Mouse
species.short_description: California deer mouse with a moderately long bicoloured tail and white underparts.
species.en_short_description: California deer mouse with a moderately long bicoloured tail and white underparts.
species.description: Recently split from the western deer mouse complex and widespread through California grassland and woodland. Field-inseparable from its relatives; locality does the work.
species.en_description: Recently split from the western deer mouse complex and widespread through California grassland and woodland. Field-inseparable from its relatives; locality does the work.

species.name: Ratón de patas blancas
species.short_description: Warm brown mouse with bright white feet and belly and a bicoloured tail.
species.en_short_description: Warm brown mouse with bright white feet and belly and a bicoloured tail.
species.description: Eastern woodland and brushy edges in New York, plus Colorado and central Mexico. Richer russet above than the Deer Mouse. Frequently enters cabins and outbuildings in autumn.
species.en_description: Eastern woodland and brushy edges in New York, plus Colorado and central Mexico. Richer russet above than the Deer Mouse. Frequently enters cabins and outbuildings in autumn.

species.name: Northern California pocket gopher
species.short_description: Large-headed pocket gopher of northern California, known by its soil mounds.
species.en_short_description: Large-headed pocket gopher of northern California, known by its soil mounds.
species.description: A northern California species with a notably broad skull. As with all gophers, the fan-shaped mounds and plugged tunnels are the practical field record rather than the animal.
species.en_description: A northern California species with a notably broad skull. As with all gophers, the fan-shaped mounds and plugged tunnels are the practical field record rather than the animal.

species.name: rata magueyera
species.short_description: Large woodrat with conspicuously big ears and a long furred tail.
species.en_short_description: Large woodrat with conspicuously big ears and a long furred tail.
species.description: Central and southern California oak woodland. Splits from the Dusky-footed Woodrat on range and ear size. Builds the same tall stick houses and is equally strictly nocturnal.
species.en_description: Central and southern California oak woodland. Splits from the Dusky-footed Woodrat on range and ear size. Builds the same tall stick houses and is equally strictly nocturnal.

species.name: Rata canguro de Sonora
species.short_description: The largest kangaroo rat: pale, white-tipped tail, entirely white hind feet.
species.en_short_description: The largest kangaroo rat: pale, white-tipped tail, entirely white hind feet.
species.description: Fine wind-blown sand in the southern California deserts. Bigger and paler than Merriam's, with white rather than dark soles. Excavates large burrow systems in dune flanks.
species.en_description: Fine wind-blown sand in the southern California deserts. Bigger and paler than Merriam's, with white rather than dark soles. Excavates large burrow systems in dune flanks.

species.name: Ratón de cactus
species.short_description: Large-eared, silky-furred desert mouse with an almost naked tail.
species.en_short_description: Large-eared, silky-furred desert mouse with an almost naked tail.
species.description: Rocky desert in southern California and throughout Baja California Sur. The sparsely haired, faintly bicoloured tail separates it from other deer mice. Shelters in cactus and rock crevices.
species.en_description: Rocky desert in southern California and throughout Baja California Sur. The sparsely haired, faintly bicoloured tail separates it from other deer mice. Shelters in cactus and rock crevices.

species.name: Metorito de pradera
species.short_description: Stocky brown vole with a short tail and tiny ears, in wet meadow.
species.en_short_description: Stocky brown vole with a short tail and tiny ears, in wet meadow.
species.description: The vole of New York fields and marsh edges. Cuts a network of grass runways and clipped stem piles. Active day and night year-round, tunnelling under snow in winter.
species.en_description: The vole of New York fields and marsh edges. Cuts a network of grass runways and clipped stem piles. Active day and night year-round, tunnelling under snow in winter.

species.name: Rata canguro de Baja California
species.short_description: Medium kangaroo rat of coastal sage and chaparral, with a crested tail.
species.en_short_description: Medium kangaroo rat of coastal sage and chaparral, with a crested tail.
species.description: Southern California and northern Baja slopes rather than open desert. Darker than the desert kangaroo rats. Bipedal hopping tracks in dust are a good sign of presence.
species.en_description: Southern California and northern Baja slopes rather than open desert. Darker than the desert kangaroo rats. Bipedal hopping tracks in dust are a good sign of presence.

species.name: Ratón piñonero
species.short_description: Large-eared mouse of Mexican pinyon and oak highlands.
species.en_short_description: Large-eared mouse of Mexican pinyon and oak highlands.
species.description: Rocky highland woodland around Mexico City and central Mexico. Notably big-eared even for a deer mouse. Shelters in rock crevices and juniper litter.
species.en_description: Rocky highland woodland around Mexico City and central Mexico. Notably big-eared even for a deer mouse. Shelters in rock crevices and juniper litter.

species.name: Castor de montaña
species.short_description: Tailless, mole-eyed burrowing rodent of wet Pacific forest; not a beaver at all.
species.en_short_description: Tailless, mole-eyed burrowing rodent of wet Pacific forest; not a beaver at all.
species.description: The most primitive living rodent, restricted to damp coastal forest in California and Washington. Almost never seen: look for clipped fern fronds stacked at burrow mouths on seepy slopes.
species.en_description: The most primitive living rodent, restricted to damp coastal forest in California and Washington. Almost never seen: look for clipped fern fronds stacked at burrow mouths on seepy slopes.

species.name: Rata Cambalachera de Cola Peluda
species.short_description: Woodrat with a genuinely squirrel-like bushy tail, on cliffs and in cabins.
species.en_short_description: Woodrat with a genuinely squirrel-like bushy tail, on cliffs and in cabins.
species.description: The packrat of Colorado, Sierra and Cascade rock country. The full bushy tail separates it from every other woodrat. Middens cemented with urine can persist for millennia.
species.en_description: The packrat of Colorado, Sierra and Cascade rock country. The full bushy tail separates it from every other woodrat. Middens cemented with urine can persist for millennia.

species.name: Rata cambalachera del desierto
species.short_description: Small grey woodrat with a furred but not bushy tail, in rocky desert scrub.
species.en_short_description: Small grey woodrat with a furred but not bushy tail, in rocky desert scrub.
species.description: Colorado Plateau and California desert. Smaller and greyer than other woodrats. Nests among cholla and rock, packing the entrance with spines as a defence.
species.en_description: Colorado Plateau and California desert. Smaller and greyer than other woodrats. Nests among cholla and rock, packing the entrance with spines as a defence.

species.name: Tuza de montaña
species.short_description: Small grey-brown gopher of mountain meadow and sagebrush, with earth-crescent mounds.
species.en_short_description: Small grey-brown gopher of mountain meadow and sagebrush, with earth-crescent mounds.
species.description: Colorado, eastern California and Washington. Winter tunnelling through snow leaves ropes of soil called eskers on the ground surface once the snow melts — a distinctive spring find.
species.en_description: Colorado, eastern California and Washington. Winter tunnelling through snow leaves ropes of soil called eskers on the ground surface once the snow melts — a distinctive spring find.

species.name: Western Meadow Vole
species.short_description: Short-tailed brown vole of northern wet meadow, split from the eastern form.
species.en_short_description: Short-tailed brown vole of northern wet meadow, split from the eastern form.
species.description: Colorado and Washington damp grassland. Identical in the field to the Eastern Meadow Vole; the two are separated by range. Runways through matted grass are the usual evidence.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington damp grassland. Identical in the field to the Eastern Meadow Vole; the two are separated by range. Runways through matted grass are the usual evidence.

species.name: Ratón de abazones arenero
species.short_description: Small pale silky pocket mouse of Baja sand flats.
species.en_short_description: Small pale silky pocket mouse of Baja sand flats.
species.description: Baja California Sur dunes and sandy desert. Soft-furred rather than spiny, and very pale. Nocturnal, filling external cheek pouches with seeds gathered from the sand surface.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur dunes and sandy desert. Soft-furred rather than spiny, and very pale. Nocturnal, filling external cheek pouches with seeds gathered from the sand surface.

species.name: Ratón de la isla Santa Catalina
species.short_description: Island deer mouse endemic to Santa Catalina Island in the Gulf of California.
species.en_short_description: Island deer mouse endemic to Santa Catalina Island in the Gulf of California.
species.description: Restricted to one Baja California Sur island, which makes any record notable. Typical deer-mouse form with large ears and a bicoloured tail. Island endemism makes it inherently vulnerable.
species.en_description: Restricted to one Baja California Sur island, which makes any record notable. Typical deer-mouse form with large ears and a bicoloured tail. Island endemism makes it inherently vulnerable.

species.name: Ratón-de abazones de California
species.short_description: Large spiny-rumped pocket mouse with a long crested tail, in California chaparral.
species.en_short_description: Large spiny-rumped pocket mouse with a long crested tail, in California chaparral.
species.description: Coastal and foothill California. Among the biggest pocket mice, with obvious rump spines and a well-crested tail. Prefers brushy slopes with leaf litter over open sand.
species.en_description: Coastal and foothill California. Among the biggest pocket mice, with obvious rump spines and a well-crested tail. Prefers brushy slopes with leaf litter over open sand.

species.name: Rata canguro común
species.short_description: Compact kangaroo rat with five toes on each hind foot and a broad-crested tail.
species.en_short_description: Compact kangaroo rat with five toes on each hind foot and a broad-crested tail.
species.description: Sandy soils in Colorado, eastern California and Washington. The five-toed hind foot separates it from four-toed relatives. Common on prairie sandhills and dune blowouts.
species.en_description: Sandy soils in Colorado, eastern California and Washington. The five-toed hind foot separates it from four-toed relatives. Common on prairie sandhills and dune blowouts.

species.name: Rata canguro de California
species.short_description: Dark-backed California kangaroo rat with a strongly white-crested tail.
species.en_short_description: Dark-backed California kangaroo rat with a strongly white-crested tail.
species.description: Central California grassland and open woodland. Darker than desert species and largely restricted to the state. Bipedal tracks and small burrow entrances under grass tussocks.
species.en_description: Central California grassland and open woodland. Darker than desert species and largely restricted to the state. Bipedal tracks and small burrow entrances under grass tussocks.

species.name: Pinzón mexicano
species.short_description: Small streaky finch; males washed rose-red on head and breast.
species.en_short_description: Small streaky finch; males washed rose-red on head and breast.
species.description: The most-observed bird across all six regions. Native to the West and Mexico, introduced to the East. Males vary from red through orange to yellow depending on diet. Sings a jumbled warble ending in a rising buzz.
species.en_description: The most-observed bird across all six regions. Native to the West and Mexico, introduced to the East. Males vary from red through orange to yellow depending on diet. Sings a jumbled warble ending in a rising buzz.

species.name: Mirlo primavera
species.short_description: Grey-backed thrush with a brick-orange breast and a broken white eye-ring.
species.en_short_description: Grey-backed thrush with a brick-orange breast and a broken white eye-ring.
species.description: Present in all six regions, on lawns everywhere. Runs, stops, tilts its head to locate worms. Dawn song is a clear caroling phrase repeated with variations, and often the first bird singing.
species.en_description: Present in all six regions, on lawns everywhere. Runs, stops, tilts its head to locate worms. Dawn song is a clear caroling phrase repeated with variations, and often the first bird singing.

species.name: Garza morena
species.short_description: Tall grey-blue heron that flies with its neck folded into a tight S.
species.en_short_description: Tall grey-blue heron that flies with its neck folded into a tight S.
species.description: Every region. Stands motionless in shallows then strikes. Far larger than any egret and unmistakably grey rather than white. Nests colonially in treetop stick platforms called heronries.
species.en_description: Every region. Stands motionless in shallows then strikes. Far larger than any egret and unmistakably grey rather than white. Nests colonially in treetop stick platforms called heronries.

species.name: Gorrión Doméstico
species.short_description: Chunky brown sparrow; males with a grey cap, black bib and chestnut nape.
species.en_short_description: Chunky brown sparrow; males with a grey cap, black bib and chestnut nape.
species.description: Introduced and now ubiquitous in all six regions, tied closely to buildings and pavement. Not a native sparrow at all but an Old World weaver relative. Nests in signs, vents and traffic lights.
species.en_description: Introduced and now ubiquitous in all six regions, tied closely to buildings and pavement. Not a native sparrow at all but an Old World weaver relative. Nests in signs, vents and traffic lights.

species.name: Gorrión cantor
species.short_description: Heavily streaked brown sparrow with a bold central breast spot.
species.en_short_description: Heavily streaked brown sparrow with a bold central breast spot.
species.description: Every region, in damp thickets and garden edges. Pumps its tail in flight. Song opens with three clear identical notes before a jumble — the most reliable field cue among streaked sparrows.
species.en_description: Every region, in damp thickets and garden edges. Pumps its tail in flight. Song opens with three clear identical notes before a jumble — the most reliable field cue among streaked sparrows.

species.name: Junco Ojos Negros
species.short_description: Slate or brown hooded sparrow that flashes white outer tail feathers in flight.
species.en_short_description: Slate or brown hooded sparrow that flashes white outer tail feathers in flight.
species.description: Winters in flocks on the ground under feeders and forest edge. Regional forms differ sharply — slate in the East, pink-sided and grey-headed in Colorado, Oregon form in the West — but all flash white tail sides.
species.en_description: Winters in flocks on the ground under feeders and forest edge. Regional forms differ sharply — slate in the East, pink-sided and grey-headed in Colorado, Oregon form in the West — but all flash white tail sides.

species.name: Tordo sargento
species.short_description: Glossy black marsh bird; males show scarlet shoulder patches edged yellow.
species.en_short_description: Glossy black marsh bird; males show scarlet shoulder patches edged yellow.
species.description: Every region, in cattail marsh and wet field. Males sing a rasping conk-la-ree from a stem with wings spread. Streaky brown females look like an entirely different species.
species.en_description: Every region, in cattail marsh and wet field. Males sing a rasping conk-la-ree from a stem with wings spread. Streaky brown females look like an entirely different species.

species.name: Garza blanca
species.short_description: Tall all-white heron with a yellow bill and black legs and feet.
species.en_short_description: Tall all-white heron with a yellow bill and black legs and feet.
species.description: Every region. Bigger than a Snowy Egret and separated by the yellow rather than black bill. Grows long lacy back plumes when breeding — the feathers that nearly caused its extinction.
species.en_description: Every region. Bigger than a Snowy Egret and separated by the yellow rather than black bill. Grows long lacy back plumes when breeding — the feathers that nearly caused its extinction.

species.name: Cormorán Orejón
species.short_description: Dark fish-eating waterbird with a hooked bill and orange throat pouch.
species.en_short_description: Dark fish-eating waterbird with a hooked bill and orange throat pouch.
species.description: Every region. Swims low with the bill tilted up, then perches with wings spread to dry. Flies in loose V-lines. Breeding adults show fine white head tufts.
species.en_description: Every region. Swims low with the bill tilted up, then perches with wings spread to dry. Flies in loose V-lines. Breeding adults show fine white head tufts.

species.name: Cuervo Norteamericano
species.short_description: All-black bird with a fan-shaped tail and a flat, even caw.
species.en_short_description: All-black bird with a fan-shaped tail and a flat, even caw.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Smaller than a Common Raven with a fan rather than wedge tail, and a clean caw rather than a croak. Forms enormous winter roosts in cities.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Smaller than a Common Raven with a fan rather than wedge tail, and a clean caw rather than a croak. Forms enormous winter roosts in cities.

species.name: Gallareta americana
species.short_description: Slate-grey waterbird with a white chicken-like bill and lobed toes.
species.en_short_description: Slate-grey waterbird with a white chicken-like bill and lobed toes.
species.description: Every region, abundant on ponds. Not a duck: it swims with a bobbing head and runs across water to take off. Lobed rather than webbed toes let it walk on lawns and mud.
species.en_description: Every region, abundant on ponds. Not a duck: it swims with a bobbing head and runs across water to take off. Lobed rather than webbed toes let it walk on lawns and mud.

species.name: Gorrión corona blanca
species.short_description: Crisp grey sparrow with a boldly black-and-white striped crown and pink bill.
species.en_short_description: Crisp grey sparrow with a boldly black-and-white striped crown and pink bill.
species.description: Every region, in flocks along hedgerows and brush piles in winter. The clean crown stripes and unstreaked grey breast are unmistakable. Whistled song varies by local dialect.
species.en_description: Every region, in flocks along hedgerows and brush piles in winter. The clean crown stripes and unstreaked grey breast are unmistakable. Whistled song varies by local dialect.

species.name: Huilota Común
species.short_description: Slim buff dove with a long pointed tail and black spots on the wing.
species.en_short_description: Slim buff dove with a long pointed tail and black spots on the wing.
species.description: Every region. Wings whistle sharply on take-off. The mournful cooing is often mistaken for an owl. Perches on wires in pairs and feeds on bare ground.
species.en_description: Every region. Wings whistle sharply on take-off. The mournful cooing is often mistaken for an owl. Perches on wires in pairs and feeds on bare ground.

species.name: Pelícano café
species.short_description: Huge coastal pelican with a long pouched bill that plunge-dives for fish.
species.en_short_description: Huge coastal pelican with a long pouched bill that plunge-dives for fish.
species.description: Coastal California, Baja, and increasingly recorded elsewhere. Dives from height with a twisting crash, unlike the White Pelican which never plunges. Flies in lines low along the swell.
species.en_description: Coastal California, Baja, and increasingly recorded elsewhere. Dives from height with a twisting crash, unlike the White Pelican which never plunges. Flies in lines low along the swell.

species.name: Colibrí cabeza roja
species.short_description: Stocky hummingbird; males with an iridescent rose-red crown and throat.
species.en_short_description: Stocky hummingbird; males with an iridescent rose-red crown and throat.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja, and the one hummingbird that stays all winter on the Pacific coast. Males display with a steep dive ending in a sharp squeak made by the tail.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja, and the one hummingbird that stays all winter on the Pacific coast. Males display with a steep dive ending in a sharp squeak made by the tail.

species.name: Carpintero de Pechera Común
species.short_description: Large brown ground-feeding woodpecker with a black chest crescent and white rump.
species.en_short_description: Large brown ground-feeding woodpecker with a black chest crescent and white rump.
species.description: Five regions. Red-shafted in the West, yellow-shafted in the East, with intergrades on the plains. Feeds on ants on lawns rather than drilling trunks. The white rump flashes in flight.
species.en_description: Five regions. Red-shafted in the West, yellow-shafted in the East, with intergrades on the plains. Feeds on ants on lawns rather than drilling trunks. The white rump flashes in flight.

species.name: Garza dedos dorados
species.short_description: Slender white egret with a black bill, black legs and bright yellow feet.
species.en_short_description: Slender white egret with a black bill, black legs and bright yellow feet.
species.description: Every region. Smaller and daintier than the Great Egret, and the golden slippers are the field mark. Actively shuffles its feet to stir up prey rather than standing still.
species.en_description: Every region. Smaller and daintier than the Great Egret, and the golden slippers are the field mark. Actively shuffles its feet to stir up prey rather than standing still.

species.name: Estornino pinto eurasiático
species.short_description: Chunky dark bird with a short tail and, in winter, dense white spotting.
species.en_short_description: Chunky dark bird with a short tail and, in winter, dense white spotting.
species.description: Introduced and abundant in all six regions. Iridescent green-purple in summer with a yellow bill. Walks rather than hops. Forms vast swirling murmurations at winter roosts.
species.en_description: Introduced and abundant in all six regions. Iridescent green-purple in summer with a yellow bill. Walks rather than hops. Forms vast swirling murmurations at winter roosts.

species.name: Chipe coronado
species.short_description: Grey warbler with a bright yellow rump patch and yellow side patches.
species.en_short_description: Grey warbler with a bright yellow rump patch and yellow side patches.
species.description: Every region and the commonest warbler in winter, because it can digest waxy berries. Audubon's form in the West has a yellow throat, Myrtle in the East a white one.
species.en_description: Every region and the commonest warbler in winter, because it can digest waxy berries. Audubon's form in the West has a yellow throat, Myrtle in the East a white one.

species.name: Rascador Moteado
species.short_description: Large dark towhee with white wing spots, rufous flanks and red eyes.
species.en_short_description: Large dark towhee with white wing spots, rufous flanks and red eyes.
species.description: Every region, scratching noisily in leaf litter under shrubs with a double-footed backward hop. Song is a buzzy trill. Far more often heard rustling than seen.
species.en_description: Every region, scratching noisily in leaf litter under shrubs with a double-footed backward hop. Song is a buzzy trill. Far more often heard rustling than seen.

species.name: Garza Nocturna Corona Negra
species.short_description: Squat grey heron with a black crown and back and large red eyes.
species.en_short_description: Squat grey heron with a black crown and back and large red eyes.
species.description: Every region. Hunches motionless at the water's edge at dusk. Juveniles are brown and heavily streaked. The flight call is a hoarse barking quok, often heard overhead after dark.
species.en_description: Every region. Hunches motionless at the water's edge at dusk. Juveniles are brown and heavily streaked. The flight call is a hoarse barking quok, often heard overhead after dark.

species.name: Sinsonte norteño
species.short_description: Slim grey bird with white wing patches that flash in flight.
species.en_short_description: Slim grey bird with white wing patches that flash in flight.
species.description: Every region. Sings long strings of imitated phrases, each repeated three or more times, sometimes through the night. Fans its wings while foraging on lawns.
species.en_description: Every region. Sings long strings of imitated phrases, each repeated three or more times, sometimes through the night. Fans its wings while foraging on lawns.

species.name: Pavo
species.short_description: Very large dark iridescent gamebird with a bare blue-and-red head.
species.en_short_description: Very large dark iridescent gamebird with a bare blue-and-red head.
species.description: Five regions, in oak and pine woodland and increasingly in suburbs. Males fan the tail and gobble in spring. Roosts in trees at night despite feeding entirely on the ground.
species.en_description: Five regions, in oak and pine woodland and increasingly in suburbs. Males fan the tail and gobble in spring. Roosts in trees at night despite feeding entirely on the ground.

species.name: Jilguerito Dominico
species.short_description: Tiny finch with a black or greenish cap, yellow underparts and white wing flashes.
species.en_short_description: Tiny finch with a black or greenish cap, yellow underparts and white wing flashes.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Smaller than the American Goldfinch with a dark rather than yellow back. Twittering flocks feed on seed heads and sunflower.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Smaller than the American Goldfinch with a dark rather than yellow back. Twittering flocks feed on seed heads and sunflower.

species.name: Chara Copetona
species.short_description: Dark crested jay with a deep blue body and blackish head.
species.en_short_description: Dark crested jay with a deep blue body and blackish head.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and central Mexico conifer forest. The tall shaggy crest and dark front separate it from every other blue jay. Loud, bold and quick to raid a picnic.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and central Mexico conifer forest. The tall shaggy crest and dark front separate it from every other blue jay. Loud, bold and quick to raid a picnic.

species.name: Chara californiana
species.short_description: Crestless blue jay with a white throat, grey back patch and blue necklace.
species.en_short_description: Crestless blue jay with a white throat, grey back patch and blue necklace.
species.description: California, Washington and Baja oak and scrub. No crest, unlike Steller's Jay. Caches thousands of acorns each autumn and remembers where. Harsh rising scolding calls.
species.en_description: California, Washington and Baja oak and scrub. No crest, unlike Steller's Jay. Caches thousands of acorns each autumn and remembers where. Harsh rising scolding calls.

species.name: Calandria Dorso Negro Menor
species.short_description: Slim oriole; males orange-yellow with a black throat, back and tail.
species.en_short_description: Slim oriole; males orange-yellow with a black throat, back and tail.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja, closely tied to palms. Weaves a hanging nest stitched to the underside of a palm frond. Visits hummingbird feeders freely.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja, closely tied to palms. Weaves a hanging nest stitched to the underside of a palm frond. Visits hummingbird feeders freely.

species.name: Chorlo tildío
species.short_description: Brown-and-white plover with two black breast bands and a rusty rump.
species.en_short_description: Brown-and-white plover with two black breast bands and a rusty rump.
species.description: Every region, on gravel, playing fields and parking lots rather than beaches. Performs a broken-wing display to lead intruders from the nest. Calls its own name loudly in flight.
species.en_description: Every region, on gravel, playing fields and parking lots rather than beaches. Performs a broken-wing display to lead intruders from the nest. Calls its own name loudly in flight.

species.name: Papamoscas negro
species.short_description: Sooty-black flycatcher with a clean white belly, always near water.
species.en_short_description: Sooty-black flycatcher with a clean white belly, always near water.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Pumps its tail from a low perch and sallies out after insects. The sharp black-and-white contrast is unlike any other flycatcher here.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Pumps its tail from a low perch and sallies out after insects. The sharp black-and-white contrast is unlike any other flycatcher here.

species.name: Gaviota occidental
species.short_description: Large dark-backed gull with a heavy yellow bill and pink legs.
species.en_short_description: Large dark-backed gull with a heavy yellow bill and pink legs.
species.description: Pacific coast from Washington to Baja. Darker-mantled than the California Gull, with a much heavier bill. The default large gull of piers and harbours on this coast.
species.en_description: Pacific coast from Washington to Baja. Darker-mantled than the California Gull, with a much heavier bill. The default large gull of piers and harbours on this coast.

species.name: Urraca de Hudson
species.short_description: Long-tailed black-and-white corvid with iridescent blue-green wings and tail.
species.en_short_description: Long-tailed black-and-white corvid with iridescent blue-green wings and tail.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Unmistakable, with a tail longer than the body. Builds bulky domed stick nests in thorny trees. Noisy, social and inquisitive.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Unmistakable, with a tail longer than the body. Builds bulky domed stick nests in thorny trees. Noisy, social and inquisitive.

species.name: Cuervo Común
species.short_description: Very large all-black bird with a wedge-shaped tail, heavy bill and shaggy throat.
species.en_short_description: Very large all-black bird with a wedge-shaped tail, heavy bill and shaggy throat.
species.description: Every region. Bigger than the American Crow with a wedge tail and a deep croaking call. Soars and tumbles in flight, often in pairs. Ranges from city to alpine to desert.
species.en_description: Every region. Bigger than the American Crow with a wedge tail and a deep croaking call. Soars and tumbles in flight, often in pairs. Ranges from city to alpine to desert.

species.name: Gaviota pico anillado
species.short_description: Medium gull with a black ring near the bill tip and yellow legs.
species.en_short_description: Medium gull with a black ring near the bill tip and yellow legs.
species.description: Every region, and the gull most likely to be inland. The clean bill ring and yellow legs separate it from the pink-legged large gulls. Abundant on parking lots and reservoirs.
species.en_description: Every region, and the gull most likely to be inland. The clean bill ring and yellow legs separate it from the pink-legged large gulls. Abundant on parking lots and reservoirs.

species.name: Zanate mexicano
species.short_description: Glossy purple-black blackbird with a very long keel-shaped tail and pale eyes.
species.en_short_description: Glossy purple-black blackbird with a very long keel-shaped tail and pale eyes.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Males are large with an extravagant tail; females are much smaller and brown. Noisy communal roosts dominate town plazas.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Males are large with an extravagant tail; females are much smaller and brown. Noisy communal roosts dominate town plazas.

species.name: Carbonero de capucha negra
species.short_description: Tiny grey bird with a black cap and bib and white cheeks.
species.en_short_description: Tiny grey bird with a black cap and bib and white cheeks.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Whistles a clear two-note fee-bee. Leads mixed feeding flocks through winter woods and takes seed from feeders fearlessly.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Whistles a clear two-note fee-bee. Leads mixed feeding flocks through winter woods and takes seed from feeders fearlessly.

species.name: Pelícano Blanco Americano
species.short_description: Enormous white pelican with black flight feathers and a huge orange bill.
species.en_short_description: Enormous white pelican with black flight feathers and a huge orange bill.
species.description: Every region on inland lakes and reservoirs. Feeds cooperatively by herding fish in the shallows rather than plunge-diving. Soars in tight synchronised flocks on thermals.
species.en_description: Every region on inland lakes and reservoirs. Feeds cooperatively by herding fish in the shallows rather than plunge-diving. Soars in tight synchronised flocks on thermals.

species.name: Cardenal rojo
species.short_description: Crested finch; males brilliant red with a black face mask.
species.en_short_description: Crested finch; males brilliant red with a black face mask.
