species.description: Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. Forms enormous colonies under bridges and in caves that stream out in columns at dusk — often the most spectacular wildlife event in a city.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. Forms enormous colonies under bridges and in caves that stream out in columns at dusk — often the most spectacular wildlife event in a city.

species.name: Murciélago ratón de California
species.short_description: Very small dark bat with tiny feet and a keeled calcar, flying erratically low.
species.en_short_description: Very small dark bat with tiny feet and a keeled calcar, flying erratically low.
species.description: California, Washington, central Mexico and Baja. One of several near-identical small myotis; flight low over water and along trails is typical. Roosts in crevices and under bark.
species.en_description: California, Washington, central Mexico and Baja. One of several near-identical small myotis; flight low over water and along trails is typical. Roosts in crevices and under bark.

species.name: Topo pata ancha
species.short_description: Stout mole with very broad front feet and velvety grey-black fur.
species.en_short_description: Stout mole with very broad front feet and velvety grey-black fur.
species.description: California valleys and foothills. Known almost entirely from its volcano-shaped soil mounds in lawns and meadows. Front feet are turned permanently outward for digging.
species.en_description: California valleys and foothills. Known almost entirely from its volcano-shaped soil mounds in lawns and meadows. Front feet are turned permanently outward for digging.

species.name: Murciélago canoso de cola peluda
species.short_description: Large bat with frosted silver-tipped mahogany fur and a heavily furred tail membrane.
species.en_short_description: Large bat with frosted silver-tipped mahogany fur and a heavily furred tail membrane.
species.description: Five regions. The frosted appearance and yellowish throat are distinctive, and it is one of the largest bats here. Roosts in foliage rather than caves, and migrates long distances.
species.en_description: Five regions. The frosted appearance and yellowish throat are distinctive, and it is one of the largest bats here. Roosts in foliage rather than caves, and migrates long distances.

species.name: Liebre de cola blanca
species.short_description: Large pale hare with a wholly white tail, turning white in winter.
species.en_short_description: Large pale hare with a wholly white tail, turning white in winter.
species.description: High plains and mountain parks in Colorado, eastern California and Washington. Bigger and paler than the Black-tailed Jackrabbit, with an all-white tail. Prefers higher, colder open country.
species.en_description: High plains and mountain parks in Colorado, eastern California and Washington. Bigger and paler than the Black-tailed Jackrabbit, with an all-white tail. Prefers higher, colder open country.

species.name: Armiño Americano
species.short_description: Very small weasel with a black-tipped tail, white in winter, brown above in summer.
species.en_short_description: Very small weasel with a black-tipped tail, white in winter, brown above in summer.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Smaller and shorter-tailed than the Long-tailed Weasel. Hunts voles under snow, so winter tracks that vanish into a hole are typical evidence.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Smaller and shorter-tailed than the Long-tailed Weasel. Hunts voles under snow, so winter tracks that vanish into a hole are typical evidence.

species.name: Murciélago orejas de embudo
species.short_description: Tiny delicate bat with funnel-shaped ears and extremely long legs and tail.
species.en_short_description: Tiny delicate bat with funnel-shaped ears and extremely long legs and tail.
species.description: Caves in Baja California Sur and mainland Mexico. Butterfly-like fluttering flight is unlike any other bat here. Highly cave-dependent, which makes colonies easy to disturb.
species.en_description: Caves in Baja California Sur and mainland Mexico. Butterfly-like fluttering flight is unlike any other bat here. Highly cave-dependent, which makes colonies easy to disturb.

species.name: Murciélago de Cañón
species.short_description: The smallest bat in the region: pale, with a black face mask and slow fluttering flight.
species.en_short_description: The smallest bat in the region: pale, with a black face mask and slow fluttering flight.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Emerges very early, often in full daylight, which makes it the bat most likely to be photographed. Flight is weak and erratic, almost moth-like.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Emerges very early, often in full daylight, which makes it the bat most likely to be photographed. Flight is weak and erratic, almost moth-like.

species.name: Conejo de monte
species.short_description: Large dark cottontail endemic to central Mexico's highlands.
species.en_short_description: Large dark cottontail endemic to central Mexico's highlands.
species.description: Mexico City's remaining scrub and pine-oak edges. The biggest of the cottontails, notably darker than US species. Endemic to central Mexico, so any record has regional value.
species.en_description: Mexico City's remaining scrub and pine-oak edges. The biggest of the cottontails, notably darker than US species. Endemic to central Mexico, so any record has regional value.

species.name: Murciélago cola peluda rojizo
species.short_description: Bright rusty-red bat with a fully furred tail membrane, roosting in foliage.
species.en_short_description: Bright rusty-red bat with a fully furred tail membrane, roosting in foliage.
species.description: Colorado and New York. The vivid brick-red fur is unmistakable. Hangs from a leaf petiole looking like a dead leaf, which is how most day roosts are found. Migratory.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. The vivid brick-red fur is unmistakable. Hangs from a leaf petiole looking like a dead leaf, which is how most day roosts are found. Migratory.

species.name: Teporingo
species.short_description: Tiny short-eared rabbit endemic to the volcanoes around Mexico City.
species.en_short_description: Tiny short-eared rabbit endemic to the volcanoes around Mexico City.
species.description: Found only in bunchgrass zacatón on the slopes of Popocatépetl, Iztaccíhuatl and neighbouring peaks. Very small with rounded ears and almost no visible tail. Endangered; a genuinely significant sighting.
species.en_description: Found only in bunchgrass zacatón on the slopes of Popocatépetl, Iztaccíhuatl and neighbouring peaks. Very small with rounded ears and almost no visible tail. Endangered; a genuinely significant sighting.

species.name: Murciélago pelo plateado
species.short_description: Blackish bat with silver-frosted back fur and a partly furred tail membrane.
species.en_short_description: Blackish bat with silver-frosted back fur and a partly furred tail membrane.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York conifer forest. Darker overall than the Hoary Bat with crisper silver tipping. Flies slowly along forest roads and streams; roosts under bark.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York conifer forest. Darker overall than the Hoary Bat with crisper silver tipping. Flies slowly along forest roads and streams; roosts under bark.

species.name: Murciélago amarillo del Oeste
species.short_description: Pale yellowish bat with a partly furred tail membrane, roosting in dead palm fronds.
species.en_short_description: Pale yellowish bat with a partly furred tail membrane, roosting in dead palm fronds.
species.description: Southern California, central Mexico and Baja. Tied closely to palms, roosting in the dead skirt beneath the crown. Yellow-buff colouring separates it from the red and hoary bats.
species.en_description: Southern California, central Mexico and Baja. Tied closely to palms, roosting in the dead skirt beneath the crown. Yellow-buff colouring separates it from the red and hoary bats.

species.name: Murciélago pescador
species.short_description: Large-footed bat with enormous clawed feet used to gaff fish from the sea surface.
species.en_short_description: Large-footed bat with enormous clawed feet used to gaff fish from the sea surface.
species.description: Endemic to islands in the Gulf of California, including Baja California Sur. The huge hind feet and claws are unlike any other bat here. Roosts under rocks on bare desert islands.
species.en_description: Endemic to islands in the Gulf of California, including Baja California Sur. The huge hind feet and claws are unlike any other bat here. Roosts under rocks on bare desert islands.

species.name: Conejo europeo
species.short_description: Grey-brown rabbit with a short white-undersided tail, living in warren colonies.
species.en_short_description: Grey-brown rabbit with a short white-undersided tail, living in warren colonies.
species.description: Feral populations in all four US regions and Baja, usually descended from released domestic stock, so odd colours and patches are common. Colonial and burrow-dwelling, unlike native cottontails.
species.en_description: Feral populations in all four US regions and Baja, usually descended from released domestic stock, so odd colours and patches are common. Colonial and burrow-dwelling, unlike native cottontails.

species.name: Murciélago orejón de Townsend
species.short_description: Medium bat with immense ears held erect, and two lumps on the muzzle.
species.en_short_description: Medium bat with immense ears held erect, and two lumps on the muzzle.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and central Mexico. The ears are almost as long as the forearm and unmistakable. Extremely sensitive to roost disturbance in caves and mines.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and central Mexico. The ears are almost as long as the forearm and unmistakable. Extremely sensitive to roost disturbance in caves and mines.

species.name: Murciélago-barba arrugada
species.short_description: Odd-faced bat with leaf-like flaps on the chin and ears that meet across the forehead.
species.en_short_description: Odd-faced bat with leaf-like flaps on the chin and ears that meet across the forehead.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. The folded, almost featureless face gives the name. Roosts in hot humid caves, often in large numbers, and hunts moths in open air.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. The folded, almost featureless face gives the name. Roosts in hot humid caves, often in large numbers, and hunts moths in open air.

species.name: Topo Nariz de Estrella
species.short_description: Mole with a ring of twenty-two fleshy pink tentacles around the snout.
species.en_short_description: Mole with a ring of twenty-two fleshy pink tentacles around the snout.
species.description: Wet meadow, marsh and stream bank in New York. The star is the most sensitive touch organ known in any mammal. Swims and forages underwater, unlike other moles.
species.en_description: Wet meadow, marsh and stream bank in New York. The star is the most sensitive touch organ known in any mammal. Swims and forages underwater, unlike other moles.

species.name: Miotis norteamericano
species.short_description: Small glossy brown bat with no keeled calcar, historically the commonest attic bat.
species.en_short_description: Small glossy brown bat with no keeled calcar, historically the commonest attic bat.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Once abundant and now devastated by white-nose syndrome in the east, so eastern records matter. Hunts insects low over water.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Once abundant and now devastated by white-nose syndrome in the east, so eastern records matter. Hunts insects low over water.

species.name: Hairy-tailed Mole
species.short_description: Stout dark mole with a short, distinctly hairy tail and a naked pointed snout.
species.en_short_description: Stout dark mole with a short, distinctly hairy tail and a naked pointed snout.
species.description: Well-drained woodland and field soils in New York. The furred tail separates it from the Eastern Mole. Its shallow tunnels raise visible ridges across lawns and forest floor.
species.en_description: Well-drained woodland and field soils in New York. The furred tail separates it from the Eastern Mole. Its shallow tunnels raise visible ridges across lawns and forest floor.

species.name: Culebra listonada común
species.short_description: Slim harmless snake with three pale stripes on a dark ground; often with red flecks.
species.en_short_description: Slim harmless snake with three pale stripes on a dark ground; often with red flecks.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The most widespread North American snake and the one most often found in gardens. Releases a musky secretion when handled. Bears live young.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The most widespread North American snake and the one most often found in gardens. Releases a musky secretion when handled. Bears live young.

species.name: Bejori de Cerca Occidental
species.short_description: Grey-brown spiny lizard; males with brilliant blue throat and belly patches.
species.en_short_description: Grey-brown spiny lizard; males with brilliant blue throat and belly patches.
species.description: California and Washington. The default lizard on fences, logs and trail-side rocks, doing push-up displays. Blue belly patches earn it the name blue-belly. Its blood kills Lyme bacteria in ticks.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The default lizard on fences, logs and trail-side rocks, doing push-up displays. Blue belly patches earn it the name blue-belly. Its blood kills Lyme bacteria in ticks.

species.name: Tortuga lagarto norteña
species.short_description: Massive dark turtle with a rough shell, huge head and a long saw-toothed tail.
species.en_short_description: Massive dark turtle with a rough shell, huge head and a long saw-toothed tail.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Powerful bite; keep clear of the head. Spends most of its life buried in mud, and is most often seen on land when a female is nesting in June.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Powerful bite; keep clear of the head. Spends most of its life buried in mud, and is most often seen on land when a female is nesting in June.

species.name: Culebra Listonada Noroccidental
species.short_description: Small variable garter snake with a narrow head and highly variable striping.
species.en_short_description: Small variable garter snake with a narrow head and highly variable striping.
species.description: California and Washington. The Pacific Northwest's most abundant snake, in lawns and blackberry thickets. Extremely variable — stripes may be yellow, red, or nearly absent. Eats mostly slugs.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The Pacific Northwest's most abundant snake, in lawns and blackberry thickets. Extremely variable — stripes may be yellow, red, or nearly absent. Eats mostly slugs.

species.name: Lagartija espinosa de las praderas
species.short_description: Small brown spiny lizard with pale dorsolateral stripes; males with blue belly patches.
species.en_short_description: Small brown spiny lizard with pale dorsolateral stripes; males with blue belly patches.
species.description: Eastern Colorado grassland and open woodland. Slimmer and more striped than the fence lizards. Climbs tree trunks and fence posts, flattening against the bark when approached.
species.en_description: Eastern Colorado grassland and open woodland. Slimmer and more striped than the fence lizards. Climbs tree trunks and fence posts, flattening against the bark when approached.

species.name: Lagartija espinosa del mezquite
species.short_description: Grey spiny lizard with fine dark crossbars and a distinct pale collar in some forms.
species.en_short_description: Grey spiny lizard with fine dark crossbars and a distinct pale collar in some forms.
species.description: Mexico City's most common lizard, on walls, magueyes and rock in the Basin of Mexico. Bears live young rather than laying eggs, unusual for a Sceloporus. Highly variable across populations.
species.en_description: Mexico City's most common lizard, on walls, magueyes and rock in the Basin of Mexico. Bears live young rather than laying eggs, unusual for a Sceloporus. Highly variable across populations.

species.name: Iguana de palo
species.short_description: Large grey iguana with a whorled spiny tail and dark shoulder bands.
species.en_short_description: Large grey iguana with a whorled spiny tail and dark shoulder bands.
species.description: Endemic to the Baja California peninsula and abundant in the cape region. Basks conspicuously on rock and in trees. Adults are largely herbivorous. Runs bipedally at speed.
species.en_description: Endemic to the Baja California peninsula and abundant in the cape region. Basks conspicuously on rock and in trees. Adults are largely herbivorous. Runs bipedally at speed.

species.name: Cascabel de pradera
species.short_description: Greenish-grey rattlesnake with dark blotches, a triangular head and a rattle.
species.en_short_description: Greenish-grey rattlesnake with dark blotches, a triangular head and a rattle.
species.description: Eastern Colorado plains and foothills. Venomous — keep well back and never handle. Dens communally in rock crevices for winter. Rattles as a warning, but not always before striking.
species.en_description: Eastern Colorado plains and foothills. Venomous — keep well back and never handle. Dens communally in rock crevices for winter. Rattles as a warning, but not always before striking.

species.name: Lagartija espinosa de collar
species.short_description: Robust dark spiny lizard with a bold black-and-white collar.
species.en_short_description: Robust dark spiny lizard with a bold black-and-white collar.
species.description: Highlands around Mexico City, on stone walls, rock outcrops and old masonry. The striking pale-bordered black collar is diagnostic. Retreats into crevices head-first when disturbed.
species.en_description: Highlands around Mexico City, on stone walls, rock outcrops and old masonry. The striking pale-bordered black collar is diagnostic. Retreats into crevices head-first when disturbed.

species.name: Tortuga pintada
species.short_description: Smooth dark turtle with red markings on the shell margin and yellow head stripes.
species.en_short_description: Smooth dark turtle with red markings on the shell margin and yellow head stripes.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Basks in rows on logs, sliding off at any approach. The red edging on the shell rim and bright yellow face lines are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Basks in rows on logs, sliding off at any approach. The red edging on the shell rim and bright yellow face lines are diagnostic.

species.name: tortuga gravada
species.short_description: Turtle with a red or yellow patch behind the eye and a yellow-striped neck.
species.en_short_description: Turtle with a red or yellow patch behind the eye and a yellow-striped neck.
species.description: Every region. The red-eared form is the ubiquitous pet-trade turtle, now feral worldwide, including Mexico City and Baja. Basks on logs and outcompetes native turtles.
species.en_description: Every region. The red-eared form is the ubiquitous pet-trade turtle, now feral worldwide, including Mexico City and Baja. Basks on logs and outcompetes native turtles.

species.name: Cachora Arenera
species.short_description: Pale slender desert lizard with bold black bands under a long curled tail.
species.en_short_description: Pale slender desert lizard with bold black bands under a long curled tail.
species.description: Southern California and Baja California Sur sand flats. Runs extremely fast on hind legs, waving the banded tail over its back as it stops. Diurnal even at peak heat.
species.en_description: Southern California and Baja California Sur sand flats. Runs extremely fast on hind legs, waving the banded tail over its back as it stops. Diurnal even at peak heat.

species.name: Cachora de Árbol Cola Negra
species.short_description: Small slim lizard with a dark tail and a fold of granular scales along the side.
species.en_short_description: Small slim lizard with a dark tail and a fold of granular scales along the side.
species.description: Southern California and throughout Baja California Sur. Clings to shrub stems and tree bark rather than rock, and is easy to miss against grey branches. Males show blue belly patches.
species.en_description: Southern California and throughout Baja California Sur. Clings to shrub stems and tree bark rather than rock, and is easy to miss against grey branches. Males show blue belly patches.

species.name: Lagartija norteña de mancha lateral
species.short_description: Small grey-brown lizard with a dark blotch just behind each foreleg.
species.en_short_description: Small grey-brown lizard with a dark blotch just behind each foreleg.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Abundant in dry open ground. Males come in three throat colours that correspond to different mating strategies, a much-studied system.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Abundant in dry open ground. Males come in three throat colours that correspond to different mating strategies, a much-studied system.

species.name: Lagarto Escorpión de América Occidental
species.short_description: Long-bodied lizard with a stiff armoured look, small legs and dark eyes.
species.en_short_description: Long-bodied lizard with a stiff armoured look, small legs and dark eyes.
species.description: California and Washington. Prefers cooler damp forest and rockpiles than its southern relative. The very long tail breaks off readily. Bears live young.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Prefers cooler damp forest and rockpiles than its southern relative. The very long tail breaks off readily. Bears live young.

species.name: Iguana de desierto
species.short_description: Pale round-bodied lizard with a long tail and rows of fine dorsal scales.
species.en_short_description: Pale round-bodied lizard with a long tail and rows of fine dorsal scales.
species.description: Southern California and Baja California Sur dunes and creosote flats. Highly heat-tolerant, active when other lizards have retreated. Largely herbivorous, feeding on creosote flowers.
species.en_description: Southern California and Baja California Sur dunes and creosote flats. Highly heat-tolerant, active when other lizards have retreated. Largely herbivorous, feeding on creosote flowers.

species.name: Culebra Listonada de Pradera
species.short_description: Garter snake with a bright orange-yellow mid-dorsal stripe and black bars on the lip.
species.en_short_description: Garter snake with a bright orange-yellow mid-dorsal stripe and black bars on the lip.
species.description: Eastern Colorado wet meadows and ditches. The vivid central stripe and the black vertical lip bars separate it from the Common Garter Snake. Hunts frogs and earthworms.
species.en_description: Eastern Colorado wet meadows and ditches. The vivid central stripe and the black vertical lip bars separate it from the Common Garter Snake. Hunts frogs and earthworms.

species.name: Lagartija espinosa de las mesetas
species.short_description: Grey spiny lizard of the Colorado Plateau; males with deep blue belly patches.
species.en_short_description: Grey spiny lizard of the Colorado Plateau; males with deep blue belly patches.
species.description: Western Colorado pinyon-juniper and slickrock country. Split from the Eastern Fence Lizard complex. Perches on rock and dead wood, doing rapid push-up displays.
species.en_description: Western Colorado pinyon-juniper and slickrock country. Split from the Eastern Fence Lizard complex. Perches on rock and dead wood, doing rapid push-up displays.

species.name: lagartija de collar del altiplano
species.short_description: Large-headed lizard with a black-and-white collar; males turquoise with a yellow head.
species.en_short_description: Large-headed lizard with a black-and-white collar; males turquoise with a yellow head.
species.description: Colorado's canyon and rimrock country. One of the most colourful North American lizards. Sprints bipedally between boulders with the tail raised. Bold and easily photographed.
species.en_description: Colorado's canyon and rimrock country. One of the most colourful North American lizards. Sprints bipedally between boulders with the tail raised. Bold and easily photographed.

species.name: Huico de Garganta Naranja
species.short_description: Slender striped whiptail with a very long tail and an orange throat when breeding.
species.en_short_description: Slender striped whiptail with a very long tail and an orange throat when breeding.
species.description: Southern California and Baja California Sur coastal scrub. Forages restlessly with jerky movements, nosing through litter for termites. Never basks still for long.
species.en_description: Southern California and Baja California Sur coastal scrub. Forages restlessly with jerky movements, nosing through litter for termites. Never basks still for long.

species.name: Topera
species.short_description: Large tan snake with dark saddle blotches, a pointed snout and a keeled scale pattern.
species.en_short_description: Large tan snake with dark saddle blotches, a pointed snout and a keeled scale pattern.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Harmless but hisses loudly and vibrates its tail, so it is frequently mistaken for a rattlesnake. Constricts rodents in their burrows.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Harmless but hisses loudly and vibrates its tail, so it is frequently mistaken for a rattlesnake. Constricts rodents in their burrows.

species.name: Camaleón de montaña de cuernos cortos
species.short_description: Flat round-bodied lizard with short blunt head horns and a fringe of side scales.
species.en_short_description: Flat round-bodied lizard with short blunt head horns and a fringe of side scales.
species.description: Colorado's shortgrass prairie and foothills. Sits motionless and relies on camouflage, so it is usually found underfoot. Eats mostly harvester ants. Bears live young.
species.en_description: Colorado's shortgrass prairie and foothills. Sits motionless and relies on camouflage, so it is usually found underfoot. Eats mostly harvester ants. Bears live young.

species.name: Falsa coralillo real oriental estadounidense
species.short_description: Grey snake with reddish-brown saddles edged in black and a Y-mark on the neck.
species.en_short_description: Grey snake with reddish-brown saddles edged in black and a Y-mark on the neck.
species.description: New York woodland, farmland and old foundations. Harmless constrictor often killed as a supposed copperhead. Frequently found under boards, rocks and sheet metal.
species.en_description: New York woodland, farmland and old foundations. Harmless constrictor often killed as a supposed copperhead. Frequently found under boards, rocks and sheet metal.

species.name: Camaleón de montaña
species.short_description: Round flat-bodied horned lizard with a crown of long spines, at high elevation.
species.en_short_description: Round flat-bodied horned lizard with a crown of long spines, at high elevation.
species.description: Highlands around Mexico City in pine-oak and grassland. Longer-horned than the US short-horned lizards. Bears live young, an adaptation to cold montane nights.
species.en_description: Highlands around Mexico City in pine-oak and grassland. Longer-horned than the US short-horned lizards. Bears live young, an adaptation to cold montane nights.

species.name: Serpiente de Agua del Norte
species.short_description: Thick-bodied dark banded snake, always near water; keels strongly when swimming.
species.en_short_description: Thick-bodied dark banded snake, always near water; keels strongly when swimming.
species.description: Colorado, California and New York. Harmless but bites readily and is constantly mistaken for a cottonmouth. Basks on overhanging branches and drops into the water when approached.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and New York. Harmless but bites readily and is constantly mistaken for a cottonmouth. Basks on overhanging branches and drops into the water when approached.

species.name: Besucona asiática
species.short_description: Pale translucent gecko with sticky toe pads, on walls near lights at night.
species.en_short_description: Pale translucent gecko with sticky toe pads, on walls near lights at night.
species.description: Introduced and established in California, Mexico City and Baja California Sur. Chirps audibly. Hunts insects drawn to porch lights, and displaces native geckos where it spreads.
species.en_description: Introduced and established in California, Mexico City and Baja California Sur. Chirps audibly. Hunts insects drawn to porch lights, and displaces native geckos where it spreads.

species.name: Lagartija alicante neovolcánico
species.short_description: Stout armoured lizard with keeled scales and a relatively short tail.
species.en_short_description: Stout armoured lizard with keeled scales and a relatively short tail.
species.description: Endemic to the volcanic highlands around Mexico City. Found in bunchgrass, under rocks and in agave rosettes. Bears live young. Cold-tolerant, active on cool overcast days.
species.en_description: Endemic to the volcanic highlands around Mexico City. Found in bunchgrass, under rocks and in agave rosettes. Bears live young. Cold-tolerant, active on cool overcast days.

species.name: Cascabel de diamantes rojos
species.short_description: Large reddish rattlesnake with pale-edged diamond blotches and a black-and-white banded tail.
species.en_short_description: Large reddish rattlesnake with pale-edged diamond blotches and a black-and-white banded tail.
species.description: Southern California and the Baja peninsula. Venomous — keep well clear. The brick-red ground colour separates it from other regional rattlesnakes. Often found in rock and cactus.
species.en_description: Southern California and the Baja peninsula. Venomous — keep well clear. The brick-red ground colour separates it from other regional rattlesnakes. Often found in rock and cactus.

species.name: Culebra terrestre del centro
species.short_description: Small brown ground snake with fine dark lines and a pale collar.
species.en_short_description: Small brown ground snake with fine dark lines and a pale collar.
species.description: Highlands around Mexico City, under stones and in grassland soil. Small, harmless and secretive, usually found while turning rocks. Feeds on insects and earthworms.
species.en_description: Highlands around Mexico City, under stones and in grassland soil. Small, harmless and secretive, usually found while turning rocks. Feeds on insects and earthworms.

species.name: Cascabel transvolcánica
species.short_description: Small dark montane rattlesnake with faint blotches and a slender rattle.
species.en_short_description: Small dark montane rattlesnake with faint blotches and a slender rattle.
species.description: High elevations around Mexico City, in pine-oak forest and alpine grassland. Venomous. One of the highest-altitude rattlesnakes in the world, found above 4,000 metres.
species.en_description: High elevations around Mexico City, in pine-oak forest and alpine grassland. Venomous. One of the highest-altitude rattlesnakes in the world, found above 4,000 metres.

species.name: Central Ratsnake
species.short_description: Large glossy black snake with a pale chin and faint traces of blotching.
species.en_short_description: Large glossy black snake with a pale chin and faint traces of blotching.
species.description: New York woodland, barns and rock ledges. Climbs well and is often found in rafters or high in trees hunting birds and eggs. Harmless; kinks its body into angular loops when alarmed.
species.en_description: New York woodland, barns and rock ledges. Climbs well and is often found in rafters or high in trees hunting birds and eggs. Harmless; kinks its body into angular loops when alarmed.

species.name: lagartija de piedra sudcaliforniana
species.short_description: Large flat-bodied lizard with blue-green speckling and dark neck bands.
species.en_short_description: Large flat-bodied lizard with blue-green speckling and dark neck bands.
species.description: Endemic to the Baja peninsula and common on granite in the cape region. Presses flat against boulders. Males develop striking turquoise flanks. Wary and hard to approach.
species.en_description: Endemic to the Baja peninsula and common on granite in the cape region. Presses flat against boulders. Males develop striking turquoise flanks. Wary and hard to approach.

species.name: Huico tigre del noroeste
species.short_description: Slim long-tailed lizard with dark reticulation and a spotted pale belly.
species.en_short_description: Slim long-tailed lizard with dark reticulation and a spotted pale belly.
species.description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Constantly on the move, jerking its head and digging in litter for termites. Very long tail, more than twice the body length.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Constantly on the move, jerking its head and digging in litter for termites. Very long tail, more than twice the body length.

species.name: Culebra parda
species.short_description: Tiny brown snake with a pale mid-dorsal band flanked by rows of small black dots.
species.en_short_description: Tiny brown snake with a pale mid-dorsal band flanked by rows of small black dots.
species.description: New York gardens, vacant lots and woodland edge. Harmless, seldom exceeding 30 cm, and eats slugs and earthworms. Commonly found under paving slabs and logs.
species.en_description: New York gardens, vacant lots and woodland edge. Harmless, seldom exceeding 30 cm, and eats slugs and earthworms. Commonly found under paving slabs and logs.

species.name: Lagartija espinosa peninsular
species.short_description: Large dark spiny lizard with rough keeled scales, endemic to the peninsula.
species.en_short_description: Large dark spiny lizard with rough keeled scales, endemic to the peninsula.
species.description: Baja California Sur, on rock, walls and tree trunks. The biggest Sceloporus in the region. Males show blue-black belly patches. Wary, retreating into crevices quickly.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur, on rock, walls and tree trunks. The biggest Sceloporus in the region. Males show blue-black belly patches. Wary, retreating into crevices quickly.

species.name: Lagartija espinosa de pastizal
species.short_description: Small grey-brown spiny lizard with a rusty wash behind the forelegs.
species.en_short_description: Small grey-brown spiny lizard with a rusty wash behind the forelegs.
species.description: Colorado, eastern California and Washington sagebrush. Smaller and finer-scaled than the fence lizards, with a distinct orange patch at the axilla. Basks on low shrubs and bare soil.
species.en_description: Colorado, eastern California and Washington sagebrush. Smaller and finer-scaled than the fence lizards, with a distinct orange patch at the axilla. Basks on low shrubs and bare soil.

species.name: culebra listonada elegante
species.short_description: Variable garter snake with a dull dorsal stripe and heavy dark checkering.
species.en_short_description: Variable garter snake with a dull dorsal stripe and heavy dark checkering.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. The most variable garter snake here, from strongly striped to almost uniformly dark. Feeds on fish, amphibians and slugs. Often far from water.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. The most variable garter snake here, from strongly striped to almost uniformly dark. Feeds on fish, amphibians and slugs. Often far from water.

species.name: Chirrionera de Baja California
species.short_description: Very long slender fast snake, dark at the head grading paler toward the tail.
species.en_short_description: Very long slender fast snake, dark at the head grading paler toward the tail.
species.description: Southern California and Baja California Sur. Extremely quick, hunting lizards actively with the head raised above the ground. Harmless but bites hard if cornered.
species.en_description: Southern California and Baja California Sur. Extremely quick, hunting lizards actively with the head raised above the ground. Harmless but bites hard if cornered.

species.name: Lagartija Lagarto Meridional
species.short_description: Long armoured lizard with a very long tail and dark crossbands on a brown ground.
species.en_short_description: Long armoured lizard with a very long tail and dark crossbands on a brown ground.
species.description: California and Washington. Common in gardens and woodpiles. Bites and thrashes if grabbed, and the tail detaches. Preys on insects, spiders and even small lizards.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Common in gardens and woodpiles. Bites and thrashes if grabbed, and the tail detaches. Preys on insects, spiders and even small lizards.

species.name: Tortuga Golfina
species.short_description: Small olive-grey sea turtle with a nearly circular shell.
species.en_short_description: Small olive-grey sea turtle with a nearly circular shell.
species.description: California, Washington and Baja California Sur, where it nests on Pacific beaches. The smallest and most abundant sea turtle. Known for mass synchronised nesting arrivals.
species.en_description: California, Washington and Baja California Sur, where it nests on Pacific beaches. The smallest and most abundant sea turtle. Known for mass synchronised nesting arrivals.

species.name: Colorado Checkered Whiptail
species.short_description: Slim whiptail with a checkered pattern over pale stripes and a very long tail.
species.en_short_description: Slim whiptail with a checkered pattern over pale stripes and a very long tail.
species.description: Southeastern Colorado canyon country, largely endemic. Reproduces by parthenogenesis, so populations are all female. Forages actively in loose soil and leaf litter.
species.en_description: Southeastern Colorado canyon country, largely endemic. Reproduces by parthenogenesis, so populations are all female. Forages actively in loose soil and leaf litter.

species.name: lagartija sorda menor
species.short_description: Small pale lizard with no external ear openings and dark paired blotches.
species.en_short_description: Small pale lizard with no external ear openings and dark paired blotches.
species.description: Eastern Colorado sandy grassland. The absent ear opening is diagnostic. Very pale, matching bare sandy ground, and it relies on stillness rather than flight.
species.en_description: Eastern Colorado sandy grassland. The absent ear opening is diagnostic. Very pale, matching bare sandy ground, and it relies on stillness rather than flight.

species.name: Falsa coralillo del Noroeste
species.short_description: Glossy black snake with bold white or cream bands or a lateral stripe.
species.en_short_description: Glossy black snake with bold white or cream bands or a lateral stripe.
species.description: Colorado, California, Mexico City region and Baja. Harmless and immune to rattlesnake venom, which it eats. Constricts prey. Some populations are striped rather than banded.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Mexico City region and Baja. Harmless and immune to rattlesnake venom, which it eats. Constricts prey. Some populations are striped rather than banded.

species.name: Plateau Striped Whiptail
species.short_description: Slender whiptail with six or seven crisp pale stripes and an unmarked bluish tail.
species.en_short_description: Slender whiptail with six or seven crisp pale stripes and an unmarked bluish tail.
species.description: Western Colorado pinyon-juniper and canyon country. All-female and parthenogenetic. The unspotted spaces between stripes separate it from the checkered whiptails.
species.en_description: Western Colorado pinyon-juniper and canyon country. All-female and parthenogenetic. The unspotted spaces between stripes separate it from the checkered whiptails.

species.name: Lagartija espinosa de Hunsaker
species.short_description: Robust spiny lizard endemic to the Baja cape, males with vivid blue-green flanks.
species.en_short_description: Robust spiny lizard endemic to the Baja cape, males with vivid blue-green flanks.
species.description: Baja California Sur only, on rock and in arroyos of the cape region. Breeding males are strikingly iridescent. Basks conspicuously on boulders in the morning.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur only, on rock and in arroyos of the cape region. Breeding males are strikingly iridescent. Basks conspicuously on boulders in the morning.

species.name: Tortuga verde
species.short_description: Large sea turtle with a smooth oval shell and a single pair of prefrontal scales.
species.en_short_description: Large sea turtle with a smooth oval shell and a single pair of prefrontal scales.
species.description: California, New York, Mexico City coast and Baja California Sur. Adults graze seagrass and algae, unusual among sea turtles. Feeding aggregations gather in Baja lagoons.
species.en_description: California, New York, Mexico City coast and Baja California Sur. Adults graze seagrass and algae, unusual among sea turtles. Feeding aggregations gather in Baja lagoons.

species.name: Lined Snake
species.short_description: Small brown snake with pale stripes and a belly marked by two rows of black half-moons.
species.en_short_description: Small brown snake with pale stripes and a belly marked by two rows of black half-moons.
species.description: Eastern Colorado grassland and vacant lots. Superficially like a small garter snake, but the paired black crescents down the belly are conclusive. Nocturnal; eats earthworms.
species.en_description: Eastern Colorado grassland and vacant lots. Superficially like a small garter snake, but the paired black crescents down the belly are conclusive. Nocturnal; eats earthworms.

species.name: Lagartija Italiana
species.short_description: Slim green-and-brown lizard with a long tail, on walls and rubble.
species.en_short_description: Slim green-and-brown lizard with a long tail, on walls and rubble.
species.description: Introduced and established in California and New York, notably on Long Island. Fast and wary, basking on stonework. Bright green flanks in males. Not native anywhere in the Americas.
species.en_description: Introduced and established in California and New York, notably on Long Island. Fast and wary, basking on stonework. Bright green flanks in males. Not native anywhere in the Americas.

species.name: Culebra de collar
species.short_description: Small slate-grey snake with a bright yellow-orange neck ring and vivid belly.
species.en_short_description: Small slate-grey snake with a bright yellow-orange neck ring and vivid belly.
species.description: Five regions. Coils its tail to display the red-orange underside when alarmed. Found under rocks, bark and debris in damp woodland. Harmless and rarely over 40 cm.
species.en_description: Five regions. Coils its tail to display the red-orange underside when alarmed. Found under rocks, bark and debris in damp woodland. Harmless and rarely over 40 cm.

species.name: Culebra parda mexicana
species.short_description: Tiny brown snake with a faint pale dorsal band and dark lateral spotting.
species.en_short_description: Tiny brown snake with a faint pale dorsal band and dark lateral spotting.
species.description: Highlands around Mexico City, in gardens, pine-oak litter and under stones. Harmless and easily overlooked. Feeds on slugs, snails and soft invertebrates.
species.en_description: Highlands around Mexico City, in gardens, pine-oak litter and under stones. Harmless and easily overlooked. Feeds on slugs, snails and soft invertebrates.

species.name: Rana de coro del Pacífico
species.short_description: Small treefrog with a dark eye stripe and toe pads; green or brown.
species.en_short_description: Small treefrog with a dark eye stripe and toe pads; green or brown.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. The loud two-note ribbit heard in films is this frog. Chorus starts in late winter in ditches and ponds. Colour changes between green and brown.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. The loud two-note ribbit heard in films is this frog. Chorus starts in late winter in ditches and ponds. Colour changes between green and brown.

species.name: Rana toro americana
species.short_description: Very large green-brown frog with no dorsolateral ridges and a deep jug-o-rum call.
species.en_short_description: Very large green-brown frog with no dorsolateral ridges and a deep jug-o-rum call.
species.description: Every region. Native to the east and invasive in the west, where it eats native frogs. The absence of back ridges separates it from other big ranids. Tadpoles take two years to mature.
species.en_description: Every region. Native to the east and invasive in the west, where it eats native frogs. The absence of back ridges separates it from other big ranids. Tadpoles take two years to mature.

species.name: Sapo de puntos rojos
species.short_description: Small flat-headed toad with red-tipped warts on a grey-buff ground.
species.en_short_description: Small flat-headed toad with red-tipped warts on a grey-buff ground.
species.description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur desert canyons. Round rather than oval parotoid glands. Calls a long high musical trill from rock pools after summer rain.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur desert canyons. Round rather than oval parotoid glands. Calls a long high musical trill from rock pools after summer rain.

species.name: Sapo chihuahuense
species.short_description: Medium toad with a bold pale mid-dorsal stripe and prominent cranial crests.
species.en_short_description: Medium toad with a bold pale mid-dorsal stripe and prominent cranial crests.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Calls a nasal bleating w-a-a-a-h from irrigation ditches and river sandbars. The white back stripe is the quickest field mark.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Calls a nasal bleating w-a-a-a-h from irrigation ditches and river sandbars. The white back stripe is the quickest field mark.

species.name: Sapo Americano
species.short_description: Warty brown toad with one or two large warts per dark spot and prominent crests.
species.en_short_description: Warty brown toad with one or two large warts per dark spot and prominent crests.
species.description: New York gardens, woods and field edges. Long musical trill lasting many seconds in spring. Enlarged parotoid glands behind the eyes touch the cranial crest.
species.en_description: New York gardens, woods and field edges. Long musical trill lasting many seconds in spring. Enlarged parotoid glands behind the eyes touch the cranial crest.

species.name: Rana leopardo de Moctezuma
species.short_description: Green-brown spotted frog with dorsolateral ridges, in Mexican highland water.
species.en_short_description: Green-brown spotted frog with dorsolateral ridges, in Mexican highland water.
species.description: Endemic to central Mexico and found in the remaining wetlands and canals of the Basin of Mexico. Historically an important local food frog. Declining with the loss of highland marsh.
species.en_description: Endemic to central Mexico and found in the remaining wetlands and canals of the Basin of Mexico. Historically an important local food frog. Declining with the loss of highland marsh.

species.name: Rana verde
species.short_description: Medium green-brown frog with dorsolateral ridges that stop short of the groin.
species.en_short_description: Medium green-brown frog with dorsolateral ridges that stop short of the groin.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Calls a single explosive note like a plucked banjo string. The partial back ridges separate it from the ridgeless Bullfrog.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Calls a single explosive note like a plucked banjo string. The partial back ridges separate it from the ridgeless Bullfrog.

species.name: salamandra de espalda roja
species.short_description: Small slender salamander with a straight rusty back stripe and a mottled belly.
species.en_short_description: Small slender salamander with a straight rusty back stripe and a mottled belly.
species.description: New York woodland, under logs and rocks. Entirely terrestrial with no aquatic larval stage. A lead-backed grey morph without the stripe is equally common.
species.en_description: New York woodland, under logs and rocks. Entirely terrestrial with no aquatic larval stage. A lead-backed grey morph without the stripe is equally common.

species.name: Tritón de California
species.short_description: Stocky orange-brown newt with a bright orange belly and warty skin on land.
species.en_short_description: Stocky orange-brown newt with a bright orange belly and warty skin on land.
species.description: California coastal ranges and Sierra foothills. Migrates to streams and ponds to breed in winter, becoming smooth-skinned in water. Skin toxins are potent; wash hands after handling.
species.en_description: California coastal ranges and Sierra foothills. Migrates to streams and ponds to breed in winter, becoming smooth-skinned in water. Skin toxins are potent; wash hands after handling.

species.name: Tritón oriental
species.short_description: Olive newt with red-bordered black spots; juveniles are brilliant orange efts.
species.en_short_description: Olive newt with red-bordered black spots; juveniles are brilliant orange efts.
species.description: New York ponds and woodland. The terrestrial red eft stage wanders forest floor for years before returning to water as an olive adult. Both stages are toxic to predators.
species.en_description: New York ponds and woodland. The terrestrial red eft stage wanders forest floor for years before returning to water as an olive adult. Both stages are toxic to predators.

species.name: Sapo occidental
species.short_description: Large toad with a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe and no cranial crests.
species.en_short_description: Large toad with a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe and no cranial crests.
species.description: California and Washington. Absent crests plus the cream back stripe separate it from Woodhouse's Toad. Walks rather than hops. Males give a soft chick-like peeping, not a trill.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Absent crests plus the cream back stripe separate it from Woodhouse's Toad. Walks rather than hops. Males give a soft chick-like peeping, not a trill.

species.name: Salamandra Delgada de California
species.short_description: Extremely slender worm-like salamander with tiny limbs and a long tail.
species.en_short_description: Extremely slender worm-like salamander with tiny limbs and a long tail.
species.description: California coastal woodland, under bark, boards and logs. Looks more like an earthworm than a salamander. Coils and springs away when uncovered. Entirely terrestrial.
species.en_description: California coastal woodland, under bark, boards and logs. Looks more like an earthworm than a salamander. Coils and springs away when uncovered. Entirely terrestrial.

species.name: sapo cavador
species.short_description: Green-mottled toad-like amphibian with vertical pupils and a black hind-foot spade.
species.en_short_description: Green-mottled toad-like amphibian with vertical pupils and a black hind-foot spade.
species.description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Spends most of the year buried, emerging in explosive numbers after heavy summer rain. Tadpoles can mature in under two weeks.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Spends most of the year buried, emerging in explosive numbers after heavy summer rain. Tadpoles can mature in under two weeks.

species.name: salamandra de piel rugosa
species.short_description: Dark brown newt with strongly granular skin and a vivid orange belly.
species.en_short_description: Dark brown newt with strongly granular skin and a vivid orange belly.
species.description: California and Washington. Among the most toxic animals in North America — its tetrodotoxin drove the evolution of resistant garter snakes. Walks openly by day on wet trails.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Among the most toxic animals in North America — its tetrodotoxin drove the evolution of resistant garter snakes. Walks openly by day on wet trails.

species.name: Rana del Bosque
species.short_description: Tan to rusty frog with a bold dark robber's mask through the eye.
species.en_short_description: Tan to rusty frog with a bold dark robber's mask through the eye.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Breeds explosively in vernal pools while ice still lingers, calling like clucking ducks. Tolerates freezing solid over winter.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Breeds explosively in vernal pools while ice still lingers, calling like clucking ducks. Tolerates freezing solid over winter.

species.name: Spring Peeper
species.short_description: Tiny tan treefrog with a dark X mark on the back.
species.en_short_description: Tiny tan treefrog with a dark X mark on the back.
species.description: New York. The shrill ascending peep repeated endlessly is the classic sound of a north-eastern spring. Far more often heard than seen; barely the size of a thumbnail.
species.en_description: New York. The shrill ascending peep repeated endlessly is the classic sound of a north-eastern spring. Far more often heard than seen; barely the size of a thumbnail.

species.name: Tlaconete regordete
species.short_description: Stout lungless salamander with a broad head and short tail, in Mexican highlands.
species.en_short_description: Stout lungless salamander with a broad head and short tail, in Mexican highlands.
species.description: Endemic to central Mexico, in pine-oak forest litter and bromeliads around Mexico City. Entirely terrestrial with direct development. Found by turning logs and moss mats.
species.en_description: Endemic to central Mexico, in pine-oak forest litter and bromeliads around Mexico City. Entirely terrestrial with direct development. Found by turning logs and moss mats.

species.name: Salamandra moteada
species.short_description: Large stout black salamander with two rows of round bright yellow spots.
species.en_short_description: Large stout black salamander with two rows of round bright yellow spots.
species.description: New York deciduous woodland. Spends the year underground, emerging on the first warm rainy nights of spring to migrate en masse to vernal pools. Unmistakable when found.
species.en_description: New York deciduous woodland. Spends the year underground, emerging on the first warm rainy nights of spring to migrate en masse to vernal pools. Unmistakable when found.

species.name: Salamandra ensatina
species.short_description: Smooth salamander with a distinctly constricted tail base and often orange limbs.
species.en_short_description: Smooth salamander with a distinctly constricted tail base and often orange limbs.
species.description: California and Washington forest. The pinched tail base is unique among western salamanders. A famous ring species, with markedly different colour forms around the Central Valley.
species.en_description: California and Washington forest. The pinched tail base is unique among western salamanders. A famous ring species, with markedly different colour forms around the Central Valley.

species.name: rana arbórea gris
species.short_description: Warty grey or green treefrog with a pale spot under the eye and yellow inner thighs.
species.en_short_description: Warty grey or green treefrog with a pale spot under the eye and yellow inner thighs.
species.description: New York. Changes colour to match bark or leaf. Calls a slow musical birdlike trill from trees, often far from water. Large toe pads for climbing.
species.en_description: New York. Changes colour to match bark or leaf. Calls a slow musical birdlike trill from trees, often far from water. Large toe pads for climbing.

species.name: Rana leopardo norteña
species.short_description: Slim green or brown frog with round dark spots ringed in pale halos.
species.en_short_description: Slim green or brown frog with round dark spots ringed in pale halos.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The neatly haloed spots and pale dorsolateral ridges are diagnostic. Declining across much of its range. Leaps long distances into water.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The neatly haloed spots and pale dorsolateral ridges are diagnostic. Declining across much of its range. Leaps long distances into water.

species.name: Salamandra del noroeste
species.short_description: Heavy-bodied brown salamander with glandular ridges and prominent parotoid swellings.
species.en_short_description: Heavy-bodied brown salamander with glandular ridges and prominent parotoid swellings.
species.description: California and Washington. Some populations stay aquatic as neotenic adults with gills. Exudes a sticky white toxin from the tail when threatened. Breeds in ponds and slow streams.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Some populations stay aquatic as neotenic adults with gills. Exudes a sticky white toxin from the tail when threatened. Breeds in ponds and slow streams.

species.name: Rana arborícola de montaña
species.short_description: Small green-brown treefrog with a dark eye stripe, in Mexican highland forest.
species.en_short_description: Small green-brown treefrog with a dark eye stripe, in Mexican highland forest.
species.description: Endemic to the highlands of central Mexico, including the mountains around Mexico City. Breeds in temporary pools and cattle tanks in pine-oak forest during the summer rains.
species.en_description: Endemic to the highlands of central Mexico, including the mountains around Mexico City. Breeds in temporary pools and cattle tanks in pine-oak forest during the summer rains.

species.name: Ajolote tigre rayado
species.short_description: Very large salamander with bold yellow blotches or bars on dark brown.
species.en_short_description: Very large salamander with bold yellow blotches or bars on dark brown.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Frequently found in basements and window wells during autumn rains. Some populations remain aquatic as gilled adults, sometimes called waterdogs.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Frequently found in basements and window wells during autumn rains. Some populations remain aquatic as gilled adults, sometimes called waterdogs.

species.name: Rana pata roja
species.short_description: Brown frog with red wash on the lower belly and hind legs and a dark eye mask.
species.en_short_description: Brown frog with red wash on the lower belly and hind legs and a dark eye mask.
species.description: California and Washington. Breeds early in cool ponds, with males calling underwater so choruses are easy to miss. The translucent red underside of the thighs is diagnostic.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Breeds early in cool ponds, with males calling underwater so choruses are easy to miss. The translucent red underside of the thighs is diagnostic.

species.name: Tlaconete dorado
species.short_description: Slim brown salamander with fine pale speckling, in Mexican pine-oak forest.
species.en_short_description: Slim brown salamander with fine pale speckling, in Mexican pine-oak forest.
species.description: Endemic to central Mexico's highlands including the ranges around Mexico City. Lungless and entirely terrestrial. Found under bark, moss and rotting logs at high elevation.
species.en_description: Endemic to central Mexico's highlands including the ranges around Mexico City. Lungless and entirely terrestrial. Found under bark, moss and rotting logs at high elevation.

species.name: Salamandra Oscura Montana de Allegheny
species.short_description: Small dusky salamander with a light-edged back stripe and a pale line from eye to jaw.
species.en_short_description: Small dusky salamander with a light-edged back stripe and a pale line from eye to jaw.
species.description: New York uplands, along seeps and spring heads. The straight pale cheek line is the key mark among dusky salamanders. Found by turning wet stones in trickling water.
species.en_description: New York uplands, along seeps and spring heads. The straight pale cheek line is the key mark among dusky salamanders. Found by turning wet stones in trickling water.

species.name: Rana Coro Boreal
species.short_description: Tiny striped chorus frog with three dark back stripes and a dark eye line.
species.en_short_description: Tiny striped chorus frog with three dark back stripes and a dark eye line.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Calls a rising crreek like a thumb run along a comb, from flooded meadows in spring. Barely 3 cm long and extremely hard to spot while calling.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Calls a rising crreek like a thumb run along a comb, from flooded meadows in spring. Barely 3 cm long and extremely hard to spot while calling.

species.name: Rana de pantano
species.short_description: Slim tan frog with two rows of squarish dark spots and bright yellow inner thighs.
species.en_short_description: Slim tan frog with two rows of squarish dark spots and bright yellow inner thighs.
species.description: New York streams and cool meadows. The squarish, non-haloed spots and yellow groin separate it from the Leopard Frog. Skin secretions are toxic to other amphibians.
species.en_description: New York streams and cool meadows. The squarish, non-haloed spots and yellow groin separate it from the Leopard Frog. Skin secretions are toxic to other amphibians.

species.name: Rana de árbol plegada
species.short_description: Green-brown treefrog with distinctly ridged skin, endemic to central Mexico.
species.en_short_description: Green-brown treefrog with distinctly ridged skin, endemic to central Mexico.
species.description: Endemic to the highlands around Mexico City in pine-fir forest. The rough ridged dorsum separates it from other Mexican treefrogs. Breeds in cold high-elevation pools.
species.en_description: Endemic to the highlands around Mexico City in pine-fir forest. The rough ridged dorsum separates it from other Mexican treefrogs. Breeds in cold high-elevation pools.

species.name: Salamandra arborícola
species.short_description: Robust brown salamander with pale yellow spots, large jaw muscles and square toe tips.
species.en_short_description: Robust brown salamander with pale yellow spots, large jaw muscles and square toe tips.
species.description: California oak woodland. Climbs high into oaks and lives in tree cavities and bromeliad-like leaf accumulations. Bites hard for a salamander and can squeak audibly.
species.en_description: California oak woodland. Climbs high into oaks and lives in tree cavities and bromeliad-like leaf accumulations. Bites hard for a salamander and can squeak audibly.

species.name: Salamandra Bilineada Norteña
species.short_description: Slim yellow-brown salamander with two dark lines running down the back.
species.en_short_description: Slim yellow-brown salamander with two dark lines running down the back.
species.description: New York streams and seeps. Common under stones at the water's edge. Larvae spend two or more years in the stream before transforming. Runs and wriggles quickly when exposed.
species.en_description: New York streams and seeps. Common under stones at the water's edge. Larvae spend two or more years in the stream before transforming. Runs and wriggles quickly when exposed.

species.name: ranita de las rocas
species.short_description: Squat warty treefrog coloured like granite, with yellow inner thighs.
species.en_short_description: Squat warty treefrog coloured like granite, with yellow inner thighs.
species.description: Colorado and central Mexico canyons. Sits pressed to boulders beside plunge pools, matching the rock almost perfectly. Calls a low nasal quacking that echoes in the canyon.
species.en_description: Colorado and central Mexico canyons. Sits pressed to boulders beside plunge pools, matching the rock almost perfectly. Calls a low nasal quacking that echoes in the canyon.

species.name: Salamandra dedos largos
species.short_description: Dark salamander with a broken yellow-green back stripe and a very long fourth toe.
species.en_short_description: Dark salamander with a broken yellow-green back stripe and a very long fourth toe.
species.description: California and Washington. Breeds in cold ponds and snowmelt pools, sometimes under ice. The elongated outer hind toe gives the name. Found under logs near water.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Breeds in cold ponds and snowmelt pools, sometimes under ice. The elongated outer hind toe gives the name. Found under logs near water.

species.name: Rana ladradora amarilla
species.short_description: Robust frog with a fold behind the head, calling with a doglike bark from rock crevices.
species.en_short_description: Robust frog with a fold behind the head, calling with a doglike bark from rock crevices.
species.description: Central Mexico highlands including around Mexico City. Lays eggs on land with direct development — no tadpole stage. Lives in limestone crevices and talus, emerging on wet nights.
species.en_description: Central Mexico highlands including around Mexico City. Lays eggs on land with direct development — no tadpole stage. Lives in limestone crevices and talus, emerging on wet nights.

species.name: Salamandra de Espalda Roja Occidental
species.short_description: Slender salamander with a straight-edged tan or reddish back stripe.
species.en_short_description: Slender salamander with a straight-edged tan or reddish back stripe.
species.description: Washington forest, under bark and rotting wood. Entirely terrestrial with no larval stage. Distinguished from slender salamanders by proportionally shorter body and sturdier limbs.
species.en_description: Washington forest, under bark and rotting wood. Entirely terrestrial with no larval stage. Distinguished from slender salamanders by proportionally shorter body and sturdier limbs.

species.name: Sapo montícola de espuela
species.short_description: Grey-green spadefoot with vertical pupils, a wedge-shaped hind-foot spade and a boss between the eyes.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green spadefoot with vertical pupils, a wedge-shaped hind-foot spade and a boss between the eyes.
species.description: Colorado and central Mexico. Emerges from burrows after monsoon downpours to breed in ephemeral pools. Calls a short low bleating snore. Tadpoles develop very fast.
species.en_description: Colorado and central Mexico. Emerges from burrows after monsoon downpours to breed in ephemeral pools. Calls a short low bleating snore. Tadpoles develop very fast.

species.name: Rana de Coro de California
species.short_description: Warty grey treefrog without a dark eye stripe, matching streamside granite.
species.en_short_description: Warty grey treefrog without a dark eye stripe, matching streamside granite.
species.description: Southern California canyons. Told from the Pacific Chorus Frog by the absence of an eye mask and a more warty, rock-coloured skin. Sits on boulders beside plunge pools.
species.en_description: Southern California canyons. Told from the Pacific Chorus Frog by the absence of an eye mask and a more warty, rock-coloured skin. Sits on boulders beside plunge pools.

species.name: Rana de las Cascadas
species.short_description: Brown frog with distinct inky black spots and a yellowish belly.
species.en_short_description: Brown frog with distinct inky black spots and a yellowish belly.
species.description: California and Washington high country. Breeds in shallow snowmelt pools and boggy meadows near treeline. The crisp black spotting without pale halos is diagnostic.
species.en_description: California and Washington high country. Breeds in shallow snowmelt pools and boggy meadows near treeline. The crisp black spotting without pale halos is diagnostic.

species.name: Salamandra pies planos
species.short_description: Very slender salamander with broad flattened feet, in Mexican cloud forest.
species.en_short_description: Very slender salamander with broad flattened feet, in Mexican cloud forest.
species.description: Endemic to the highlands of central Mexico near Mexico City. Climbs bromeliads and mossy trunks using expanded webbed feet. Lungless and entirely terrestrial.
species.en_description: Endemic to the highlands of central Mexico near Mexico City. Climbs bromeliads and mossy trunks using expanded webbed feet. Lungless and entirely terrestrial.

species.name: Ajolote arroyero de la Sierra de las Cruces
species.short_description: Dark aquatic salamander that often retains gills as an adult, in cold Mexican streams.
species.en_short_description: Dark aquatic salamander that often retains gills as an adult, in cold Mexican streams.
species.description: Endemic to the mountain streams of central Mexico near Mexico City. Frequently neotenic, keeping larval gills for life. Threatened by water extraction and pollution.
species.en_description: Endemic to the mountain streams of central Mexico near Mexico City. Frequently neotenic, keeping larval gills for life. Threatened by water extraction and pollution.

species.name: Rana patas amarillas
species.short_description: Grey-brown frog with a granular skin and lemon-yellow undersides to the hind legs.
species.en_short_description: Grey-brown frog with a granular skin and lemon-yellow undersides to the hind legs.
species.description: California foothill streams. Breeds in flowing water on cobble bars, timed to receding spring flows. Declining sharply with dam operations. Well camouflaged against gravel.
species.en_description: California foothill streams. Breeds in flowing water on cobble bars, timed to receding spring flows. Declining sharply with dam operations. Well camouflaged against gravel.

species.name: Sapo de Fowler
species.short_description: Toad with a pale back stripe, three or more warts per dark spot and a plain white chest.
species.en_short_description: Toad with a pale back stripe, three or more warts per dark spot and a plain white chest.
species.description: New York, especially sandy coastal areas. Calls a harsh nasal waaah lasting a couple of seconds. Distinguished from American Toad by more warts per spot and an unspotted breast.
species.en_description: New York, especially sandy coastal areas. Calls a harsh nasal waaah lasting a couple of seconds. Distinguished from American Toad by more warts per spot and an unspotted breast.

species.name: rana de patas rojas
species.short_description: Large brown-red frog with dark blotches and red wash on the belly and hind legs.
species.en_short_description: Large brown-red frog with dark blotches and red wash on the belly and hind legs.
species.description: California ponds and slow streams. The largest native western ranid and a threatened species — the frog of Mark Twain's jumping-frog story. Breeds in deep still pools.
species.en_description: California ponds and slow streams. The largest native western ranid and a threatened species — the frog of Mark Twain's jumping-frog story. Breeds in deep still pools.

species.name: Salamandra Limosa Norteña
species.short_description: Black salamander flecked with silvery-white spots, producing sticky glue when handled.
species.en_short_description: Black salamander flecked with silvery-white spots, producing sticky glue when handled.
species.description: New York woodland slopes and ravines. The secretion is genuinely adhesive and hard to wash off. Entirely terrestrial, found under rocks and logs on wooded hillsides.
species.en_description: New York woodland slopes and ravines. The secretion is genuinely adhesive and hard to wash off. Entirely terrestrial, found under rocks and logs on wooded hillsides.

species.name: Salamandra gigante del Pacífico
species.short_description: Very large marbled brown salamander with a massive head, in cold forest streams.
species.en_short_description: Very large marbled brown salamander with a massive head, in cold forest streams.
species.description: California and Washington. One of the largest terrestrial salamanders in the world, reaching over 30 cm. Can bark when alarmed. Larvae live years in cold rocky streams.
species.en_description: California and Washington. One of the largest terrestrial salamanders in the world, reaching over 30 cm. Can bark when alarmed. Larvae live years in cold rocky streams.

species.name: Ranita del Pedregal
species.short_description: Small robust frog with large toe pads, calling a sharp peep from volcanic rock.
species.en_short_description: Small robust frog with large toe pads, calling a sharp peep from volcanic rock.
species.description: Endemic to the Pedregal lava fields and surrounds of Mexico City. Lays eggs on land with direct development. Lives in lava crevices, emerging on humid nights in the rainy season.
species.en_description: Endemic to the Pedregal lava fields and surrounds of Mexico City. Lays eggs on land with direct development. Lives in lava crevices, emerging on humid nights in the rainy season.

species.name: Salamandra Delgada de Vientre Negro
species.short_description: Very slim worm-like salamander with a dark, finely speckled belly.
species.en_short_description: Very slim worm-like salamander with a dark, finely speckled belly.
species.description: Southern California. Even more slender than the California Slender Salamander, and separated by the dark rather than pale belly. Found under bark, boards and rocks in damp weather.
species.en_description: Southern California. Even more slender than the California Slender Salamander, and separated by the dark rather than pale belly. Found under bark, boards and rocks in damp weather.

species.name: Salamandra gigante de California
species.short_description: Large marbled salamander with a broad head, restricted to central California streams.
species.en_short_description: Large marbled salamander with a broad head, restricted to central California streams.
species.description: A California endemic of cold coastal streams near San Francisco. Very similar to the Pacific Giant Salamander but with a more restricted range and finer marbling.
species.en_description: A California endemic of cold coastal streams near San Francisco. Very similar to the Pacific Giant Salamander but with a more restricted range and finer marbling.

species.name: Sapo gigante
species.short_description: Very large warty toad with huge triangular parotoid glands behind the eyes.
species.en_short_description: Very large warty toad with huge triangular parotoid glands behind the eyes.
species.description: Central Mexico, including the Mexico City region. Also called the Cane Toad. The enormous parotoid glands secrete potent toxins dangerous to dogs. Gathers under lights at night.
species.en_description: Central Mexico, including the Mexico City region. Also called the Cane Toad. The enormous parotoid glands secrete potent toxins dangerous to dogs. Gathers under lights at night.

species.name: Abeja melífera europea
species.short_description: Golden-brown banded bee with pollen baskets on the hind legs.
species.en_short_description: Golden-brown banded bee with pollen baskets on the hind legs.
species.description: The most-observed insect in all six regions. Introduced everywhere in the Americas but essential to agriculture. Distinguished from bumble bees by its slimmer, less furry body and from wasps by the fuzz.
species.en_description: The most-observed insect in all six regions. Introduced everywhere in the Americas but essential to agriculture. Distinguished from bumble bees by its slimmer, less furry body and from wasps by the fuzz.

species.name: Catarina asiática
species.short_description: Variable ladybird with a white M-shaped mark behind the head.
species.en_short_description: Variable ladybird with a white M-shaped mark behind the head.
species.description: Five regions. Spots range from none to nineteen, so the black M on the white pronotum is the reliable mark. Introduced for aphid control and now aggregates indoors in autumn.
species.en_description: Five regions. Spots range from none to nineteen, so the black M on the white pronotum is the reliable mark. Introduced for aphid control and now aggregates indoors in autumn.

species.name: Mariposa monarca
species.short_description: Large orange butterfly with heavy black veins and white-spotted black margins.
species.en_short_description: Large orange butterfly with heavy black veins and white-spotted black margins.
species.description: Every region. Famous for multi-generational migration to Mexican overwintering forests. Caterpillars feed only on milkweed. Males have a black scent spot on each hindwing vein.
species.en_description: Every region. Famous for multi-generational migration to Mexican overwintering forests. Caterpillars feed only on milkweed. Males have a black scent spot on each hindwing vein.

species.name: Polilla esfinge de rayas blancas
species.short_description: Large hawkmoth with a white-striped body and pink hindwing bands; hovers like a hummingbird.
species.en_short_description: Large hawkmoth with a white-striped body and pink hindwing bands; hovers like a hummingbird.
species.description: Five regions. Frequently mistaken for a hummingbird at dusk flowers. Caterpillars are variable green-and-black and can appear in enormous numbers after desert rains.
species.en_description: Five regions. Frequently mistaken for a hummingbird at dusk flowers. Caterpillars are variable green-and-black and can appear in enormous numbers after desert rains.

species.name: Catarina de siete puntos
species.short_description: Red ladybird with exactly seven black spots and small white patches at the shoulders.
species.en_short_description: Red ladybird with exactly seven black spots and small white patches at the shoulders.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced from Europe. The fixed spot count separates it from the wildly variable Asian Lady Beetle. Common in gardens, hedgerows and meadow edges.
