species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced from Europe. The fixed spot count separates it from the wildly variable Asian Lady Beetle. Common in gardens, hedgerows and meadow edges.

species.name: Catarina convergente
species.short_description: Orange ladybird with about twelve spots and two converging white dashes on the pronotum.
species.en_short_description: Orange ladybird with about twelve spots and two converging white dashes on the pronotum.
species.description: Five regions and the common native ladybird of the West. Migrates to mountain slopes to aggregate in huge overwintering masses, which are then collected for garden sale.
species.en_description: Five regions and the common native ladybird of the West. Migrates to mountain slopes to aggregate in huge overwintering masses, which are then collected for garden sale.

species.name: Mariposa Vanesa pintada
species.short_description: Orange-brown butterfly with white-spotted black wingtips and four small eyespots below.
species.en_short_description: Orange-brown butterfly with white-spotted black wingtips and four small eyespots below.
species.description: Every region. Undertakes irruptive mass migrations, sometimes millions strong across the West. Caterpillars feed on thistle and mallow. One of the most widespread butterflies on earth.
species.en_description: Every region. Undertakes irruptive mass migrations, sometimes millions strong across the West. Caterpillars feed on thistle and mallow. One of the most widespread butterflies on earth.

species.name: Blanquilla de la col
species.short_description: Small white butterfly with black wingtips and one or two black forewing spots.
species.en_short_description: Small white butterfly with black wingtips and one or two black forewing spots.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and now the most abundant white butterfly in North America. Caterpillars are the green cabbage worm of vegetable gardens. Males have one spot, females two.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and now the most abundant white butterfly in North America. Caterpillars are the green cabbage worm of vegetable gardens. Males have one spot, females two.

species.name: Avispa papelera europea
species.short_description: Slender yellow-and-black wasp with orange antennae, building open combs.
species.en_short_description: Slender yellow-and-black wasp with orange antennae, building open combs.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and now widespread. Nests are exposed umbrella-shaped paper combs under eaves. Orange antennae separate it from yellowjackets.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and now widespread. Nests are exposed umbrella-shaped paper combs under eaves. Orange antennae separate it from yellowjackets.

species.name: Abejorro del noreste de Estados Unidos
species.short_description: Robust furry bumble bee with a yellow thorax and a single yellow band on the abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Robust furry bumble bee with a yellow thorax and a single yellow band on the abdomen.
species.description: New York and Washington. The commercially reared bumble bee used in greenhouses, and the commonest eastern species. Nests underground in colonies of a few hundred.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. The commercially reared bumble bee used in greenhouses, and the commonest eastern species. Nests underground in colonies of a few hundred.

species.name: Mantis Religiosa
species.short_description: Green or brown mantis with a distinctive bullseye spot inside each foreleg.
species.en_short_description: Green or brown mantis with a distinctive bullseye spot inside each foreleg.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and widely established. The black-and-white ring on the inner front leg is the reliable identification. Lays foamy egg cases on stems.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and widely established. The black-and-white ring on the inner front leg is the reliable identification. Lays foamy egg cases on stems.

species.name: chinche americana del pino
species.short_description: Long brown leaf-footed bug with flared hind legs and a white zigzag across the wings.
species.en_short_description: Long brown leaf-footed bug with flared hind legs and a white zigzag across the wings.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Enters houses in autumn seeking shelter and buzzes loudly in flight. Harmless, though it releases a pungent smell if handled.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Enters houses in autumn seeking shelter and buzzes loudly in flight. Harmless, though it releases a pungent smell if handled.

species.name: Chinche linterna manchada
species.short_description: Grey planthopper with black-spotted forewings and vivid red-and-black hindwings.
species.en_short_description: Grey planthopper with black-spotted forewings and vivid red-and-black hindwings.
species.description: New York, where it is a serious invasive pest. Hops powerfully rather than flying far. Egg masses look like smears of grey mud on trunks. Worth reporting to state authorities.
species.en_description: New York, where it is a serious invasive pest. Hops powerfully rather than flying far. Egg masses look like smears of grey mud on trunks. Worth reporting to state authorities.

species.name: Polilla Tigre Isabella
species.short_description: Dull orange-buff moth; its caterpillar is the banded woolly bear.
species.en_short_description: Dull orange-buff moth; its caterpillar is the banded woolly bear.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The bristly black-and-rust woolly bear caterpillar is far better known than the adult moth. Overwinters as a caterpillar, freezing solid.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The bristly black-and-rust woolly bear caterpillar is far better known than the adult moth. Overwinters as a caterpillar, freezing solid.

species.name: Mariposa cometa tigre de Baja California
species.short_description: Large yellow swallowtail with bold black tiger stripes and blue-and-orange tail spots.
species.en_short_description: Large yellow swallowtail with bold black tiger stripes and blue-and-orange tail spots.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Patrols streamside cottonwoods and willows, and is one of the most conspicuous butterflies in western towns. Caterpillars bear large false eyespots.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Patrols streamside cottonwoods and willows, and is one of the most conspicuous butterflies in western towns. Caterpillars bear large false eyespots.

species.name: Polilla Bruja
species.short_description: Very large dark moth with intricate wave patterns and a comma-shaped forewing mark.
species.en_short_description: Very large dark moth with intricate wave patterns and a comma-shaped forewing mark.
species.description: Colorado, Mexico City and Baja. Wingspan can exceed 15 cm, making it one of the largest moths here. Strays far north in late summer. Surrounded by folklore across Mexico.
species.en_description: Colorado, Mexico City and Baja. Wingspan can exceed 15 cm, making it one of the largest moths here. Strays far north in late summer. Surrounded by folklore across Mexico.

species.name: Mariposa Velo de Duelo
species.short_description: Dark maroon butterfly with a ragged cream border and a row of blue spots.
species.en_short_description: Dark maroon butterfly with a ragged cream border and a row of blue spots.
species.description: Five regions. Overwinters as an adult, so it is often the first butterfly seen on a warm late-winter day. Feeds on sap and rotting fruit more than flowers.
species.en_description: Five regions. Overwinters as an adult, so it is often the first butterfly seen on a warm late-winter day. Feeds on sap and rotting fruit more than flowers.

species.name: Mariposa Lunita tejana
species.short_description: Small dark brown butterfly with white and orange markings and a scalloped wing edge.
species.en_short_description: Small dark brown butterfly with white and orange markings and a scalloped wing edge.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Flies low and fast along arroyos and trail edges. Caterpillars feed on acanthus family plants. Common but easily overlooked.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Flies low and fast along arroyos and trail edges. Caterpillars feed on acanthus family plants. Common but easily overlooked.

species.name: Black-tailed Bumble Bee
species.short_description: Bumble bee with a red-orange abdominal band and a black tail.
species.en_short_description: Bumble bee with a red-orange abdominal band and a black tail.
species.description: California and Washington. One of the earliest bumble bees each spring on the Pacific coast. The rusty mid-abdomen with a black tip is the field mark. Nests underground and in cavities.
species.en_description: California and Washington. One of the earliest bumble bees each spring on the Pacific coast. The rusty mid-abdomen with a black tip is the field mark. Nests underground and in cavities.

species.name: Mariposa cometa xochiquetzal
species.short_description: Very large pale yellow swallowtail with narrow black stripes and two tails per hindwing.
species.en_short_description: Very large pale yellow swallowtail with narrow black stripes and two tails per hindwing.
species.description: Colorado, Washington and Mexico City. The largest butterfly in much of the West. The doubled hindwing tails separate it from the Western Tiger Swallowtail. Uses ash and chokecherry.
species.en_description: Colorado, Washington and Mexico City. The largest butterfly in much of the West. The doubled hindwing tails separate it from the Western Tiger Swallowtail. Uses ash and chokecherry.

species.name: Abejorro de cinturón café
species.short_description: Bumble bee with a yellow thorax and a narrow brown crescent band on the abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Bumble bee with a yellow thorax and a narrow brown crescent band on the abdomen.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. The brownish rather than yellow abdominal band is diagnostic but subtle. Common in prairie and old field habitats. Nests on or near the ground.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. The brownish rather than yellow abdominal band is diagnostic but subtle. Common in prairie and old field habitats. Nests on or near the ground.

species.name: Langosta gris norteña
species.short_description: Large mottled grey-brown grasshopper that flies strongly and far.
species.en_short_description: Large mottled grey-brown grasshopper that flies strongly and far.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Big enough to be mistaken for a bird in flight. Flies with a clattering sound. Feeds on a wide range of shrubs and can be locally abundant.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Big enough to be mistaken for a bird in flight. Flies with a clattering sound. Feeds on a wide range of shrubs and can be locally abundant.

species.name: Abejorro de Hunt
species.short_description: Bumble bee with bold yellow and rust-orange banding on a black ground.
species.en_short_description: Bumble bee with bold yellow and rust-orange banding on a black ground.
species.description: Colorado, Washington and Mexico City. The bright tricoloured pattern makes it one of the more recognisable western bumble bees. Common in mountain meadows and gardens.
species.en_description: Colorado, Washington and Mexico City. The bright tricoloured pattern makes it one of the more recognisable western bumble bees. Common in mountain meadows and gardens.

species.name: Woodland Skipper
species.short_description: Small orange skipper with a hooked antenna and rapid darting flight.
species.en_short_description: Small orange skipper with a hooked antenna and rapid darting flight.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Abundant in late summer on roadside flowers. Perches with forewings and hindwings held at different angles, typical of grass skippers.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Abundant in late summer on roadside flowers. Perches with forewings and hindwings held at different angles, typical of grass skippers.

species.name: Chinche marmolada asiática
species.short_description: Shield-shaped mottled brown bug with white bands on the antennae and abdominal edge.
species.en_short_description: Shield-shaped mottled brown bug with white bands on the antennae and abdominal edge.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Invasive agricultural pest that overwinters indoors in large numbers. The alternating light bands on the antennae are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Invasive agricultural pest that overwinters indoors in large numbers. The alternating light bands on the antennae are diagnostic.

species.name: Rayadora azul
species.short_description: Small dragonfly; males with a powder-blue abdomen, green eyes and a white face.
species.en_short_description: Small dragonfly; males with a powder-blue abdomen, green eyes and a white face.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Perches on emergent stems with wings angled forward and down. Females are boldly striped yellow and black. Very common at ponds.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Perches on emergent stems with wings angled forward and down. Females are boldly striped yellow and black. Very common at ponds.

species.name: Mariposa Almirante Rojo
species.short_description: Dark butterfly with a bold orange-red band across each forewing and white tip spots.
species.en_short_description: Dark butterfly with a bold orange-red band across each forewing and white tip spots.
species.description: Five regions. Territorial and inquisitive, often landing on people. Caterpillars feed on nettles. Migrates northward in spring, sometimes in noticeable pulses.
species.en_description: Five regions. Territorial and inquisitive, often landing on people. Caterpillars feed on nettles. Migrates northward in spring, sometimes in noticeable pulses.

species.name: mayate de la calabaza
species.short_description: Robust flower scarab, mottled and hairy, feeding inside squash and cactus blooms.
species.en_short_description: Robust flower scarab, mottled and hairy, feeding inside squash and cactus blooms.
species.description: Mexico City region. One of the flower beetles known locally as mayates. Adults push into large flowers to feed on pollen. Buzzes loudly and heavily in flight.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. One of the flower beetles known locally as mayates. Adults push into large flowers to feed on pollen. Buzzes loudly and heavily in flight.

species.name: Mariposa pasionaria motas blancas
species.short_description: Bright orange butterfly with elongated forewings and large silver spots beneath.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange butterfly with elongated forewings and large silver spots beneath.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. The metallic silver undersides are unmistakable when perched. Caterpillars are orange with black spines and feed only on passionflower vines.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. The metallic silver undersides are unmistakable when perched. Caterpillars are orange with black spines and feed only on passionflower vines.

species.name: Fuzzy-Horned Bumble Bee
species.short_description: Small shaggy bumble bee with yellow and rust bands and a very hairy appearance.
species.en_short_description: Small shaggy bumble bee with yellow and rust bands and a very hairy appearance.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Notably long and untidy pile compared with other bumble bees. A mountain and northern-forest species, common on subalpine wildflowers.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Notably long and untidy pile compared with other bumble bees. A mountain and northern-forest species, common on subalpine wildflowers.

species.name: Abejorro de cara amarilla
species.short_description: Black bumble bee with a yellow face, yellow thoracic band and one yellow abdominal band.
species.en_short_description: Black bumble bee with a yellow face, yellow thoracic band and one yellow abdominal band.
species.description: California and Washington. The commonest bumble bee on the Pacific coast, in gardens and coastal scrub. The yellow face against an otherwise black head is the field mark.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The commonest bumble bee on the Pacific coast, in gardens and coastal scrub. The yellow face against an otherwise black head is the field mark.

species.name: Mariposa Sedosa Gris
species.short_description: Small grey butterfly with a thin hair-like tail and an orange spot near it.
species.en_short_description: Small grey butterfly with a thin hair-like tail and an orange spot near it.
species.description: Every region. Rubs its hindwings together so the tails and eyespot mimic a head, deflecting attacks. One of the most widespread butterflies in North America.
species.en_description: Every region. Rubs its hindwings together so the tails and eyespot mimic a head, deflecting attacks. One of the most widespread butterflies in North America.

species.name: Escarabajo japonés
species.short_description: Metallic green beetle with coppery wing covers and white tufts along the sides.
species.en_short_description: Metallic green beetle with coppery wing covers and white tufts along the sides.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Invasive and destructive, skeletonising leaves of roses, grapes and lindens. The five white hair tufts on each side of the abdomen are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Invasive and destructive, skeletonising leaves of roses, grapes and lindens. The five white hair tufts on each side of the abdomen are diagnostic.

species.name: Rayadora abigarrada
species.short_description: Slender dragonfly with a mottled brown-and-red abdomen and pale thoracic stripes.
species.en_short_description: Slender dragonfly with a mottled brown-and-red abdomen and pale thoracic stripes.
species.description: Five regions. One of the earliest and latest dragonflies on the wing, and a genuine migrant. Perches flat on bare ground and gravel rather than vegetation.
species.en_description: Five regions. One of the earliest and latest dragonflies on the wing, and a genuine migrant. Perches flat on bare ground and gravel rather than vegetation.

species.name: Chapulín rayado
species.short_description: Large yellow-green grasshopper with two pale stripes converging on the wingtips.
species.en_short_description: Large yellow-green grasshopper with two pale stripes converging on the wingtips.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. A common grassland and roadside species that can reach outbreak densities. The converging back stripes are the identification.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. A common grassland and roadside species that can reach outbreak densities. The converging back stripes are the identification.

species.name: Avispón de cara blanca
species.short_description: Large black-and-white social wasp that builds a grey football-shaped paper nest.
species.en_short_description: Large black-and-white social wasp that builds a grey football-shaped paper nest.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Actually a yellowjacket rather than a true hornet. Aggressively defends the aerial nest. The ivory-white face is unmistakable.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Actually a yellowjacket rather than a true hornet. Aggressively defends the aerial nest. The ivory-white face is unmistakable.

species.name: Mariposa almirante del oeste
species.short_description: Dark butterfly with a white band across both wings and orange forewing tips.
species.en_short_description: Dark butterfly with a white band across both wings and orange forewing tips.
species.description: California and Washington. Patrols streamside willows and defends perches against passing birds. The orange wingtip separates it from the related white admirals.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Patrols streamside willows and defends perches against passing birds. The orange wingtip separates it from the related white admirals.

species.name: Mariposa reina
species.short_description: Rich chestnut-brown butterfly with scattered white spots and thin black veins.
species.en_short_description: Rich chestnut-brown butterfly with scattered white spots and thin black veins.
species.description: Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. Darker and less strongly veined than the Monarch, with white spots across the forewing. Also a milkweed feeder and equally toxic.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. Darker and less strongly veined than the Monarch, with white spots across the forewing. Also a milkweed feeder and equally toxic.

species.name: Noctuido de la acedera
species.short_description: Brown noctuid moth with bright orange-yellow hindwings edged in black.
species.en_short_description: Brown noctuid moth with bright orange-yellow hindwings edged in black.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe and now abundant. Flashes the hidden yellow hindwings when disturbed. Larvae are cutworms.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe and now abundant. Flashes the hidden yellow hindwings when disturbed. Larvae are cutworms.

species.name: Polilla manchada de pasto
species.short_description: Yellow-brown moth with dark bands; caterpillar black at both ends with a yellow middle.
species.en_short_description: Yellow-brown moth with dark bands; caterpillar black at both ends with a yellow middle.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. The banded caterpillar is often confused with a woolly bear. Feeds on willow, alder and poplar. Adults have translucent patterned wings.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. The banded caterpillar is often confused with a woolly bear. Feeds on willow, alder and poplar. Adults have translucent patterned wings.

species.name: Chapulín diferencial
species.short_description: Stout olive-brown grasshopper with black herringbone chevrons on the hind femur.
species.en_short_description: Stout olive-brown grasshopper with black herringbone chevrons on the hind femur.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The bold black V-marks on the thigh are diagnostic. A significant crop pest in outbreak years. Common on weedy field margins.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The bold black V-marks on the thigh are diagnostic. A significant crop pest in outbreak years. Common on weedy field margins.

species.name: Avispa chaqueta amarilla occidental
species.short_description: Black-and-yellow social wasp with a broad yellow eye surround, nesting underground.
species.en_short_description: Black-and-yellow social wasp with a broad yellow eye surround, nesting underground.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. The wasp responsible for most late-summer picnic conflicts in the West. Nests in ground cavities. Scavenges meat and sugar aggressively.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. The wasp responsible for most late-summer picnic conflicts in the West. Nests in ground cavities. Scavenges meat and sugar aggressively.

species.name: Rayadora blanca de Lydia
species.short_description: Stocky dragonfly; males with a chalky-white abdomen and broad black wing bands.
species.en_short_description: Stocky dragonfly; males with a chalky-white abdomen and broad black wing bands.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The powdery white abdomen is unmistakable. Perches flat on the ground or on rocks. Females have brown bodies and zigzag wing spots.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The powdery white abdomen is unmistakable. Perches flat on the ground or on rocks. Females have brown bodies and zigzag wing spots.

species.name: Mosca calígrafa
species.short_description: Tiny hoverfly with a yellow-and-black striped abdomen, hovering over flowers.
species.en_short_description: Tiny hoverfly with a yellow-and-black striped abdomen, hovering over flowers.
species.description: Five regions. A syrphid fly, not a bee — two wings, not four, and it hovers motionless. Larvae are important aphid predators in gardens. Extremely common but easy to overlook.
species.en_description: Five regions. A syrphid fly, not a bee — two wings, not four, and it hovers motionless. Larvae are important aphid predators in gardens. Extremely common but easy to overlook.

species.name: Mariposa cometa golondrina del Anís
species.short_description: Black-and-yellow swallowtail with a broad yellow band and blue-and-orange hindwing spots.
species.en_short_description: Black-and-yellow swallowtail with a broad yellow band and blue-and-orange hindwing spots.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Caterpillars feed on fennel and native carrot-family plants. Males hilltop in spring, patrolling ridge crests for females.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Caterpillars feed on fennel and native carrot-family plants. Males hilltop in spring, patrolling ridge crests for females.

species.name: Mariposa Vanesa occidental
species.short_description: Small orange butterfly with an orange rather than white forewing bar and four blue-cored eyespots.
species.en_short_description: Small orange butterfly with an orange rather than white forewing bar and four blue-cored eyespots.
species.description: California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Separated from the Painted Lady by the orange subapical bar. Uses mallows as host plants. Common in gardens and vacant lots.
species.en_description: California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. Separated from the Painted Lady by the orange subapical bar. Uses mallows as host plants. Common in gardens and vacant lots.

species.name: Saltarina de tablero común
species.short_description: Small grey-and-white checkered skipper with a bluish furry body.
species.en_short_description: Small grey-and-white checkered skipper with a bluish furry body.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Flies fast and low over bare ground and weedy patches. The bold black-and-white checkering is distinctive among small skippers.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Flies fast and low over bare ground and weedy patches. The bold black-and-white checkering is distinctive among small skippers.

species.name: Great Golden Digger Wasp
species.short_description: Large wasp with a rust-orange abdomen base, golden thoracic hair and black legs.
species.en_short_description: Large wasp with a rust-orange abdomen base, golden thoracic hair and black legs.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Solitary; digs nest burrows in bare soil and provisions them with paralysed katydids. Non-aggressive despite its size.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Solitary; digs nest burrows in bare soil and provisions them with paralysed katydids. Non-aggressive despite its size.

species.name: Abejorro zumbador
species.short_description: Large bumble bee with broad yellow bands on the thorax and abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Large bumble bee with broad yellow bands on the thorax and abdomen.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. A desert and subtropical species, often visiting agave and desert legume flowers. Among the larger bumble bees in the region.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. A desert and subtropical species, often visiting agave and desert legume flowers. Among the larger bumble bees in the region.

species.name: Polilla tigre de manchas plateadas
species.short_description: Brown moth with rows of silvery-white spots on the forewings.
species.en_short_description: Brown moth with rows of silvery-white spots on the forewings.
species.description: California and Washington. Caterpillars are dense rusty-brown tussock larvae that feed communally on Douglas-fir and other conifers, sometimes defoliating branches.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Caterpillars are dense rusty-brown tussock larvae that feed communally on Douglas-fir and other conifers, sometimes defoliating branches.

species.name: Coyote
species.short_description: Slender grey-buff wild dog with a narrow muzzle and a low, bushy, black-tipped tail.
species.en_short_description: Slender grey-buff wild dog with a narrow muzzle and a low, bushy, black-tipped tail.
species.description: The most-observed wild carnivore across all six regions, at home from Colorado ranchland to Mexico City parks and Brooklyn cemeteries. Runs with its tail down, unlike a dog. Group yipping at dusk is diagnostic. Hunts rodents, rabbits and whatever a city provides.
species.en_description: The most-observed wild carnivore across all six regions, at home from Colorado ranchland to Mexico City parks and Brooklyn cemeteries. Runs with its tail down, unlike a dog. Group yipping at dusk is diagnostic. Hunts rodents, rabbits and whatever a city provides.

species.name: Oso negro americano
species.short_description: Heavy-bodied bear with no shoulder hump and a straight facial profile; colour ranges black to cinnamon.
species.en_short_description: Heavy-bodied bear with no shoulder hump and a straight facial profile; colour ranges black to cinnamon.
species.description: Common in Colorado's oak and aspen zone, the Cascades and the Adirondacks. Brown-phase animals are frequent in the West and are still this species. Overturned logs, clawed aspen trunks and raided bins are the usual signs. Denning runs roughly November to April.
species.en_description: Common in Colorado's oak and aspen zone, the Cascades and the Adirondacks. Brown-phase animals are frequent in the West and are still this species. Overturned logs, clawed aspen trunks and raided bins are the usual signs. Denning runs roughly November to April.

species.name: Lobo marino californiano
species.short_description: Barking, sleek-brown eared seal that walks on rotating flippers; males grow a domed forehead crest.
species.en_short_description: Barking, sleek-brown eared seal that walks on rotating flippers; males grow a domed forehead crest.
species.description: Hauls out noisily on jetties, buoys and Baja rocks. Told from a true seal by visible ear flaps and the ability to prop up on its front flippers. The Sea of Cortez colonies around La Paz are a reliable year-round sighting.
species.en_description: Hauls out noisily on jetties, buoys and Baja rocks. Told from a true seal by visible ear flaps and the ability to prop up on its front flippers. The Sea of Cortez colonies around La Paz are a reliable year-round sighting.

species.name: Zorro Rojo
species.short_description: Rusty-orange fox with black stockings and a white-tipped brush of a tail.
species.en_short_description: Rusty-orange fox with black stockings and a white-tipped brush of a tail.
species.description: Field edges, golf courses and suburbs across Colorado, the Pacific Northwest and New York. The white tail tip is the quickest separation from Gray Fox. Hunts voles with a high pounce through snow or grass. Largely crepuscular but easily seen by day where undisturbed.
species.en_description: Field edges, golf courses and suburbs across Colorado, the Pacific Northwest and New York. The white tail tip is the quickest separation from Gray Fox. Hunts voles with a high pounce through snow or grass. Largely crepuscular but easily seen by day where undisturbed.

species.name: Lince Americano
species.short_description: Short-tailed spotted cat about twice house-cat size, with tufted ears and ruffed cheeks.
species.en_short_description: Short-tailed spotted cat about twice house-cat size, with tufted ears and ruffed cheeks.
species.description: The most widespread wild cat in the Americas and present in every one of the six regions. The stubby black-barred tail rules out Mountain Lion instantly. Hunts rabbits and rodents in chaparral, scrub and rocky canyon country. Secretive but regularly caught on trail cameras.
species.en_description: The most widespread wild cat in the Americas and present in every one of the six regions. The stubby black-barred tail rules out Mountain Lion instantly. Hunts rabbits and rodents in chaparral, scrub and rocky canyon country. Secretive but regularly caught on trail cameras.

species.name: Foca común
species.short_description: Plump, spotted true seal with no ear flaps that hauls out on tide rocks and sandbars.
species.en_short_description: Plump, spotted true seal with no ear flaps that hauls out on tide rocks and sandbars.
species.description: Puget Sound, the California coast, Baja lagoons and Long Island beaches. Hitches along on its belly rather than walking, unlike a sea lion. Curious at the surface, often floating vertically with only the head showing, watching a person on shore.
species.en_description: Puget Sound, the California coast, Baja lagoons and Long Island beaches. Hitches along on its belly rather than walking, unlike a sea lion. Curious at the surface, often floating vertically with only the head showing, watching a person on shore.

species.name: Zorra gris
species.short_description: Grizzled grey fox with rusty flanks and a black stripe running the length of the tail.
species.en_short_description: Grizzled grey fox with rusty flanks and a black stripe running the length of the tail.
species.description: The only American canid that routinely climbs trees, using rotating wrists to reach branches. Prefers brushy woodland and canyon scrub from Colorado through Mexico City to the Baja cape. The black tail stripe and black tail tip separate it from Red Fox.
species.en_description: The only American canid that routinely climbs trees, using rotating wrists to reach branches. Prefers brushy woodland and canyon scrub from Colorado through Mexico City to the Baja cape. The black tail stripe and black tail tip separate it from Red Fox.

species.name: Puma
species.short_description: Long, plain-tawny cat with a very long black-tipped tail; also called Puma or Cougar.
species.en_short_description: Long, plain-tawny cat with a very long black-tipped tail; also called Puma or Cougar.
species.description: Present but rarely seen throughout the western regions. The uniformly unspotted coat and tail nearly as long as the body are conclusive. Follows deer, so deer concentrations are where tracks appear. Most records are camera-trap images or a single set of prints in mud.
species.en_description: Present but rarely seen throughout the western regions. The uniformly unspotted coat and tail nearly as long as the body are conclusive. Follows deer, so deer concentrations are where tracks appear. Most records are camera-trap images or a single set of prints in mud.

species.name: León marino de Steller
species.short_description: Very large pale-blond sea lion; bulls carry a thick maned neck and a blunt, bear-like head.
species.en_short_description: Very large pale-blond sea lion; bulls carry a thick maned neck and a blunt, bear-like head.
species.description: The big northern sea lion of Washington and northern California haul-outs. Roars and growls rather than barking like a California Sea Lion, and is markedly paler and heavier. Adult males can exceed a tonne, dwarfing anything else on the rock.
species.en_description: The big northern sea lion of Washington and northern California haul-outs. Roars and growls rather than barking like a California Sea Lion, and is markedly paler and heavier. Adult males can exceed a tonne, dwarfing anything else on the rock.

species.name: Elefante marino norteño
species.short_description: Enormous grey seal; adult males bear an inflatable pendulous snout and scarred pink chest shield.
species.en_short_description: Enormous grey seal; adult males bear an inflatable pendulous snout and scarred pink chest shield.
species.description: Breeding beaches in California and along the Baja coast fill with hauled-out animals in winter. Even resting subadults are far larger than a Harbor Seal. Spends most of the year at sea diving to extraordinary depths, returning to the same beach to moult.
species.en_description: Breeding beaches in California and along the Baja coast fill with hauled-out animals in winter. Even resting subadults are far larger than a Harbor Seal. Spends most of the year at sea diving to extraordinary depths, returning to the same beach to moult.

species.name: Zorra desértica
species.short_description: Small, pale buff-grey fox of open shortgrass prairie with a black-tipped tail and dark muzzle patches.
species.en_short_description: Small, pale buff-grey fox of open shortgrass prairie with a black-tipped tail and dark muzzle patches.
species.description: A Colorado eastern-plains specialist, cat-sized and much smaller than a Red Fox. Digs multi-entrance dens in open grassland and hunts insects and rodents at night. Prairie conversion to cropland removed most of its range, so a sighting is worth recording carefully.
species.en_description: A Colorado eastern-plains specialist, cat-sized and much smaller than a Red Fox. Digs multi-entrance dens in open grassland and hunts insects and rodents at night. Prairie conversion to cropland removed most of its range, so a sighting is worth recording carefully.

species.name: Foca gris
species.short_description: Large seal with a long, straight, horse-like muzzle and parallel wide-set nostrils.
species.en_short_description: Large seal with a long, straight, horse-like muzzle and parallel wide-set nostrils.
species.description: The bulkier of the two north-east seals, increasing on Long Island beaches and outer sandbars. The Roman-nosed profile separates it from the snub-faced Harbor Seal even at long range. Hauls out in mixed groups through the winter months.
species.en_description: The bulkier of the two north-east seals, increasing on Long Island beaches and outer sandbars. The Roman-nosed profile separates it from the snub-faced Harbor Seal even at long range. Hauls out in mixed groups through the winter months.

species.name: Lobo gris
species.short_description: Large grey-brown wild dog with long legs, blocky muzzle and a straight tail carried level.
species.en_short_description: Large grey-brown wild dog with long legs, blocky muzzle and a straight tail carried level.
species.description: Reintroduced to Colorado and recolonising Washington, so a genuine sighting is a notable record. Much bigger and longer-legged than a Coyote, with a broader muzzle and smaller ears in proportion. Travels in family packs; single animals disperse enormous distances.
species.en_description: Reintroduced to Colorado and recolonising Washington, so a genuine sighting is a notable record. Much bigger and longer-legged than a Coyote, with a broader muzzle and smaller ears in proportion. Travels in family packs; single animals disperse enormous distances.

species.name: Zorrita del desierto
species.short_description: Tiny desert fox with huge ears, a slight frame and a black-tipped tail.
species.en_short_description: Tiny desert fox with huge ears, a slight frame and a black-tipped tail.
species.description: Arid basins in western Colorado, the California deserts and Baja California Sur. The oversized ears radiate heat and are the fastest field mark against the shortgrass Swift Fox. Strictly nocturnal, denning in loose sandy soil and hunting kangaroo rats.
species.en_description: Arid basins in western Colorado, the California deserts and Baja California Sur. The oversized ears radiate heat and are the fastest field mark against the shortgrass Swift Fox. Strictly nocturnal, denning in loose sandy soil and hunting kangaroo rats.

species.name: Saltarina negrita
species.short_description: Stocky black jumping spider with a white triangle on the abdomen and iridescent green fangs.
species.en_short_description: Stocky black jumping spider with a white triangle on the abdomen and iridescent green fangs.
species.description: Five regions and the most-observed spider here. Hunts by stalking and leaping rather than building a web. Turns to watch you with large forward-facing eyes. Harmless.
species.en_description: Five regions and the most-observed spider here. Hunts by stalking and leaping rather than building a web. Turns to watch you with large forward-facing eyes. Harmless.

species.name: Araña Europea de Jardín
species.short_description: Brown orbweaver with a distinct white cross of spots on the abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Brown orbweaver with a distinct white cross of spots on the abdomen.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced from Europe and abundant in gardens by late summer. Rebuilds its wheel-shaped web nightly. The dorsal cross is diagnostic.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced from Europe and abundant in gardens by late summer. Rebuilds its wheel-shaped web nightly. The dorsal cross is diagnostic.

species.name: Araña manchada de jardín
species.short_description: Grey-brown orbweaver with heavily banded legs and a mottled angular abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Grey-brown orbweaver with heavily banded legs and a mottled angular abdomen.
species.description: Five regions. Builds large webs on buildings, fences and streamside vegetation, often in dense colonies. Hides in a retreat by day and sits in the hub at night.
species.en_description: Five regions. Builds large webs on buildings, fences and streamside vegetation, often in dense colonies. Hides in a retreat by day and sits in the hub at night.

species.name: Viuda negra norteña
species.short_description: Glossy black spider with a red hourglass on the underside of the abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Glossy black spider with a red hourglass on the underside of the abdomen.
species.description: Five regions. Venomous — do not handle, though bites are rare and seldom serious. Builds an irregular tangled web low down in woodpiles, meter boxes and under garden furniture.
species.en_description: Five regions. Venomous — do not handle, though bites are rare and seldom serious. Builds an irregular tangled web low down in woodpiles, meter boxes and under garden furniture.

species.name: Araña Cebra
species.short_description: Small jumping spider boldly striped black and white.
species.en_short_description: Small jumping spider boldly striped black and white.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Hunts on sunlit walls, fences and window frames. Introduced from Europe. Tilts its body to track movement, and jumps readily.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Hunts on sunlit walls, fences and window frames. Introduced from Europe. Tilts its body to track movement, and jumps readily.

species.name: Araña saltarina verde dorada
species.short_description: Metallic green-gold jumping spider with a pale abdominal border.
species.en_short_description: Metallic green-gold jumping spider with a pale abdominal border.
species.description: Colorado, New York, Mexico City and Baja. Iridescent scales give a coppery-green sheen in sunlight. Hunts on foliage rather than walls. One of the most striking local salticids.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York, Mexico City and Baja. Iridescent scales give a coppery-green sheen in sunlight. Hunts on foliage rather than walls. One of the most striking local salticids.

species.name: Araña plateada de jardín
species.short_description: Orbweaver with a silvery front body and a boldly patterned notched abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Orbweaver with a silvery front body and a boldly patterned notched abdomen.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Sits head-down at the hub of a web bearing a conspicuous zigzag silk stabilimentum. Legs held in pairs forming an X.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Sits head-down at the hub of a web bearing a conspicuous zigzag silk stabilimentum. Legs held in pairs forming an X.

species.name: Araña tejedora espinosa
species.short_description: Tiny hard-shelled orbweaver with six sharp abdominal spines, often white and black.
species.en_short_description: Tiny hard-shelled orbweaver with six sharp abdominal spines, often white and black.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Looks more like a seed pod than a spider. Colour varies from white through yellow to red. Builds small webs at head height on trails.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Looks more like a seed pod than a spider. Colour varies from white through yellow to red. Builds small webs at head height on trails.

species.name: Falsa viuda negra mordedora
species.short_description: Glossy brown spider with cream markings and a bulbous abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Glossy brown spider with cream markings and a bulbous abdomen.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and spreading. Resembles a widow in shape but lacks the hourglass and is brown, not black. Common on building exteriors.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and spreading. Resembles a widow in shape but lacks the hourglass and is brown, not black. Common on building exteriors.

species.name: Araña caza cochinillas
species.short_description: Shiny red-brown spider with a pale cream abdomen and very large forward-pointing fangs.
species.en_short_description: Shiny red-brown spider with a pale cream abdomen and very large forward-pointing fangs.
species.description: All six regions. Hunts woodlice under stones and logs at night, using its outsized jaws to pierce their armour. Nocturnal and unmistakable in colour.
species.en_description: All six regions. Hunts woodlice under stones and logs at night, using its outsized jaws to pierce their armour. Nocturnal and unmistakable in colour.

species.name: Alacrán de la corteza bajeño
species.short_description: Slender pale yellow scorpion with thin pincers and a fine tail.
species.en_short_description: Slender pale yellow scorpion with thin pincers and a fine tail.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Medically significant — its sting is genuinely dangerous and warrants prompt attention. Climbs walls and hides in shoes and bedding. Fluoresces under UV light.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Medically significant — its sting is genuinely dangerous and warrants prompt attention. Climbs walls and hides in shoes and bedding. Fluoresces under UV light.

species.name: Araña de jardín bandeada
species.short_description: Large orbweaver with fine silver, yellow and black abdominal banding.
species.en_short_description: Large orbweaver with fine silver, yellow and black abdominal banding.
species.description: All six regions. Builds a large vertical orb in tall grass and shrubs in late summer. Paler and more finely banded than the Yellow Garden Spider. Sits head-down at the hub.
species.en_description: All six regions. Builds a large vertical orb in tall grass and shrubs in late summer. Paler and more finely banded than the Yellow Garden Spider. Sits head-down at the hub.

species.name: Araña de cruz
species.short_description: Rusty-brown orbweaver with a hairy abdomen and strongly banded legs.
species.en_short_description: Rusty-brown orbweaver with a hairy abdomen and strongly banded legs.
species.description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Active mainly at night, when it builds large webs on porches and eaves. Hides in a curled leaf or crevice by day.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Active mainly at night, when it builds large webs on porches and eaves. Hides in a curled leaf or crevice by day.

species.name: Tejedora de huertos
species.short_description: Small elongate spider with a silvery-green abdomen and orange spots below.
species.en_short_description: Small elongate spider with a silvery-green abdomen and orange spots below.
species.description: California and New York. Builds a small horizontal orb in shrubs and hangs beneath it. The bright green and silver body with a splash of orange is distinctive.
species.en_description: California and New York. Builds a small horizontal orb in shrubs and hangs beneath it. The bright green and silver body with a splash of orange is distinctive.

species.name: Goldenrod Crab Spider
species.short_description: Squat white or yellow ambush spider with long crab-like front legs.
species.en_short_description: Squat white or yellow ambush spider with long crab-like front legs.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Sits motionless in flowers, changing between white and yellow over several days to match the bloom. No web; ambushes visiting bees.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Sits motionless in flowers, changing between white and yellow over several days to match the bloom. No web; ambushes visiting bees.

species.name: Viuda café
species.short_description: Mottled brown widow with an orange hourglass and a spiky-edged egg sac.
species.en_short_description: Mottled brown widow with an orange hourglass and a spiky-edged egg sac.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and spreading fast. Less venomous than the black widow. The distinctive spiked, fluffy egg sacs are the easiest confirmation.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and spreading fast. Less venomous than the black widow. The distinctive spiked, fluffy egg sacs are the easiest confirmation.

species.name: Araña amarilla de jardín
species.short_description: Large orbweaver with bold yellow-and-black abdominal markings and silver carapace.
species.en_short_description: Large orbweaver with bold yellow-and-black abdominal markings and silver carapace.
species.description: All six regions. Builds a big vertical orb with a thick zigzag silk band down the middle. Females are large and conspicuous in late summer gardens and meadows.
species.en_description: All six regions. Builds a big vertical orb with a thick zigzag silk band down the middle. Females are large and conspicuous in late summer gardens and meadows.

species.name: Tendarapo áspero del desierto
species.short_description: Flattened brown arachnid with long whip-like feelers and spiny grasping pedipalps.
species.en_short_description: Flattened brown arachnid with long whip-like feelers and spiny grasping pedipalps.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Neither spider nor scorpion, and completely harmless — it has no venom or sting. Nocturnal, found under rocks and in caves. Moves sideways like a crab.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Neither spider nor scorpion, and completely harmless — it has no venom or sting. Nocturnal, found under rocks and in caves. Moves sideways like a crab.

species.name: Tan Jumping Spider
species.short_description: Flattened grey-tan jumping spider with a scalloped chevron pattern.
species.en_short_description: Flattened grey-tan jumping spider with a scalloped chevron pattern.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Lives on tree bark and wooden fences, where its mottled pattern hides it well. Flattens into crevices. Often found on porch railings.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Lives on tree bark and wooden fences, where its mottled pattern hides it well. Flattens into crevices. Often found on porch railings.

species.name: Araña saltarina de cola roja
species.short_description: Large jumping spider; males black with a solid red abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Large jumping spider; males black with a solid red abdomen.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. The plain red abdomen without white markings separates males from the Bold Jumping Spider. Females have a central black stripe.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. The plain red abdomen without white markings separates males from the Bold Jumping Spider. Females have a central black stripe.

species.name: Araña cangrejo gigante
species.short_description: Large flat fast-moving spider with legs held out sideways.
species.en_short_description: Large flat fast-moving spider with legs held out sideways.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Enters houses and hunts cockroaches on walls. Harmless despite alarming size and speed. Carries a flat white egg sac under the body.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Enters houses and hunts cockroaches on walls. Harmless despite alarming size and speed. Carries a flat white egg sac under the body.

species.name: Araña saltarina gris de pared
species.short_description: Flattened grey jumping spider with two dark side stripes, on sunlit walls.
species.en_short_description: Flattened grey jumping spider with two dark side stripes, on sunlit walls.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and closely tied to buildings. Hunts on stucco and masonry in full sun. Males are darker with white palps.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and closely tied to buildings. Hunts on stucco and masonry in full sun. Males are darker with white palps.

species.name: Falsa Viuda Negra Doméstica
species.short_description: Glossy dark purple-brown spider with a rounded abdomen and no hourglass.
species.en_short_description: Glossy dark purple-brown spider with a rounded abdomen and no hourglass.
species.description: All six regions. Common in sheds, cellars and under sills. Frequently mistaken for a black widow but is browner, lacks the red hourglass and is far less venomous.
species.en_description: All six regions. Common in sheds, cellars and under sills. Frequently mistaken for a black widow but is browner, lacks the red hourglass and is far less venomous.

species.name: American Nursery Web Spider
species.short_description: Slim brown spider with a dark-edged central stripe, sitting on leaf tips with legs paired.
species.en_short_description: Slim brown spider with a dark-edged central stripe, sitting on leaf tips with legs paired.
species.description: New York. Carries its egg sac in the jaws, then builds a silk nursery tent over foliage and guards it. Rests with the first two leg pairs held together and forward.
species.en_description: New York. Carries its egg sac in the jaws, then builds a silk nursery tent over foliage and guards it. Rests with the first two leg pairs held together and forward.

species.name: Colonus hesperus
species.short_description: Small dark jumping spider with pale markings, in western scrub and leaf litter.
species.en_short_description: Small dark jumping spider with pale markings, in western scrub and leaf litter.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. A ground-and-litter jumping spider rather than a wall dweller. Cryptically marked and easily overlooked among dry leaves.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. A ground-and-litter jumping spider rather than a wall dweller. Cryptically marked and easily overlooked among dry leaves.

species.name: Araña pescadora oscura
species.short_description: Very large mottled grey-brown spider with banded legs, often far from water.
species.en_short_description: Very large mottled grey-brown spider with banded legs, often far from water.
species.description: New York. Among the largest spiders in the north-east, with a leg span that can exceed 7 cm. Found on tree trunks, docks and inside buildings. Harmless.
species.en_description: New York. Among the largest spiders in the north-east, with a leg span that can exceed 7 cm. Found on tree trunks, docks and inside buildings. Harmless.

species.name: Araña patona
species.short_description: Pale spindly spider with extremely long thin legs, in a loose tangled web.
species.en_short_description: Pale spindly spider with extremely long thin legs, in a loose tangled web.
species.description: Five regions. The daddy-long-legs spider of basements and garages. Vibrates rapidly in its web when disturbed, becoming a blur. Preys on other spiders, including widows.
species.en_description: Five regions. The daddy-long-legs spider of basements and garages. Vibrates rapidly in its web when disturbed, becoming a blur. Preys on other spiders, including widows.

species.name: Araña patona
species.short_description: Small round body on extremely long legs; not a spider at all.
species.en_short_description: Small round body on extremely long legs; not a spider at all.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. An opilionid — one body segment, two eyes, no venom and no silk. Common on walls and vegetation. Legs detach easily if grabbed.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. An opilionid — one body segment, two eyes, no venom and no silk. Common on walls and vegetation. Legs detach easily if grabbed.

species.name: Alacrán marrón del centro
species.short_description: Stout brown scorpion with thick pincers and a relatively heavy tail.
species.en_short_description: Stout brown scorpion with thick pincers and a relatively heavy tail.
species.description: Mexico City region. Sting is painful but not dangerous, unlike the slender bark scorpions. Found under stones and bark in highland scrub. Fluoresces under UV light.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Sting is painful but not dangerous, unlike the slender bark scorpions. Found under stones and bark in highland scrub. Fluoresces under UV light.

species.name: Araña saltarina verde metálico
species.short_description: Tiny iridescent green-bronze jumping spider that mimics a leaf beetle.
species.en_short_description: Tiny iridescent green-bronze jumping spider that mimics a leaf beetle.
species.description: Five regions. Its metallic sheen and rounded shape imitate a chrysomelid beetle, deterring predators. Hunts on foliage in gardens and scrub. Very small and easily missed.
species.en_description: Five regions. Its metallic sheen and rounded shape imitate a chrysomelid beetle, deterring predators. Hunts on foliage in gardens and scrub. Very small and easily missed.

species.name: Alacrán de Baja California Sur
species.short_description: Large pale desert hairy scorpion with hairy tail segments and heavy pincers.
species.en_short_description: Large pale desert hairy scorpion with hairy tail segments and heavy pincers.
species.description: Baja California Sur. One of the largest scorpions in the region. Sting is painful but not medically serious. Digs deep burrows in sandy desert soil; strictly nocturnal.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. One of the largest scorpions in the region. Sting is painful but not medically serious. Digs deep burrows in sandy desert soil; strictly nocturnal.

species.name: Araña cazadora dorada
species.short_description: Large pale tan huntsman with long sideways-held legs and dark leg joints.
species.en_short_description: Large pale tan huntsman with long sideways-held legs and dark leg joints.
species.description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Hunts at night on rock faces and walls without a web. Fast and startling but harmless. Often found in desert dwellings.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Hunts at night on rock faces and walls without a web. Fast and startling but harmless. Often found in desert dwellings.

species.name: Araña lince verde
species.short_description: Bright green spider with translucent spiny legs and red markings around the eyes.
species.en_short_description: Bright green spider with translucent spiny legs and red markings around the eyes.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Ambushes pollinators on flower heads without a web. Guards a spiky egg sac fiercely. Can spit venom short distances when defending eggs.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Ambushes pollinators on flower heads without a web. Guards a spiky egg sac fiercely. Can spit venom short distances when defending eggs.

species.name: Falsa viuda negra triangulada
species.short_description: Small spider with a pale abdomen bearing a row of dark triangular marks.
species.en_short_description: Small spider with a pale abdomen bearing a row of dark triangular marks.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Extremely common in the corners of houses and garages. The zigzag row of triangles down the back is diagnostic. Harmless.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Extremely common in the corners of houses and garages. The zigzag row of triangles down the back is diagnostic. Harmless.

species.name: Giant House Spider
species.short_description: Large brown funnel-web spider with long legs and a mottled abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Large brown funnel-web spider with long legs and a mottled abdomen.
species.description: Washington. Builds a flat sheet web with a funnel retreat in sheds and crawl spaces. Males wander indoors in autumn looking for mates, which is when most are seen.
species.en_description: Washington. Builds a flat sheet web with a funnel retreat in sheds and crawl spaces. Males wander indoors in autumn looking for mates, which is when most are seen.

species.name: Koch's Wolf Spider
species.short_description: Medium grey-brown wolf spider with a pale central band on the carapace.
species.en_short_description: Medium grey-brown wolf spider with a pale central band on the carapace.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Hunts on the ground without a web. Females carry the egg sac attached to the spinnerets, then the spiderlings on the abdomen.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Hunts on the ground without a web. Females carry the egg sac attached to the spinnerets, then the spiderlings on the abdomen.

species.name: Wetland Giant Wolf Spider
species.short_description: Large brown wolf spider with a pale carapace stripe, in damp meadow and marsh.
species.en_short_description: Large brown wolf spider with a pale carapace stripe, in damp meadow and marsh.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. One of the largest wolf spiders here. Eyes reflect brightly in a headtorch beam, which is the easiest way to find it at night.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. One of the largest wolf spiders here. Eyes reflect brightly in a headtorch beam, which is the easiest way to find it at night.

species.name: Garrapata de patas negras
species.short_description: Very small dark-legged tick; the vector of Lyme disease.
species.en_short_description: Very small dark-legged tick; the vector of Lyme disease.
species.description: New York, in leaf litter and long grass. Nymphs are poppy-seed sized and responsible for most transmissions. Worth recording for public-health value; check clothing after fieldwork.
species.en_description: New York, in leaf litter and long grass. Nymphs are poppy-seed sized and responsible for most transmissions. Worth recording for public-health value; check clothing after fieldwork.

species.name: Bronze Jumping Spider
species.short_description: Slim bronze-brown jumping spider; males with white side stripes on the carapace.
species.en_short_description: Slim bronze-brown jumping spider; males with white side stripes on the carapace.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Hunts on foliage and low vegetation. Males have distinctly banded front legs used in courtship displays. Common but inconspicuous.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Hunts on foliage and low vegetation. Males have distinctly banded front legs used in courtship displays. Common but inconspicuous.

species.name: Garrapata americana de perro
species.short_description: Brown tick with ornate white-grey mottling on the shield.
species.en_short_description: Brown tick with ornate white-grey mottling on the shield.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Larger than the black-legged tick, with conspicuous pale marbling. Can transmit Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Found along trail edges.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Larger than the black-legged tick, with conspicuous pale marbling. Can transmit Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Found along trail edges.

species.name: Araña de tierra
species.short_description: Dark spider with a white abdominal marking shaped like a clerical collar.
species.en_short_description: Dark spider with a white abdominal marking shaped like a clerical collar.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Runs fast in erratic bursts. Nocturnal hunter with no web. Frequently found indoors; bites are uncommon and mild.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Runs fast in erratic bursts. Nocturnal hunter with no web. Frequently found indoors; bites are uncommon and mild.

species.name: Western Forest Scorpion
species.short_description: Dark brown to blackish forest scorpion with stout pincers.
species.en_short_description: Dark brown to blackish forest scorpion with stout pincers.
species.description: California and Washington. Unusual among scorpions in preferring cool damp forest, found under logs and bark. Sting is mild. Fluoresces strongly under UV light.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Unusual among scorpions in preferring cool damp forest, found under logs and bark. Sting is mild. Fluoresces strongly under UV light.

species.name: Syspira longipes
species.short_description: Long-legged pale running spider of arid scrub, active at night.
species.en_short_description: Long-legged pale running spider of arid scrub, active at night.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. A fast nocturnal ground hunter with notably long legs. Found under debris and in leaf litter of desert washes.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. A fast nocturnal ground hunter with notably long legs. Found under debris and in leaf litter of desert washes.

species.name: Araña manchada de monte
species.short_description: Mottled brown orbweaver with banded legs, in Mexican highlands.
species.en_short_description: Mottled brown orbweaver with banded legs, in Mexican highlands.
species.description: Mexico City region. Close relative of the Western Spotted Orbweaver and similarly builds large webs on walls and vegetation. Mainly nocturnal.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Close relative of the Western Spotted Orbweaver and similarly builds large webs on walls and vegetation. Mainly nocturnal.

species.name: Araña de panza espinosa
species.short_description: Small hard-bodied spider with a white spiny abdomen and black markings.
species.en_short_description: Small hard-bodied spider with a white spiny abdomen and black markings.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Builds a tight vertical orb across woodland trails at face height — often the spider you walk into. Abdomen is armoured with sharp spines.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Builds a tight vertical orb across woodland trails at face height — often the spider you walk into. Abdomen is armoured with sharp spines.

species.name: Six-spotted Orbweaver
species.short_description: Small pale green or cream orbweaver with a few dark abdominal spots.
species.en_short_description: Small pale green or cream orbweaver with a few dark abdominal spots.
species.description: Five regions. Builds small orbs in shrubs and conifer branches. The soft green colouring fades to cream in preserved specimens but is bright in life.
species.en_description: Five regions. Builds small orbs in shrubs and conifer branches. The soft green colouring fades to cream in preserved specimens but is bright in life.

species.name: Syspira tigrina
species.short_description: Slender striped running spider endemic to the Baja peninsula.
species.en_short_description: Slender striped running spider endemic to the Baja peninsula.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Nocturnal ground hunter with fine longitudinal striping. Found in desert arroyos under rocks and dead cactus. Rarely recorded, so sightings have value.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Nocturnal ground hunter with fine longitudinal striping. Found in desert arroyos under rocks and dead cactus. Rarely recorded, so sightings have value.

species.name: Apache Jumping Spider
species.short_description: Large jumping spider with a vivid orange-red abdomen and black carapace.
species.en_short_description: Large jumping spider with a vivid orange-red abdomen and black carapace.
species.description: Colorado. One of the most brightly coloured jumping spiders in the region, favouring open arid grassland and scrub. Stalks prey on the ground and on low plants.
species.en_description: Colorado. One of the most brightly coloured jumping spiders in the region, favouring open arid grassland and scrub. Stalks prey on the ground and on low plants.

species.name: Western Lynx Spider
species.short_description: Small straw-coloured lynx spider with spiny legs and a tapered abdomen.
species.en_short_description: Small straw-coloured lynx spider with spiny legs and a tapered abdomen.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Ambushes insects on flowers and foliage without a web. Much smaller and duller than the Green Lynx Spider.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Ambushes insects on flowers and foliage without a web. Much smaller and duller than the Green Lynx Spider.

species.name: Striped Fishing Spider
species.short_description: Large grey-brown fishing spider with pale stripes along the abdomen edges.
species.en_short_description: Large grey-brown fishing spider with pale stripes along the abdomen edges.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Sits at the water's edge with front legs on the surface, detecting vibrations. Can run across water and dive to escape. Harmless.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Sits at the water's edge with front legs on the surface, detecting vibrations. Can run across water and dive to escape. Harmless.

species.name: Ballena jorobada
species.short_description: Stocky baleen whale with very long white-edged flippers, a knobbly head and a bushy blow.
species.en_short_description: Stocky baleen whale with very long white-edged flippers, a knobbly head and a bushy blow.
species.description: The most-reported whale across California, Washington, New York Bight and Baja. Breaches and lob-tails freely, and raises broad flukes with individually unique white patterning before a deep dive. Feeds by lunging through bait balls, sometimes cooperatively.
species.en_description: The most-reported whale across California, Washington, New York Bight and Baja. Breaches and lob-tails freely, and raises broad flukes with individually unique white patterning before a deep dive. Feeds by lunging through bait balls, sometimes cooperatively.

species.name: Grey Whale
species.short_description: Mottled grey whale encrusted with barnacles, no dorsal fin, and a heart-shaped double blow.
species.en_short_description: Mottled grey whale encrusted with barnacles, no dorsal fin, and a heart-shaped double blow.
species.description: The signature Baja California Sur sighting: the Pacific population calves in the peninsula's lagoons between January and March, then passes California and Washington on migration. Knuckled ridge along the back replaces a dorsal fin.
species.en_description: The signature Baja California Sur sighting: the Pacific population calves in the peninsula's lagoons between January and March, then passes California and Washington on migration. Knuckled ridge along the back replaces a dorsal fin.

species.name: Orca
species.short_description: Black-and-white toothed whale with a white eye patch, grey saddle and very tall triangular dorsal fin.
species.en_short_description: Black-and-white toothed whale with a white eye patch, grey saddle and very tall triangular dorsal fin.
species.description: Resident and transient pods off Washington and California, with occasional Baja records. Males carry a dorsal fin up to two metres tall; females a shorter curved one. Travels in tight matrilineal groups that surface together.
species.en_description: Resident and transient pods off Washington and California, with occasional Baja records. Males carry a dorsal fin up to two metres tall; females a shorter curved one. Travels in tight matrilineal groups that surface together.

species.name: Common Bottlenose Dolphin
species.short_description: Robust grey dolphin with a short thick beak and a permanent upcurved mouthline.
species.en_short_description: Robust grey dolphin with a short thick beak and a permanent upcurved mouthline.
species.description: Coastal groups along California and throughout the Gulf of California. Bow-rides boats readily and often forages in the surf zone. Heavier-bodied and plainer than the Common Dolphin, without any flank hourglass pattern.
species.en_description: Coastal groups along California and throughout the Gulf of California. Bow-rides boats readily and often forages in the surf zone. Heavier-bodied and plainer than the Common Dolphin, without any flank hourglass pattern.

species.name: Delfín Mular de Tamanend
species.short_description: Western North Atlantic bottlenose, split from the common form; robust grey with a stubby beak.
species.en_short_description: Western North Atlantic bottlenose, split from the common form; robust grey with a stubby beak.
species.description: The bottlenose seen off Long Island and the New York coast, recognised as a separate species from the Pacific animals. Field-inseparable from Common Bottlenose in practice, so range is what identifies it here.
species.en_description: The bottlenose seen off Long Island and the New York coast, recognised as a separate species from the Pacific animals. Field-inseparable from Common Bottlenose in practice, so range is what identifies it here.

species.name: Delfín común
species.short_description: Slim dolphin with a bold tan-and-grey hourglass pattern along each flank.
species.en_short_description: Slim dolphin with a bold tan-and-grey hourglass pattern along each flank.
species.description: Travels in fast, noisy schools that can number many hundreds, especially off southern California and in the Gulf of California. The criss-cross flank pattern under the dorsal fin is unmistakable in good light.
species.en_description: Travels in fast, noisy schools that can number many hundreds, especially off southern California and in the Gulf of California. The criss-cross flank pattern under the dorsal fin is unmistakable in good light.

species.name: Harbour Porpoise
species.short_description: Small, shy, dark porpoise with a low triangular dorsal fin and no beak.
species.en_short_description: Small, shy, dark porpoise with a low triangular dorsal fin and no beak.
species.description: Puget Sound, the northern California coast and the New York Bight. Surfaces with an unobtrusive roll and rarely leaps, so it is easy to overlook. The blunt beakless head separates porpoises from all dolphins.
species.en_description: Puget Sound, the northern California coast and the New York Bight. Surfaces with an unobtrusive roll and rarely leaps, so it is easy to overlook. The blunt beakless head separates porpoises from all dolphins.

species.name: Delfín de Risso
species.short_description: Blunt-headed grey dolphin, heavily scarred to near-white with age, with a tall dorsal fin.
species.en_short_description: Blunt-headed grey dolphin, heavily scarred to near-white with age, with a tall dorsal fin.
species.description: Deep-water animal seen off California, Baja and occasionally New York canyons. Old adults look almost entirely pale from accumulated rake marks. The vertical crease down the melon and absence of a beak are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Deep-water animal seen off California, Baja and occasionally New York canyons. Old adults look almost entirely pale from accumulated rake marks. The vertical crease down the melon and absence of a beak are diagnostic.

species.name: Ballena azul
species.short_description: The largest animal that has ever lived; mottled blue-grey with a tiny dorsal fin far back.
species.en_short_description: The largest animal that has ever lived; mottled blue-grey with a tiny dorsal fin far back.
species.description: Summers off California and feeds in the Gulf of California in winter. The tall columnar blow can reach nine metres. The broad flat rostrum with a single central ridge separates it from a Fin Whale at close range.
species.en_description: Summers off California and feeds in the Gulf of California in winter. The tall columnar blow can reach nine metres. The broad flat rostrum with a single central ridge separates it from a Fin Whale at close range.

species.name: Delfín de costados blancos
species.short_description: Boldly marked dolphin with a two-tone hooked dorsal fin and pale grey flank suspenders.
species.en_short_description: Boldly marked dolphin with a two-tone hooked dorsal fin and pale grey flank suspenders.
species.description: Offshore Washington and California waters, often in large energetic schools that leap in unison. The strongly falcate, sharply bicoloured dorsal fin is the field mark that carries at distance.
species.en_description: Offshore Washington and California waters, often in large energetic schools that leap in unison. The strongly falcate, sharply bicoloured dorsal fin is the field mark that carries at distance.

species.name: Ballena menor
species.short_description: Small baleen whale with a pointed snout and, in the North Atlantic and Pacific, a white flipper band.
species.en_short_description: Small baleen whale with a pointed snout and, in the North Atlantic and Pacific, a white flipper band.
species.description: Regular but inconspicuous off Washington, California, Baja and New York. Surfaces snout-first, showing the dorsal fin almost immediately, and the blow is often invisible. Rarely raises flukes.
species.en_description: Regular but inconspicuous off Washington, California, Baja and New York. Surfaces snout-first, showing the dorsal fin almost immediately, and the blow is often invisible. Rarely raises flukes.

species.name: Ballena de aleta
species.short_description: Very large fast whale with asymmetrical jaw colouring — white on the right side only.
species.en_short_description: Very large fast whale with asymmetrical jaw colouring — white on the right side only.
species.description: Second-largest whale, seen off California, Baja, Washington and the New York canyons. The tall angled dorsal fin appears soon after the blow. The right-side-white lower jaw is unique among whales.
