species.en_description: Second-largest whale, seen off California, Baja, Washington and the New York canyons. The tall angled dorsal fin appears soon after the blow. The right-side-white lower jaw is unique among whales.

species.name: Ballena de esperma
species.short_description: Enormous square-headed whale with a wrinkled body, low hump and a blow angled forward-left.
species.en_short_description: Enormous square-headed whale with a wrinkled body, low hump and a blow angled forward-left.
species.description: Deep-water animal off California, Baja and the Atlantic canyons. The huge blunt box of a head is unmistakable. Logs motionless at the surface between very long, very deep squid-hunting dives.
species.en_description: Deep-water animal off California, Baja and the Atlantic canyons. The huge blunt box of a head is unmistakable. Logs motionless at the surface between very long, very deep squid-hunting dives.

species.name: Dall's Porpoise
species.short_description: Small, boldly black-and-white porpoise that throws a distinctive rooster-tail spray.
species.en_short_description: Small, boldly black-and-white porpoise that throws a distinctive rooster-tail spray.
species.description: The fastest small cetacean, common in Washington waters and off northern California. Never leaps clear, instead cutting the surface so hard it kicks up a V of spray. Sharply patterned unlike the drab Harbour Porpoise.
species.en_description: The fastest small cetacean, common in Washington waters and off northern California. Never leaps clear, instead cutting the surface so hard it kicks up a V of spray. Sharply patterned unlike the drab Harbour Porpoise.

species.name: Trucha arcoiris
species.short_description: Silvery trout with black spotting and a broad pink-red lateral stripe.
species.en_short_description: Silvery trout with black spotting and a broad pink-red lateral stripe.
species.description: Five regions. Native to the Pacific slope and stocked almost everywhere else. Sea-run fish are called steelhead. The rosy flank band and heavily spotted tail are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Five regions. Native to the Pacific slope and stocked almost everywhere else. Sea-run fish are called steelhead. The rosy flank band and heavily spotted tail are diagnostic.

species.name: Mojarra oreja azul
species.short_description: Deep-bodied sunfish with vertical bars, a dark ear flap and a small mouth.
species.en_short_description: Deep-bodied sunfish with vertical bars, a dark ear flap and a small mouth.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The dark blotch at the rear of the dorsal fin and the black opercular flap identify it. Nests in shallow colonial saucers.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The dark blotch at the rear of the dorsal fin and the black opercular flap identify it. Nests in shallow colonial saucers.

species.name: Lobina negra
species.short_description: Green bass with a dark lateral blotch band and a jaw extending past the eye.
species.en_short_description: Green bass with a dark lateral blotch band and a jaw extending past the eye.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced widely and a major predator in warm lakes. The jaw hinge reaching behind the eye separates it from the Smallmouth Bass.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced widely and a major predator in warm lakes. The jaw hinge reaching behind the eye separates it from the Smallmouth Bass.

species.name: Trucha de arroyo
species.short_description: Dark olive char with pale worm-like markings and red spots ringed in blue halos.
species.en_short_description: Dark olive char with pale worm-like markings and red spots ringed in blue halos.
species.description: Five regions. Native to the east and introduced in the west. The white leading edges on the lower fins and blue-haloed red spots are unmistakable.
species.en_description: Five regions. Native to the east and introduced in the west. The white leading edges on the lower fins and blue-haloed red spots are unmistakable.

species.name: Carpa común europea
species.short_description: Heavy-bodied bronze fish with large scales and two pairs of barbels.
species.en_short_description: Heavy-bodied bronze fish with large scales and two pairs of barbels.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and now abundant in warm turbid water. Roots in the bottom, clouding ponds. Spawning fish thrash noisily in the shallows in spring.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and now abundant in warm turbid water. Roots in the bottom, clouding ponds. Spawning fish thrash noisily in the shallows in spring.

species.name: Charrasco de Piscina de Marea
species.short_description: Small mottled sculpin with a large head, found in rocky intertidal pools.
species.en_short_description: Small mottled sculpin with a large head, found in rocky intertidal pools.
species.description: California and Washington. Changes colour to match its pool within days. Can find its way back to a home pool after displacement. The commonest fish in Pacific tidepools.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Changes colour to match its pool within days. Can find its way back to a home pool after displacement. The commonest fish in Pacific tidepools.

species.name: Trucha común
species.short_description: Golden-brown trout with black and rusty spots ringed in pale halos.
species.en_short_description: Golden-brown trout with black and rusty spots ringed in pale halos.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe. Squarer tail and halo-ringed spots separate it from Rainbow Trout. Wary and largely nocturnal when large.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe. Squarer tail and halo-ringed spots separate it from Rainbow Trout. Wary and largely nocturnal when large.

species.name: Tilapia del Nilo
species.short_description: Deep-bodied grey cichlid with vertical bars on the tail fin.
species.en_short_description: Deep-bodied grey cichlid with vertical bars on the tail fin.
species.description: Colorado and Mexico City. Introduced for aquaculture and now feral in warm water, including Mexican canals and reservoirs. Mouthbroods its young. Tolerates poor water quality.
species.en_description: Colorado and Mexico City. Introduced for aquaculture and now feral in warm water, including Mexican canals and reservoirs. Mouthbroods its young. Tolerates poor water quality.

species.name: charrasco lanudo
species.short_description: Small tidepool sculpin with a fringe of cirri on the head and mottled colouring.
species.en_short_description: Small tidepool sculpin with a fringe of cirri on the head and mottled colouring.
species.description: California rocky shores. Distinguished from the Tidepool Sculpin by the woolly fringe of small filaments on the head. Survives hours out of water in damp crevices.
species.en_description: California rocky shores. Distinguished from the Tidepool Sculpin by the woolly fringe of small filaments on the head. Survives hours out of water in damp crevices.

species.name: Pez erizo apache
species.short_description: Tan pufferfish covered in long erectile spines with dark blotches.
species.en_short_description: Tan pufferfish covered in long erectile spines with dark blotches.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Inflates into a spiny ball when threatened. Common in the Gulf of California over sand and reef. Crushes molluscs with fused beak-like teeth.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Inflates into a spiny ball when threatened. Common in the Gulf of California over sand and reef. Crushes molluscs with fused beak-like teeth.

species.name: perca sol
species.short_description: Brilliantly coloured sunfish with orange spotting and a red-tipped ear flap.
species.en_short_description: Brilliantly coloured sunfish with orange spotting and a red-tipped ear flap.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Wavy blue-green lines on the cheek and the crimson spot on the opercular flap separate it from the Bluegill. Feeds heavily on snails.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Wavy blue-green lines on the cheek and the crimson spot on the opercular flap separate it from the Bluegill. Feeds heavily on snails.

species.name: Lobina de boca pequeña
species.short_description: Bronze bass with dark vertical bars and a jaw ending below the eye.
species.en_short_description: Bronze bass with dark vertical bars and a jaw ending below the eye.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Prefers cooler, rockier, clearer water than the Largemouth. Bars rather than a lateral stripe, and red eyes.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Prefers cooler, rockier, clearer water than the Largemouth. Bars rather than a lateral stripe, and red eyes.

species.name: Guayacón mosquito
species.short_description: Tiny grey livebearer with an upturned mouth, at the water surface.
species.en_short_description: Tiny grey livebearer with an upturned mouth, at the water surface.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced worldwide for mosquito control, often to the detriment of native fish. Females are noticeably larger. Bears live young rather than laying eggs.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced worldwide for mosquito control, often to the detriment of native fish. Females are noticeably larger. Bears live young rather than laying eggs.

species.name: Rocky Mountain Cutthroat Trout
species.short_description: Trout with a crimson slash under the jaw and heavy spotting toward the tail.
species.en_short_description: Trout with a crimson slash under the jaw and heavy spotting toward the tail.
species.description: Colorado headwaters, where it is the native trout. The red-orange cutthroat mark on the lower jaw is diagnostic. Restricted to cold clean streams above introduced-trout barriers.
species.en_description: Colorado headwaters, where it is the native trout. The red-orange cutthroat mark on the lower jaw is diagnostic. Restricted to cold clean streams above introduced-trout barriers.

species.name: Petaca banderita
species.short_description: Small silvery damselfish with five bold dark bars and a yellow back.
species.en_short_description: Small silvery damselfish with five bold dark bars and a yellow back.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Abundant on rocky reefs and around piers in the Gulf of California. Males guard purple egg patches on rock and defend them aggressively.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Abundant on rocky reefs and around piers in the Gulf of California. Males guard purple egg patches on rock and defend them aggressively.

species.name: Botete aletas punteadas
species.short_description: Pufferfish either black with white spots or entirely bright yellow.
species.en_short_description: Pufferfish either black with white spots or entirely bright yellow.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Two dramatically different colour morphs occur in the same population. Grazes coral and algae with fused teeth. Highly toxic if eaten.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Two dramatically different colour morphs occur in the same population. Grazes coral and algae with fused teeth. Highly toxic if eaten.

species.name: Salmón chinook
species.short_description: Large salmon with black gums and small spots on both tail lobes.
species.en_short_description: Large salmon with black gums and small spots on both tail lobes.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. The largest Pacific salmon, also called king salmon. Black mouth interior is the key mark. Spawners turn dark olive to maroon.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. The largest Pacific salmon, also called king salmon. Black mouth interior is the key mark. Spawners turn dark olive to maroon.

species.name: Arcoiris de Cortés
species.short_description: Small wrasse with a yellow saddle and a violet head; changes colour with sex and age.
species.en_short_description: Small wrasse with a yellow saddle and a violet head; changes colour with sex and age.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Abundant in Gulf of California reef habitat. Individuals change sex and colour as they mature, so several distinct patterns occur together.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Abundant in Gulf of California reef habitat. Individuals change sex and colour as they mature, so several distinct patterns occur together.

species.name: Perca amarilla
species.short_description: Golden-yellow fish with six or seven dark vertical bars and orange lower fins.
species.en_short_description: Golden-yellow fish with six or seven dark vertical bars and orange lower fins.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Schools in weedy lake margins. The crisp dark saddles over a yellow ground and two separate dorsal fins are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Schools in weedy lake margins. The crisp dark saddles over a yellow ground and two separate dorsal fins are diagnostic.

species.name: Salmón Plateado
species.short_description: Salmon with white gums, a black tongue and spots on the upper tail lobe only.
species.en_short_description: Salmon with white gums, a black tongue and spots on the upper tail lobe only.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Also called silver salmon. Spawning males develop a hooked snout and brilliant red flanks. White gums separate it from Chinook.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Also called silver salmon. Spawning males develop a hooked snout and brilliant red flanks. White gums separate it from Chinook.

species.name: Cachorro de arroyo común
species.short_description: Slender olive minnow with a dark lateral band and a dark spot at the tail base.
species.en_short_description: Slender olive minnow with a dark lateral band and a dark spot at the tail base.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Common in small streams. Breeding males develop rosy fins and tubercles on the snout. Builds a gravel nest pit and ridge.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Common in small streams. Breeding males develop rosy fins and tubercles on the snout. Builds a gravel nest pit and ridge.

species.name: Cirujano barbero
species.short_description: Dark grey surgeonfish with a yellow tail and black caudal spine plates.
species.en_short_description: Dark grey surgeonfish with a yellow tail and black caudal spine plates.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Named for the scalpel-like spines at the tail base, used in defence. Grazes algae in schools over Gulf of California reefs.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Named for the scalpel-like spines at the tail base, used in defence. Grazes algae in schools over Gulf of California reefs.

species.name: Guatopote manchado
species.short_description: Small olive livebearer with a dark spot at the tail base and orange fins in males.
species.en_short_description: Small olive livebearer with a dark spot at the tail base and orange fins in males.
species.description: Mexico City region. A native Mexican poeciliid of springs, canals and slow streams. Bears live young. Males are smaller and more colourful than females.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. A native Mexican poeciliid of springs, canals and slow streams. Bears live young. Males are smaller and more colourful than females.

species.name: Perca Sol Goliat
species.short_description: Stocky sunfish with a large mouth, blue-green flecking and pale fin margins.
species.en_short_description: Stocky sunfish with a large mouth, blue-green flecking and pale fin margins.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. More elongate and larger-mouthed than a Bluegill. Tolerates warm, low-oxygen water where other sunfish fail.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. More elongate and larger-mouthed than a Bluegill. Tolerates warm, low-oxygen water where other sunfish fail.

species.name: Ángel real
species.short_description: Deep-bodied dark angelfish with a bold vertical white bar and orange tail.
species.en_short_description: Deep-bodied dark angelfish with a bold vertical white bar and orange tail.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A signature Gulf of California reef fish. Juveniles have additional pale bars. Grazes sponges and algae, often in pairs along rock walls.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A signature Gulf of California reef fish. Juveniles have additional pale bars. Grazes sponges and algae, often in pairs along rock walls.

species.name: Jaqueta garibaldi
species.short_description: Brilliant orange fish with a deep body; juveniles spangled with electric-blue spots.
species.en_short_description: Brilliant orange fish with a deep body; juveniles spangled with electric-blue spots.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur kelp forests. California's state marine fish and unmistakable. Males tend and defend algal nests. Juveniles look like a different species.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur kelp forests. California's state marine fish and unmistakable. Males tend and defend algal nests. Juveniles look like a different species.

species.name: Salmón Chum
species.short_description: Salmon with no distinct spots and, when spawning, purple-green vertical calico bars.
species.en_short_description: Salmon with no distinct spots and, when spawning, purple-green vertical calico bars.
species.description: Washington. Also called dog salmon for the large canine teeth of spawning males. The absence of clear black spotting separates it from other Pacific salmon.
species.en_description: Washington. Also called dog salmon for the large canine teeth of spawning males. The absence of clear black spotting separates it from other Pacific salmon.

species.name: Threespine Stickleback
species.short_description: Tiny armoured fish with three sharp dorsal spines and bony side plates.
species.en_short_description: Tiny armoured fish with three sharp dorsal spines and bony side plates.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. A classic subject of evolutionary study, with marine, brackish and freshwater forms. Breeding males build nests and turn red-throated.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. A classic subject of evolutionary study, with marine, brackish and freshwater forms. Breeding males build nests and turn red-throated.

species.name: Lacha tirana
species.short_description: Silvery deep-bodied herring with a dark shoulder spot and a strongly forked tail.
species.en_short_description: Silvery deep-bodied herring with a dark shoulder spot and a strongly forked tail.
species.description: New York coastal waters. Forms enormous dense schools that draw whales, ospreys and striped bass inshore. Filter-feeds on plankton. Ecologically pivotal.
species.en_description: New York coastal waters. Forms enormous dense schools that draw whales, ospreys and striped bass inshore. Filter-feeds on plankton. Ecologically pivotal.

species.name: chupapiedra norteña
species.short_description: Flattened tadpole-shaped fish with a suction disc formed from the pelvic fins.
species.en_short_description: Flattened tadpole-shaped fish with a suction disc formed from the pelvic fins.
species.description: California and Washington. Clings to the underside of intertidal boulders with remarkable force. Found by carefully turning rocks at low tide; replace them afterwards.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Clings to the underside of intertidal boulders with remarkable force. Found by carefully turning rocks at low tide; replace them afterwards.

species.name: Lobina rayada del Atlántico
species.short_description: Silvery streamlined fish with seven or eight crisp dark horizontal stripes.
species.en_short_description: Silvery streamlined fish with seven or eight crisp dark horizontal stripes.
species.description: California and New York. Native to the Atlantic and introduced to the Pacific. Anadromous, running up rivers to spawn. A major sport fish on both coasts.
species.en_description: California and New York. Native to the Atlantic and introduced to the Pacific. Anadromous, running up rivers to spawn. A major sport fish on both coasts.

species.name: Perca de roca
species.short_description: Bronze sunfish with rows of dark spots, red eyes and a large mouth.
species.en_short_description: Bronze sunfish with rows of dark spots, red eyes and a large mouth.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. The red eye and mottled rows of dark blotches are diagnostic. Prefers rocky stream pools and lake shorelines.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. The red eye and mottled rows of dark blotches are diagnostic. Prefers rocky stream pools and lake shorelines.

species.name: High Cockscomb
species.short_description: Eel-like intertidal fish with a fleshy crest along the top of the head.
species.en_short_description: Eel-like intertidal fish with a fleshy crest along the top of the head.
species.description: California and Washington. Found under rocks and in crevices at low tide, able to breathe air while stranded. Males develop an orange-tinged crest when breeding.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Found under rocks and in crevices at low tide, able to breathe air while stranded. Males develop an orange-tinged crest when breeding.

species.name: chopa verde
species.short_description: Dark olive fish with one or two white spots on the back and striking blue-green eyes.
species.en_short_description: Dark olive fish with one or two white spots on the back and striking blue-green eyes.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Grazes algae in kelp beds and surge channels. The vivid opalescent eye is the source of the name and is visible underwater.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Grazes algae in kelp beds and surge channels. The vivid opalescent eye is the source of the name and is visible underwater.

species.name: charrasco  de astas
species.short_description: Grey-brown estuarine sculpin with a branched antler-like spine on the gill cover.
species.en_short_description: Grey-brown estuarine sculpin with a branched antler-like spine on the gill cover.
species.description: California and Washington. Common on estuarine mudflats and sandy shallows. The forked preopercular spine is diagnostic and sharp. Buries in sand with only eyes showing.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Common on estuarine mudflats and sandy shallows. The forked preopercular spine is diagnostic and sharp. Buries in sand with only eyes showing.

species.name: Matalote blanco
species.short_description: Cylindrical bronze fish with a fleshy downward-facing sucker mouth.
species.en_short_description: Cylindrical bronze fish with a fleshy downward-facing sucker mouth.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Vacuums invertebrates from stream and lake bottoms. Migrates upstream in large numbers to spawn over gravel in spring, when it is easiest to see.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Vacuums invertebrates from stream and lake bottoms. Migrates upstream in large numbers to spawn over gravel in spring, when it is easiest to see.

species.name: Jaqueta gigante
species.short_description: Large dark damselfish; juveniles brilliant blue with electric spotting.
species.en_short_description: Large dark damselfish; juveniles brilliant blue with electric spotting.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Adults are sooty brown-black with a yellow tail; juveniles are vivid iridescent blue. Territorial on Gulf of California rocky reefs.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Adults are sooty brown-black with a yellow tail; juveniles are vivid iridescent blue. Territorial on Gulf of California rocky reefs.

species.name: mojarra brillosa
species.short_description: Small silvery perch with faint vertical bars and yellow-and-dark fin markings.
species.en_short_description: Small silvery perch with faint vertical bars and yellow-and-dark fin markings.
species.description: California and Washington. Bears live young, unusual among marine fishes. Abundant around piers, pilings and eelgrass. Often the first fish caught off a Puget Sound dock.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Bears live young, unusual among marine fishes. Abundant around piers, pilings and eelgrass. Often the first fish caught off a Puget Sound dock.

species.name: Cabrilla sargacera
species.short_description: Olive-brown bass with pale blotches on the back and a notched dorsal fin.
species.en_short_description: Olive-brown bass with pale blotches on the back and a notched dorsal fin.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Also called calico bass. Ambushes prey within kelp canopy. Slow-growing, so large individuals are decades old.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Also called calico bass. Ambushes prey within kelp canopy. Slow-growing, so large individuals are decades old.

species.name: vieja mexicana
species.short_description: Wrasse with two dark stripes; large males develop a bulging forehead and long fins.
species.en_short_description: Wrasse with two dark stripes; large males develop a bulging forehead and long fins.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Females and juveniles are yellowish with dark bands; dominant males are dramatically different, with a fleshy hump. Common on Gulf reefs.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Females and juveniles are yellowish with dark bands; dominant males are dramatically different, with a fleshy hump. Common on Gulf reefs.

species.name: molva
species.short_description: Large mottled predatory fish with a huge mouth and a long spineless body.
species.en_short_description: Large mottled predatory fish with a huge mouth and a long spineless body.
species.description: California and Washington. Not a cod at all but a greenling. Flesh is sometimes blue-green. Males guard egg masses on rock through winter. A prized sport fish.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Not a cod at all but a greenling. Flesh is sometimes blue-green. Males guard egg masses on rock through winter. A prized sport fish.

species.name: sapo de aleta lucia
species.short_description: Dark elongate fish with rows of light-producing photophores along the belly.
species.en_short_description: Dark elongate fish with rows of light-producing photophores along the belly.
species.description: California and Washington. Males hum loudly from nests under intertidal rocks in summer to attract females — audible from shore. Photophores glow faintly in the dark.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Males hum loudly from nests under intertidal rocks in summer to attract females — audible from shore. Photophores glow faintly in the dark.

species.name: Corneta pintada
species.short_description: Extremely elongate fish with a long tubular snout and a whip-like tail filament.
species.en_short_description: Extremely elongate fish with a long tubular snout and a whip-like tail filament.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Hovers motionless over reef and sand, then sucks in prey through the tube snout. Often mistaken for a floating stick.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Hovers motionless over reef and sand, then sucks in prey through the tube snout. Often mistaken for a floating stick.

species.name: Mojarra negra
species.short_description: Deep silvery fish with irregular dark speckling and a large dorsal fin.
species.en_short_description: Deep silvery fish with irregular dark speckling and a large dorsal fin.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Speckles are scattered rather than in vertical bars, which separates it from the White Crappie. Schools around submerged timber.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Speckles are scattered rather than in vertical bars, which separates it from the White Crappie. Schools around submerged timber.

species.name: Eastern Blacknose Dace
species.short_description: Small streamlined minnow with a dark lateral band from snout to tail.
species.en_short_description: Small streamlined minnow with a dark lateral band from snout to tail.
species.description: New York. Abundant in cool rocky streams and headwaters. Breeding males develop rusty-orange fins and lateral band. Often the most numerous fish in a small brook.
species.en_description: New York. Abundant in cool rocky streams and headwaters. Breeding males develop rusty-orange fins and lateral band. Often the most numerous fish in a small brook.

species.name: cabezón
species.short_description: Very large sculpin with a broad head, fleshy nose flap and no scales.
species.en_short_description: Very large sculpin with a broad head, fleshy nose flap and no scales.
species.description: California and Washington. The biggest sculpin on the Pacific coast. Colouring ranges from green to red. Roe is toxic to humans. Males guard egg masses in rocky nests.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The biggest sculpin on the Pacific coast. Colouring ranges from green to red. Roe is toxic to humans. Males guard egg masses in rocky nests.

species.name: Pacific Sand Lance
species.short_description: Very slender silvery fish with a pointed snout that burrows into sand.
species.en_short_description: Very slender silvery fish with a pointed snout that burrows into sand.
species.description: Washington. Dives headfirst into sand to escape predators and to rest. Forms dense schools that are a critical forage fish for salmon, seabirds and marine mammals.
species.en_description: Washington. Dives headfirst into sand to escape predators and to rest. Forms dense schools that are a critical forage fish for salmon, seabirds and marine mammals.

species.name: Anguila americana
species.short_description: Long snake-like fish with a continuous fin along the back and tail.
species.en_short_description: Long snake-like fish with a continuous fin along the back and tail.
species.description: New York. Spawns in the Sargasso Sea and migrates as transparent glass eels into fresh water, where it may live decades. Nocturnal and often found under cover by day.
species.en_description: New York. Spawns in the Sargasso Sea and migrates as transparent glass eels into fresh water, where it may live decades. Nocturnal and often found under cover by day.

species.name: cochi
species.short_description: Grey diamond-shaped fish with a locking dorsal spine and small tough scales.
species.en_short_description: Grey diamond-shaped fish with a locking dorsal spine and small tough scales.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Locks itself into crevices with the trigger spine so it cannot be pulled out. Crushes urchins and molluscs with strong jaws. Common over Gulf reefs.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Locks itself into crevices with the trigger spine so it cannot be pulled out. Crushes urchins and molluscs with strong jaws. Common over Gulf reefs.

species.name: Borracho mono
species.short_description: Small dark blenny with a blunt head, fringed crest and prominent canine teeth.
species.en_short_description: Small dark blenny with a blunt head, fringed crest and prominent canine teeth.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Perches on rock in the surge zone, darting between holes. Territorial and pugnacious for its size. Grazes algae from wave-washed rock.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Perches on rock in the surge zone, darting between holes. Territorial and pugnacious for its size. Grazes algae from wave-washed rock.

species.name: timboco
species.short_description: Small tree hung with clusters of bright yellow trumpet flowers.
species.en_short_description: Small tree hung with clusters of bright yellow trumpet flowers.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Flowers in the rainy season and again through autumn, followed by long slender bean-like pods. Widely planted in streets and gardens.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Flowers in the rainy season and again through autumn, followed by long slender bean-like pods. Widely planted in streets and gardens.

species.name: Álamo temblón
species.short_description: Slender tree with smooth chalk-white bark and round leaves that tremble in any breeze.
species.en_short_description: Slender tree with smooth chalk-white bark and round leaves that tremble in any breeze.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Spreads by root suckers, so a whole grove is often one organism. Turns brilliant gold in autumn — the signature Colorado display.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Spreads by root suckers, so a whole grove is often one organism. Turns brilliant gold in autumn — the signature Colorado display.

species.name: ayarín
species.short_description: Tall conifer with soft flat needles and cones bearing three-pointed papery bracts.
species.en_short_description: Tall conifer with soft flat needles and cones bearing three-pointed papery bracts.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Not a true fir; the protruding mouse-tail bracts between cone scales are unique and settle the identification instantly.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Not a true fir; the protruding mouse-tail bracts between cone scales are unique and settle the identification instantly.

species.name: Negundo
species.short_description: Maple with compound leaves of three to five leaflets, unlike any other maple.
species.en_short_description: Maple with compound leaves of three to five leaflets, unlike any other maple.
species.description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Fast-growing and often multi-trunked along streams and in vacant lots. Paired winged samaras confirm it is a maple.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Fast-growing and often multi-trunked along streams and in vacant lots. Paired winged samaras confirm it is a maple.

species.name: Palma blanca
species.short_description: Very tall slender palm with a fan-shaped crown and a skirt of dead fronds.
species.en_short_description: Very tall slender palm with a fan-shaped crown and a skirt of dead fronds.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja California Sur. Native to Baja and planted worldwide. Taller and much thinner-trunked than the California Fan Palm.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja California Sur. Native to Baja and planted worldwide. Taller and much thinner-trunked than the California Fan Palm.

species.name: Tuya gigante
species.short_description: Large conifer with fragrant scale-like foliage in flat sprays and fibrous reddish bark.
species.en_short_description: Large conifer with fragrant scale-like foliage in flat sprays and fibrous reddish bark.
species.description: Washington. A defining tree of Pacific Northwest rainforest. Foliage sprays droop gracefully. Rot-resistant wood central to Northwest Coast cultures.
species.en_description: Washington. A defining tree of Pacific Northwest rainforest. Foliage sprays droop gracefully. Rot-resistant wood central to Northwest Coast cultures.

species.name: pino blanco americano
species.short_description: Tall pine with soft blue-green needles in bundles of five and long slender cones.
species.en_short_description: Tall pine with soft blue-green needles in bundles of five and long slender cones.
species.description: New York. The only five-needled pine in the north-east, which makes counting a bundle conclusive. Historically the mast timber of colonial navies.
species.en_description: New York. The only five-needled pine in the north-east, which makes counting a bundle conclusive. Historically the mast timber of colonial navies.

species.name: Encino verde
species.short_description: Evergreen oak with small cupped holly-like leaves and a broad spreading crown.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen oak with small cupped holly-like leaves and a broad spreading crown.
species.description: California. The characteristic oak of coastal hills and valleys. Leaves are convex with spiny margins. Supports an exceptional diversity of insects and birds.
species.en_description: California. The characteristic oak of coastal hills and valleys. Leaves are convex with spiny margins. Supports an exceptional diversity of insects and birds.

species.name: Oyamel neovolcánico
species.short_description: Tall dark fir with glossy needles, forming the forests where Monarchs overwinter.
species.en_short_description: Tall dark fir with glossy needles, forming the forests where Monarchs overwinter.
species.description: Mexico City region. Called oyamel, it forms the high-elevation forest belt around the Valley of Mexico and shelters overwintering Monarch butterflies.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Called oyamel, it forms the high-elevation forest belt around the Valley of Mexico and shelters overwintering Monarch butterflies.

species.name: pino real
species.short_description: Large pine with long needles in threes and jigsaw-puzzle orange bark plates.
species.en_short_description: Large pine with long needles in threes and jigsaw-puzzle orange bark plates.
species.description: Colorado. Bark smells distinctly of vanilla or butterscotch in warm sun. Open park-like stands on the Front Range are its classic habitat.
species.en_description: Colorado. Bark smells distinctly of vanilla or butterscotch in warm sun. Open park-like stands on the Front Range are its classic habitat.

species.name: arce de hoja grande
species.short_description: Maple with enormous deeply lobed leaves, often draped in moss.
species.en_short_description: Maple with enormous deeply lobed leaves, often draped in moss.
species.description: California and Washington. Leaves can exceed 30 cm across, the largest of any maple. Trunks in Northwest rainforest carry thick moss and licorice fern gardens.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Leaves can exceed 30 cm across, the largest of any maple. Trunks in Northwest rainforest carry thick moss and licorice fern gardens.

species.name: Haya americana
species.short_description: Smooth grey-barked tree with elliptical toothed leaves and spiny husked nuts.
species.en_short_description: Smooth grey-barked tree with elliptical toothed leaves and spiny husked nuts.
species.description: New York. The pale silvery bark is unmistakable and unfortunately attracts carving. Leaves often persist bleached and papery through winter on young trees.
species.en_description: New York. The pale silvery bark is unmistakable and unfortunately attracts carving. Leaves often persist bleached and papery through winter on young trees.

species.name: Tulípero de Virginia
species.short_description: Very tall straight tree with distinctive squared four-lobed leaves and tulip-like flowers.
species.en_short_description: Very tall straight tree with distinctive squared four-lobed leaves and tulip-like flowers.
species.description: New York. The oddly notched leaf shape is unlike any other tree. Greenish-orange tulip flowers appear high in the crown in late spring. Grows exceptionally tall.
species.en_description: New York. The oddly notched leaf shape is unlike any other tree. Greenish-orange tulip flowers appear high in the crown in late spring. Grows exceptionally tall.

species.name: sassafras
species.short_description: Small tree bearing leaves of three shapes — entire, mitten-shaped and three-lobed.
species.en_short_description: Small tree bearing leaves of three shapes — entire, mitten-shaped and three-lobed.
species.description: New York. Crushed leaves and twigs are strongly aromatic. The mix of leaf shapes on one branch is diagnostic. Brilliant orange and red autumn colour.
species.en_description: New York. Crushed leaves and twigs are strongly aromatic. The mix of leaf shapes on one branch is diagnostic. Brilliant orange and red autumn colour.

species.name: fresno mexicano
species.short_description: Large fast-growing ash with compound leaves and a broad dense crown.
species.en_short_description: Large fast-growing ash with compound leaves and a broad dense crown.
species.description: California and Mexico City. Also called evergreen ash and planted heavily as a street tree in Mexico City, where it is now among the commonest urban trees.
species.en_description: California and Mexico City. Also called evergreen ash and planted heavily as a street tree in Mexico City, where it is now among the commonest urban trees.

species.name: Ahuejote
species.short_description: Streamside willow with narrow leaves, pale beneath, and reddish young twigs.
species.en_short_description: Streamside willow with narrow leaves, pale beneath, and reddish young twigs.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Called ahuejote, it was planted in rows to stabilise the chinampa canals of Xochimilco and still lines them.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Called ahuejote, it was planted in rows to stabilise the chinampa canals of Xochimilco and still lines them.

species.name: Amate amarillo
species.short_description: Fig with pale yellowish bark that grips bare rock with sprawling roots.
species.en_short_description: Fig with pale yellowish bark that grips bare rock with sprawling roots.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Called amate, it grows directly from cliff faces and boulders in arroyos, its roots splitting the rock. Heart-shaped leaves with red veins.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Called amate, it grows directly from cliff faces and boulders in arroyos, its roots splitting the rock. Heart-shaped leaves with red veins.

species.name: secuoya roja
species.short_description: The tallest tree on earth: fibrous red bark, flat needles, a massive columnar trunk.
species.en_short_description: The tallest tree on earth: fibrous red bark, flat needles, a massive columnar trunk.
species.description: California. Restricted to the coastal fog belt, which supplies much of its water directly through the canopy. Resprouts from the base after fire and cutting.
species.en_description: California. Restricted to the coastal fog belt, which supplies much of its water directly through the canopy. Resprouts from the base after fire and cutting.

species.name: Abeto Oriental
species.short_description: Conifer with short flat needles in two ranks and tiny cones at branch tips.
species.en_short_description: Conifer with short flat needles in two ranks and tiny cones at branch tips.
species.description: New York. Casts deep shade in ravines and along streams. Needles have two pale lines beneath. Threatened by the hemlock woolly adelgid across its range.
species.en_description: New York. Casts deep shade in ravines and along streams. Needles have two pale lines beneath. Threatened by the hemlock woolly adelgid across its range.

species.name: enebro
species.short_description: Low spreading conifer with sharp awl-shaped needles in whorls of three.
species.en_short_description: Low spreading conifer with sharp awl-shaped needles in whorls of three.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Usually a sprawling shrub rather than a tree. Berry-like cones ripen blue-black over two years and flavour gin.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Usually a sprawling shrub rather than a tree. Berry-like cones ripen blue-black over two years and flavour gin.

species.name: Laurel de California
species.short_description: Evergreen tree with narrow leathery leaves that are intensely aromatic when crushed.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen tree with narrow leathery leaves that are intensely aromatic when crushed.
species.description: California. The scent is far stronger and more camphor-like than culinary bay. Grows in canyons and mixed woodland. Hosts the pathogen behind sudden oak death.
species.en_description: California. The scent is far stronger and more camphor-like than culinary bay. Grows in canyons and mixed woodland. Hosts the pathogen behind sudden oak death.

species.name: arce rojo
species.short_description: Maple with three-lobed leaves, red leaf stalks and brilliant scarlet autumn colour.
species.en_short_description: Maple with three-lobed leaves, red leaf stalks and brilliant scarlet autumn colour.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Native in the east and widely planted elsewhere. Flowers red and very early, before the leaves emerge.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Native in the east and widely planted elsewhere. Flowers red and very early, before the leaves emerge.

species.name: Arce de Noruega
species.short_description: Maple with broad five-lobed leaves and samaras spreading in a nearly straight line.
species.en_short_description: Maple with broad five-lobed leaves and samaras spreading in a nearly straight line.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and invasive in the north-east. Broken leaf stalks exude milky sap, which separates it from native maples.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and invasive in the north-east. Broken leaf stalks exude milky sap, which separates it from native maples.

species.name: arce enredadera
species.short_description: Sprawling multi-stemmed maple with nearly circular many-lobed leaves.
species.en_short_description: Sprawling multi-stemmed maple with nearly circular many-lobed leaves.
species.description: Washington. Forms leaning thickets in the understorey of Northwest conifer forest. Turns vivid scarlet and orange in shaded autumn woods.
species.en_description: Washington. Forms leaning thickets in the understorey of Northwest conifer forest. Turns vivid scarlet and orange in shaded autumn woods.

species.name: western hemlock
species.short_description: Conifer with a drooping leader shoot and needles of unequal lengths.
species.en_short_description: Conifer with a drooping leader shoot and needles of unequal lengths.
species.description: Washington. The nodding topmost shoot is visible from a distance and identifies it. Extremely shade-tolerant, so it dominates late-successional Northwest forest.
species.en_description: Washington. The nodding topmost shoot is visible from a distance and identifies it. Extremely shade-tolerant, so it dominates late-successional Northwest forest.

species.name: Chopo americano
species.short_description: Large fast-growing tree with triangular toothed leaves and deeply furrowed grey bark.
species.en_short_description: Large fast-growing tree with triangular toothed leaves and deeply furrowed grey bark.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Releases cottony seed masses in early summer that drift in visible clouds. Leaves rustle loudly in wind.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Releases cottony seed masses in early summer that drift in visible clouds. Leaves rustle loudly in wind.

species.name: enebro de Virginia
species.short_description: Dense conical juniper with scale-like foliage and powder-blue berry cones.
species.en_short_description: Dense conical juniper with scale-like foliage and powder-blue berry cones.
species.description: Colorado, California and New York. A juniper rather than a cedar. Colonises abandoned pasture aggressively. Aromatic heartwood used for chests and pencils.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and New York. A juniper rather than a cedar. Colonises abandoned pasture aggressively. Aromatic heartwood used for chests and pencils.

species.name: enebro de las Rocallosas
species.short_description: Juniper with fine grey-green scale foliage and shredding fibrous bark.
species.en_short_description: Juniper with fine grey-green scale foliage and shredding fibrous bark.
species.description: Colorado. Forms open woodland with pinyon on dry foothill slopes. Often gnarled and picturesque on exposed rimrock. Blue berry cones feed wintering birds.
species.en_description: Colorado. Forms open woodland with pinyon on dry foothill slopes. Often gnarled and picturesque on exposed rimrock. Blue berry cones feed wintering birds.

species.name: Encino
species.short_description: Thicket-forming oak with deeply lobed leaves, rarely more than a large shrub.
species.en_short_description: Thicket-forming oak with deeply lobed leaves, rarely more than a large shrub.
species.description: Colorado. Forms dense clonal stands called oak brush across the foothills. Acorns are a key food for bears in late summer. Turns russet and gold in autumn.
species.en_description: Colorado. Forms dense clonal stands called oak brush across the foothills. Acorns are a key food for bears in late summer. Turns russet and gold in autumn.

species.name: Encino quiebra hacha
species.short_description: Evergreen oak with thick leathery leaves showing a raised net of veins beneath.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen oak with thick leathery leaves showing a raised net of veins beneath.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja California Sur. The prominent reticulate venation on the underside gives the name. Common in highland pine-oak forest.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja California Sur. The prominent reticulate venation on the underside gives the name. Common in highland pine-oak forest.

species.name: pino de San Pedro Mártir
species.short_description: Slender straight pine with needles in pairs and small prickly cones.
species.en_short_description: Slender straight pine with needles in pairs and small prickly cones.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Grows in dense even-aged stands after fire; cones need heat to open. Long straight trunks were used for lodge poles.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Grows in dense even-aged stands after fire; cones need heat to open. Long straight trunks were used for lodge poles.

species.name: Pino ayacahuite
species.short_description: Tall pine with soft drooping needles in fives and very long pendulous cones.
species.en_short_description: Tall pine with soft drooping needles in fives and very long pendulous cones.
species.description: Mexico City region. Cones can exceed 30 cm and hang conspicuously. Grows in the humid highland forests around the Valley of Mexico.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Cones can exceed 30 cm and hang conspicuously. Grows in the humid highland forests around the Valley of Mexico.

species.name: Morera asiática
species.short_description: Small tree with variably lobed glossy leaves and sweet white to purple fruit.
species.en_short_description: Small tree with variably lobed glossy leaves and sweet white to purple fruit.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced from Asia for silkworm culture and now naturalised. Leaf shape varies wildly on the same tree. Fruit stains pavements heavily.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced from Asia for silkworm culture and now naturalised. Leaf shape varies wildly on the same tree. Fruit stains pavements heavily.

species.name: Arce de Pennsylvania
species.short_description: Understorey maple with green bark striped vertically in white.
species.en_short_description: Understorey maple with green bark striped vertically in white.
species.description: New York. The green-and-white striped bark is unique among north-eastern trees. Large three-lobed leaves, sometimes called goosefoot maple for their shape.
species.en_description: New York. The green-and-white striped bark is unique among north-eastern trees. Large three-lobed leaves, sometimes called goosefoot maple for their shape.

species.name: Encino del valle
species.short_description: Massive deciduous oak with deeply lobed leaves and a broad drooping crown.
species.en_short_description: Massive deciduous oak with deeply lobed leaves and a broad drooping crown.
species.description: California. The largest North American oak, endemic to California's valleys. Ancient specimens are landmark trees. Long pointed acorns.
species.en_description: California. The largest North American oak, endemic to California's valleys. Ancient specimens are landmark trees. Long pointed acorns.

species.name: California black oak
species.short_description: Deciduous oak with large deeply lobed leaves tipped with bristles.
species.en_short_description: Deciduous oak with large deeply lobed leaves tipped with bristles.
species.description: California. Bristle-tipped lobes place it in the red oak group. Leaves flush pink in spring and turn yellow-brown in autumn. Acorns were a staple food for many peoples.
species.en_description: California. Bristle-tipped lobes place it in the red oak group. Leaves flush pink in spring and turn yellow-brown in autumn. Acorns were a staple food for many peoples.

species.name: cedro blanco
species.short_description: Tall conifer with fine drooping scale foliage and small round woody cones.
species.en_short_description: Tall conifer with fine drooping scale foliage and small round woody cones.
species.description: Mexico City region. Widely planted for windbreaks and in churchyards across the highlands. Foliage hangs in soft pendulous sprays.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Widely planted for windbreaks and in churchyards across the highlands. Foliage hangs in soft pendulous sprays.

species.name: Encino blanco
species.short_description: Oak with rounded lobed leaves and pale ashy flaky bark.
species.en_short_description: Oak with rounded lobed leaves and pale ashy flaky bark.
species.description: New York. Rounded rather than bristle-tipped lobes place it in the white oak group. Acorns are sweet and mature in a single season. Long-lived and broad-crowned.
species.en_description: New York. Rounded rather than bristle-tipped lobes place it in the white oak group. Acorns are sweet and mature in a single season. Long-lived and broad-crowned.

species.name: Rocky Mountain maple
species.short_description: Small shrubby maple with three-lobed leaves and reddish twigs.
species.en_short_description: Small shrubby maple with three-lobed leaves and reddish twigs.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Grows as a multi-stemmed shrub or small tree along mountain streams and in rocky draws. Bright yellow to orange autumn colour.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Grows as a multi-stemmed shrub or small tree along mountain streams and in rocky draws. Bright yellow to orange autumn colour.

species.name: aliso
species.short_description: Large tree with mottled peeling white-and-tan bark and huge palmate leaves.
species.en_short_description: Large tree with mottled peeling white-and-tan bark and huge palmate leaves.
species.description: California. Follows watercourses through otherwise dry country, so a line of sycamores marks a creek. Crooked leaning trunks and ball-shaped seed heads.
species.en_description: California. Follows watercourses through otherwise dry country, so a line of sycamores marks a creek. Crooked leaning trunks and ball-shaped seed heads.

species.name: Palma de Taco
species.short_description: Stout fan palm with blue-green fronds, native to Baja arroyos.
species.en_short_description: Stout fan palm with blue-green fronds, native to Baja arroyos.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Grows wild in canyon oases of the cape region, forming palm groves around springs. Shorter and thicker-trunked than the fan palms.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Grows wild in canyon oases of the cape region, forming palm groves around springs. Shorter and thicker-trunked than the fan palms.

species.name: encino
species.short_description: Evergreen oak with variable leaves, golden fuzz beneath when young.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen oak with variable leaves, golden fuzz beneath when young.
species.description: California. Also called maul oak for its extremely hard wood. Leaves range from spiny to entire on the same tree. Thick acorn cups covered in golden scurf.
species.en_description: California. Also called maul oak for its extremely hard wood. Leaves range from spiny to entire on the same tree. Thick acorn cups covered in golden scurf.

species.name: Aliso rojo
species.short_description: Fast-growing tree with grey bark, toothed leaves with rolled margins and small woody cones.
species.en_short_description: Fast-growing tree with grey bark, toothed leaves with rolled margins and small woody cones.
species.description: Washington. Colonises disturbed ground and fixes nitrogen, enriching the soil. Wood turns bright orange when cut. Dominant along Northwest streams and clearcuts.
species.en_description: Washington. Colonises disturbed ground and fixes nitrogen, enriching the soil. Wood turns bright orange when cut. Dominant along Northwest streams and clearcuts.

species.name: Pino dulce
species.short_description: Small bushy pine with short needles in pairs and large edible seeds.
species.en_short_description: Small bushy pine with short needles in pairs and large edible seeds.
species.description: Colorado and California. Forms pinyon-juniper woodland across the Colorado Plateau. Pine nuts are a significant food for people, jays and bears in mast years.
species.en_description: Colorado and California. Forms pinyon-juniper woodland across the Colorado Plateau. Pine nuts are a significant food for people, jays and bears in mast years.

species.name: Abeto alpino
species.short_description: Narrow spire-shaped fir with dense blue-green needles, near treeline.
species.en_short_description: Narrow spire-shaped fir with dense blue-green needles, near treeline.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. The extremely narrow crown sheds heavy snow. Upright purple cones sit at the very top. Forms krummholz mats at the highest elevations.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. The extremely narrow crown sheds heavy snow. Upright purple cones sit at the very top. Forms krummholz mats at the highest elevations.

species.name: Palma datilera
species.short_description: Tall feather-leaved palm with a rough patterned trunk and hanging fruit clusters.
species.en_short_description: Tall feather-leaved palm with a rough patterned trunk and hanging fruit clusters.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Introduced from the Old World and naturalised at desert oases and springs. Pinnate rather than fan-shaped fronds.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Introduced from the Old World and naturalised at desert oases and springs. Pinnate rather than fan-shaped fronds.

species.name: encino roble
species.short_description: Evergreen oak of Baja peninsular highlands with thick warty-veined leaves.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen oak of Baja peninsular highlands with thick warty-veined leaves.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular oak of the Sierra de la Laguna and similar ranges. Leathery leaves with a rough tuberculate surface. Locally called encino roble.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular oak of the Sierra de la Laguna and similar ranges. Leathery leaves with a rough tuberculate surface. Locally called encino roble.

species.name: Encino arroyero
species.short_description: Oak endemic to the Baja cape region, growing along seasonal watercourses.
species.en_short_description: Oak endemic to the Baja cape region, growing along seasonal watercourses.
species.description: Baja California Sur only, in arroyos of the cape region. Narrow leathery leaves. A restricted endemic of conservation concern, so records are valuable.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur only, in arroyos of the cape region. Narrow leathery leaves. A restricted endemic of conservation concern, so records are valuable.

species.name: Tanoak
species.short_description: Evergreen tree with thick toothed leaves and acorns in bristly cups.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen tree with thick toothed leaves and acorns in bristly cups.
species.description: California. Neither a true oak nor a beech but intermediate, with upright catkin spikes. Heavily affected by sudden oak death. Bark was once used for tanning leather.
species.en_description: California. Neither a true oak nor a beech but intermediate, with upright catkin spikes. Heavily affected by sudden oak death. Bark was once used for tanning leather.

species.name: Nogal americano
species.short_description: Large tree with long compound leaves and round green husked nuts.
species.en_short_description: Large tree with long compound leaves and round green husked nuts.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Roots release juglone, which suppresses many nearby plants. Husks stain hands black. Highly prized dark timber.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Roots release juglone, which suppresses many nearby plants. Husks stain hands black. Highly prized dark timber.

species.name: Milenrama eurasiática
species.short_description: Flat-topped clusters of small white flowers over finely divided feathery leaves.
species.en_short_description: Flat-topped clusters of small white flowers over finely divided feathery leaves.
species.description: Five regions. The most-observed wildflower here, in meadows, roadsides and lawns from sea level to alpine. Foliage is strongly aromatic when crushed. Long used medicinally.
species.en_description: Five regions. The most-observed wildflower here, in meadows, roadsides and lawns from sea level to alpine. Foliage is strongly aromatic when crushed. Long used medicinally.

species.name: Gordolobo común
species.short_description: Tall unbranched spike of yellow flowers rising from a rosette of woolly grey leaves.
species.en_short_description: Tall unbranched spike of yellow flowers rising from a rosette of woolly grey leaves.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe. First-year rosettes are thick and felted; the flowering stalk can exceed two metres.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe. First-year rosettes are thick and felted; the flowering stalk can exceed two metres.

species.name: adelfilla de hoja estrecha
species.short_description: Tall spike of magenta-pink four-petalled flowers opening from the bottom up.
species.en_short_description: Tall spike of magenta-pink four-petalled flowers opening from the bottom up.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Colonises burns and clearings en masse, hence the name. Seeds drift on silky white plumes in late summer.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Colonises burns and clearings en masse, hence the name. Seeds drift on silky white plumes in late summer.

species.name: Amapola de California
species.short_description: Silky orange four-petalled cup over finely dissected blue-green foliage.
species.en_short_description: Silky orange four-petalled cup over finely dissected blue-green foliage.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. California's state flower, carpeting hillsides orange in spring. Petals close on cold or overcast days and at night.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. California's state flower, carpeting hillsides orange in spring. Petals close on cold or overcast days and at night.

species.name: aguja del pastor
species.short_description: Small pink five-petalled flowers and long beaked fruit that coils when dry.
species.en_short_description: Small pink five-petalled flowers and long beaked fruit that coils when dry.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and abundant on disturbed ground. The corkscrew seed tail drills the seed into soil as humidity changes. Ferny leaves in flat rosettes.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and abundant on disturbed ground. The corkscrew seed tail drills the seed into soil as humidity changes. Ferny leaves in flat rosettes.

species.name: Trillium del Pacífico
species.short_description: Single white three-petalled flower above a whorl of three broad leaves.
species.en_short_description: Single white three-petalled flower above a whorl of three broad leaves.
species.description: California and Washington. Flowers fade to pink or purple with age. Slow-growing — picking the flower can kill the plant, since it takes the leaves too.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Flowers fade to pink or purple with age. Slow-growing — picking the flower can kill the plant, since it takes the leaves too.

species.name: Algodoncillo llamativo
species.short_description: Domed clusters of pink star-shaped flowers on stout stems with milky sap.
species.en_short_description: Domed clusters of pink star-shaped flowers on stout stems with milky sap.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. A primary Monarch host plant in the West. Velvety grey-green leaves. Seed pods split to release silk-borne seeds.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. A primary Monarch host plant in the West. Velvety grey-green leaves. Seed pods split to release silk-borne seeds.

species.name: diente de león
species.short_description: Solitary yellow composite head on a hollow stalk over a toothed basal rosette.
species.en_short_description: Solitary yellow composite head on a hollow stalk over a toothed basal rosette.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and universal in lawns and verges. Every part exudes milky latex. The spherical seed head of parachuted achenes is unmistakable.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and universal in lawns and verges. Every part exudes milky latex. The spherical seed head of parachuted achenes is unmistakable.

species.name: blue columbine
species.short_description: Nodding flower with long blue-violet spurs and a white central cup.
species.en_short_description: Nodding flower with long blue-violet spurs and a white central cup.
species.description: Colorado, where it is the state flower. Grows in mountain meadows and aspen glades. The long nectar spurs are reached by hawkmoths and hummingbirds.
species.en_description: Colorado, where it is the state flower. Grows in mountain meadows and aspen glades. The long nectar spurs are reached by hawkmoths and hummingbirds.

species.name: Raíz de víbora blanca
species.short_description: Loose clusters of fuzzy white flower heads over toothed heart-shaped leaves.
species.en_short_description: Loose clusters of fuzzy white flower heads over toothed heart-shaped leaves.
species.description: New York. Blooms late in shaded woods and edges. Highly toxic — it caused milk sickness in the nineteenth century when cattle grazed it.
species.en_description: New York. Blooms late in shaded woods and edges. Highly toxic — it caused milk sickness in the nineteenth century when cattle grazed it.

species.name: artemisa
species.short_description: Tall coarse plant with deeply cut leaves, silvery beneath, and inconspicuous flowers.
species.en_short_description: Tall coarse plant with deeply cut leaves, silvery beneath, and inconspicuous flowers.
species.description: New York. Introduced and aggressively weedy on disturbed ground. Aromatic when crushed. The sharply bicoloured leaf, green above and white below, identifies it.
species.en_description: New York. Introduced and aggressively weedy on disturbed ground. Aromatic when crushed. The sharply bicoloured leaf, green above and white below, identifies it.

species.name: Campanilla morada
species.short_description: Twining vine with heart-shaped leaves and purple to pink funnel flowers.
species.en_short_description: Twining vine with heart-shaped leaves and purple to pink funnel flowers.
species.description: New York and Mexico City. Flowers open at dawn and wilt by afternoon. Native to Mexico and naturalised widely. Climbs by twining stems, not tendrils.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City. Flowers open at dawn and wilt by afternoon. Native to Mexico and naturalised widely. Climbs by twining stems, not tendrils.

species.name: Correhuela de Eurasia
species.short_description: Trailing vine with arrowhead leaves and small white-to-pink funnel flowers.
species.en_short_description: Trailing vine with arrowhead leaves and small white-to-pink funnel flowers.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and a persistent agricultural weed with roots metres deep. Smaller-flowered than morning glories.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and a persistent agricultural weed with roots metres deep. Smaller-flowered than morning glories.

species.name: common cowparsnip
species.short_description: Very large umbel of white flowers over huge maple-like compound leaves.
species.en_short_description: Very large umbel of white flowers over huge maple-like compound leaves.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Can exceed two metres. Sap causes blistering skin burns in sunlight, so handle with care. Grows in moist meadows.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Can exceed two metres. Sap causes blistering skin burns in sunlight, so handle with care. Grows in moist meadows.

species.name: Dedalera
species.short_description: Tall one-sided spike of drooping pink-purple bells spotted inside.
species.en_short_description: Tall one-sided spike of drooping pink-purple bells spotted inside.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced from Europe and naturalised on roadsides and clearings. Highly toxic; the source of digitalis.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced from Europe and naturalised on roadsides and clearings. Highly toxic; the source of digitalis.

species.name: Llantén menor
species.short_description: Basal rosette of strongly ribbed narrow leaves with a short brown flower cone.
species.en_short_description: Basal rosette of strongly ribbed narrow leaves with a short brown flower cone.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and universal in lawns and paths. Anthers protrude in a pale ring around the flower head. The parallel leaf ribs are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and universal in lawns and paths. Anthers protrude in a pale ring around the flower head. The parallel leaf ribs are diagnostic.

species.name: Mastuerzo sudamericano
species.short_description: Round shield-shaped leaves and spurred orange, yellow or red flowers.
species.en_short_description: Round shield-shaped leaves and spurred orange, yellow or red flowers.
species.description: California and Mexico City. Native to South America, escaped from gardens and naturalised on coastal slopes. Leaves and flowers are edible and peppery.
species.en_description: California and Mexico City. Native to South America, escaped from gardens and naturalised on coastal slopes. Leaves and flowers are edible and peppery.

species.name: Trébol blanco
species.short_description: Creeping stems with three-part leaves and rounded white flower heads.
species.en_short_description: Creeping stems with three-part leaves and rounded white flower heads.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and ubiquitous in lawns. Leaflets often carry a pale chevron. Fixes nitrogen, which is why grass grows greener around it.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and ubiquitous in lawns. Leaflets often carry a pale chevron. Fixes nitrogen, which is why grass grows greener around it.

species.name: algodoncillo común
species.short_description: Domed clusters of dusty-pink fragrant flowers on stout stems with milky sap.
species.en_short_description: Domed clusters of dusty-pink fragrant flowers on stout stems with milky sap.
species.description: New York. The principal Monarch host in the east. Broad opposite leaves and warty seed pods. Strongly and sweetly scented in full bloom.
species.en_description: New York. The principal Monarch host in the east. Broad opposite leaves and warty seed pods. Strongly and sweetly scented in full bloom.

species.name: Bretónica
species.short_description: Low plant with a dense squarish head of violet two-lipped flowers.
species.en_short_description: Low plant with a dense squarish head of violet two-lipped flowers.
species.description: Five regions. Grows in lawns, meadows and trail edges, often flowering below mowing height. Square stems place it in the mint family.
species.en_description: Five regions. Grows in lawns, meadows and trail edges, often flowering below mowing height. Square stems place it in the mint family.

species.name: Cardo común
species.short_description: Spiny thistle with a large purple flower head and sharply prickly winged stems.
species.en_short_description: Spiny thistle with a large purple flower head and sharply prickly winged stems.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and weedy. Leaves are spiny on both surfaces. The flower head has a distinctly flask-shaped spiny base. Attracts goldfinches to the seed.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and weedy. Leaves are spiny on both surfaces. The flower head has a distinctly flask-shaped spiny base. Attracts goldfinches to the seed.

species.name: Hierba del Ajo
species.short_description: Rosettes and stems with toothed heart-shaped leaves smelling of garlic when crushed.
species.en_short_description: Rosettes and stems with toothed heart-shaped leaves smelling of garlic when crushed.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Aggressively invasive in eastern woodlands, where it suppresses native wildflowers. Small four-petalled white flowers.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Aggressively invasive in eastern woodlands, where it suppresses native wildflowers. Small four-petalled white flowers.

species.name: pipa de indio
species.short_description: Waxy translucent white stem with a single nodding flower and no green leaves.
species.en_short_description: Waxy translucent white stem with a single nodding flower and no green leaves.
species.description: New York, Washington and Mexico City. Entirely without chlorophyll, drawing nutrition from fungi linked to tree roots. Blackens as it ages. Appears suddenly in deep shade.
species.en_description: New York, Washington and Mexico City. Entirely without chlorophyll, drawing nutrition from fungi linked to tree roots. Blackens as it ages. Appears suddenly in deep shade.

species.name: Trébol rojo eurasiático
species.short_description: Three-part leaves and dense rounded heads of rose-purple flowers.
species.en_short_description: Three-part leaves and dense rounded heads of rose-purple flowers.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced as forage and now naturalised. Larger and more upright than White Clover, with pale leaf chevrons and hairy stems.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced as forage and now naturalised. Larger and more upright than White Clover, with pale leaf chevrons and hairy stems.

species.name: Achicoria
species.short_description: Wiry branched stems bearing sky-blue ragged-edged flower heads.
species.en_short_description: Wiry branched stems bearing sky-blue ragged-edged flower heads.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and abundant on roadsides. Flowers open in the morning and close by midday. Roots are roasted as a coffee substitute.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and abundant on roadsides. Flowers open in the morning and close by midday. Roots are roasted as a coffee substitute.

species.name: cardo cundidor
species.short_description: Slender thistle with small pale purple heads and spiny leaves on unwinged stems.
species.en_short_description: Slender thistle with small pale purple heads and spiny leaves on unwinged stems.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced and spreads by creeping roots, forming large clonal patches. Smaller-headed and less fiercely spiny than Bull Thistle.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced and spreads by creeping roots, forming large clonal patches. Smaller-headed and less fiercely spiny than Bull Thistle.

species.name: geranio de San Roberto
species.short_description: Delicate fern-like reddish foliage with small bright pink five-petalled flowers.
species.en_short_description: Delicate fern-like reddish foliage with small bright pink five-petalled flowers.
species.description: New York and Washington. Introduced and invasive in Northwest forest, where it is called stinky Bob for its pungent scent. Foliage flushes deep red in sun.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. Introduced and invasive in Northwest forest, where it is called stinky Bob for its pungent scent. Foliage flushes deep red in sun.

species.name: dulcámara
species.short_description: Scrambling vine with purple star flowers and yellow beaks, and red egg-shaped berries.
species.en_short_description: Scrambling vine with purple star flowers and yellow beaks, and red egg-shaped berries.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced and toxic. Flowers and ripe berries often appear together. Leaves frequently have two small basal lobes.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced and toxic. Flowers and ripe berries often appear together. Leaves frequently have two small basal lobes.

species.name: Jabonera europea
species.short_description: Low sprawling plant with small salmon-orange or blue five-petalled flowers.
species.en_short_description: Low sprawling plant with small salmon-orange or blue five-petalled flowers.
species.description: California, New York, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and widespread on disturbed ground. Flowers close in dull weather, earning the name poor man's weatherglass.
species.en_description: California, New York, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced and widespread on disturbed ground. Flowers close in dull weather, earning the name poor man's weatherglass.

species.name: Bola del rey
species.short_description: Tall square stem with tiers of spherical spiny whorls bearing furry orange flowers.
species.en_short_description: Tall square stem with tiers of spherical spiny whorls bearing furry orange flowers.
species.description: Mexico City region. Introduced from Africa and naturalised in the highlands. The stacked globular whorls up the stem are unmistakable. Visited by hummingbirds.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Introduced from Africa and naturalised in the highlands. The stacked globular whorls up the stem are unmistakable. Visited by hummingbirds.

species.name: dalia roja
species.short_description: Single scarlet to orange flower head with a yellow centre on a slender stem.
species.en_short_description: Single scarlet to orange flower head with a yellow centre on a slender stem.
species.description: Mexico City region. A wild ancestor of garden dahlias and Mexico's national flower. Grows on rocky slopes and roadsides in the highlands, flowering in the rainy season.
