species.en_description: Mexico City region. A wild ancestor of garden dahlias and Mexico's national flower. Grows on rocky slopes and roadsides in the highlands, flowering in the rainy season.

species.name: sulfur buckwheat
species.short_description: Dense umbels of pale yellow flowers over mats of spoon-shaped leaves.
species.en_short_description: Dense umbels of pale yellow flowers over mats of spoon-shaped leaves.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Flowers age to rust-orange, so a single plant shows both colours. A key nectar source for montane butterflies.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Flowers age to rust-orange, so a single plant shows both colours. A key nectar source for montane butterflies.

species.name: Margarita común europea
species.short_description: Small white-rayed daisy with a yellow centre on a short leafless stalk.
species.en_short_description: Small white-rayed daisy with a yellow centre on a short leafless stalk.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced from Europe and common in mown lawns. Rays are often pink-tipped beneath. Closes at night.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced from Europe and common in mown lawns. Rays are often pink-tipped beneath. Closes at night.

species.name: Zanahoria
species.short_description: Lacy flat umbel of tiny white flowers, often with one dark purple central floret.
species.en_short_description: Lacy flat umbel of tiny white flowers, often with one dark purple central floret.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Also called Queen Anne's lace. The single dark floret and a bristly three-forked bract beneath the umbel are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Also called Queen Anne's lace. The single dark floret and a bristly three-forked bract beneath the umbel are diagnostic.

species.name: Hierba del golpe
species.short_description: Low plant with four-petalled pink flowers and toothed lance-shaped leaves.
species.en_short_description: Low plant with four-petalled pink flowers and toothed lance-shaped leaves.
species.description: Mexico City region. Common on lawns, verges and disturbed ground in the highlands. Flowers open in the afternoon. Known locally as hierba del golpe.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Common on lawns, verges and disturbed ground in the highlands. Flowers open in the afternoon. Known locally as hierba del golpe.

species.name: prairie pasqueflower
species.short_description: Silky-haired lavender cup flowering before the leaves expand.
species.en_short_description: Silky-haired lavender cup flowering before the leaves expand.
species.description: Colorado. One of the earliest prairie and foothill wildflowers, appearing as snow retreats. Dense silvery hairs insulate the flower. Feathery seed heads follow.
species.en_description: Colorado. One of the earliest prairie and foothill wildflowers, appearing as snow retreats. Dense silvery hairs insulate the flower. Feathery seed heads follow.

species.name: Col de Mofeta Occidental
species.short_description: Huge bright yellow hood around a green flower spike, in swampy ground.
species.en_short_description: Huge bright yellow hood around a green flower spike, in swampy ground.
species.description: California and Washington. Emits a strong musky odour that attracts pollinating beetles and flies. Leaves grow enormous after flowering, often over a metre long.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Emits a strong musky odour that attracts pollinating beetles and flies. Leaves grow enormous after flowering, often over a metre long.

species.name: Corazón De La Virgen Occidental
species.short_description: Nodding pink heart-shaped flowers over finely divided ferny foliage.
species.en_short_description: Nodding pink heart-shaped flowers over finely divided ferny foliage.
species.description: California and Washington. Grows in moist shaded forest. Seeds carry oily appendages that ants collect and disperse. Foliage dies back by midsummer.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Grows in moist shaded forest. Seeds carry oily appendages that ants collect and disperse. Foliage dies back by midsummer.

species.name: lamio púrpura
species.short_description: Low plant with soft purple-tinged triangular leaves and small pink-purple hooded flowers.
species.en_short_description: Low plant with soft purple-tinged triangular leaves and small pink-purple hooded flowers.
species.description: New York and Washington. Introduced and among the earliest spring flowers on bare soil. Square stems; despite the name it does not sting.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. Introduced and among the earliest spring flowers on bare soil. Square stems; despite the name it does not sting.

species.name: Gunnison's Mariposa Lily
species.short_description: Three broad white to lavender petals with a purple band and fringed gland.
species.en_short_description: Three broad white to lavender petals with a purple band and fringed gland.
species.description: Colorado. Grows in mountain meadows and open pine forest. The intricate banded markings inside the cup are its distinguishing feature. Bulbs were formerly eaten.
species.en_description: Colorado. Grows in mountain meadows and open pine forest. The intricate banded markings inside the cup are its distinguishing feature. Bulbs were formerly eaten.

species.name: Hierba carmín
species.short_description: Tall red-stemmed plant with drooping racemes of dark purple berries.
species.en_short_description: Tall red-stemmed plant with drooping racemes of dark purple berries.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. All parts are toxic, particularly the root. Berries stain intensely and were once used as ink. Stems turn brilliant magenta by autumn.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. All parts are toxic, particularly the root. Berries stain intensely and were once used as ink. Stems turn brilliant magenta by autumn.

species.name: Scarlet Globemallow
species.short_description: Low spreading plant with brick-orange cup flowers and grey-green lobed leaves.
species.en_short_description: Low spreading plant with brick-orange cup flowers and grey-green lobed leaves.
species.description: Colorado. Common on shortgrass prairie and roadsides. Foliage has a scurfy star-shaped hairiness typical of the mallow family. Drought-tolerant and long-flowering.
species.en_description: Colorado. Common on shortgrass prairie and roadsides. Foliage has a scurfy star-shaped hairiness typical of the mallow family. Drought-tolerant and long-flowering.

species.name: pearly everlasting
species.short_description: Clusters of papery white bracts around small yellow centres, on woolly stems.
species.en_short_description: Clusters of papery white bracts around small yellow centres, on woolly stems.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The bracts persist unchanged for months, which is the origin of the name. Grows on dry banks and clearings.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The bracts persist unchanged for months, which is the origin of the name. Grows on dry banks and clearings.

species.name: Scarlet Gilia
species.short_description: Tall spike of vivid red trumpet flowers over sticky-hairy dissected leaves.
species.en_short_description: Tall spike of vivid red trumpet flowers over sticky-hairy dissected leaves.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Hummingbird-pollinated, and flower colour fades to pink later in the season as hawkmoths take over. Strongly skunky scent.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Hummingbird-pollinated, and flower colour fades to pink later in the season as hawkmoths take over. Strongly skunky scent.

species.name: Cicuta
species.short_description: Tall purple-blotched hollow stems with lacy leaves and white umbels.
species.en_short_description: Tall purple-blotched hollow stems with lacy leaves and white umbels.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Extremely poisonous — the plant that killed Socrates. Purple stem splotches and a musty smell separate it from wild carrot.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Extremely poisonous — the plant that killed Socrates. Purple stem splotches and a musty smell separate it from wild carrot.

species.name: western blue-eyed grass
species.short_description: Grass-like leaves with flat blue-violet six-petalled flowers and a yellow eye.
species.en_short_description: Grass-like leaves with flat blue-violet six-petalled flowers and a yellow eye.
species.description: California. An iris relative rather than a grass. Flowers open in morning sun in coastal grassland and close by afternoon. Flattened two-edged stems.
species.en_description: California. An iris relative rather than a grass. Flowers open in morning sun in coastal grassland and close by afternoon. Flattened two-edged stems.

species.name: Maravilla
species.short_description: Bushy plant with trumpet flowers in magenta, yellow or white opening late in the day.
species.en_short_description: Bushy plant with trumpet flowers in magenta, yellow or white opening late in the day.
species.description: Mexico City region. Native to Mexico. Flowers open in late afternoon and are moth-pollinated. A single plant can bear differently coloured blooms.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Native to Mexico. Flowers open in late afternoon and are moth-pollinated. A single plant can bear differently coloured blooms.

species.name: Solomon's plume
species.short_description: Arching stem with alternate ribbed leaves ending in a plume of tiny white flowers.
species.en_short_description: Arching stem with alternate ribbed leaves ending in a plume of tiny white flowers.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Flowers form a branched terminal cluster, unlike the paired hanging bells of true Solomon's seal. Red speckled berries follow.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Flowers form a branched terminal cluster, unlike the paired hanging bells of true Solomon's seal. Red speckled berries follow.

species.name: Whipple's penstemon
species.short_description: Nodding tubular flowers in deep wine-purple to dusky maroon.
species.en_short_description: Nodding tubular flowers in deep wine-purple to dusky maroon.
species.description: Colorado. A high-elevation penstemon of subalpine meadows and rocky slopes. The unusually dark, almost black-purple flowers are distinctive among mountain wildflowers.
species.en_description: Colorado. A high-elevation penstemon of subalpine meadows and rocky slopes. The unusually dark, almost black-purple flowers are distinctive among mountain wildflowers.

species.name: western columbine
species.short_description: Nodding flower with red spurred sepals and yellow blades.
species.en_short_description: Nodding flower with red spurred sepals and yellow blades.
species.description: California and Washington. Hummingbird-pollinated and unmistakable in red and yellow. Grows in moist shaded seeps, streambanks and mountain meadows.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Hummingbird-pollinated and unmistakable in red and yellow. Grows in moist shaded seeps, streambanks and mountain meadows.

species.name: Zarza del Salmón
species.short_description: Thicket-forming shrub with magenta flowers and soft orange-to-red raspberry-like fruit.
species.en_short_description: Thicket-forming shrub with magenta flowers and soft orange-to-red raspberry-like fruit.
species.description: California and Washington. Dominates damp Northwest understorey and streambanks. Fruit ripens early, varying from salmon-orange to deep red on the same patch. Canes have weak prickles.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Dominates damp Northwest understorey and streambanks. Fruit ripens early, varying from salmon-orange to deep red on the same patch. Canes have weak prickles.

species.name: salal
species.short_description: Leathery evergreen shrub with urn-shaped pink-white flowers and dark edible berries.
species.en_short_description: Leathery evergreen shrub with urn-shaped pink-white flowers and dark edible berries.
species.description: California and Washington. Forms dense knee-to-shoulder-high thickets in Northwest forest. Thick glossy oval leaves are widely cut for the florist trade.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Forms dense knee-to-shoulder-high thickets in Northwest forest. Thick glossy oval leaves are widely cut for the florist trade.

species.name: Frambuesa Dedal
species.short_description: Thornless shrub with large soft maple-like leaves and flat red raspberry-like fruit.
species.en_short_description: Thornless shrub with large soft maple-like leaves and flat red raspberry-like fruit.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Fruit is shallow like a thimble and falls apart when picked. Completely prickle-free, unlike other brambles. Large white flowers.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Fruit is shallow like a thimble and falls apart when picked. Completely prickle-free, unlike other brambles. Large white flowers.

species.name: Roble venenoso del pacífico
species.short_description: Shrub or vine with glossy leaves in threes, turning brilliant red in autumn.
species.en_short_description: Shrub or vine with glossy leaves in threes, turning brilliant red in autumn.
species.description: California and Washington. Causes severe contact dermatitis; learn it and avoid it. Leaflets in threes with scalloped lobes. Bare winter stems remain irritant.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Causes severe contact dermatitis; learn it and avoid it. Leaflets in threes with scalloped lobes. Bare winter stems remain irritant.

species.name: flor de borrego
species.short_description: Low grey shrub with needle-like leaves and dense heads of white flowers ageing rust.
species.en_short_description: Low grey shrub with needle-like leaves and dense heads of white flowers ageing rust.
species.description: California. A dominant coastal sage scrub shrub and a major nectar source for native bees. Flower heads persist rust-brown through summer and autumn.
species.en_description: California. A dominant coastal sage scrub shrub and a major nectar source for native bees. Flower heads persist rust-brown through summer and autumn.

species.name: toyón
species.short_description: Evergreen shrub with toothed leathery leaves and heavy clusters of red berries.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen shrub with toothed leathery leaves and heavy clusters of red berries.
species.description: California. Also called Christmas berry for its winter fruit display, which feeds robins and waxwings. Flat clusters of small white flowers in early summer.
species.en_description: California. Also called Christmas berry for its winter fruit display, which feeds robins and waxwings. Flat clusters of small white flowers in early summer.

species.name: Hierba de conejo de Guadalupe
species.short_description: Grey-green shrub with slender flexible stems and dense heads of bright yellow flowers.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green shrub with slender flexible stems and dense heads of bright yellow flowers.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Blooms late, colouring sagebrush country gold in autumn. Stems contain latex, which was investigated as a rubber source.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Blooms late, colouring sagebrush country gold in autumn. Stems contain latex, which was investigated as a rubber source.

species.name: creeping mahonia
species.short_description: Low creeping shrub with holly-like spiny evergreen leaflets and blue berries.
species.en_short_description: Low creeping shrub with holly-like spiny evergreen leaflets and blue berries.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Forms ground cover in dry pine forest. Leaves flush bronze-purple in winter cold. Yellow flower clusters in spring; tart edible fruit.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Forms ground cover in dry pine forest. Leaves flush bronze-purple in winter cold. Yellow flower clusters in spring; tart edible fruit.

species.name: saúco rojo
species.short_description: Shrub with compound leaves, domed clusters of cream flowers and bright red berries.
species.en_short_description: Shrub with compound leaves, domed clusters of cream flowers and bright red berries.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Berries are red rather than the blue-black of other elders and should not be eaten raw. Pithy stems break easily.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Berries are red rather than the blue-black of other elders and should not be eaten raw. Pithy stems break easily.

species.name: Tabaquillo sudamericano
species.short_description: Sprawling shrub with blue-green paddle leaves and drooping yellow tubular flowers.
species.en_short_description: Sprawling shrub with blue-green paddle leaves and drooping yellow tubular flowers.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Native to South America and naturalised on disturbed ground and washes. All parts are toxic. Hummingbirds work the flowers.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Native to South America and naturalised on disturbed ground and washes. All parts are toxic. Hummingbirds work the flowers.

species.name: Zarza de California
species.short_description: Slender trailing bramble with three leaflets and small sweet black fruit.
species.en_short_description: Slender trailing bramble with three leaflets and small sweet black fruit.
species.description: California and Washington. The native Pacific blackberry, far more slender and less aggressive than invasive Himalayan blackberry. Fruit is small but exceptionally flavoured.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The native Pacific blackberry, far more slender and less aggressive than invasive Himalayan blackberry. Fruit is small but exceptionally flavoured.

species.name: Arbusto del coyote
species.short_description: Rounded evergreen shrub with small toothed resinous leaves and fluffy seed heads.
species.en_short_description: Rounded evergreen shrub with small toothed resinous leaves and fluffy seed heads.
species.description: California. A keystone shrub of coastal scrub. Male and female plants are separate; females turn cottony-white with seed in autumn. Sticky aromatic foliage.
species.en_description: California. A keystone shrub of coastal scrub. Male and female plants are separate; females turn cottony-white with seed in autumn. Sticky aromatic foliage.

species.name: Llovizna
species.short_description: Arching shrub with plumes of creamy flowers that fade to persistent tan.
species.en_short_description: Arching shrub with plumes of creamy flowers that fade to persistent tan.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Flower sprays foam down the branches, hence the name. Dried plumes remain through winter. Extremely hard wood used for tools.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Flower sprays foam down the branches, hence the name. Dried plumes remain through winter. Extremely hard wood used for tools.

species.name: Madreselva
species.short_description: Shrub with paired yellow tubular flowers set in leafy bracts and paired black berries.
species.en_short_description: Shrub with paired yellow tubular flowers set in leafy bracts and paired black berries.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Bracts turn deep red-purple as the twin berries ripen, making a striking combination. Grows in moist thickets and streambanks.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Bracts turn deep red-purple as the twin berries ripen, making a striking combination. Grows in moist thickets and streambanks.

species.name: Ciruela India
species.short_description: Early-flowering shrub with drooping white flowers smelling of cucumber.
species.en_short_description: Early-flowering shrub with drooping white flowers smelling of cucumber.
species.description: California and Washington. Among the first shrubs to bloom in the Northwest, often in February. Crushed leaves smell distinctly of cucumber or watermelon rind.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Among the first shrubs to bloom in the Northwest, often in February. Crushed leaves smell distinctly of cucumber or watermelon rind.

species.name: Cascade Oregon-grape
species.short_description: Low shrub with long pinnate leaves of many spiny leathery leaflets.
species.en_short_description: Low shrub with long pinnate leaves of many spiny leathery leaflets.
species.description: Washington. Forms carpets in Northwest conifer forest. More leaflets and a shorter stature than tall Oregon grape. Yellow flower spikes and blue berries.
species.en_description: Washington. Forms carpets in Northwest conifer forest. More leaflets and a shorter stature than tall Oregon grape. Yellow flower spikes and blue berries.

species.name: Gobernadora
species.short_description: Open desert shrub with small resinous olive leaves smelling strongly after rain.
species.en_short_description: Open desert shrub with small resinous olive leaves smelling strongly after rain.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. The defining shrub of North American hot deserts. Clonal rings can be thousands of years old. The scent after rain is unmistakable.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. The defining shrub of North American hot deserts. Clonal rings can be thousands of years old. The scent after rain is unmistakable.

species.name: Artemisa de California
species.short_description: Soft grey-green shrub with thread-like divided leaves and a powerful sage scent.
species.en_short_description: Soft grey-green shrub with thread-like divided leaves and a powerful sage scent.
species.description: California. A dominant coastal sage scrub species. Foliage is finely dissected and intensely aromatic. Semi-deciduous, dropping leaves in the driest months.
species.en_description: California. A dominant coastal sage scrub species. Foliage is finely dissected and intensely aromatic. Semi-deciduous, dropping leaves in the driest months.

species.name: Flor de mono naranja
species.short_description: Shrub with sticky narrow leaves and tubular apricot-orange two-lipped flowers.
species.en_short_description: Shrub with sticky narrow leaves and tubular apricot-orange two-lipped flowers.
species.description: California. Common on dry slopes and road cuts. The flower's stigma snaps shut when touched by a pollinator, a mechanism easily triggered with a grass stem.
species.en_description: California. Common on dry slopes and road cuts. The flower's stigma snaps shut when touched by a pollinator, a mechanism easily triggered with a grass stem.

species.name: Trompetilla
species.short_description: Slender shrub with whorled leaves and clusters of long scarlet tubular flowers.
species.en_short_description: Slender shrub with whorled leaves and clusters of long scarlet tubular flowers.
species.description: Mexico City region. Called trompetilla. Hummingbird-pollinated and flowers over a long season on rocky slopes. Widely used in traditional Mexican medicine.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Called trompetilla. Hummingbird-pollinated and flowers over a long season on rocky slopes. Widely used in traditional Mexican medicine.

species.name: Evergreen Huckleberry
species.short_description: Compact evergreen shrub with small glossy leathery leaves and small black berries.
species.en_short_description: Compact evergreen shrub with small glossy leathery leaves and small black berries.
species.description: California and Washington. New growth flushes bronze-red. Berries ripen late and are intensely flavoured. Shade-tolerant and common in coastal forest.
species.en_description: California and Washington. New growth flushes bronze-red. Berries ripen late and are intensely flavoured. Shade-tolerant and common in coastal forest.

species.name: Saúco azul
species.short_description: Shrub or small tree with large flat cream flower clusters and powder-blue berries.
species.en_short_description: Shrub or small tree with large flat cream flower clusters and powder-blue berries.
species.description: California and Washington. The waxy bloom on the fruit gives the blue colour; rubbing it off reveals near-black skin. Berries are edible cooked.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The waxy bloom on the fruit gives the blue colour; rubbing it off reveals near-black skin. Berries are edible cooked.

species.name: mahonia
species.short_description: Upright shrub with glossy spiny compound leaves, yellow flower spikes and blue berries.
species.en_short_description: Upright shrub with glossy spiny compound leaves, yellow flower spikes and blue berries.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Oregon's state flower. Taller and with fewer, larger leaflets than the Cascade species. Inner bark is bright yellow with berberine.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Oregon's state flower. Taller and with fewer, larger leaflets than the Cascade species. Inner bark is bright yellow with berberine.

species.name: Arándano Rojo Occidental
species.short_description: Airy green-stemmed shrub with small thin leaves and translucent red berries.
species.en_short_description: Airy green-stemmed shrub with small thin leaves and translucent red berries.
species.description: Washington. Almost always rooted on rotting stumps and nurse logs in Northwest forest. Strongly angled green twigs are visible even when leafless.
species.en_description: Washington. Almost always rooted on rotting stumps and nurse logs in Northwest forest. Strongly angled green twigs are visible even when leafless.

species.name: flor de rocío
species.short_description: Rounded desert shrub with silvery-white leaves and yellow daisy flowers on long stalks.
species.en_short_description: Rounded desert shrub with silvery-white leaves and yellow daisy flowers on long stalks.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. The felted white leaves reflect sun and reduce water loss. Blooms in dense golden mounds after winter rain. Stems exude fragrant resin.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. The felted white leaves reflect sun and reduce water loss. Blooms in dense golden mounds after winter rain. Stems exude fragrant resin.

species.name: shrubby cinquefoil
species.short_description: Low twiggy shrub with small five-part leaves and butter-yellow five-petalled flowers.
species.en_short_description: Low twiggy shrub with small five-part leaves and butter-yellow five-petalled flowers.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Flowers over a very long season in mountain meadows and along streams. Shredding papery bark on older stems. Widely planted in gardens.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Flowers over a very long season in mountain meadows and along streams. Shredding papery bark on older stems. Widely planted in gardens.

species.name: California brittlebush
species.short_description: Green-leaved brittlebush with yellow daisy flowers and a dark central disc.
species.en_short_description: Green-leaved brittlebush with yellow daisy flowers and a dark central disc.
species.description: California. Differs from the desert brittlebush in having green rather than silvery leaves and a brown-purple flower centre. A coastal sage scrub species.
species.en_description: California. Differs from the desert brittlebush in having green rather than silvery leaves and a brown-purple flower centre. A coastal sage scrub species.

species.name: golden currant
species.short_description: Shrub with lobed leaves and drooping clusters of fragrant golden-yellow flowers.
species.en_short_description: Shrub with lobed leaves and drooping clusters of fragrant golden-yellow flowers.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Flowers smell strongly of cloves. Fruit ripens from amber to black. Grows in draws and along streams in dry country.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Flowers smell strongly of cloves. Fruit ripens from amber to black. Grows in draws and along streams in dry country.

species.name: Grosellero rojo
species.short_description: Shrub with maple-like leaves and hanging racemes of deep pink to red flowers.
species.en_short_description: Shrub with maple-like leaves and hanging racemes of deep pink to red flowers.
species.description: California and Washington. Blooms very early, an important nectar source for returning Rufous Hummingbirds. Blue-black berries with a waxy bloom follow.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Blooms very early, an important nectar source for returning Rufous Hummingbirds. Blue-black berries with a waxy bloom follow.

species.name: Perlita blanca
species.short_description: Thicket shrub with small oval leaves and clusters of waxy white berries.
species.en_short_description: Thicket shrub with small oval leaves and clusters of waxy white berries.
species.description: California and Washington. The porcelain-white fruit persists into winter and is unmistakable. Berries are mildly toxic to people. Small pink bell flowers.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The porcelain-white fruit persists into winter and is unmistakable. Berries are mildly toxic to people. Small pink bell flowers.

species.name: black sage
species.short_description: Aromatic shrub with wrinkled dark green leaves and tiered whorls of pale blue flowers.
species.en_short_description: Aromatic shrub with wrinkled dark green leaves and tiered whorls of pale blue flowers.
species.description: California. A coastal sage scrub dominant and a prime honey plant. Flower whorls are spaced up the stem like beads. Foliage darkens and curls in drought.
species.en_description: California. A coastal sage scrub dominant and a prime honey plant. Flower whorls are spaced up the stem like beads. Foliage darkens and curls in drought.

species.name: Saladito
species.short_description: Evergreen shrub with thick leathery leaves and sticky reddish berries.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen shrub with thick leathery leaves and sticky reddish berries.
species.description: California. Berries are coated in a tart resin that was steeped to make a lemonade-like drink. Leaves are folded and leathery. Common on coastal bluffs.
species.en_description: California. Berries are coated in a tart resin that was steeped to make a lemonade-like drink. Leaves are folded and leathery. Common on coastal bluffs.

species.name: Caoba de montaña
species.short_description: Shrub with small wedge-shaped toothed leaves and feathery twisted seed plumes.
species.en_short_description: Shrub with small wedge-shaped toothed leaves and feathery twisted seed plumes.
species.description: Colorado. The long silvery corkscrew plumes on the fruit are conspicuous in late summer. Important winter browse for deer and elk. Extremely dense wood.
species.en_description: Colorado. The long silvery corkscrew plumes on the fruit are conspicuous in late summer. Important winter browse for deer and elk. Extremely dense wood.

species.name: lentisco
species.short_description: Large evergreen shrub with folded taco-shaped leaves and cream flower clusters.
species.en_short_description: Large evergreen shrub with folded taco-shaped leaves and cream flower clusters.
species.description: California. Leaves fold along the midrib, which is diagnostic. Frost-sensitive, so its distribution historically guided citrus planting. Aromatic when crushed.
species.en_description: California. Leaves fold along the midrib, which is diagnostic. Frost-sensitive, so its distribution historically guided citrus planting. Aromatic when crushed.

species.name: chamizo
species.short_description: Wiry evergreen shrub with tiny needle-like leaves in bundles and cream flower sprays.
species.en_short_description: Wiry evergreen shrub with tiny needle-like leaves in bundles and cream flower sprays.
species.description: California. The most widespread chaparral shrub, often forming pure stands. Highly flammable and adapted to reburn, resprouting from a basal burl.
species.en_description: California. The most widespread chaparral shrub, often forming pure stands. Highly flammable and adapted to reburn, resprouting from a basal burl.

species.name: Batamote
species.short_description: Willow-like shrub with narrow toothed leaves and clusters of fluffy white flower heads.
species.en_short_description: Willow-like shrub with narrow toothed leaves and clusters of fluffy white flower heads.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Lines washes and streambeds. Looks like a willow but is a composite, with dandelion-like seed fluff. Fast-growing in wet gravel.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Lines washes and streambeds. Looks like a willow but is a composite, with dandelion-like seed fluff. Fast-growing in wet gravel.

species.name: Mazo del diablo
species.short_description: Sprawling shrub armed with dense spines, with huge maple-like leaves and red berry spikes.
species.en_short_description: Sprawling shrub armed with dense spines, with huge maple-like leaves and red berry spikes.
species.description: Washington. Formidable spines cover stems and leaf veins alike. Grows in wet Northwest forest and seeps. Culturally important as medicine to many coastal peoples.
species.en_description: Washington. Formidable spines cover stems and leaf veins alike. Grows in wet Northwest forest and seeps. Culturally important as medicine to many coastal peoples.

species.name: rosa novia
species.short_description: Arching thorny rose with clusters of small white flowers and tiny red hips.
species.en_short_description: Arching thorny rose with clusters of small white flowers and tiny red hips.
species.description: New York. Introduced and severely invasive in eastern fields and woodland edges. Flowers in dense many-flowered clusters, unlike native single-flowered roses.
species.en_description: New York. Introduced and severely invasive in eastern fields and woodland edges. Flowers in dense many-flowered clusters, unlike native single-flowered roses.

species.name: cerezo de Virginia
species.short_description: Shrub or small tree with oval toothed leaves, white flower spikes and dark astringent fruit.
species.en_short_description: Shrub or small tree with oval toothed leaves, white flower spikes and dark astringent fruit.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Fruit is intensely puckering raw but excellent in jelly. Leaves and pits contain cyanogenic compounds. Important wildlife food.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Fruit is intensely puckering raw but excellent in jelly. Leaves and pits contain cyanogenic compounds. Important wildlife food.

species.name: gayuba
species.short_description: Prostrate evergreen mat with small leathery leaves and bright red berries.
species.en_short_description: Prostrate evergreen mat with small leathery leaves and bright red berries.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Also called kinnikinnick. Forms dense ground cover on sandy and rocky soil. Pink urn-shaped flowers; mealy tasteless fruit.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Also called kinnikinnick. Forms dense ground cover on sandy and rocky soil. Pink urn-shaped flowers; mealy tasteless fruit.

species.name: wax currant
species.short_description: Small twiggy shrub with sticky lobed leaves and translucent red berries.
species.en_short_description: Small twiggy shrub with sticky lobed leaves and translucent red berries.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Foliage is glandular and smells resinous. Pale pink tubular flowers. Grows on dry rocky slopes in foothill and montane zones.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Foliage is glandular and smells resinous. Pale pink tubular flowers. Grows on dry rocky slopes in foothill and montane zones.

species.name: higuerilla
species.short_description: Coarse shrub with huge palmate leaves, often red-tinged, and spiny seed capsules.
species.en_short_description: Coarse shrub with huge palmate leaves, often red-tinged, and spiny seed capsules.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Naturalised on disturbed ground and washes. Seeds contain ricin and are extremely poisonous. Grows very fast to several metres.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Naturalised on disturbed ground and washes. Seeds contain ricin and are extremely poisonous. Grows very fast to several metres.

species.name: Chichicastle manso
species.short_description: Coarse shrub with enormous felted leaves covered in irritating stinging hairs.
species.en_short_description: Coarse shrub with enormous felted leaves covered in irritating stinging hairs.
species.description: Mexico City region. Called chichicastle. The dense bristles cause a persistent itch, hence the English name. Large clusters of violet flowers. Grows on lava and road cuts.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Called chichicastle. The dense bristles cause a persistent itch, hence the English name. Large clusters of violet flowers. Grows on lava and road cuts.

species.name: Tepozán blanco
species.short_description: Shrub or small tree with large soft grey-green leaves and spikes of tiny cream flowers.
species.en_short_description: Shrub or small tree with large soft grey-green leaves and spikes of tiny cream flowers.
species.description: Mexico City region. A pioneer of disturbed slopes and lava fields in the Valley of Mexico. Leaves are woolly beneath. Widely used in traditional medicine.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. A pioneer of disturbed slopes and lava fields in the Valley of Mexico. Leaves are woolly beneath. Widely used in traditional medicine.

species.name: palo loco
species.short_description: Thick-stemmed succulent shrub, leafless much of the year, with yellow daisy flowers.
species.en_short_description: Thick-stemmed succulent shrub, leafless much of the year, with yellow daisy flowers.
species.description: Mexico City region. Called palo loco. Fat pale water-storing stems grow on lava fields such as the Pedregal. Flowers in the dry season when leafless.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Called palo loco. Fat pale water-storing stems grow on lava fields such as the Pedregal. Flowers in the dry season when leafless.

species.name: Palo Adán
species.short_description: Spiny wand-like shrub with clusters of red tubular flowers at the branch tips.
species.en_short_description: Spiny wand-like shrub with clusters of red tubular flowers at the branch tips.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Called palo Adán, a peninsular relative of ocotillo. Slender thorny stems leaf out after rain and go bare in drought. Hummingbird-pollinated.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Called palo Adán, a peninsular relative of ocotillo. Slender thorny stems leaf out after rain and go bare in drought. Hummingbird-pollinated.

species.name: northern spicebush
species.short_description: Understorey shrub with aromatic leaves, early yellow flower clusters and red berries.
species.en_short_description: Understorey shrub with aromatic leaves, early yellow flower clusters and red berries.
species.description: New York. Crushed twigs and leaves smell strongly of citrus and spice. Blooms before leafing out. Host plant for the Spicebush Swallowtail.
species.en_description: New York. Crushed twigs and leaves smell strongly of citrus and spice. Blooms before leafing out. Host plant for the Spicebush Swallowtail.

species.name: beaked hazelnut
species.short_description: Shrub with doubly toothed leaves and nuts enclosed in a long bristly beaked husk.
species.en_short_description: Shrub with doubly toothed leaves and nuts enclosed in a long bristly beaked husk.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The tubular beaked husk is diagnostic. Catkins hang in late winter. Nuts are edible but usually taken by squirrels first.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The tubular beaked husk is diagnostic. Catkins hang in late winter. Nuts are edible but usually taken by squirrels first.

species.name: Helecho dulce
species.short_description: Low shrub with narrow deeply lobed fern-like leaves that are strongly aromatic.
species.en_short_description: Low shrub with narrow deeply lobed fern-like leaves that are strongly aromatic.
species.description: New York. Not a fern at all but a flowering shrub that fixes nitrogen. Grows on sandy barrens and roadsides. Crushed foliage is sweetly resinous.
species.en_description: New York. Not a fern at all but a flowering shrub that fixes nitrogen. Grows on sandy barrens and roadsides. Crushed foliage is sweetly resinous.

species.name: Árbol de la cera
species.short_description: Semi-evergreen shrub with leathery aromatic leaves and waxy grey-blue berries.
species.en_short_description: Semi-evergreen shrub with leathery aromatic leaves and waxy grey-blue berries.
species.description: New York. Common on coastal sand and barrens. The wax coating on the fruit was boiled to make bayberry candles. Fixes nitrogen; forms dense colonial thickets.
species.en_description: New York. Common on coastal sand and barrens. The wax coating on the fruit was boiled to make bayberry candles. Fixes nitrogen; forms dense colonial thickets.

species.name: Cardón
species.short_description: Enormous columnar cactus branching from a short thick trunk.
species.en_short_description: Enormous columnar cactus branching from a short thick trunk.
species.description: Baja California Sur, where it is called cardón and is the signature plant of the peninsula. The largest cactus in the world, reaching 20 metres and centuries in age.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur, where it is called cardón and is the signature plant of the peninsula. The largest cactus in the world, reaching 20 metres and centuries in age.

species.name: Stringy Stonecrop
species.short_description: Low mat of fleshy pointed leaves in whorls of three with yellow star flowers.
species.en_short_description: Low mat of fleshy pointed leaves in whorls of three with yellow star flowers.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced from Asia and naturalised on walls and rockeries. Stems root wherever they touch soil, so it spreads readily.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced from Asia and naturalised on walls and rockeries. Stems root wherever they touch soil, so it spreads readily.

species.name: nopal del este
species.short_description: Low sprawling pricklypear with flat green pads and large yellow flowers.
species.en_short_description: Low sprawling pricklypear with flat green pads and large yellow flowers.
species.description: California and New York. The eastern pricklypear, hardy enough for New York sand barrens. Pads shrivel and lie flat through winter, then re-inflate in spring.
species.en_description: California and New York. The eastern pricklypear, hardy enough for New York sand barrens. Pads shrivel and lie flat through winter, then re-inflate in spring.

species.name: Choya pelona
species.short_description: Cholla with cylindrical jointed segments forming chain-like branches.
species.en_short_description: Cholla with cylindrical jointed segments forming chain-like branches.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Segments detach easily and root where they fall. Spines are barbed and difficult to remove — carry a comb. Flowers dull purple to bronze.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Segments detach easily and root where they fall. Spines are barbed and difficult to remove — carry a comb. Flowers dull purple to bronze.

species.name: Lanceleaf Stonecrop
species.short_description: Small succulent rosettes with narrow pointed leaves and dense yellow flower clusters.
species.en_short_description: Small succulent rosettes with narrow pointed leaves and dense yellow flower clusters.
species.description: Colorado and Washington. Grows on rock outcrops and gravelly alpine slopes. Leaves often flush red in strong sun and drought. Very drought-hardy.
species.en_description: Colorado and Washington. Grows on rock outcrops and gravelly alpine slopes. Leaves often flush red in strong sun and drought. Very drought-hardy.

species.name: Tememetla
species.short_description: Large rosette of broad wavy grey-pink leaves with a tall arching flower stalk.
species.en_short_description: Large rosette of broad wavy grey-pink leaves with a tall arching flower stalk.
species.description: Mexico City region. Called tememetla. Grows on volcanic rock and cliffs in the Valley of Mexico. Leaves have an iridescent metallic sheen. Pink-red flowers on long stems.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Called tememetla. Grows on volcanic rock and cliffs in the Valley of Mexico. Leaves have an iridescent metallic sheen. Pink-red flowers on long stems.

species.name: Pitaya de Baja California
species.short_description: Sprawling columnar cactus whose stems lean over and root where they touch ground.
species.en_short_description: Sprawling columnar cactus whose stems lean over and root where they touch ground.
species.description: Baja California Sur, where it is called pitaya agria. The scrambling habit that lets it advance across the desert gives it the English name. Fruit is tart and edible.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur, where it is called pitaya agria. The scrambling habit that lets it advance across the desert gives it the English name. Fruit is tart and edible.

species.name: Choya plateada
species.short_description: Compact cholla densely covered in pale straw-coloured spines.
species.en_short_description: Compact cholla densely covered in pale straw-coloured spines.
species.description: California. The dense pale spination gives a silvery glow in low sun. Grows on desert bajadas and rocky slopes. Yellow-green to bronze flowers.
species.en_description: California. The dense pale spination gives a silvery glow in low sun. Grows on desert bajadas and rocky slopes. Yellow-green to bronze flowers.

species.name: Nopal peludito
species.short_description: Low clumping pricklypear with flat pads and long white spines.
species.en_short_description: Low clumping pricklypear with flat pads and long white spines.
species.description: Colorado. Abundant on shortgrass prairie. Bright yellow flowers with occasional pink forms. Pads shrink and wrinkle over winter as a freeze-avoidance strategy.
species.en_description: Colorado. Abundant on shortgrass prairie. Bright yellow flowers with occasional pink forms. Pads shrink and wrinkle over winter as a freeze-avoidance strategy.

species.name: uvas de gato
species.short_description: Dense low mat of tiny fleshy leaves smothered in bright yellow star flowers.
species.en_short_description: Dense low mat of tiny fleshy leaves smothered in bright yellow star flowers.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced from Europe and naturalised on walls, roofs and gravel. Leaves have a sharp peppery taste, hence the name.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Introduced from Europe and naturalised on walls, roofs and gravel. Leaves have a sharp peppery taste, hence the name.

species.name: conchita
species.short_description: Large rosette of broad leaves coated in chalky white powder, with a tall red flower stalk.
species.en_short_description: Large rosette of broad leaves coated in chalky white powder, with a tall red flower stalk.
species.description: California. The heavy white bloom reflects sunlight and repels insects; do not rub it off. Grows on coastal cliffs and rock faces. Arching pink-red flower stems.
species.en_description: California. The heavy white bloom reflects sunlight and repels insects; do not rub it off. Grows on coastal cliffs and rock faces. Arching pink-red flower stems.

species.name: Mountain Ball Cactus
species.short_description: Small spherical cactus with dense radiating spines, at high elevation.
species.en_short_description: Small spherical cactus with dense radiating spines, at high elevation.
species.description: Colorado. One of the hardiest cacti, growing in mountain grassland and gravel above 3,000 metres. Pink to yellow-green flowers open at the crown in early summer.
species.en_description: Colorado. One of the hardiest cacti, growing in mountain grassland and gravel above 3,000 metres. Pink to yellow-green flowers open at the crown in early summer.

species.name: Choya diamante
species.short_description: Sparse cholla with very thin pencil-like grey stems and few spines.
species.en_short_description: Sparse cholla with very thin pencil-like grey stems and few spines.
species.description: California. The slenderest of the chollas, with dark ashy stems that look almost dead. Grows on desert pavement. Small bronze-brown flowers.
species.en_description: California. The slenderest of the chollas, with dark ashy stems that look almost dead. Grows on desert pavement. Small bronze-brown flowers.

species.name: Siempreviva hojas de lanza
species.short_description: Rosette of narrow green-to-reddish fleshy leaves with a branched flower stalk.
species.en_short_description: Rosette of narrow green-to-reddish fleshy leaves with a branched flower stalk.
species.description: California. Grows in rock crevices and on road cuts. Less powdery than the chalk dudleya, with narrower leaves. Yellow to red star-shaped flowers.
species.en_description: California. Grows in rock crevices and on road cuts. Less powdery than the chalk dudleya, with narrower leaves. Yellow to red star-shaped flowers.

species.name: Columbia Plateau Cactus
species.short_description: Small ball cactus with stout spines, in dry scabland.
species.en_short_description: Small ball cactus with stout spines, in dry scabland.
species.description: Washington. A hardy cactus of the arid Columbia Basin, surviving cold wet winters. Grows low among basalt gravel. Magenta to yellow flowers at the crown.
species.en_description: Washington. A hardy cactus of the arid Columbia Basin, surviving cold wet winters. Grows low among basalt gravel. Magenta to yellow flowers at the crown.

species.name: Choya güera
species.short_description: Densely golden-spined cholla with a furry deceptive appearance.
species.en_short_description: Densely golden-spined cholla with a furry deceptive appearance.
species.description: California, Mexico City region and Baja. Looks soft but the barbed spines are among the worst in the desert. Reproduces almost entirely from fallen joints, forming clone stands.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City region and Baja. Looks soft but the barbed spines are among the worst in the desert. Reproduces almost entirely from fallen joints, forming clone stands.

species.name: Pacific stonecrop
species.short_description: Spreading succulent with plump blue-green leaves and clusters of yellow flowers.
species.en_short_description: Spreading succulent with plump blue-green leaves and clusters of yellow flowers.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Grows in rock crevices and on talus in mountain terrain. Leaves are noticeably fat and often red-flushed at the tips.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Grows in rock crevices and on talus in mountain terrain. Leaves are noticeably fat and often red-flushed at the tips.

species.name: Queen's Crown
species.short_description: Upright succulent stems with fleshy leaves topped by dense rose-pink flower clusters.
species.en_short_description: Upright succulent stems with fleshy leaves topped by dense rose-pink flower clusters.
species.description: Colorado. Grows in wet alpine meadows and along snowmelt streams. Foliage turns crimson in autumn. Related to the more familiar roseroots.
species.en_description: Colorado. Grows in wet alpine meadows and along snowmelt streams. Foliage turns crimson in autumn. Related to the more familiar roseroots.

species.name: Choya californiana
species.short_description: Cholla with dark purple-tinged joints and long straw spines, near the coast.
species.en_short_description: Cholla with dark purple-tinged joints and long straw spines, near the coast.
species.description: California. Grows on coastal bluffs and terraces rather than inland desert. Joints detach and root freely. Magenta flowers; fruit often proliferates into chains.
species.en_description: California. Grows on coastal bluffs and terraces rather than inland desert. Joints detach and root freely. Magenta flowers; fruit often proliferates into chains.

species.name: Biznaga barril de Baja California
species.short_description: Barrel-shaped cactus with heavy curved red-tinged spines, leaning toward the sun.
species.en_short_description: Barrel-shaped cactus with heavy curved red-tinged spines, leaning toward the sun.
species.description: California. Mature plants tilt noticeably southwest, earning the name compass cactus. Yellow flowers ring the crown. Grows on rocky desert slopes and washes.
species.en_description: California. Mature plants tilt noticeably southwest, earning the name compass cactus. Yellow flowers ring the crown. Grows on rocky desert slopes and washes.

species.name: Oregon Stonecrop
species.short_description: Rosettes of flat spoon-shaped leaves with yellow flower clusters, on wet rock.
species.en_short_description: Rosettes of flat spoon-shaped leaves with yellow flower clusters, on wet rock.
species.description: Washington. Grows on mossy rock outcrops and cliff seeps in the Northwest. Leaves are flatter and broader than most stonecrops and flush bronze in sun.
species.en_description: Washington. Grows on mossy rock outcrops and cliff seeps in the Northwest. Leaves are flatter and broader than most stonecrops and flush bronze in sun.

species.name: Brittle Pricklypear
species.short_description: Small pricklypear with easily detached rounded pads and long spines.
species.en_short_description: Small pricklypear with easily detached rounded pads and long spines.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Pads break off at a touch, which is how it spreads — and how it ends up in boot soles. The most cold-hardy North American cactus.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Pads break off at a touch, which is how it spreads — and how it ends up in boot soles. The most cold-hardy North American cactus.

species.name: Uva de gato
species.short_description: Mat-forming succulent with cylindrical leaves and clusters of small white flowers.
species.en_short_description: Mat-forming succulent with cylindrical leaves and clusters of small white flowers.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe. Colonises walls, gravel roofs and rockeries. Foliage reddens strongly in drought and cold.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced from Europe. Colonises walls, gravel roofs and rockeries. Foliage reddens strongly in drought and cold.

species.name: alicoche casa de rata
species.short_description: Clumping cylindrical cactus with stout spines, endemic to the Baja peninsula.
species.en_short_description: Clumping cylindrical cactus with stout spines, endemic to the Baja peninsula.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Forms sprawling clumps among rocks in the cape region. Magenta to pink flowers. Locally called alicoche. A peninsular endemic.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Forms sprawling clumps among rocks in the cape region. Magenta to pink flowers. Locally called alicoche. A peninsular endemic.

species.name: Biznaga barril de San José
species.short_description: Barrel cactus with strong hooked spines, endemic to southern Baja.
species.en_short_description: Barrel cactus with strong hooked spines, endemic to southern Baja.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular barrel cactus of coastal plains and rocky slopes near San José del Cabo. Yellow to red flowers ring the crown after rain.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular barrel cactus of coastal plains and rocky slopes near San José del Cabo. Yellow to red flowers ring the crown after rain.

species.name: Choya
species.short_description: Cholla of the California desert transition zone with dense spines and bronze flowers.
species.en_short_description: Cholla of the California desert transition zone with dense spines and bronze flowers.
species.description: California. A regionally restricted cholla, considered by some a hybrid lineage. Grows on desert slopes in the eastern Peninsular Ranges.
species.en_description: California. A regionally restricted cholla, considered by some a hybrid lineage. Grows on desert slopes in the eastern Peninsular Ranges.

species.name: Bluff Lettuce
species.short_description: Compact rosette of thick pale grey-green leaves on coastal rock.
species.en_short_description: Compact rosette of thick pale grey-green leaves on coastal rock.
species.description: California. Grows directly on sea cliffs and headland rock, often in salt spray. Leaves flush pink-red at the margins. Yellow flowers on short stalks.
species.en_description: California. Grows directly on sea cliffs and headland rock, often in salt spray. Leaves flush pink-red at the margins. Yellow flowers on short stalks.

species.name: Biznaga llavina
species.short_description: Small cylindrical cactus with hooked central spines and pink flowers.
species.en_short_description: Small cylindrical cactus with hooked central spines and pink flowers.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. The hooked spine is diagnostic. Grows among rocks and under shrubs. Small red fruit follows the pink funnel flowers.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. The hooked spine is diagnostic. Grows among rocks and under shrubs. Small red fruit follows the pink funnel flowers.

species.name: Canyon liveforever
species.short_description: Rosette of flat fleshy leaves in rock crevices, with yellow to red flowers.
species.en_short_description: Rosette of flat fleshy leaves in rock crevices, with yellow to red flowers.
species.description: California. Grows wedged into cliff faces and canyon walls throughout the state. Highly variable across its range. Flower stalks arch outward from the rock.
species.en_description: California. Grows wedged into cliff faces and canyon walls throughout the state. Highly variable across its range. Flower stalks arch outward from the rock.

species.name: Wormleaf Stonecrop
species.short_description: Slender succulent with very narrow cylindrical leaves and yellow flower clusters.
species.en_short_description: Slender succulent with very narrow cylindrical leaves and yellow flower clusters.
species.description: California and Washington. Leaves are narrow and worm-like, unlike the flat rosettes of other stonecrops. Grows on dry rocky slopes and outcrops.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Leaves are narrow and worm-like, unlike the flat rosettes of other stonecrops. Grows on dry rocky slopes and outcrops.

species.name: Nopal del castor
species.short_description: Spineless-looking blue-grey pads with vivid magenta flowers.
species.en_short_description: Spineless-looking blue-grey pads with vivid magenta flowers.
species.description: California. Pads lack long spines but carry dense clusters of tiny barbed glochids that are worse to remove. The magenta bloom is among the most vivid in the desert.
species.en_description: California. Pads lack long spines but carry dense clusters of tiny barbed glochids that are worse to remove. The magenta bloom is among the most vivid in the desert.

species.name: Nopal de castilla
species.short_description: Large pricklypear with big flat pads and heavy edible fruit.
species.en_short_description: Large pricklypear with big flat pads and heavy edible fruit.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. The cultivated nopal of Mexican cooking, both pads and tunas. Naturalised widely. Often nearly spineless in cultivated forms.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. The cultivated nopal of Mexican cooking, both pads and tunas. Naturalised widely. Often nearly spineless in cultivated forms.

species.name: Estrella de la tarde
species.short_description: Small ball cactus with dense star-patterned spine clusters and magenta flowers.
species.en_short_description: Small ball cactus with dense star-patterned spine clusters and magenta flowers.
species.description: Colorado and California. Grows low among prairie grass and gravel, easily overlooked until it flowers. The radiating spine clusters form neat stars.
species.en_description: Colorado and California. Grows low among prairie grass and gravel, easily overlooked until it flowers. The radiating spine clusters form neat stars.

species.name: Biznaga de brazalete
species.short_description: Small clustering cactus with hooked spines, endemic to the Baja cape.
species.en_short_description: Small clustering cactus with hooked spines, endemic to the Baja cape.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Restricted to the cape region, growing among rocks and under thornscrub. Small red-pink flowers near the stem tips. Locally called biznaga.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Restricted to the cape region, growing among rocks and under thornscrub. Small red-pink flowers near the stem tips. Locally called biznaga.

species.name: nopal raizudo
species.short_description: Low pricklypear with broad flat pads, few spines and large yellow flowers.
species.en_short_description: Low pricklypear with broad flat pads, few spines and large yellow flowers.
species.description: Colorado, California and New York. Pads are broader and less spiny than plains pricklypear. Produces juicy red-purple fruit. Hardy far north and east.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and New York. Pads are broader and less spiny than plains pricklypear. Produces juicy red-purple fruit. Hardy far north and east.

species.name: Cabeza de viejo
species.short_description: Columnar cactus with grey-green stems and a shaggy grey beard of bristles at the tips.
species.en_short_description: Columnar cactus with grey-green stems and a shaggy grey beard of bristles at the tips.
species.description: Baja California Sur. The mass of long grey bristles on flowering stem tips gives the name cabeza de viejo. Flowers open at night, pollinated by a specialised moth.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. The mass of long grey bristles on flowering stem tips gives the name cabeza de viejo. Flowers open at night, pollinated by a specialised moth.

species.name: Dedos de dama
species.short_description: Clumping succulent with narrow cylindrical finger-like leaves.
species.en_short_description: Clumping succulent with narrow cylindrical finger-like leaves.
species.description: California. Forms dense mounds of upright fleshy fingers on coastal slopes and rock. Pale yellow to red flowers. Leaves are notably round in cross-section.
species.en_description: California. Forms dense mounds of upright fleshy fingers on coastal slopes and rock. Pale yellow to red flowers. Leaves are notably round in cross-section.

species.name: Cardenche
species.short_description: Upright shrubby cholla with jointed cylindrical branches and a woody skeleton.
species.en_short_description: Upright shrubby cholla with jointed cylindrical branches and a woody skeleton.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Grows tree-like to two metres. Magenta flowers followed by persistent yellow fruit. Dead stems leave a lattice skeleton.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Grows tree-like to two metres. Magenta flowers followed by persistent yellow fruit. Dead stems leave a lattice skeleton.

species.name: siempreviva copalito
species.short_description: Small succulent shrub with a thick peeling trunk and rosettes of fleshy leaves.
species.en_short_description: Small succulent shrub with a thick peeling trunk and rosettes of fleshy leaves.
species.description: California and Mexico City. A miniature tree-form stonecrop of Mexican volcanic rock, with papery bark on a swollen stem. Grows on the Pedregal lava fields.
species.en_description: California and Mexico City. A miniature tree-form stonecrop of Mexican volcanic rock, with papery bark on a swollen stem. Grows on the Pedregal lava fields.

species.name: Pitayo dulce
species.short_description: Multiple slender columnar stems rising in a cluster from near ground level.
species.en_short_description: Multiple slender columnar stems rising in a cluster from near ground level.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Called pitayo dulce for its sweet fruit, historically a staple harvest. Flowers open at night. Forms distinctive many-armed candelabra clumps.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Called pitayo dulce for its sweet fruit, historically a staple harvest. Flowers open at night. Forms distinctive many-armed candelabra clumps.

species.name: Broad-leaved Stonecrop
species.short_description: Flat rosettes of broad spoon-shaped leaves, often chalky white, with yellow flowers.
species.en_short_description: Flat rosettes of broad spoon-shaped leaves, often chalky white, with yellow flowers.
species.description: California and Washington. Grows on shaded rock faces and mossy outcrops. The powdery white forms are especially striking. Leaves flush pink in exposed sites.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Grows on shaded rock faces and mossy outcrops. The powdery white forms are especially striking. Leaves flush pink in exposed sites.

species.name: western roseroot
species.short_description: Fleshy stems with flat blue-green leaves topped by dense dark red flower clusters.
species.en_short_description: Fleshy stems with flat blue-green leaves topped by dense dark red flower clusters.
species.description: Colorado. Grows in alpine rock crevices and wet tundra. Roots are thick and aromatic when cut. Foliage turns deep red late in the season.
species.en_description: Colorado. Grows in alpine rock crevices and wet tundra. Roots are thick and aromatic when cut. Foliage turns deep red late in the season.

species.name: Maguey pulquero
species.short_description: Massive agave with broad grey-green leaves curving inward and heavy terminal spines.
species.en_short_description: Massive agave with broad grey-green leaves curving inward and heavy terminal spines.
species.description: California and Mexico City region. Called maguey pulquero — the principal agave tapped for pulque. Flowers once after decades on a towering branched stalk, then dies.
species.en_description: California and Mexico City region. Called maguey pulquero — the principal agave tapped for pulque. Flowers once after decades on a towering branched stalk, then dies.

species.name: Maguey del desierto
species.short_description: Compact agave with stiff grey leaves, marginal teeth and a tall unbranched flower spike.
species.en_short_description: Compact agave with stiff grey leaves, marginal teeth and a tall unbranched flower spike.
species.description: California. Grows on desert slopes and bajadas. Flowering stalks rise three to four metres with dense yellow flowers. Roasted hearts were an important food.
species.en_description: California. Grows on desert slopes and bajadas. Flowering stalks rise three to four metres with dense yellow flowers. Roasted hearts were an important food.

species.name: Lechuguilla
species.short_description: Agave with broad yellow-green leaves and a branched flowering stalk, endemic to the cape.
species.en_short_description: Agave with broad yellow-green leaves and a branched flowering stalk, endemic to the cape.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Endemic to the peninsula's cape region, growing on rocky slopes and arroyo banks. Golden flowers on a tall panicle. Used locally for distillates.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Endemic to the peninsula's cape region, growing on rocky slopes and arroyo banks. Golden flowers on a tall panicle. Used locally for distillates.

species.name: mezcal
species.short_description: Small to medium agave with narrow toothed leaves, endemic to southern Baja.
species.en_short_description: Small to medium agave with narrow toothed leaves, endemic to southern Baja.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A cape-region endemic of rocky desert slopes. Smaller than most agaves, forming offsets into clumps. Yellow flowers on a slender spike.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A cape-region endemic of rocky desert slopes. Smaller than most agaves, forming offsets into clumps. Yellow flowers on a slender spike.

species.name: Maguey Blanco
species.short_description: Very large agave with sprawling grey-blue leaves and a huge branched flower stalk.
species.en_short_description: Very large agave with sprawling grey-blue leaves and a huge branched flower stalk.
species.description: California and Mexico City region. Widely planted and naturalised worldwide. Flowers once after many years on a stalk up to eight metres, then dies leaving offsets.
species.en_description: California and Mexico City region. Widely planted and naturalised worldwide. Flowers once after many years on a stalk up to eight metres, then dies leaving offsets.

species.name: Maguey de Baja California
species.short_description: Agave with pale glaucous leaves and a tall branched inflorescence, endemic to Baja.
species.en_short_description: Agave with pale glaucous leaves and a tall branched inflorescence, endemic to Baja.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Endemic to the peninsula around La Paz and the Sierra de la Giganta, on rocky slopes and cliffs. Distinctly waxy blue-grey leaves.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Endemic to the peninsula around La Paz and the Sierra de la Giganta, on rocky slopes and cliffs. Distinctly waxy blue-grey leaves.

species.name: Yuca de las grandes planicies
species.short_description: Clump of stiff narrow blue-green blades with a spike of waxy cream bells.
species.en_short_description: Clump of stiff narrow blue-green blades with a spike of waxy cream bells.
species.description: Colorado. A prairie yucca with fibrous leaf margins that peel into curling threads. Pollinated exclusively by yucca moths. Flower stalks rise a metre or more.
species.en_description: Colorado. A prairie yucca with fibrous leaf margins that peel into curling threads. Pollinated exclusively by yucca moths. Flower stalks rise a metre or more.

species.name: Yuca de chaparral
species.short_description: Dense sphere of rigid grey dagger leaves with a towering flower spike.
species.en_short_description: Dense sphere of rigid grey dagger leaves with a towering flower spike.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Also called our Lord's candle. Grows for years as a spiny ball, then sends up a three-metre flower mast, blooms once and dies.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Also called our Lord's candle. Grows for years as a spiny ball, then sends up a three-metre flower mast, blooms once and dies.

species.name: gallo
species.short_description: Tufted grass with flattened stem bases and one-sided clumped flower panicles.
species.en_short_description: Tufted grass with flattened stem bases and one-sided clumped flower panicles.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced as forage and now widespread on roadsides and meadows. The distinctly flattened shoot base and lopsided seed head are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced as forage and now widespread on roadsides and meadows. The distinctly flattened shoot base and lopsided seed head are diagnostic.

species.name: Zacate africano
species.short_description: Ornamental bunchgrass with arching purple-pink bottlebrush flower spikes.
species.en_short_description: Ornamental bunchgrass with arching purple-pink bottlebrush flower spikes.
species.description: California, New York, Mexico City and Baja. Escaped from landscaping and now seriously invasive in dry regions, where it carries fire into desert scrub.
species.en_description: California, New York, Mexico City and Baja. Escaped from landscaping and now seriously invasive in dry regions, where it carries fire into desert scrub.

species.name: Carrizo
species.short_description: Very tall reed with broad leaves and large feathery purple-brown plumes.
species.en_short_description: Very tall reed with broad leaves and large feathery purple-brown plumes.
species.description: All six regions. Forms dense monocultures in marsh and ditch. The aggressive introduced lineage displaces native wetland plants; a native lineage also exists.
species.en_description: All six regions. Forms dense monocultures in marsh and ditch. The aggressive introduced lineage displaces native wetland plants; a native lineage also exists.

species.name: Cebadilla ratonera
species.short_description: Annual grass with a flat bristly barley-like spike that breaks into barbed segments.
species.en_short_description: Annual grass with a flat bristly barley-like spike that breaks into barbed segments.
species.description: All six regions. Introduced and abundant on pavement edges and vacant lots. The barbed segments work into socks, fur and dogs' ears.
species.en_description: All six regions. Introduced and abundant on pavement edges and vacant lots. The barbed segments work into socks, fur and dogs' ears.

species.name: bromo suave
species.short_description: Sod-forming grass with smooth stems and open drooping panicles, often purple-tinged.
species.en_short_description: Sod-forming grass with smooth stems and open drooping panicles, often purple-tinged.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced for pasture and now dominant in many grasslands, where it crowds out native prairie species.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced for pasture and now dominant in many grasslands, where it crowds out native prairie species.

species.name: Pasto africano rosado
species.short_description: Slender annual grass with fluffy rose-pink flower heads fading to silver.
species.en_short_description: Slender annual grass with fluffy rose-pink flower heads fading to silver.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced from Africa and invasive on disturbed dry ground. The bright pink haze of flowering stands is unmistakable.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Introduced from Africa and invasive on disturbed dry ground. The bright pink haze of flowering stands is unmistakable.

species.name: Zacate africano plumoso
species.short_description: Bunchgrass with tall soft white feathery plumes.
species.en_short_description: Bunchgrass with tall soft white feathery plumes.
species.description: Colorado, California and Mexico City. Introduced as an ornamental and naturalised on roadsides. Plumes are paler and softer than fountain grass, ageing to cream.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Mexico City. Introduced as an ornamental and naturalised on roadsides. Plumes are paler and softer than fountain grass, ageing to cream.

species.name: pasto buffel
species.short_description: Coarse tussock grass with bristly grey-purple cylindrical seed heads.
species.en_short_description: Coarse tussock grass with bristly grey-purple cylindrical seed heads.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Introduced for cattle forage and now one of the most damaging desert invaders, fuelling fires that kill cacti.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Introduced for cattle forage and now one of the most damaging desert invaders, fuelling fires that kill cacti.

species.name: Lágrimas
species.short_description: Annual grass with large flattened papery spikelets dangling on thread-like stalks.
species.en_short_description: Annual grass with large flattened papery spikelets dangling on thread-like stalks.
species.description: California and Washington. Introduced from the Mediterranean. The oversized nodding spikelets rattle audibly in wind and dry to a straw colour.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Introduced from the Mediterranean. The oversized nodding spikelets rattle audibly in wind and dry to a straw colour.

species.name: Pasto espiguilla
species.short_description: Soft annual grass with drooping purple-tinged nodding panicles, drying early to red-brown.
species.en_short_description: Soft annual grass with drooping purple-tinged nodding panicles, drying early to red-brown.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and transformative: it cures early and carries fire through sagebrush that cannot regenerate fast enough.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and transformative: it cures early and carries fire through sagebrush that cannot regenerate fast enough.

species.name: Carrizo asiático gigante
species.short_description: Enormous bamboo-like grass with thick canes several metres tall.
species.en_short_description: Enormous bamboo-like grass with thick canes several metres tall.
species.description: All six regions. Introduced and highly invasive along watercourses, where it consumes water and chokes channels. Canes were traditionally used for reeds and roofing.
species.en_description: All six regions. Introduced and highly invasive along watercourses, where it consumes water and chokes channels. Canes were traditionally used for reeds and roofing.

species.name: Huizapol
species.short_description: Low wiry rhizomatous grass with stiff blades, in saline soils.
species.en_short_description: Low wiry rhizomatous grass with stiff blades, in saline soils.
species.description: All six regions. Tolerates high salinity by excreting salt crystals onto its leaves, which can be seen and tasted. Forms turf on salt flats and marsh margins.
species.en_description: All six regions. Tolerates high salinity by excreting salt crystals onto its leaves, which can be seen and tasted. Forms turf on salt flats and marsh margins.

species.name: Alpiste Cinta
species.short_description: Tall robust grass with broad flat blades and a narrow spreading panicle.
species.en_short_description: Tall robust grass with broad flat blades and a narrow spreading panicle.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and invasive in wetlands, forming dense stands that exclude everything else. Panicles turn straw-purple.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced and invasive in wetlands, forming dense stands that exclude everything else. Panicles turn straw-purple.

species.name: Grama cebollera
species.short_description: Small grass whose flower head produces purple bulblets instead of ordinary seeds.
