species.en_short_description: Small grass whose flower head produces purple bulblets instead of ordinary seeds.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced. The head of tiny plantlets with dark purple bases is unique and unmistakable. Dies back by early summer.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced. The head of tiny plantlets with dark purple bases is unique and unmistakable. Dies back by early summer.

species.name: Tigrillo ruso del norte
species.short_description: Bunchgrass with a distinctly flattened comb-like spike.
species.en_short_description: Bunchgrass with a distinctly flattened comb-like spike.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Introduced from Eurasia and widely sown for rangeland reclamation, where it persists and resists native reestablishment.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Introduced from Eurasia and widely sown for rangeland reclamation, where it persists and resists native reestablishment.

species.name: Pasto de terciopelo
species.short_description: Soft velvety grass with grey-green hairy leaves and pinkish-white panicles.
species.en_short_description: Soft velvety grass with grey-green hairy leaves and pinkish-white panicles.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced. The whole plant is densely soft-hairy, so it feels like felt. Common in damp meadows and pasture.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced. The whole plant is densely soft-hairy, so it feels like felt. Common in damp meadows and pasture.

species.name: Navajita
species.short_description: Short bunchgrass with one to three curved comb-like seed spikes resembling eyebrows.
species.en_short_description: Short bunchgrass with one to three curved comb-like seed spikes resembling eyebrows.
species.description: Five regions. The dominant native shortgrass of the Colorado plains and a state grass of New Mexico. The eyelash-shaped one-sided spikes are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Five regions. The dominant native shortgrass of the Colorado plains and a state grass of New Mexico. The eyelash-shaped one-sided spikes are diagnostic.

species.name: cebada cimarrona
species.short_description: Grass with a soft nodding brush of long silky awns, often flushed pink.
species.en_short_description: Grass with a soft nodding brush of long silky awns, often flushed pink.
species.description: Five regions. Native and beautiful in low light, but the barbed awns injure grazing livestock. Abundant in alkaline soils, ditches and roadsides.
species.en_description: Five regions. Native and beautiful in low light, but the barbed awns injure grazing livestock. Abundant in alkaline soils, ditches and roadsides.

species.name: cadillo huizapol
species.short_description: Low annual grass with spiny burs that cling to clothing and fur.
species.en_short_description: Low annual grass with spiny burs that cling to clothing and fur.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A desert sandbur of coastal dunes and sandy flats. The spiny bur enclosing the seed is the plant's dispersal mechanism and its nuisance.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A desert sandbur of coastal dunes and sandy flats. The spiny bur enclosing the seed is the plant's dispersal mechanism and its nuisance.

species.name: Pasto pampa
species.short_description: Massive tussock with sharp-edged leaves and towering silvery-white plumes.
species.en_short_description: Massive tussock with sharp-edged leaves and towering silvery-white plumes.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced ornamental, invasive on the California coast. Leaf edges cut skin. Plumes rise well over two metres.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced ornamental, invasive on the California coast. Leaf edges cut skin. Plumes rise well over two metres.

species.name: Cola de zorra
species.short_description: Small annual grass with a soft dense silky-bristled cylindrical head.
species.en_short_description: Small annual grass with a soft dense silky-bristled cylindrical head.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and common in damp disturbed ground, ditches and pond margins. The plush bottlebrush head is soft to the touch, unlike barley spikes.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and common in damp disturbed ground, ditches and pond margins. The plush bottlebrush head is soft to the touch, unlike barley spikes.

species.name: Barbas de macho
species.short_description: Softly hairy annual brome with a compact erect panicle.
species.en_short_description: Softly hairy annual brome with a compact erect panicle.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced and abundant in grassland and verges. Softer-hairy and more compact-headed than other bromes. Dries early.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced and abundant in grassland and verges. Softer-hairy and more compact-headed than other bromes. Dries early.

species.name: Jouvea pilosa
species.short_description: Coarse coastal grass with stiff spreading stems, on Baja beaches and dunes.
species.en_short_description: Coarse coastal grass with stiff spreading stems, on Baja beaches and dunes.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A salt-tolerant coastal grass of the Pacific peninsula shoreline, binding beach sand. Male and female plants are separate and look quite different.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A salt-tolerant coastal grass of the Pacific peninsula shoreline, binding beach sand. Male and female plants are separate and look quite different.

species.name: Bromo
species.short_description: Tall annual brome with very long drooping awns and a nodding open panicle.
species.en_short_description: Tall annual brome with very long drooping awns and a nodding open panicle.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced. The exceptionally long stiff awns catch in socks and pet fur. Also called ripgut brome.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Introduced. The exceptionally long stiff awns catch in socks and pet fur. Also called ripgut brome.

species.name: American lyme grass
species.short_description: Stout blue-grey coastal grass with thick spikes, on beach sand.
species.en_short_description: Stout blue-grey coastal grass with thick spikes, on beach sand.
species.description: California and Washington. A native dune-binding grass with broad glaucous leaves. Grows in the loose sand above the strand line, spreading by strong rhizomes.
species.en_description: California and Washington. A native dune-binding grass with broad glaucous leaves. Grows in the loose sand above the strand line, spreading by strong rhizomes.

species.name: zacate primavera
species.short_description: Slender grass with a narrow spike-like panicle, smelling of hay when crushed.
species.en_short_description: Slender grass with a narrow spike-like panicle, smelling of hay when crushed.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced. Contains coumarin, giving fresh-cut grass its characteristic sweet hay scent. One of the earliest grasses to flower.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Introduced. Contains coumarin, giving fresh-cut grass its characteristic sweet hay scent. One of the earliest grasses to flower.

species.name: giant wild rye
species.short_description: Very large native bunchgrass with thick dense spikes on tall stems.
species.en_short_description: Very large native bunchgrass with thick dense spikes on tall stems.
species.description: California and Washington. Forms substantial clumps on coastal slopes and canyon bottoms. Once far more widespread in California grassland before grazing reduced it.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Forms substantial clumps on coastal slopes and canyon bottoms. Once far more widespread in California grassland before grazing reduced it.

species.name: Gallitos
species.short_description: Low creeping turf grass with finger-like radiating seed spikes.
species.en_short_description: Low creeping turf grass with finger-like radiating seed spikes.
species.description: All six regions. Introduced lawn and pasture grass, now a persistent weed. Spreads by both above-ground runners and rhizomes. The digitate seed head is diagnostic.
species.en_description: All six regions. Introduced lawn and pasture grass, now a persistent weed. Spreads by both above-ground runners and rhizomes. The digitate seed head is diagnostic.

species.name: Triguillo desértico
species.short_description: Bunchgrass with a bushy spike of widely spreading bristly awns.
species.en_short_description: Bunchgrass with a bushy spike of widely spreading bristly awns.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. A valuable native bunchgrass of sagebrush country. The spike breaks up into barbed units that screw into soil to plant themselves.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. A valuable native bunchgrass of sagebrush country. The spike breaks up into barbed units that screw into soil to plant themselves.

species.name: grama estrellada
species.short_description: Annual grass with a dense one-sided bristly ovate flower cluster.
species.en_short_description: Annual grass with a dense one-sided bristly ovate flower cluster.
species.description: California and Washington. Introduced from the Mediterranean. The lopsided prickly head on a slender stem is distinctive. Common on dry banks and roadsides.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Introduced from the Mediterranean. The lopsided prickly head on a slender stem is distinctive. Common on dry banks and roadsides.

species.name: Arroz indio
species.short_description: Airy bunchgrass with a very open, finely branched, almost cloud-like panicle.
species.en_short_description: Airy bunchgrass with a very open, finely branched, almost cloud-like panicle.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. A native grass of sandy soils, also called Indian ricegrass. Seeds were an important traditional food. The delicate panicle catches light.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. A native grass of sandy soils, also called Indian ricegrass. Seeds were an important traditional food. The delicate panicle catches light.

species.name: Gulf Grama
species.short_description: Small grama grass with slender curved one-sided spikes, on Baja slopes.
species.en_short_description: Small grama grass with slender curved one-sided spikes, on Baja slopes.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular grama of dry rocky slopes and desert grassland. Like other gramas it carries comb-like spikes along one side of the axis.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular grama of dry rocky slopes and desert grassland. Like other gramas it carries comb-like spikes along one side of the axis.

species.name: Red Brome
species.short_description: Small annual brome with a dense reddish-purple compact panicle.
species.en_short_description: Small annual brome with a dense reddish-purple compact panicle.
species.description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Introduced and a major desert fire fuel. Dries early to a distinct rusty red, colouring whole slopes.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Introduced and a major desert fire fuel. Dries early to a distinct rusty red, colouring whole slopes.

species.name: zacate timothy
species.short_description: Grass with a long dense cylindrical spike-like head on a stiff stem.
species.en_short_description: Grass with a long dense cylindrical spike-like head on a stiff stem.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced hay grass, naturalised widely. The narrow cat-tail-like head is unmistakable. A significant hay-fever allergen.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Introduced hay grass, naturalised widely. The narrow cat-tail-like head is unmistakable. A significant hay-fever allergen.

species.name: Pasto pata de pollo
species.short_description: Low annual grass with two to five stiff radiating spikes at the stem tip.
species.en_short_description: Low annual grass with two to five stiff radiating spikes at the stem tip.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Introduced from Africa and naturalised in warm disturbed ground. The spikes radiate like a bird's foot, each with crowded flat spikelets.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Introduced from Africa and naturalised in warm disturbed ground. The spikes radiate like a bird's foot, each with crowded flat spikelets.

species.name: Pasto de pantano salado
species.short_description: Low mat-forming saline grass with short stiff blades, on tidal flats.
species.en_short_description: Low mat-forming saline grass with short stiff blades, on tidal flats.
species.description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Forms low turf on salt flats and estuarine margins. Extremely salt-tolerant, spreading by tough runners.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Baja California Sur. Forms low turf on salt flats and estuarine margins. Extremely salt-tolerant, spreading by tough runners.

species.name: Navajita
species.short_description: Small annual grama with several short curved spikes, appearing quickly after rain.
species.en_short_description: Small annual grama with several short curved spikes, appearing quickly after rain.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Completes its life cycle in about six weeks following desert rain, hence the name. Forms a brief green flush on desert flats.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Completes its life cycle in about six weeks following desert rain, hence the name. Forms a brief green flush on desert flats.

species.name: Zacate azul
species.short_description: Small soft bright green annual grass with an open triangular panicle.
species.en_short_description: Small soft bright green annual grass with an open triangular panicle.
species.description: Five regions. Introduced and one of the most widespread plants on earth, in lawns, cracks and paths. Flowers almost year-round wherever it is not frozen.
species.en_description: Five regions. Introduced and one of the most widespread plants on earth, in lawns, cracks and paths. Flowers almost year-round wherever it is not frozen.

species.name: Banderilla
species.short_description: Grass with numerous small spikes hanging along one side of a slender arching stem.
species.en_short_description: Grass with numerous small spikes hanging along one side of a slender arching stem.
species.description: Five regions. A native prairie grass with a distinctive one-sided arrangement of oat-like spikelets. Anthers are bright orange when flowering.
species.en_description: Five regions. A native prairie grass with a distinctive one-sided arrangement of oat-like spikelets. Anthers are bright orange when flowering.

species.name: Navajita aguja
species.short_description: Small annual grama with sharply pointed spikelets that cluster into needle-like units.
species.en_short_description: Small annual grama with sharply pointed spikelets that cluster into needle-like units.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. A desert grama that dries to a sharp bristly state. Seed units are barbed and catch readily in socks and fur.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. A desert grama that dries to a sharp bristly state. Seed units are barbed and catch readily in socks and fur.

species.name: Helecho de Espada Occidental
species.short_description: Large evergreen fern with once-divided fronds; each leaflet has a small basal thumb.
species.en_short_description: Large evergreen fern with once-divided fronds; each leaflet has a small basal thumb.
species.description: California and Washington. The dominant fern of Pacific Northwest forest floors, forming waist-high clumps. The hilt-like lobe at each leaflet base is the field mark.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The dominant fern of Pacific Northwest forest floors, forming waist-high clumps. The hilt-like lobe at each leaflet base is the field mark.

species.name: helecho águila
species.short_description: Coarse fern with large triangular thrice-divided fronds on a single tall stalk.
species.en_short_description: Coarse fern with large triangular thrice-divided fronds on a single tall stalk.
species.description: Five regions. One of the most widespread plants on earth. Spreads by deep rhizomes into fields and clearings. Contains carcinogens; not a safe wild food.
species.en_description: Five regions. One of the most widespread plants on earth. Spreads by deep rhizomes into fields and clearings. Contains carcinogens; not a safe wild food.

species.name: cola de caballo de campo
species.short_description: Jointed hollow green stems in whorls of fine branches; separate pale spore stalks in spring.
species.en_short_description: Jointed hollow green stems in whorls of fine branches; separate pale spore stalks in spring.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. An ancient lineage with no true leaves. Fertile stems appear first, pale and unbranched, before the green shoots.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. An ancient lineage with no true leaves. Fertile stems appear first, pale and unbranched, before the green shoots.

species.name: Helecho dorado
species.short_description: Small drought-hardy fern with fronds coated golden-yellow beneath.
species.en_short_description: Small drought-hardy fern with fronds coated golden-yellow beneath.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Curls tightly when dry and revives after rain. The golden farina on the underside is diagnostic. Grows in rock crevices.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Curls tightly when dry and revives after rain. The golden farina on the underside is diagnostic. Grows in rock crevices.

species.name: goldback fern
species.short_description: Small triangular fern with bright yellow powder on the underside of the frond.
species.en_short_description: Small triangular fern with bright yellow powder on the underside of the frond.
species.description: California and Washington. Pressing a frond against dark cloth leaves a gold print. Curls up in summer drought and unfurls with autumn rain.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Pressing a frond against dark cloth leaves a gold print. Curls up in summer drought and unfurls with autumn rain.

species.name: sensitive fern
species.short_description: Coarse fern with broadly winged frond axes and separate bead-like fertile fronds.
species.en_short_description: Coarse fern with broadly winged frond axes and separate bead-like fertile fronds.
species.description: New York. Named for how quickly the fronds blacken at the first frost. Grows in wet meadows and ditches. Fertile fronds persist stiff and dark through winter.
species.en_description: New York. Named for how quickly the fronds blacken at the first frost. Grows in wet meadows and ditches. Fertile fronds persist stiff and dark through winter.

species.name: Lemmon's Cloak Fern
species.short_description: Small desert fern with fronds densely coated in pale waxy powder beneath.
species.en_short_description: Small desert fern with fronds densely coated in pale waxy powder beneath.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A rock-crevice fern of arid canyons. The white farinose coating reduces water loss. Fronds curl inward during drought.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A rock-crevice fern of arid canyons. The white farinose coating reduces water loss. Fronds curl inward during drought.

species.name: Baja California false cloak fern
species.short_description: Small cliff fern with white-powdered undersides, endemic to the peninsula.
species.en_short_description: Small cliff fern with white-powdered undersides, endemic to the peninsula.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular endemic of shaded rock faces and canyon walls. Very drought-tolerant, resurrecting after rain from an apparently dead state.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A peninsular endemic of shaded rock faces and canyon walls. Very drought-tolerant, resurrecting after rain from an apparently dead state.

species.name: Myriopteris peninsularis
species.short_description: Small lip fern with beaded segments, endemic to the Baja peninsula.
species.en_short_description: Small lip fern with beaded segments, endemic to the Baja peninsula.
species.description: Baja California Sur. Grows in rock crevices in the arid ranges of the peninsula. Fronds have small rounded bead-like segments and roll up in drought.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. Grows in rock crevices in the arid ranges of the peninsula. Fronds have small rounded bead-like segments and roll up in drought.

species.name: Coffee Fern
species.short_description: Wiry-stemmed fern with rounded blue-green leaflets on dark brittle stalks.
species.en_short_description: Wiry-stemmed fern with rounded blue-green leaflets on dark brittle stalks.
species.description: California. Grows on dry rocky banks and chaparral edges, unusual for a fern. The dark shining stems and round leaflets are distinctive. Drought-deciduous.
species.en_description: California. Grows on dry rocky banks and chaparral edges, unusual for a fern. The dark shining stems and round leaflets are distinctive. Drought-deciduous.

species.name: Christmas fern
species.short_description: Evergreen once-divided fern; each leaflet has a small ear at its base.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen once-divided fern; each leaflet has a small ear at its base.
species.description: New York. Stays green through winter, which is the origin of the name. The stocking-shaped leaflets with a basal lobe separate it from other eastern ferns.
species.en_description: New York. Stays green through winter, which is the origin of the name. The stocking-shaped leaflets with a basal lobe separate it from other eastern ferns.

species.name: Helecho culantrillo
species.short_description: Delicate fern with fan-shaped leaflets on glossy black wiry stalks, on wet rock.
species.en_short_description: Delicate fern with fan-shaped leaflets on glossy black wiry stalks, on wet rock.
species.description: Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. Grows at seeps, springs and travertine faces, often where water drips constantly. Fronds arch outward from the rock.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Mexico City and Baja. Grows at seeps, springs and travertine faces, often where water drips constantly. Fronds arch outward from the rock.

species.name: Cola de caballo
species.short_description: Very stout jointed horsetail with dense whorls of fine branches, forming tall thickets.
species.en_short_description: Very stout jointed horsetail with dense whorls of fine branches, forming tall thickets.
species.description: California and Washington. The largest North American horsetail, reaching well over a metre. Grows in wet ditches and seeps. Pale unbranched fertile shoots in spring.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The largest North American horsetail, reaching well over a metre. Grows in wet ditches and seeps. Pale unbranched fertile shoots in spring.

species.name: California Maidenhair Fern
species.short_description: Fern with fan-shaped leaflets on black stalks, dying back in summer.
species.en_short_description: Fern with fan-shaped leaflets on black stalks, dying back in summer.
species.description: California. Grows on shaded stream banks and canyon walls. Drought-deciduous, disappearing entirely in dry months and returning with winter rain.
species.en_description: California. Grows on shaded stream banks and canyon walls. Drought-deciduous, disappearing entirely in dry months and returning with winter rain.

species.name: coastal woodfern
species.short_description: Robust fern with twice-divided fronds and toothed spiny-tipped leaflets.
species.en_short_description: Robust fern with twice-divided fronds and toothed spiny-tipped leaflets.
species.description: California and Washington. Grows on shaded slopes and among rocks in coastal woodland. Coarser and more finely cut than sword fern, with a leathery texture.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Grows on shaded slopes and among rocks in coastal woodland. Coarser and more finely cut than sword fern, with a leathery texture.

species.name: western maidenhair fern
species.short_description: Fern with fronds spreading in a flat fan from the top of a black stalk.
species.en_short_description: Fern with fronds spreading in a flat fan from the top of a black stalk.
species.description: California and Washington. The distinctive palmate arrangement, with all branches radiating from one point, separates it from other maidenhairs. Grows at wet seeps.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The distinctive palmate arrangement, with all branches radiating from one point, separates it from other maidenhairs. Grows at wet seeps.

species.name: helecho de tres hojas
species.short_description: Small stiff fern with leaflets in threes on dark wiry stalks.
species.en_short_description: Small stiff fern with leaflets in threes on dark wiry stalks.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A rock-crevice fern of arid highlands. Leaflets are narrow and leathery, arranged in threes along the frond.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A rock-crevice fern of arid highlands. Leaflets are narrow and leathery, arranged in threes along the frond.

species.name: giant chain fern
species.short_description: Very large fern with once-divided fronds reaching two metres, spore cases in chains.
species.en_short_description: Very large fern with once-divided fronds reaching two metres, spore cases in chains.
species.description: California and Washington. The largest fern in North America. Spore cases form chain-like rows along the veins, which gives the name. Grows at springs and seeps.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The largest fern in North America. Spore cases form chain-like rows along the veins, which gives the name. Grows at springs and seeps.

species.name: lonchite
species.short_description: Fern with two frond types: spreading sterile fronds and stiff upright fertile ones.
species.en_short_description: Fern with two frond types: spreading sterile fronds and stiff upright fertile ones.
species.description: California and Washington. The dimorphic fronds are diagnostic — a flat rosette with erect narrow spore-bearing fronds standing in the centre. Prefers damp acidic forest.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The dimorphic fronds are diagnostic — a flat rosette with erect narrow spore-bearing fronds standing in the centre. Prefers damp acidic forest.

species.name: Helecho pata de pájaro
species.short_description: Small stiff grey-green fern with narrow leaflets clustered like a bird's foot.
species.en_short_description: Small stiff grey-green fern with narrow leaflets clustered like a bird's foot.
species.description: California. Grows in dry rock crevices in chaparral and foothill woodland. Leaflets are firm and pointed, arranged in threes at the frond tips.
species.en_description: California. Grows in dry rock crevices in chaparral and foothill woodland. Leaflets are firm and pointed, arranged in threes at the frond tips.

species.name: ítamo real
species.short_description: Rock fern with heart-shaped leathery leaflets on dark stalks.
species.en_short_description: Rock fern with heart-shaped leathery leaflets on dark stalks.
species.description: Mexico City region. Grows in crevices on shaded volcanic rock and cliff faces in the highlands. The cordate leaflet bases give the name.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Grows in crevices on shaded volcanic rock and cliff faces in the highlands. The cordate leaflet bases give the name.

species.name: Helecho perejil
species.short_description: Small delicate fern with finely divided fronds and brittle straw-coloured stalks.
species.en_short_description: Small delicate fern with finely divided fronds and brittle straw-coloured stalks.
species.description: All six regions. The most widespread fern here, growing in rock crevices from desert canyons to alpine talus. Fronds break easily, hence the name.
species.en_description: All six regions. The most widespread fern here, growing in rock crevices from desert canyons to alpine talus. Fronds break easily, hence the name.

species.name: California Cloak-fern
species.short_description: Tiny desert fern with white or yellowish powder on the frond underside.
species.en_short_description: Tiny desert fern with white or yellowish powder on the frond underside.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Grows in crevices on desert rock. The farinose coating varies from cream to gold. Survives long drought fully desiccated.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Grows in crevices on desert rock. The farinose coating varies from cream to gold. Survives long drought fully desiccated.

species.name: Helecho de Regaliz
species.short_description: Once-divided fern growing from mossy tree trunks, with a sweet-tasting rhizome.
species.en_short_description: Once-divided fern growing from mossy tree trunks, with a sweet-tasting rhizome.
species.description: California and Washington. Grows as an epiphyte on bigleaf maple branches and mossy rock. The rhizome tastes distinctly of licorice. Dies back in summer drought.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Grows as an epiphyte on bigleaf maple branches and mossy rock. The rhizome tastes distinctly of licorice. Dies back in summer drought.

species.name: lady fern
species.short_description: Lacy twice- to thrice-divided fern in graceful upright clumps.
species.en_short_description: Lacy twice- to thrice-divided fern in graceful upright clumps.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Grows in moist forest, seeps and streamsides. Fronds are notably delicate and finely cut, tapering at both ends.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Grows in moist forest, seeps and streamsides. Fronds are notably delicate and finely cut, tapering at both ends.

species.name: Patitas negras
species.short_description: Fine maidenhair with small overlapping fan-shaped leaflets on dark stalks.
species.en_short_description: Fine maidenhair with small overlapping fan-shaped leaflets on dark stalks.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Grows on damp shaded rock and walls in the highlands and canyon oases. Fronds are notably soft and drooping.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Grows on damp shaded rock and walls in the highlands and canyon oases. Fronds are notably soft and drooping.

species.name: California Polypody
species.short_description: Simple once-divided fern with a leathery frond, growing on rock and mossy trunks.
species.en_short_description: Simple once-divided fern with a leathery frond, growing on rock and mossy trunks.
species.description: California. Appears with winter rain and dies back in summer. Round spore cases sit in two rows on the underside. Grows on shaded rock faces and in oak duff.
species.en_description: California. Appears with winter rain and dies back in summer. Round spore cases sit in two rows on the underside. Grows on shaded rock faces and in oak duff.

species.name: Caña carricillo
species.short_description: Slender green jointed stems with few or no branches and dark-banded joints.
species.en_short_description: Slender green jointed stems with few or no branches and dark-banded joints.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Grows in damp sandy soil and ditches. Nearly unbranched, so it looks like a stand of green rods.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Grows in damp sandy soil and ditches. Nearly unbranched, so it looks like a stand of green rods.

species.name: intermediate wood fern
species.short_description: Evergreen fern with lacy thrice-divided fronds and glandular hairs.
species.en_short_description: Evergreen fern with lacy thrice-divided fronds and glandular hairs.
species.description: New York. Common in rich eastern woodland. Stays green over winter, flattening under snow. Distinguished from close relatives by fine glandular hairs on the axes.
species.en_description: New York. Common in rich eastern woodland. Stays green over winter, flattening under snow. Distinguished from close relatives by fine glandular hairs on the axes.

species.name: American parsley fern
species.short_description: Small fern whose sterile fronds look like flat parsley and fertile fronds are narrower.
species.en_short_description: Small fern whose sterile fronds look like flat parsley and fertile fronds are narrower.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Grows in rock crevices and talus in mountain terrain. The two frond types differ noticeably, the fertile ones taller and narrower.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Grows in rock crevices and talus in mountain terrain. The two frond types differ noticeably, the fertile ones taller and narrower.

species.name: Asplenium blepharodes
species.short_description: Small spleenwort with narrow once-divided fronds, on Baja rock.
species.en_short_description: Small spleenwort with narrow once-divided fronds, on Baja rock.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A crevice fern of shaded canyon rock in the peninsular ranges. Spore cases form narrow lines along the veins, typical of spleenworts.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A crevice fern of shaded canyon rock in the peninsular ranges. Spore cases form narrow lines along the veins, typical of spleenworts.

species.name: Helecho culantrillo
species.short_description: Maidenhair with small fan-shaped leaflets on fine black stalks.
species.en_short_description: Maidenhair with small fan-shaped leaflets on fine black stalks.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Grows on damp shaded rock, walls and springs in the highlands. Delicate arching fronds; smaller than the black maidenhair.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. Grows on damp shaded rock, walls and springs in the highlands. Delicate arching fronds; smaller than the black maidenhair.

species.name: helecho trébol de agua
species.short_description: Aquatic fern that looks exactly like a four-leaf clover floating on water.
species.en_short_description: Aquatic fern that looks exactly like a four-leaf clover floating on water.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. A true fern despite appearances, with four wedge-shaped leaflets. Grows in seasonal pools and pond margins.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. A true fern despite appearances, with four wedge-shaped leaflets. Grows in seasonal pools and pond margins.

species.name: marginal wood fern
species.short_description: Leathery blue-green evergreen fern with spore cases right at the leaflet margins.
species.en_short_description: Leathery blue-green evergreen fern with spore cases right at the leaflet margins.
species.description: New York. The marginal position of the round spore cases is diagnostic and easy to check. Grows on rocky wooded slopes and ledges. Fronds are thick and leathery.
species.en_description: New York. The marginal position of the round spore cases is diagnostic and easy to check. Grows on rocky wooded slopes and ledges. Fronds are thick and leathery.

species.name: hay-scented fern
species.short_description: Yellow-green lacy fern smelling of cut hay when crushed, forming dense colonies.
species.en_short_description: Yellow-green lacy fern smelling of cut hay when crushed, forming dense colonies.
species.description: New York. Spreads aggressively by rhizomes into forest openings, forming carpets that inhibit tree seedlings. The hay scent when bruised confirms it.
species.en_description: New York. Spreads aggressively by rhizomes into forest openings, forming carpets that inhibit tree seedlings. The hay scent when bruised confirms it.

species.name: Caña carricillo
species.short_description: Stiff unbranched evergreen green stems with dark joints, growing in dense stands.
species.en_short_description: Stiff unbranched evergreen green stems with dark joints, growing in dense stands.
species.description: Five regions. Also called scouring rush; silica in the stems made it a traditional pot scourer. Grows in wet sand and along ditches. Stays green all year.
species.en_description: Five regions. Also called scouring rush; silica in the stems made it a traditional pot scourer. Grows in wet sand and along ditches. Stays green all year.

species.name: New York fern
species.short_description: Light green fern whose fronds taper to a point at both ends.
species.en_short_description: Light green fern whose fronds taper to a point at both ends.
species.description: New York. The double taper, narrowing gradually to nothing at the base, is the reliable field mark. Forms extensive colonies in eastern woodland.
species.en_description: New York. The double taper, narrowing gradually to nothing at the base, is the reliable field mark. Forms extensive colonies in eastern woodland.

species.name: cinnamon fern
species.short_description: Large fern with vase-like sterile fronds and separate cinnamon-brown fertile spikes.
species.en_short_description: Large fern with vase-like sterile fronds and separate cinnamon-brown fertile spikes.
species.description: New York. Tufts of rusty wool at each leaflet base are diagnostic. The fertile fronds stand in the middle of the crown and turn cinnamon. Grows in swamps and wet woods.
species.en_description: New York. Tufts of rusty wool at each leaflet base are diagnostic. The fertile fronds stand in the middle of the crown and turn cinnamon. Grows in swamps and wet woods.

species.name: Showy Maiden Fern
species.short_description: Fern with once-divided fronds and softly hairy axes, at seeps and springs.
species.en_short_description: Fern with once-divided fronds and softly hairy axes, at seeps and springs.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Grows in permanently wet rock seeps and canyon oases. Fronds are soft-textured with fine hairs along the axis.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Grows in permanently wet rock seeps and canyon oases. Fronds are soft-textured with fine hairs along the axis.

species.name: ebony spleenwort
species.short_description: Small fern with a shining dark purple-brown stalk and neat paired leaflets with basal ears.
species.en_short_description: Small fern with a shining dark purple-brown stalk and neat paired leaflets with basal ears.
species.description: Colorado and New York. The polished dark stalk is diagnostic. Grows on rocky banks, walls and limestone. Evergreen fertile fronds stand upright.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. The polished dark stalk is diagnostic. Grows on rocky banks, walls and limestone. Evergreen fertile fronds stand upright.

species.name: Musgo plateado
species.short_description: Tiny silvery-white cushions in pavement cracks and on concrete.
species.en_short_description: Tiny silvery-white cushions in pavement cracks and on concrete.
species.description: Five regions and the most-observed moss here. Leaf tips are colourless, giving the whole cushion a metallic silver sheen. Thrives on the harshest urban surfaces.
species.en_description: Five regions and the most-observed moss here. Leaf tips are colourless, giving the whole cushion a metallic silver sheen. Thrives on the harshest urban surfaces.

species.name: stairstep moss
species.short_description: Feathery moss whose shoots grow in distinct annual tiers like a staircase.
species.en_short_description: Feathery moss whose shoots grow in distinct annual tiers like a staircase.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Each year's growth arches from the previous one, so age can be counted in steps. Forms deep carpets in old conifer forest.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Each year's growth arches from the previous one, so age can be counted in steps. Forms deep carpets in old conifer forest.

species.name: bristly haircap moss
species.short_description: Short stiff moss with grey-tipped leaves ending in a fine colourless hair point.
species.en_short_description: Short stiff moss with grey-tipped leaves ending in a fine colourless hair point.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Grows on dry sand and thin gravelly soil. The whitish hair tips give the turf a hoary appearance.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Grows on dry sand and thin gravelly soil. The whitish hair tips give the turf a hoary appearance.

species.name: Streamside Leptodictyum Moss
species.short_description: Loose sprawling green moss on wet wood and rock at water's edge.
species.en_short_description: Loose sprawling green moss on wet wood and rock at water's edge.
species.description: Five regions. Grows submerged or in the splash zone of streams, ponds and ditches. Shoots are irregularly branched and limp when out of water.
species.en_description: Five regions. Grows submerged or in the splash zone of streams, ponds and ditches. Shoots are irregularly branched and limp when out of water.

species.name: Ciliate Hoarmoss
species.short_description: Grey-green moss forming rough mats on exposed rock, with hair-pointed leaves.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green moss forming rough mats on exposed rock, with hair-pointed leaves.
species.description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Looks hoary-white when dry and turns dark green within seconds of wetting. Common on boulders and outcrops.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Looks hoary-white when dry and turns dark green within seconds of wetting. Common on boulders and outcrops.

species.name: dendroalsia moss
species.short_description: Tree moss with curved frond-like shoots that curl into tight hooks when dry.
species.en_short_description: Tree moss with curved frond-like shoots that curl into tight hooks when dry.
species.description: California and Washington. Grows on oak and maple trunks. The dramatic curling when dry and unfurling when wet is the easiest way to recognise it.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Grows on oak and maple trunks. The dramatic curling when dry and unfurling when wet is the easiest way to recognise it.

species.name: brocade moss
species.short_description: Glossy golden-green moss forming flat mats on rotting wood.
species.en_short_description: Glossy golden-green moss forming flat mats on rotting wood.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Shoots are regularly branched and lie flat, with a silky sheen. Common on decaying logs and tree bases in damp forest.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. Shoots are regularly branched and lie flat, with a silky sheen. Common on decaying logs and tree bases in damp forest.

species.name: Musgo de barba
species.short_description: Small moss whose dry leaves twist into a spiral claw around the stem.
species.en_short_description: Small moss whose dry leaves twist into a spiral claw around the stem.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Grows on soil, walls and rock in dry places. The strongly twisted dry shoots and reddish capsules are diagnostic.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Grows on soil, walls and rock in dry places. The strongly twisted dry shoots and reddish capsules are diagnostic.

species.name: Water Pocket Moss
species.short_description: Small aquatic moss with leaves in a flat plane, growing submerged.
species.en_short_description: Small aquatic moss with leaves in a flat plane, growing submerged.
species.description: California, New York and Baja California Sur. Grows fully submerged on rocks and wood in ponds and slow streams. Leaves are arranged in one plane like a tiny fern frond.
species.en_description: California, New York and Baja California Sur. Grows fully submerged on rocks and wood in ponds and slow streams. Leaves are arranged in one plane like a tiny fern frond.

species.name: Ontario rhodobryum moss
species.short_description: Moss with rosettes of broad leaves at the top of an upright stem, like tiny palms.
species.en_short_description: Moss with rosettes of broad leaves at the top of an upright stem, like tiny palms.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. The rosette form is unusual and unmistakable among mosses. Grows on calcareous soil and rock in shaded woodland.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. The rosette form is unusual and unmistakable among mosses. Grows on calcareous soil and rock in shaded woodland.

species.name: Musgo estrella
species.short_description: Small moss whose leaves spread into a star when wet and twist tightly when dry.
species.en_short_description: Small moss whose leaves spread into a star when wet and twist tightly when dry.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Very drought-tolerant, common on dry soil, walls and roofs. The wet-dry transformation is dramatic and quick.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Very drought-tolerant, common on dry soil, walls and roofs. The wet-dry transformation is dramatic and quick.

species.name: Musgo hoguera
species.short_description: Short-lived moss with abundant nodding pear-shaped capsules on orange stalks.
species.en_short_description: Short-lived moss with abundant nodding pear-shaped capsules on orange stalks.
species.description: Five regions. Colonises burnt ground, ash and disturbed soil rapidly, hence the name. Often the first moss to appear on a fire scar or plant pot.
species.en_description: Five regions. Colonises burnt ground, ash and disturbed soil rapidly, hence the name. Often the first moss to appear on a fire scar or plant pot.

species.name: Musgo junípero
species.short_description: Stiff upright moss with bluish leaves whose reddish tips fold inward when dry.
species.en_short_description: Stiff upright moss with bluish leaves whose reddish tips fold inward when dry.
species.description: Five regions. Grows on dry acidic soil, sandy banks and burnt ground. Male plants bear conspicuous orange-red splash cups at the shoot tips.
species.en_description: Five regions. Grows on dry acidic soil, sandy banks and burnt ground. Male plants bear conspicuous orange-red splash cups at the shoot tips.

species.name: delicate fern moss
species.short_description: Finely triple-branched feathery moss forming soft flat green mats.
species.en_short_description: Finely triple-branched feathery moss forming soft flat green mats.
species.description: California, New York and Mexico City. The three-times-divided branching pattern gives an intricate fern-like texture. Grows on soil, logs and rock in shade.
species.en_description: California, New York and Mexico City. The three-times-divided branching pattern gives an intricate fern-like texture. Grows on soil, logs and rock in shade.

species.name: Oregon Beaked Moss
species.short_description: Feathery moss forming extensive flat carpets on Northwest forest floors.
species.en_short_description: Feathery moss forming extensive flat carpets on Northwest forest floors.
species.description: California and Washington. One of the dominant carpet mosses in Pacific Northwest woodland. Shoots are regularly pinnate with slender tapering branches.
species.en_description: California and Washington. One of the dominant carpet mosses in Pacific Northwest woodland. Shoots are regularly pinnate with slender tapering branches.

species.name: rough goose neck moss
species.short_description: Robust moss with strongly curved shoot tips and coarse spreading leaves.
species.en_short_description: Robust moss with strongly curved shoot tips and coarse spreading leaves.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Shoot tips arch over like a goose's neck. Leaves are pleated and turned to one side. Forms loose deep mats in forest.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Shoot tips arch over like a goose's neck. Leaves are pleated and turned to one side. Forms loose deep mats in forest.

species.name: Menzies' Tree Moss
species.short_description: Moss shaped like a miniature tree: a bare stem topped with a spreading crown.
species.en_short_description: Moss shaped like a miniature tree: a bare stem topped with a spreading crown.
species.description: California and Washington. The distinct trunk-and-canopy form is unmistakable. Grows on damp soil, rotten wood and rock in shaded Northwest forest.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The distinct trunk-and-canopy form is unmistakable. Grows on damp soil, rotten wood and rock in shaded Northwest forest.

species.name: Pincushion Moss
species.short_description: Pale whitish-green moss forming dense rounded cushions.
species.en_short_description: Pale whitish-green moss forming dense rounded cushions.
species.description: New York. Leaves are unusually thick and spongy, giving the cushion a bluish-white cast. Grows on acidic forest soil and among rocks in dry woodland.
species.en_description: New York. Leaves are unusually thick and spongy, giving the cushion a bluish-white cast. Grows on acidic forest soil and among rocks in dry woodland.

species.name: Waved Silk-moss
species.short_description: Glossy moss with broad flat leaves that are distinctly transversely wrinkled.
species.en_short_description: Glossy moss with broad flat leaves that are distinctly transversely wrinkled.
species.description: California and Washington. The undulating wave across each leaf is diagnostic. Grows on humus and rotting wood in wet coastal forest, with a silky sheen.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The undulating wave across each leaf is diagnostic. Grows on humus and rotting wood in wet coastal forest, with a silky sheen.

species.name: Cat's Tail Moss
species.short_description: Moss with cylindrical worm-like shoots of tightly overlapping blunt leaves.
species.en_short_description: Moss with cylindrical worm-like shoots of tightly overlapping blunt leaves.
species.description: California and Washington. Shoots look like small furry tails. Grows on tree trunks, branches and rock in humid Northwest forest, often hanging in curtains.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Shoots look like small furry tails. Grows on tree trunks, branches and rock in humid Northwest forest, often hanging in curtains.

species.name: Red-stemmed Feather Moss
species.short_description: Feathery moss with conspicuous bright red stems visible through the foliage.
species.en_short_description: Feathery moss with conspicuous bright red stems visible through the foliage.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. The red stem is the reliable field mark. Forms extensive deep carpets in conifer forest and bog margins.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. The red stem is the reliable field mark. Forms extensive deep carpets in conifer forest and bog margins.

species.name: Ostrich-plume Moss
species.short_description: Moss with flat plume-like shoots and leaves curved neatly to one side.
species.en_short_description: Moss with flat plume-like shoots and leaves curved neatly to one side.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Looks like a row of green feathers laid on the ground. All leaves sweep in the same direction. Grows in cool conifer forest.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Looks like a row of green feathers laid on the ground. All leaves sweep in the same direction. Grows in cool conifer forest.

species.name: Woodsy Thyme-moss
species.short_description: Moss with broad rounded translucent leaves on arching stems.
species.en_short_description: Moss with broad rounded translucent leaves on arching stems.
species.description: New York. Leaves are unusually large and thin for a moss, with a visible border and toothed tips. Grows on soil, logs and rock in moist woodland.
species.en_description: New York. Leaves are unusually large and thin for a moss, with a visible border and toothed tips. Grows on soil, logs and rock in moist woodland.

species.name: musgo
species.short_description: Glossy yellow-green moss with flattened shoots and erect cylindrical capsules.
species.en_short_description: Glossy yellow-green moss with flattened shoots and erect cylindrical capsules.
species.description: New York. Forms shining flat mats on tree bases, logs and shaded rock. Capsules stand straight up on reddish stalks, which is unusual and helpful.
species.en_description: New York. Forms shining flat mats on tree bases, logs and shaded rock. Capsules stand straight up on reddish stalks, which is unusual and helpful.

species.name: Badge Moss
species.short_description: Large moss with broad toothed leaves in flat sprays on arching stems.
species.en_short_description: Large moss with broad toothed leaves in flat sprays on arching stems.
species.description: California and Washington. One of the larger and more conspicuous Northwest forest mosses. Leaves are wide and bordered, giving a distinctly leafy look.
species.en_description: California and Washington. One of the larger and more conspicuous Northwest forest mosses. Leaves are wide and bordered, giving a distinctly leafy look.

species.name: tree-skirt moss
species.short_description: Moss forming a dense skirt around the base of tree trunks.
species.en_short_description: Moss forming a dense skirt around the base of tree trunks.
species.description: New York and Washington. Grows in a characteristic collar on the lower trunk and root flare, particularly on calcareous bark. Shoots taper and curve when dry.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. Grows in a characteristic collar on the lower trunk and root flare, particularly on calcareous bark. Shoots taper and curve when dry.

species.name: Musgo de tejas
species.short_description: Moss with flattened shoots of overlapping wavy leaves, on tree bark.
species.en_short_description: Moss with flattened shoots of overlapping wavy leaves, on tree bark.
species.description: New York and Washington. Leaves overlap like roof shingles and are transversely undulate. Grows on trunks and branches in humid old-growth forest.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. Leaves overlap like roof shingles and are transversely undulate. Grows on trunks and branches in humid old-growth forest.

species.name: lesser smoothcap
species.short_description: Moss with wavy translucent leaves that curl and crisp strongly when dry.
species.en_short_description: Moss with wavy translucent leaves that curl and crisp strongly when dry.
species.description: New York. Leaves are unusually thin with a visible midrib and undulations. Grows on bare soil, banks and trail edges. Curls into a tangle in dry weather.
species.en_description: New York. Leaves are unusually thin with a visible midrib and undulations. Grows on bare soil, banks and trail edges. Curls into a tangle in dry weather.

species.name: Musgo epífito
species.short_description: Small epiphytic moss forming low tufts on bark, with strongly twisted dry leaves.
species.en_short_description: Small epiphytic moss forming low tufts on bark, with strongly twisted dry leaves.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Grows on tree trunks in urban and suburban settings, tolerating pollution and drought well.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Grows on tree trunks in urban and suburban settings, tolerating pollution and drought well.

species.name: Common Haircap Moss
species.short_description: Tall stiff upright moss with dark green pointed leaves spreading star-like.
species.en_short_description: Tall stiff upright moss with dark green pointed leaves spreading star-like.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Among the largest mosses, reaching well over 10 cm. Capsules are distinctly four-angled and box-like on long stalks.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Among the largest mosses, reaching well over 10 cm. Capsules are distinctly four-angled and box-like on long stalks.

species.name: Common Apple-moss
species.short_description: Blue-green tuft with almost spherical capsules held on very short stalks.
species.en_short_description: Blue-green tuft with almost spherical capsules held on very short stalks.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. The near-spherical apple-shaped capsules nestled among the leaves are unmistakable. Grows on shaded banks and rock crevices.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. The near-spherical apple-shaped capsules nestled among the leaves are unmistakable. Grows on shaded banks and rock crevices.

species.name: Pipecleaner Moss
species.short_description: Robust moss with stiff shoots and pleated leaves curved to one side.
species.en_short_description: Robust moss with stiff shoots and pleated leaves curved to one side.
species.description: Washington. A high-elevation Northwest forest moss, forming deep loose mats under subalpine fir and mountain hemlock. Shoots feel wiry and coarse.
species.en_description: Washington. A high-elevation Northwest forest moss, forming deep loose mats under subalpine fir and mountain hemlock. Shoots feel wiry and coarse.

species.name: Lanky Moss
species.short_description: Large loose moss with spreading pointed leaves and long straggling shoots.
species.en_short_description: Large loose moss with spreading pointed leaves and long straggling shoots.
species.description: Washington. One of the most abundant carpet mosses in Pacific Northwest rainforest. Shoots are long and untidy, with leaves standing well out from the stem.
species.en_description: Washington. One of the most abundant carpet mosses in Pacific Northwest rainforest. Shoots are long and untidy, with leaves standing well out from the stem.

species.name: rhizomnium moss
species.short_description: Moss with large rounded unbordered leaves on reddish stems.
species.en_short_description: Moss with large rounded unbordered leaves on reddish stems.
species.description: California and Washington. Leaves are broad, thin and almost circular, giving a distinctly leafy appearance. Grows on wet humus and rotting wood in shaded forest.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Leaves are broad, thin and almost circular, giving a distinctly leafy appearance. Grows on wet humus and rotting wood in shaded forest.

species.name: Crome Sphagnum
species.short_description: Pale bog moss with strongly spreading, sharply recurved branch leaves.
species.en_short_description: Pale bog moss with strongly spreading, sharply recurved branch leaves.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. A peat moss of wet forest and fen margins. The strongly bent-back leaves give a bristly squarrose appearance.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. A peat moss of wet forest and fen margins. The strongly bent-back leaves give a bristly squarrose appearance.

species.name: hongo matamoscas
species.short_description: Scarlet cap flecked with white warts on a white stem with a ring and bulbous base.
species.en_short_description: Scarlet cap flecked with white warts on a white stem with a ring and bulbous base.
species.description: All six regions and the most-observed fungus here. Toxic and psychoactive, never a food. Grows with birch, pine and spruce. Cap fades to orange with age and rain.
species.en_description: All six regions and the most-observed fungus here. Toxic and psychoactive, never a food. Grows with birch, pine and spruce. Cap fades to orange with age and rain.

species.name: Nanacate
species.short_description: Small fan-shaped grey furry bracket whose gills are split lengthwise.
species.en_short_description: Small fan-shaped grey furry bracket whose gills are split lengthwise.
species.description: Five regions. The lengthwise-split gills are unique and diagnostic under a hand lens. Revives repeatedly after drying. One of the most widespread fungi on earth.
species.en_description: Five regions. The lengthwise-split gills are unique and diagnostic under a hand lens. Revives repeatedly after drying. One of the most widespread fungi on earth.

species.name: Matacandil
species.short_description: Tall white cylindrical cap covered in shaggy scales, dissolving into black ink.
species.en_short_description: Tall white cylindrical cap covered in shaggy scales, dissolving into black ink.
species.description: All six regions. Edible when very fresh but deliquesces into black liquid within hours of picking. Pushes up through lawns, gravel and even asphalt.
species.en_description: All six regions. Edible when very fresh but deliquesces into black liquid within hours of picking. Pushes up through lawns, gravel and even asphalt.

species.name: Hongo cabeza roja
species.short_description: Small bright red-brown sticky cap on a white stem, in wood chips.
species.en_short_description: Small bright red-brown sticky cap on a white stem, in wood chips.
species.description: California, Washington and Mexico City. Almost always in landscaping bark and mulch, often in large troops. The vivid brick-red cap fades to tan as it dries.
species.en_description: California, Washington and Mexico City. Almost always in landscaping bark and mulch, often in large troops. The vivid brick-red cap fades to tan as it dries.

species.name: Tapón de tinta brillante
species.short_description: Tawny pleated cap dusted with glistening mica-like granules, in clusters on wood.
species.en_short_description: Tawny pleated cap dusted with glistening mica-like granules, in clusters on wood.
species.description: Five regions. The sparkling granules wash off in rain, so old caps look plain. Grows in dense tufts at the base of stumps and buried roots.
species.en_description: Five regions. The sparkling granules wash off in rain, so old caps look plain. Grows in dense tufts at the base of stumps and buried roots.

species.name: Soldadito
species.short_description: Tall dry stalked puffball with a shaggy cap that never opens, in desert sand.
species.en_short_description: Tall dry stalked puffball with a shaggy cap that never opens, in desert sand.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Resembles a shaggy mane but stays closed and turns to dry black spore dust rather than ink. A true desert specialist.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Resembles a shaggy mane but stays closed and turns to dry black spore dust rather than ink. A true desert specialist.

species.name: Hongo calabaza occidental
species.short_description: Orange-olive funnel cap with true gills running down the stem, in clusters on wood.
species.en_short_description: Orange-olive funnel cap with true gills running down the stem, in clusters on wood.
species.description: California. Toxic, and the western look-alike that causes chanterelle poisonings. Gills are sharp and blade-like, unlike a chanterelle's blunt ridges. Faintly bioluminescent.
species.en_description: California. Toxic, and the western look-alike that causes chanterelle poisonings. Gills are sharp and blade-like, unlike a chanterelle's blunt ridges. Faintly bioluminescent.

species.name: hongo pera
species.short_description: Small brown pear-shaped puffball growing in dense clusters on rotting wood.
species.en_short_description: Small brown pear-shaped puffball growing in dense clusters on rotting wood.
species.description: All six regions. The only common puffball that fruits directly on wood, which settles the identification. Puffs spores through an apical pore when tapped.
species.en_description: All six regions. The only common puffball that fruits directly on wood, which settles the identification. Puffs spores through an apical pore when tapped.

species.name: Hongo coral coronado
species.short_description: Branched white coral fungus whose branch tips end in tiny crowns.
species.en_short_description: Branched white coral fungus whose branch tips end in tiny crowns.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The crown-shaped tips are diagnostic among coral fungi. Grows on hardwood logs, often in large candelabra-like masses.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The crown-shaped tips are diagnostic among coral fungi. Grows on hardwood logs, often in large candelabra-like masses.

species.name: Oreja de puerco
species.short_description: Bright orange-red crusted mass; a parasitic fungus consuming another mushroom.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange-red crusted mass; a parasitic fungus consuming another mushroom.
species.description: All six regions. Not a mushroom in its own right but Hypomyces growing over a Russula or Lactarius, remaking it into a hard orange club. Smells of seafood.
species.en_description: All six regions. Not a mushroom in its own right but Hypomyces growing over a Russula or Lactarius, remaking it into a hard orange club. Smells of seafood.

species.name: Questionable Stropharia
species.short_description: Large pale yellow-brown slimy cap with white veil fragments on the margin.
species.en_short_description: Large pale yellow-brown slimy cap with white veil fragments on the margin.
species.description: California and Washington. Common in Northwest forest duff and wood chips. The hanging shaggy veil remnants around the cap edge are distinctive. Purple-brown spores.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Common in Northwest forest duff and wood chips. The hanging shaggy veil remnants around the cap edge are distinctive. Purple-brown spores.

species.name: Hongo falo de la arena
species.short_description: White spongy stalk topped by a pitted olive-brown cap that reeks of carrion.
species.en_short_description: White spongy stalk topped by a pitted olive-brown cap that reeks of carrion.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. The smell attracts flies, which disperse the spores. Emerges from a pinkish-violet egg buried in sand or mulch.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. The smell attracts flies, which disperse the spores. Emerges from a pinkish-violet egg buried in sand or mulch.

species.name: Hongo azufroso
species.short_description: Dense clusters of sulphur-yellow caps with greenish gills, on stumps.
species.en_short_description: Dense clusters of sulphur-yellow caps with greenish gills, on stumps.
species.description: Five regions. Toxic and bitter. Gills start yellow then turn distinctly green-grey, which separates it from honey mushrooms growing in similar tufts.
species.en_description: Five regions. Toxic and bitter. Gills start yellow then turn distinctly green-grey, which separates it from honey mushrooms growing in similar tufts.

species.name: Eastern American jack-o'-lantern
species.short_description: Bright orange clustered mushroom with true gills descending the stem.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange clustered mushroom with true gills descending the stem.
species.description: New York. Toxic; the eastern counterpart of the western jack-o'-lantern and equally mistaken for chanterelle. Gills glow faintly green in complete darkness.
species.en_description: New York. Toxic; the eastern counterpart of the western jack-o'-lantern and equally mistaken for chanterelle. Gills glow faintly green in complete darkness.

species.name: Hongo cola de guajolote
species.short_description: Thin tough leathery bracket, hairy above with concentric orange-yellow zones.
species.en_short_description: Thin tough leathery bracket, hairy above with concentric orange-yellow zones.
species.description: Five regions. Grows in tiered rows on dead hardwood. Has no pores or gills, just a smooth spore surface beneath. Extremely common and long-persisting.
species.en_description: Five regions. Grows in tiered rows on dead hardwood. Has no pores or gills, just a smooth spore surface beneath. Extremely common and long-persisting.

species.name: Parasol verde
species.short_description: Large white parasol with brownish scales and gills that age dull green.
species.en_short_description: Large white parasol with brownish scales and gills that age dull green.
species.description: Five regions. The most common cause of mushroom poisoning in North America, since it fruits in lawns and resembles edible parasols. Green spore print is conclusive.
species.en_description: Five regions. The most common cause of mushroom poisoning in North America, since it fruits in lawns and resembles edible parasols. Green spore print is conclusive.

species.name: Pedo de coyote
species.short_description: White to tan puffball covered in small conical spines, on a short stalk.
species.en_short_description: White to tan puffball covered in small conical spines, on a short stalk.
species.description: All six regions. Edible when the flesh is pure white throughout. Releases spores in visible puffs from a top pore when mature. Grows in troops on forest floor.
species.en_description: All six regions. Edible when the flesh is pure white throughout. Releases spores in visible puffs from a top pore when mature. Grows in troops on forest floor.

species.name: Hongo de cera
species.short_description: Small crowded orange-tan fan-shaped crusts fused along fallen branches.
species.en_short_description: Small crowded orange-tan fan-shaped crusts fused along fallen branches.
species.description: New York, Washington and Mexico City. Forms long ranks of small fused fans on dead oak branches. Smooth beneath, with no pores. Persists year-round.
species.en_description: New York, Washington and Mexico City. Forms long ranks of small fused fans on dead oak branches. Smooth beneath, with no pores. Persists year-round.

species.name: Micena naranja
species.short_description: Small bright orange bell cap on a slender stem, on rotting hardwood.
species.en_short_description: Small bright orange bell cap on a slender stem, on rotting hardwood.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Vivid orange throughout and slimy when fresh. Delicate and easily overlooked. Grows singly or in small scattered groups.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Vivid orange throughout and slimy when fresh. Delicate and easily overlooked. Grows singly or in small scattered groups.

species.name: Hongo huevo estrellado
species.short_description: Bright egg-yellow slimy cap that fades and collapses within hours.
species.en_short_description: Bright egg-yellow slimy cap that fades and collapses within hours.
species.description: Five regions. Appears on lawns, dung and rich soil after rain, often gone by afternoon. Starts vividly yellow and pales to buff-grey as it flattens.
species.en_description: Five regions. Appears on lawns, dung and rich soil after rain, often gone by afternoon. Starts vividly yellow and pales to buff-grey as it flattens.

species.name: Late Oyster
species.short_description: Olive-green fan bracket with a short furry stem and pale yellowish gills.
species.en_short_description: Olive-green fan bracket with a short furry stem and pale yellowish gills.
species.description: New York and Washington. Fruits in late autumn and early winter after other mushrooms have gone. The greenish cap over yellow gills is distinctive on hardwood logs.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. Fruits in late autumn and early winter after other mushrooms have gone. The greenish cap over yellow gills is distinctive on hardwood logs.

species.name: Pie azul
species.short_description: Lilac-tinged cap and stem with pale pinkish-buff gills, in leaf litter.
species.en_short_description: Lilac-tinged cap and stem with pale pinkish-buff gills, in leaf litter.
species.description: Five regions. Edible and sought after, with a faintly floral smell. The violet tones fade with age. Fruits late in the season in rich humus and compost.
species.en_description: Five regions. Edible and sought after, with a faintly floral smell. The violet tones fade with age. Fruits late in the season in rich humus and compost.

species.name: Hongo gelatina naranja
species.short_description: Bright orange gelatinous blobs with a whitish attachment point, on conifer wood.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange gelatinous blobs with a whitish attachment point, on conifer wood.
species.description: Five regions. Rubbery when moist and shrinks to a hard orange crust in drought, reviving after rain. Grows on debarked conifer logs and stumps.
species.en_description: Five regions. Rubbery when moist and shrinks to a hard orange crust in drought, reviving after rain. Grows on debarked conifer logs and stumps.

species.name: Toothed Jelly Fungus
species.short_description: Translucent grey jelly tongue with soft spines on the underside.
species.en_short_description: Translucent grey jelly tongue with soft spines on the underside.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Feels like rubber and is the only jelly fungus with teeth. Grows on rotting conifer wood, often on the underside.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Feels like rubber and is the only jelly fungus with teeth. Grows on rotting conifer wood, often on the underside.

species.name: Hongo oreja dorada
species.short_description: Golden-yellow gelatinous lobed mass with a whitish core, on hardwood.
species.en_short_description: Golden-yellow gelatinous lobed mass with a whitish core, on hardwood.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Parasitises a crust fungus, which is why a pale core runs through it. Firmer and brighter than witch's butter.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Parasitises a crust fungus, which is why a pale core runs through it. Firmer and brighter than witch's butter.

species.name: Hongo astas de carbón
species.short_description: Small black upright clubs with white powdery tips, on dead wood.
species.en_short_description: Small black upright clubs with white powdery tips, on dead wood.
species.description: California, Washington and Mexico City. Looks like a snuffed candle wick. Tough and persistent, fruiting year-round on hardwood stumps and buried wood.
species.en_description: California, Washington and Mexico City. Looks like a snuffed candle wick. Tough and persistent, fruiting year-round on hardwood stumps and buried wood.

species.name: Cemita roja
species.short_description: Stout mushroom with a deep red-brown cap, pale pores and a fat white stem.
species.en_short_description: Stout mushroom with a deep red-brown cap, pale pores and a fat white stem.
species.description: Colorado and Mexico City region. A prized edible bolete of the southern Rockies and Mexican highlands, fruiting with spruce and fir after summer monsoon rain.
species.en_description: Colorado and Mexico City region. A prized edible bolete of the southern Rockies and Mexican highlands, fruiting with spruce and fir after summer monsoon rain.

species.name: Hongo ostra dorado
species.short_description: Bright yellow clustered fan caps with white gills, on hardwood.
species.en_short_description: Bright yellow clustered fan caps with white gills, on hardwood.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Cultivated and now escaped and spreading in eastern woodland, where it may displace native fungi. Vivid lemon-yellow throughout.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Cultivated and now escaped and spreading in eastern woodland, where it may displace native fungi. Vivid lemon-yellow throughout.

species.name: Stinking Orange Oyster
species.short_description: Bright orange furry fan bracket with orange gills and a strong unpleasant smell.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange furry fan bracket with orange gills and a strong unpleasant smell.
species.description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. The dense orange fuzz on the cap and the foul odour are diagnostic. Grows in overlapping rows on conifer logs.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. The dense orange fuzz on the cap and the foul odour are diagnostic. Grows in overlapping rows on conifer logs.

species.name: Hongo Amarillo de las Macetas
species.short_description: Small bright yellow pleated parasol with a ring, in houseplant pots.
species.en_short_description: Small bright yellow pleated parasol with a ring, in houseplant pots.
species.description: All six regions. Almost always in potting soil, greenhouses and mulch. Vivid sulphur-yellow, powdery, and collapses quickly. Harmless to plants but toxic if eaten.
species.en_description: All six regions. Almost always in potting soil, greenhouses and mulch. Vivid sulphur-yellow, powdery, and collapses quickly. Harmless to plants but toxic if eaten.

species.name: Corneta
species.short_description: Orange scaly funnel with a wrinkled buff spore surface running down the stem.
species.en_short_description: Orange scaly funnel with a wrinkled buff spore surface running down the stem.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Vase- or trumpet-shaped with coarse scales inside the funnel. Causes stomach upset for many people despite being sold.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Vase- or trumpet-shaped with coarse scales inside the funnel. Causes stomach upset for many people despite being sold.

species.name: Micena sangrante
species.short_description: Small reddish-brown bell cap on a fine stem that bleeds dark red juice when broken.
species.en_short_description: Small reddish-brown bell cap on a fine stem that bleeds dark red juice when broken.
species.description: Five regions. Snapping the stem releases a wine-red drop, which is conclusive. Grows in tight clusters on rotting hardwood. Gills edged with reddish-brown.
species.en_description: Five regions. Snapping the stem releases a wine-red drop, which is conclusive. Grows in tight clusters on rotting hardwood. Gills edged with reddish-brown.

species.name: Luminescent Panellus
species.short_description: Small tough tan kidney-shaped bracket with fine gills; glows green in darkness.
species.en_short_description: Small tough tan kidney-shaped bracket with fine gills; glows green in darkness.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. One of the most reliably bioluminescent fungi — the gills give a faint green glow after twenty minutes of full dark adaptation.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. One of the most reliably bioluminescent fungi — the gills give a faint green glow after twenty minutes of full dark adaptation.
