species.name: Gírgola Común
species.short_description: Grey-brown fan cap with white gills running down a very short off-centre stem.
species.en_short_description: Grey-brown fan cap with white gills running down a very short off-centre stem.
species.description: Five regions. A widely eaten wild mushroom, growing in shelving clusters on dead hardwood. Faintly anise-scented. Preys on nematodes, unusually for a fungus.
species.en_description: Five regions. A widely eaten wild mushroom, growing in shelving clusters on dead hardwood. Faintly anise-scented. Preys on nematodes, unusually for a fungus.

species.name: Hongo temblón amarillo
species.short_description: Bright golden-yellow gelatinous folded blobs on dead hardwood branches.
species.en_short_description: Bright golden-yellow gelatinous folded blobs on dead hardwood branches.
species.description: Five regions. Shrinks to a hard orange film in dry weather and rehydrates after rain. Softer and more translucent than golden ear, with no pale core.
species.en_description: Five regions. Shrinks to a hard orange film in dry weather and rehydrates after rain. Softer and more translucent than golden ear, with no pale core.

species.name: American Amber Jelly Fungus
species.short_description: Dark amber-brown rubbery discs and lobes fusing along hardwood branches.
species.en_short_description: Dark amber-brown rubbery discs and lobes fusing along hardwood branches.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Firm and gelatinous, often merging into long ridges. Dries to a thin black crust and revives with rain. Common on fallen oak.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Firm and gelatinous, often merging into long ridges. Dries to a thin black crust and revives with rain. Common on fallen oak.

species.name: Western Black Elfin Saddle
species.short_description: Black irregular saddle-shaped cap on a deeply ribbed pale stem.
species.en_short_description: Black irregular saddle-shaped cap on a deeply ribbed pale stem.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. The lumpy folded black cap and fluted stem are unmistakable. Grows on soil in conifer forest in autumn.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. The lumpy folded black cap and fluted stem are unmistakable. Grows on soil in conifer forest in autumn.

species.name: Hongo cazahuate
species.short_description: Honey-brown clustered caps with fine scales, a ring on the stem and white gills.
species.en_short_description: Honey-brown clustered caps with fine scales, a ring on the stem and white gills.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. A serious tree pathogen; black bootlace cords run under the bark of infected roots. Edible cooked but upsets some people.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. A serious tree pathogen; black bootlace cords run under the bark of infected roots. Edible cooked but upsets some people.

species.name: Painted Suillus
species.short_description: Dry red-scaly cap over yellow pores, on a stem with a ring.
species.en_short_description: Dry red-scaly cap over yellow pores, on a stem with a ring.
species.description: New York. Grows only with eastern white pine. The shaggy crimson scales over a yellow pore surface are distinctive. Flesh bruises pinkish then brown.
species.en_description: New York. Grows only with eastern white pine. The shaggy crimson scales over a yellow pore surface are distinctive. Flesh bruises pinkish then brown.

species.name: Hongo jaula roja
species.short_description: Hollow bright red lattice sphere emerging from a white egg, smelling of carrion.
species.en_short_description: Hollow bright red lattice sphere emerging from a white egg, smelling of carrion.
species.description: California. One of the most bizarre fungi in the region. The red cage attracts flies with a powerful stench. Grows in mulch, gardens and wood chips.
species.en_description: California. One of the most bizarre fungi in the region. The red cage attracts flies with a powerful stench. Grows in mulch, gardens and wood chips.

species.name: Mulch Maids
species.short_description: Straw-brown to tan sticky caps in troops on landscaping bark.
species.en_short_description: Straw-brown to tan sticky caps in troops on landscaping bark.
species.description: Colorado, California and Mexico City. Almost exclusively in wood-chip mulch, often in large numbers after irrigation. Purple-brown spore print; veil remnants on the stem.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Mexico City. Almost exclusively in wood-chip mulch, often in large numbers after irrigation. Purple-brown spore print; veil remnants on the stem.

species.name: Hongo de la muerte
species.short_description: Greenish-olive cap with white gills, a ring and a sac-like cup at the stem base.
species.en_short_description: Greenish-olive cap with white gills, a ring and a sac-like cup at the stem base.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Responsible for most fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide. Introduced with European trees and now spreading with oaks. Never eat.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Responsible for most fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide. Introduced with European trees and now spreading with oaks. Never eat.

species.name: golden milkcap
species.short_description: Yellowish zoned cap with a bearded margin, exuding white milk when cut.
species.en_short_description: Yellowish zoned cap with a bearded margin, exuding white milk when cut.
species.description: California and Mexico City region. Bleeds white latex that tastes intensely acrid. The fringed hairy cap edge is characteristic. Grows with alder and oak.
species.en_description: California and Mexico City region. Bleeds white latex that tastes intensely acrid. The fringed hairy cap edge is characteristic. Grows with alder and oak.

species.name: Cramp Balls
species.short_description: Hard black spherical crusts on dead wood, with concentric rings inside.
species.en_short_description: Hard black spherical crusts on dead wood, with concentric rings inside.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Charcoal-like and extremely tough, persisting for years. Cutting one reveals fine concentric silver-grey bands. Common on fallen oak.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Charcoal-like and extremely tough, persisting for years. Cutting one reveals fine concentric silver-grey bands. Common on fallen oak.

species.name: Enchilado
species.short_description: Orange funnel cap with fine forking gills and a felty texture.
species.en_short_description: Orange funnel cap with fine forking gills and a felty texture.
species.description: Five regions. Gills are true blades that fork repeatedly, unlike a chanterelle's blunt ridges. Flesh is thin and orange throughout rather than white. Best avoided.
species.en_description: Five regions. Gills are true blades that fork repeatedly, unlike a chanterelle's blunt ridges. Flesh is thin and orange throughout rather than white. Best avoided.

species.name: ceramic parchment
species.short_description: Hard whitish crust cracked into small tile-like plates on bare oak wood.
species.en_short_description: Hard whitish crust cracked into small tile-like plates on bare oak wood.
species.description: New York. The mosaic of cracked ceramic-looking plates is unmistakable. Grows on decorticated oak logs, persisting for many years and slowly expanding.
species.en_description: New York. The mosaic of cracked ceramic-looking plates is unmistakable. Grows on decorticated oak logs, persisting for many years and slowly expanding.

species.name: Pale Brittlestem
species.short_description: Pale tan fragile cap with a whitish margin, in clusters on buried wood.
species.en_short_description: Pale tan fragile cap with a whitish margin, in clusters on buried wood.
species.description: All six regions. Very brittle and quick to collapse. Cap fades from tan to nearly white as it dries. Dark purple-brown spore print. Common in lawns and gardens.
species.en_description: All six regions. Very brittle and quick to collapse. Cap fades from tan to nearly white as it dries. Dark purple-brown spore print. Common in lawns and gardens.

species.name: Pacific Golden Chanterelle
species.short_description: Golden funnel-shaped mushroom with blunt forking ridges instead of gills.
species.en_short_description: Golden funnel-shaped mushroom with blunt forking ridges instead of gills.
species.description: California and Washington. Washington's state mushroom and a prized edible. Blunt wrinkled ridges, a fruity apricot smell and white interior flesh separate it from look-alikes.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Washington's state mushroom and a prized edible. Blunt wrinkled ridges, a fruity apricot smell and white interior flesh separate it from look-alikes.

species.name: Hongo pie de liebre
species.short_description: Grey conical cap covered in fine white woolly fibres, splitting and curling upward.
species.en_short_description: Grey conical cap covered in fine white woolly fibres, splitting and curling upward.
species.description: All six regions. Extremely short-lived, often appearing and collapsing within a day. The soft hairy covering gives the name. Common in mulch and rich soil.
species.en_description: All six regions. Extremely short-lived, often appearing and collapsing within a day. The soft hairy covering gives the name. Common in mulch and rich soil.

species.name: Ringless Honey Mushroom
species.short_description: Tawny clustered caps with no ring on the stem and white gills.
species.en_short_description: Tawny clustered caps with no ring on the stem and white gills.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Separated from the true honey mushroom by the absence of a stem ring. Grows in very dense tufts from hardwood roots and stumps.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Separated from the true honey mushroom by the absence of a stem ring. Grows in very dense tufts from hardwood roots and stumps.

species.name: Cola de pavo
species.short_description: Thin flexible bracket banded in concentric zones of many colours.
species.en_short_description: Thin flexible bracket banded in concentric zones of many colours.
species.description: Five regions and the most-observed bracket here. Grows in overlapping rosettes on dead hardwood. Underside is white with very fine pores. Highly variable colouring.
species.en_description: Five regions and the most-observed bracket here. Grows in overlapping rosettes on dead hardwood. Underside is white with very fine pores. Highly variable colouring.

species.name: Hongo silla de montar
species.short_description: Large fan-shaped cream bracket with brown feathery scales and a short lateral stem.
species.en_short_description: Large fan-shaped cream bracket with brown feathery scales and a short lateral stem.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Fruits in spring on hardwood wounds. Smells of watermelon rind when fresh. Pores are large and angular.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Fruits in spring on hardwood wounds. Smells of watermelon rind when fresh. Pores are large and angular.

species.name: Hongo de repisa
species.short_description: Thick woody bracket with a resinous reddish-brown band at the margin.
species.en_short_description: Thick woody bracket with a resinous reddish-brown band at the margin.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Grows on conifers, especially Douglas-fir. Perennial and hard, adding a new pale margin each year.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Mexico City. Grows on conifers, especially Douglas-fir. Perennial and hard, adding a new pale margin each year.

species.name: Northern Red Belt
species.short_description: Hoof-shaped woody conk with a red-brown zone and a white pore surface.
species.en_short_description: Hoof-shaped woody conk with a red-brown zone and a white pore surface.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. A northern conifer bracket. The lacquered red band above a cream margin is the field mark. Perennial and very tough.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. A northern conifer bracket. The lacquered red band above a cream margin is the field mark. Perennial and very tough.

species.name: hongo de la corteza de las coníferas
species.short_description: Small round tan bracket completely enclosed beneath by a membrane with a single hole.
species.en_short_description: Small round tan bracket completely enclosed beneath by a membrane with a single hole.
species.description: Five regions. Unique among polypores in sealing its pore surface behind a veil pierced by one pore. Fruits on recently killed conifers, often after bark beetle attack.
species.en_description: Five regions. Unique among polypores in sealing its pore surface behind a veil pierced by one pore. Fruits on recently killed conifers, often after bark beetle attack.

species.name: Hongo de repisa naranja
species.short_description: Thin bracket, bright orange-red above and below.
species.en_short_description: Thin bracket, bright orange-red above and below.
species.description: Colorado, New York, Mexico City and Baja. The vivid cinnabar colour on both surfaces is unmistakable. Fades to pale orange with age. Grows on dead hardwood.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York, Mexico City and Baja. The vivid cinnabar colour on both surfaces is unmistakable. Fades to pale orange with age. Grows on dead hardwood.

species.name: Ganoderma polychromum
species.short_description: Broad flat bracket with a varnished multi-toned upper surface.
species.en_short_description: Broad flat bracket with a varnished multi-toned upper surface.
species.description: California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. A varnished-conk relative on hardwood trunks and stumps. Upper surface shows bands of red, brown and ochre.
species.en_description: California, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. A varnished-conk relative on hardwood trunks and stumps. Upper surface shows bands of red, brown and ochre.

species.name: Hongo cinabrio de repisa
species.short_description: Bright orange-red thin bracket with a paler pore surface beneath.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange-red thin bracket with a paler pore surface beneath.
species.description: Five regions. Very close to the cinnabar bracket and often treated as the same; slightly duller pore surface. Grows on dead deciduous branches, often birch.
species.en_description: Five regions. Very close to the cinnabar bracket and often treated as the same; slightly duller pore surface. Grows on dead deciduous branches, often birch.

species.name: Spring Polypore
species.short_description: Small funnel-shaped tan bracket with large hexagonal pores and a central stem.
species.en_short_description: Small funnel-shaped tan bracket with large hexagonal pores and a central stem.
species.description: All six regions. The coarse honeycomb pore surface is diagnostic. Fruits early in the season on fallen hardwood twigs and branches. Tough and leathery.
species.en_description: All six regions. The coarse honeycomb pore surface is diagnostic. Fruits early in the season on fallen hardwood twigs and branches. Tough and leathery.

species.name: Hongo de repisa
species.short_description: Stalkless varnished bracket, red-brown above with a white pore surface.
species.en_short_description: Stalkless varnished bracket, red-brown above with a white pore surface.
species.description: Five regions. Grows in shelving clusters at the base of hardwood trees and stumps. The glossy lacquered crust and pure white margin are distinctive when fresh.
species.en_description: Five regions. Grows in shelving clusters at the base of hardwood trees and stumps. The glossy lacquered crust and pure white margin are distinctive when fresh.

species.name: Hongo repisa azufre
species.short_description: Thick fleshy bright orange-and-yellow shelving bracket.
species.en_short_description: Thick fleshy bright orange-and-yellow shelving bracket.
species.description: California, Washington and Mexico City. The western sulphur shelf, growing on eucalyptus and oak. Fleshy and edible when very young, though it upsets some people.
species.en_description: California, Washington and Mexico City. The western sulphur shelf, growing on eucalyptus and oak. Fleshy and edible when very young, though it upsets some people.

species.name: Pollo del bosque
species.short_description: Overlapping fleshy shelves, orange above and sulphur-yellow beneath.
species.en_short_description: Overlapping fleshy shelves, orange above and sulphur-yellow beneath.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. A well-known edible when young and tender. Turns chalky and brittle with age. Grows on oak and other hardwoods.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. A well-known edible when young and tender. Turns chalky and brittle with age. Grows on oak and other hardwoods.

species.name: Lentinus berteroi
species.short_description: Tough funnel-shaped bracket with a central stem and coarse pores.
species.en_short_description: Tough funnel-shaped bracket with a central stem and coarse pores.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A tropical and subtropical polypore of dead hardwood in the peninsula's arroyos. Leathery, drought-hardy and long-persisting.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A tropical and subtropical polypore of dead hardwood in the peninsula's arroyos. Leathery, drought-hardy and long-persisting.

species.name: Phaeolus hispidoides
species.short_description: Thick velvety brown bracket that bruises dark, with a maze-like pore surface.
species.en_short_description: Thick velvety brown bracket that bruises dark, with a maze-like pore surface.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Grows at the base of conifers and hardwoods. The hairy upper surface and staining pores are characteristic. Used as a dye fungus.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Grows at the base of conifers and hardwoods. The hairy upper surface and staining pores are characteristic. Used as a dye fungus.

species.name: Hongo dorado de repisa
species.short_description: Varnished bracket with a golden to red-brown lacquered crust and a short stem.
species.en_short_description: Varnished bracket with a golden to red-brown lacquered crust and a short stem.
species.description: California, New York, Mexico City and Baja. A stalked varnished conk on hardwood roots and stumps, often with a distinctly golden tone toward the margin.
species.en_description: California, New York, Mexico City and Baja. A stalked varnished conk on hardwood roots and stumps, often with a distinctly golden tone toward the margin.

species.name: Gilled Polypore
species.short_description: Thin white-to-grey bracket whose underside bears radiating gill-like plates.
species.en_short_description: Thin white-to-grey bracket whose underside bears radiating gill-like plates.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. A polypore whose pores are stretched into true gills, which is unusual and diagnostic. Grows on dead birch and other hardwoods.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. A polypore whose pores are stretched into true gills, which is unusual and diagnostic. Grows on dead birch and other hardwoods.

species.name: Coral-pink Merulius
species.short_description: Soft spreading crust in bright coral-pink with a wrinkled surface.
species.en_short_description: Soft spreading crust in bright coral-pink with a wrinkled surface.
species.description: New York, Mexico City and Baja. The vivid salmon-pink colour is unmistakable when fresh, fading to buff. Spreads over the underside of fallen hardwood.
species.en_description: New York, Mexico City and Baja. The vivid salmon-pink colour is unmistakable when fresh, fading to buff. Spreads over the underside of fallen hardwood.

species.name: Hongo ahumado de repisa
species.short_description: Thin grey-brown bracket with a distinctly smoky grey-black pore surface.
species.en_short_description: Thin grey-brown bracket with a distinctly smoky grey-black pore surface.
species.description: All six regions. The dark grey underside contrasting with a paler top is the field mark. Grows in tiers and effused sheets on dead hardwood.
species.en_description: All six regions. The dark grey underside contrasting with a paler top is the field mark. Grows in tiers and effused sheets on dead hardwood.

species.name: Trembling Crust
species.short_description: Soft gelatinous crust, whitish to pink, with a wrinkled folded lower surface.
species.en_short_description: Soft gelatinous crust, whitish to pink, with a wrinkled folded lower surface.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Rubbery and translucent when wet, drying to a thin film. Forms small brackets with a spreading crust behind them.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Rubbery and translucent when wet, drying to a thin film. Forms small brackets with a spreading crust behind them.

species.name: Hongo del Artista
species.short_description: Large flat perennial conk with a dull grey crust and a white surface that marks when scratched.
species.en_short_description: Large flat perennial conk with a dull grey crust and a white surface that marks when scratched.
species.description: Five regions. Drawing on the white pore surface leaves a permanent brown line, hence the name. Grows on hardwood trunks, adding a layer each year for decades.
species.en_description: Five regions. Drawing on the white pore surface leaves a permanent brown line, hence the name. Grows on hardwood trunks, adding a layer each year for decades.

species.name: Sombrerito bailador
species.short_description: Tough funnel bracket with a hairy fringed margin and a central stem.
species.en_short_description: Tough funnel bracket with a hairy fringed margin and a central stem.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A tropical polypore with a distinctly hairy cap and fringed edge. Grows on dead hardwood in warm climates.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A tropical polypore with a distinctly hairy cap and fringed edge. Grows on dead hardwood in warm climates.

species.name: West Coast Reishi
species.short_description: Very large varnished bracket, red-brown above, on conifers.
species.en_short_description: Very large varnished bracket, red-brown above, on conifers.
species.description: California and Washington. The Pacific varnished conk, growing on hemlock and fir. Can reach 50 cm across. Glossy lacquered crust with a thick white margin when growing.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The Pacific varnished conk, growing on hemlock and fir. Can reach 50 cm across. Glossy lacquered crust with a thick white margin when growing.

species.name: Yesquero del abedul
species.short_description: Smooth pale grey-brown kidney-shaped bracket on birch, with a rim of skin.
species.en_short_description: Smooth pale grey-brown kidney-shaped bracket on birch, with a rim of skin.
species.description: New York, Washington and Mexico City. Found almost exclusively on birch. The smooth suede-like surface peels at the edge. Traditionally used as a razor strop and tinder.
species.en_description: New York, Washington and Mexico City. Found almost exclusively on birch. The smooth suede-like surface peels at the edge. Traditionally used as a razor strop and tinder.

species.name: Hongo de barniz del abeto
species.short_description: Glossy red-lacquered bracket with a white margin, on conifers.
species.en_short_description: Glossy red-lacquered bracket with a white margin, on conifers.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Grows on hemlock and other conifers, often with a lateral stem. The mahogany-red varnished crust is highly distinctive when fresh.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Grows on hemlock and other conifers, often with a lateral stem. The mahogany-red varnished crust is highly distinctive when fresh.

species.name: Orange Sponge Polypore
species.short_description: Soft bright orange spongy mass with large ragged pores, on conifer logs.
species.en_short_description: Soft bright orange spongy mass with large ragged pores, on conifer logs.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Unusually soft for a polypore, with a coarse torn pore surface. Fruits under snow and appears at snowmelt in mountain forest.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Unusually soft for a polypore, with a coarse torn pore surface. Fruits under snow and appears at snowmelt in mountain forest.

species.name: Hongo de repisa abultado
species.short_description: Thick whitish bracket with a lumpy base and elongated maze-like pores.
species.en_short_description: Thick whitish bracket with a lumpy base and elongated maze-like pores.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Pores are stretched radially into slots rather than round holes. Often greened by algae on the upper surface with age.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Pores are stretched radially into slots rather than round holes. Often greened by algae on the upper surface with age.

species.name: Conifer Chicken of the Woods
species.short_description: Fleshy orange shelving bracket on conifers, yellow beneath.
species.en_short_description: Fleshy orange shelving bracket on conifers, yellow beneath.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. The conifer-dwelling sulphur shelf. Frequently causes stomach upset, unlike the hardwood species, so it is not recommended eating.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. The conifer-dwelling sulphur shelf. Frequently causes stomach upset, unlike the hardwood species, so it is not recommended eating.

species.name: Hongo roseta
species.short_description: Small pale rosette-shaped bracket with a toothed spore surface.
species.en_short_description: Small pale rosette-shaped bracket with a toothed spore surface.
species.description: Mexico City region. Forms neat rosettes on dead hardwood in the highlands. The underside bears irregular teeth rather than clean pores.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Forms neat rosettes on dead hardwood in the highlands. The underside bears irregular teeth rather than clean pores.

species.name: hen of the woods
species.short_description: Large clustered rosette of grey-brown overlapping fronds at the base of oaks.
species.en_short_description: Large clustered rosette of grey-brown overlapping fronds at the base of oaks.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Washington. A prized edible, also called maitake. Returns to the same oak year after year. Fronds are fan-shaped with white pores beneath.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Washington. A prized edible, also called maitake. Returns to the same oak year after year. Fronds are fan-shaped with white pores beneath.

species.name: Rosy Conk
species.short_description: Small woody bracket with a rose-pink pore surface fading to brown.
species.en_short_description: Small woody bracket with a rose-pink pore surface fading to brown.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The pink underside is the field mark, though it dulls with age. Grows in tiers on dead conifer wood.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The pink underside is the field mark, though it dulls with age. Grows in tiers on dead conifer wood.

species.name: Resinous Polypore
species.short_description: Thick soft bracket, dark brown above with a white pore surface exuding droplets.
species.en_short_description: Thick soft bracket, dark brown above with a white pore surface exuding droplets.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Young specimens weep resinous drops. Fleshy when fresh, becoming hard and black. Smells pleasantly of anise.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Young specimens weep resinous drops. Fleshy when fresh, becoming hard and black. Smells pleasantly of anise.

species.name: Ochre Spreading Tooth
species.short_description: Thin ochre crust with small brackets, bearing fine spines beneath.
species.en_short_description: Thin ochre crust with small brackets, bearing fine spines beneath.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Baja. Spreads across fallen branches with a toothed rather than pored surface. Warm ochre-orange colour throughout.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Baja. Spreads across fallen branches with a toothed rather than pored surface. Warm ochre-orange colour throughout.

species.name: White-pored Chicken of the Woods
species.short_description: Orange rosette bracket with a distinctly white pore surface, at tree bases.
species.en_short_description: Orange rosette bracket with a distinctly white pore surface, at tree bases.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Grows from roots as a ground-level rosette rather than a trunk shelf. White pores separate it from the yellow-pored species.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Grows from roots as a ground-level rosette rather than a trunk shelf. White pores separate it from the yellow-pored species.

species.name: Wrinkled Crust
species.short_description: Bright orange-pink radiating crust with wrinkled ridges.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange-pink radiating crust with wrinkled ridges.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Forms flat patches with fine radiating folds on dead hardwood. Vivid when fresh, drying to dull orange-brown.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Forms flat patches with fine radiating folds on dead hardwood. Vivid when fresh, drying to dull orange-brown.

species.name: Hongo parasol
species.short_description: Small funnel-shaped leathery bracket on a slender off-centre stem.
species.en_short_description: Small funnel-shaped leathery bracket on a slender off-centre stem.
species.description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A warm-climate polypore of dead hardwood. Tough and umbrella-like, persisting through dry spells.
species.en_description: Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A warm-climate polypore of dead hardwood. Tough and umbrella-like, persisting through dry spells.

species.name: Ganoderma zonatum
species.short_description: Varnished bracket with concentric zoning, growing on palms.
species.en_short_description: Varnished bracket with concentric zoning, growing on palms.
species.description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Almost exclusively on palm trunks, where it is a lethal butt-rot pathogen. The zoned lacquered crust identifies it.
species.en_description: California, Mexico City and Baja. Almost exclusively on palm trunks, where it is a lethal butt-rot pathogen. The zoned lacquered crust identifies it.

species.name: Artist's Conk
species.short_description: Large perennial conk with a hard grey crust and a bruising white pore surface.
species.en_short_description: Large perennial conk with a hard grey crust and a bruising white pore surface.
species.description: California and Washington. The western counterpart of the artist's bracket, with a thicker crust. Grows on hardwood trunks, especially oak and maple.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The western counterpart of the artist's bracket, with a thicker crust. Grows on hardwood trunks, especially oak and maple.

species.name: Ochre-banded Conk
species.short_description: Woody bracket with ochre-brown banding and a cream pore surface.
species.en_short_description: Woody bracket with ochre-brown banding and a cream pore surface.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. A northern conifer conk similar to the red belts but with warmer ochre zoning. Perennial and hard.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. A northern conifer conk similar to the red belts but with warmer ochre zoning. Perennial and hard.

species.name: Black-staining Polypore
species.short_description: Large rosette of grey-brown fronds that stain black where handled.
species.en_short_description: Large rosette of grey-brown fronds that stain black where handled.
species.description: New York. Similar to hen of the woods but bruising black within minutes, which is conclusive. Grows at the base of hardwood trees and from buried roots.
species.en_description: New York. Similar to hen of the woods but bruising black within minutes, which is conclusive. Grows at the base of hardwood trees and from buried roots.

species.name: fragrant bracket
species.short_description: Thick whitish bracket smelling strongly of anise.
species.en_short_description: Thick whitish bracket smelling strongly of anise.
species.description: California, New York and Baja California Sur. The sweet aniseed smell is the easiest confirmation. Grows on willow and poplar. Corky and pale throughout.
species.en_description: California, New York and Baja California Sur. The sweet aniseed smell is the easiest confirmation. Grows on willow and poplar. Corky and pale throughout.

species.name: Truncospora mexicana
species.short_description: Small hard bracket with thick walls and a pale pore surface.
species.en_short_description: Small hard bracket with thick walls and a pale pore surface.
species.description: Baja California Sur. A subtropical polypore of dead hardwood in peninsular arroyos. Small, tough and long-persisting through drought.
species.en_description: Baja California Sur. A subtropical polypore of dead hardwood in peninsular arroyos. Small, tough and long-persisting through drought.

species.name: Thin-walled Maze Polypore
species.short_description: Flat bracket with concentric zones and elongated maze-like pores that bruise red.
species.en_short_description: Flat bracket with concentric zones and elongated maze-like pores that bruise red.
species.description: New York and Washington. The pore surface reddens where touched when fresh. Pores are stretched into a labyrinth. Grows on willow and birch branches.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. The pore surface reddens where touched when fresh. Pores are stretched into a labyrinth. Grows on willow and birch branches.

species.name: Blushing Rosette
species.short_description: Irregular cream rosette bracket that bruises reddish, often growing from soil.
species.en_short_description: Irregular cream rosette bracket that bruises reddish, often growing from soil.
species.description: Five regions. Fruits from buried roots, so it appears to grow on the ground. Flesh and pores flush pink-red when cut or handled. Shape is highly irregular.
species.en_description: Five regions. Fruits from buried roots, so it appears to grow on the ground. Flesh and pores flush pink-red when cut or handled. Shape is highly irregular.

species.name: Western cauliflower mushroom
species.short_description: Large cream mass of flattened wavy ribbons, like a sea sponge or cauliflower.
species.en_short_description: Large cream mass of flattened wavy ribbons, like a sea sponge or cauliflower.
species.description: California and Washington. A choice edible growing at the base of conifers from a deep root parasite. Requires careful cleaning; grit hides between the ribbons.
species.en_description: California and Washington. A choice edible growing at the base of conifers from a deep root parasite. Requires careful cleaning; grit hides between the ribbons.

species.name: Milk-white Toothed Polypore
species.short_description: Thin white crust with brackets, the underside breaking into flattened teeth.
species.en_short_description: Thin white crust with brackets, the underside breaking into flattened teeth.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Starts as pores that tear into irregular teeth as it matures. Common on dead hardwood branches year-round.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Starts as pores that tear into irregular teeth as it matures. Common on dead hardwood branches year-round.

species.name: Tinder Polypore
species.short_description: Hard grey hoof-shaped perennial conk with a smooth banded crust.
species.en_short_description: Hard grey hoof-shaped perennial conk with a smooth banded crust.
species.description: New York and Washington. Related to the fungus historically carried for fire-lighting and prepared as amadou. Grows on birch and beech trunks for many years.
species.en_description: New York and Washington. Related to the fungus historically carried for fire-lighting and prepared as amadou. Grows on birch and beech trunks for many years.

species.name: Lilac oysterling
species.short_description: Tough violet-tinged fan cap with lilac gills, fading to tan.
species.en_short_description: Tough violet-tinged fan cap with lilac gills, fading to tan.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Young specimens are distinctly lilac; older ones fade to leathery buff. Grows on hardwood stumps and logs.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Young specimens are distinctly lilac; older ones fade to leathery buff. Grows on hardwood stumps and logs.

species.name: violet-toothed polypore
species.short_description: Thin hairy grey bracket with a violet-tinged pore surface breaking into teeth.
species.en_short_description: Thin hairy grey bracket with a violet-tinged pore surface breaking into teeth.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The purple underside is the field mark, fading with age. Grows in dense overlapping tiers on dead hardwood.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The purple underside is the field mark, fading with age. Grows in dense overlapping tiers on dead hardwood.

species.name: Berkeley's Polypore
species.short_description: Very large cream rosette of thick fronds with coarse pores, at oak bases.
species.en_short_description: Very large cream rosette of thick fronds with coarse pores, at oak bases.
species.description: New York. Can reach 60 cm across, among the largest fungi in the east. Tough and fibrous. A root and butt rot pathogen of oaks.
species.en_description: New York. Can reach 60 cm across, among the largest fungi in the east. Tough and fibrous. A root and butt rot pathogen of oaks.

species.name: Hongo de laminillas de las coníferas
species.short_description: Rusty-brown bracket with a hairy top and gill-like maze plates beneath.
species.en_short_description: Rusty-brown bracket with a hairy top and gill-like maze plates beneath.
species.description: All six regions. The underside bears elongated gill-like ridges rather than pores. Common on cut conifer lumber, stumps and construction timber.
species.en_description: All six regions. The underside bears elongated gill-like ridges rather than pores. Common on cut conifer lumber, stumps and construction timber.

species.name: Liquen escudo verde
species.short_description: Loosely attached apple-green foliose lichen with wrinkled ridges, on bark.
species.en_short_description: Loosely attached apple-green foliose lichen with wrinkled ridges, on bark.
species.description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. The most-observed lichen here. Forms broad pale-green rosettes on tree trunks. Ridges bear granular powdery patches.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. The most-observed lichen here. Forms broad pale-green rosettes on tree trunks. Ridges bear granular powdery patches.

species.name: Liquen de encino
species.short_description: Tufted pale grey-green lichen with flattened forking branches, white beneath.
species.en_short_description: Tufted pale grey-green lichen with flattened forking branches, white beneath.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Branches are strap-like and channelled, with a distinctly whiter underside. Harvested commercially as a perfume fixative.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Branches are strap-like and channelled, with a distinctly whiter underside. Harvested commercially as a perfume fixative.

species.name: Pulmonaria de árbol
species.short_description: Large leafy lichen with a ridged, pitted green surface resembling lung tissue.
species.en_short_description: Large leafy lichen with a ridged, pitted green surface resembling lung tissue.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Bright green when wet, dull brown when dry. An indicator of clean air and old forest. Fixes nitrogen via cyanobacteria.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Bright green when wet, dull brown when dry. An indicator of clean air and old forest. Fixes nitrogen via cyanobacteria.

species.name: ojos de oro
species.short_description: Small tufted orange-yellow lichen with disc-shaped fruiting bodies fringed in lashes.
species.en_short_description: Small tufted orange-yellow lichen with disc-shaped fruiting bodies fringed in lashes.
species.description: California, New York and Baja California Sur. The eyelash-fringed orange discs are unmistakable. Grows on twigs of shrubs and small trees in open sunny places.
species.en_description: California, New York and Baja California Sur. The eyelash-fringed orange discs are unmistakable. Grows on twigs of shrubs and small trees in open sunny places.

species.name: Liquen de roca amarillo
species.short_description: Bright sulphur-yellow crust broken into small angular tiles on rock.
species.en_short_description: Bright sulphur-yellow crust broken into small angular tiles on rock.
species.description: Five regions. Forms vivid yellow patches on siliceous rock in sunny exposed sites. The colour is startling against grey stone and visible at a distance.
species.en_description: Five regions. Forms vivid yellow patches on siliceous rock in sunny exposed sites. The colour is startling against grey stone and visible at a distance.

species.name: lace lichen
species.short_description: Pale grey-green net-like lichen hanging in long mesh curtains from branches.
species.en_short_description: Pale grey-green net-like lichen hanging in long mesh curtains from branches.
species.description: California, Washington and Baja California Sur. California's state lichen. The reticulate lacy structure is unique. Drapes oak and pine in the coastal fog belt.
species.en_description: California, Washington and Baja California Sur. California's state lichen. The reticulate lacy structure is unique. Drapes oak and pine in the coastal fog belt.

species.name: Elegant Sunburst Lichen
species.short_description: Bright orange rosette lichen forming neat circles on rock.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange rosette lichen forming neat circles on rock.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Grows on nutrient-enriched rock, often below bird perches. Vivid orange lobes radiate from a central mass of discs.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Grows on nutrient-enriched rock, often below bird perches. Vivid orange lobes radiate from a central mass of discs.

species.name: Liquen escudo verde manchado
species.short_description: Pale yellow-green foliose lichen with white speckles and powdery lobe margins.
species.en_short_description: Pale yellow-green foliose lichen with white speckles and powdery lobe margins.
species.description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. The white pores on the surface and the granular fringe along the edges separate it from plain greenshields.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. The white pores on the surface and the granular fringe along the edges separate it from plain greenshields.

species.name: Líquen de roca
species.short_description: Tightly attached olive-green lichen forming crusty patches on rock.
species.en_short_description: Tightly attached olive-green lichen forming crusty patches on rock.
species.description: Five regions. Adheres closely to stone so it cannot be lifted intact. Yellow-green when dry, darker when wet. One of the commonest rock lichens in dry regions.
species.en_description: Five regions. Adheres closely to stone so it cannot be lifted intact. Yellow-green when dry, darker when wet. One of the commonest rock lichens in dry regions.

species.name: Frosted Rock Tripe
species.short_description: Large brown leathery leaf attached to rock at a single central point.
species.en_short_description: Large brown leathery leaf attached to rock at a single central point.
species.description: Five regions. Hangs off boulders like a scrap of leather, pale and net-veined beneath. Brittle when dry and rubbery when wet. Historically eaten as survival food.
species.en_description: Five regions. Hangs off boulders like a scrap of leather, pale and net-veined beneath. Brittle when dry and rubbery when wet. Historically eaten as survival food.

species.name: Frosted Rosette Lichen
species.short_description: Grey rosette lichen with a white frosted bloom on the lobe tips.
species.en_short_description: Grey rosette lichen with a white frosted bloom on the lobe tips.
species.description: California and Mexico City region. The powdery white coating gives a frosted look. Forms neat circular patches on bark and twigs in open sunny sites.
species.en_description: California and Mexico City region. The powdery white coating gives a frosted look. Forms neat circular patches on bark and twigs in open sunny sites.

species.name: Liquen de roseta
species.short_description: Small grey rosette lichen with narrow lobes and black-centred fruiting discs.
species.en_short_description: Small grey rosette lichen with narrow lobes and black-centred fruiting discs.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Forms tidy star-shaped rosettes on twigs and bark. Dark discs with pale grey rims stud the centre.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. Forms tidy star-shaped rosettes on twigs and bark. Dark discs with pale grey rims stud the centre.

species.name: Lettuce Lichen
species.short_description: Large pale green ruffled lichen with lobed crinkled edges, like lettuce leaves.
species.en_short_description: Large pale green ruffled lichen with lobed crinkled edges, like lettuce leaves.
species.description: California and Washington. Falls from old-growth canopy after storms, which is how it is usually found. Fixes nitrogen and is important winter browse for deer and elk.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Falls from old-growth canopy after storms, which is how it is usually found. Fixes nitrogen and is important winter browse for deer and elk.

species.name: Stonewall Rim Lichen
species.short_description: Pale grey-green crust with crowded fruiting discs, on stone walls and concrete.
species.en_short_description: Pale grey-green crust with crowded fruiting discs, on stone walls and concrete.
species.description: Five regions. Thrives on man-made stone, mortar and concrete as readily as natural rock. Forms tight patches studded with pale-rimmed brown discs.
species.en_description: Five regions. Thrives on man-made stone, mortar and concrete as readily as natural rock. Forms tight patches studded with pale-rimmed brown discs.

species.name: wolf lichen
species.short_description: Shrubby bright chartreuse-yellow lichen with angular branches, on conifer bark.
species.en_short_description: Shrubby bright chartreuse-yellow lichen with angular branches, on conifer bark.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. The startling yellow-green colour comes from vulpinic acid, which is toxic — it was historically used to poison wolves.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. The startling yellow-green colour comes from vulpinic acid, which is toxic — it was historically used to poison wolves.

species.name: Moondust Speckled Lichen
species.short_description: Pale grey-green foliose lichen with white surface speckles and broad rounded lobes.
species.en_short_description: Pale grey-green foliose lichen with white surface speckles and broad rounded lobes.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. The scattered white pores across the upper surface are the field mark. Grows flat against hardwood bark.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. The scattered white pores across the upper surface are the field mark. Grows flat against hardwood bark.

species.name: Candy Lichen
species.short_description: Pale mint-green crust studded with bright pink fruiting discs.
species.en_short_description: Pale mint-green crust studded with bright pink fruiting discs.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. The pink-on-green combination is unlike any other lichen here. Grows on rotting wood, peat and soil in damp cool forest.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. The pink-on-green combination is unlike any other lichen here. Grows on rotting wood, peat and soil in damp cool forest.

species.name: Orange Rock Posy
species.short_description: Cushion lichen with pale lobes and crowded orange to yellow fruiting discs.
species.en_short_description: Cushion lichen with pale lobes and crowded orange to yellow fruiting discs.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Forms small tight rosettes on exposed rock in dry mountain country. The mass of warm-toned discs fills the centre.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Forms small tight rosettes on exposed rock in dry mountain country. The mass of warm-toned discs fills the centre.

species.name: Liquen escudo verde manchado
species.short_description: Yellow-green foliose lichen with white speckles and smooth lobe edges.
species.en_short_description: Yellow-green foliose lichen with white speckles and smooth lobe edges.
species.description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Like the powder-edged species but with plain rather than granular margins. Forms broad rosettes on bark.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, New York and Mexico City. Like the powder-edged species but with plain rather than granular margins. Forms broad rosettes on bark.

species.name: Liquen de barba
species.short_description: Pale grey-green tufted lichen with bristly branches and a tough elastic core.
species.en_short_description: Pale grey-green tufted lichen with bristly branches and a tough elastic core.
species.description: Five regions. Pulling a branch reveals a white elastic central cord, which confirms the genus. Hangs in short untidy tufts from conifer twigs.
species.en_description: Five regions. Pulling a branch reveals a white elastic central cord, which confirms the genus. Hangs in short untidy tufts from conifer twigs.

species.name: Liquen de roseta meloso
species.short_description: Small pale grey rosette lichen with granular powdery lobe tips.
species.en_short_description: Small pale grey rosette lichen with granular powdery lobe tips.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Extremely common on urban and suburban bark, tolerating pollution well. Forms ragged grey rosettes with mealy edges.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Extremely common on urban and suburban bark, tolerating pollution well. Forms ragged grey rosettes with mealy edges.

species.name: Powdered Sunshine Lichen
species.short_description: Bright yellow foliose lichen with powdery margins, on conifer bark.
species.en_short_description: Bright yellow foliose lichen with powdery margins, on conifer bark.
species.description: Colorado and New York. Vivid sulphur-yellow throughout, with granular powder along the lobe edges. Grows on conifer trunks and branches in cool forest.
species.en_description: Colorado and New York. Vivid sulphur-yellow throughout, with granular powder along the lobe edges. Grows on conifer trunks and branches in cool forest.

species.name: Common Antler Lichen
species.short_description: Grey-green shrubby lichen with flattened antler-like forking branches.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green shrubby lichen with flattened antler-like forking branches.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Branches are strap-shaped and fork repeatedly like antlers, with a white underside. Grows on conifer and hardwood bark.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Branches are strap-shaped and fork repeatedly like antlers, with a white underside. Grows on conifer and hardwood bark.

species.name: Netted shield lichen
species.short_description: Grey foliose lichen with a network of fine white cracks and ridges.
species.en_short_description: Grey foliose lichen with a network of fine white cracks and ridges.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The reticulate white cracking across the grey surface is diagnostic. Very common on bark and wood; pollution-tolerant.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The reticulate white cracking across the grey surface is diagnostic. Very common on bark and wood; pollution-tolerant.

species.name: Liquen mapa amarillo
species.short_description: Bright yellow-green crust divided by black lines into map-like territories.
species.en_short_description: Bright yellow-green crust divided by black lines into map-like territories.
species.description: Five regions. Grows on hard siliceous rock in exposed mountain and alpine sites. Used to date glacial retreat, since it grows at a measurable slow rate.
species.en_description: Five regions. Grows on hard siliceous rock in exposed mountain and alpine sites. Used to date glacial retreat, since it grows at a measurable slow rate.

species.name: Hooded Sunburst Lichen
species.short_description: Small orange lichen with hooded upturned lobe tips bearing powdery granules.
species.en_short_description: Small orange lichen with hooded upturned lobe tips bearing powdery granules.
species.description: Five regions. Forms bright orange patches on bark and rock, often on nutrient-rich surfaces. Lobe tips curl up into hoods filled with granular powder.
species.en_description: Five regions. Forms bright orange patches on bark and rock, often on nutrient-rich surfaces. Lobe tips curl up into hoods filled with granular powder.

species.name: Common Toadskin Lichen
species.short_description: Brown lichen attached at one point, its surface covered in blister-like pimples.
species.en_short_description: Brown lichen attached at one point, its surface covered in blister-like pimples.
species.description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The pustular warty surface gives the name. Attached centrally to rock like other rock tripes but with a bumpy texture.
species.en_description: Colorado, New York and Mexico City. The pustular warty surface gives the name. Attached centrally to rock like other rock tripes but with a bumpy texture.

species.name: Streaked Rosette Lichen
species.short_description: Grey-green rosette lichen with dark streaks radiating along the lobes.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green rosette lichen with dark streaks radiating along the lobes.
species.description: Mexico City region. Forms broad flat rosettes on bark in the highlands. The dark radial streaking on the upper surface distinguishes it from plain rosette lichens.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. Forms broad flat rosettes on bark in the highlands. The dark radial streaking on the upper surface distinguishes it from plain rosette lichens.

species.name: Brown-eyed Wolf Lichen
species.short_description: Chartreuse shrubby lichen with prominent brown fruiting discs.
species.en_short_description: Chartreuse shrubby lichen with prominent brown fruiting discs.
species.description: California and Washington. The same startling yellow-green as wolf lichen but producing abundant brown discs rather than powdery granules. On conifer bark and wood.
species.en_description: California and Washington. The same startling yellow-green as wolf lichen but producing abundant brown discs rather than powdery granules. On conifer bark and wood.

species.name: Devil's matchstick
species.short_description: Tiny grey stalks each topped with a shiny black ball, on rock.
species.en_short_description: Tiny grey stalks each topped with a shiny black ball, on rock.
species.description: California and Washington. Looks exactly like a cluster of spent matches. Grows on damp shaded rock in Northwest forest, often with mosses.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Looks exactly like a cluster of spent matches. Grows on damp shaded rock in Northwest forest, often with mosses.

species.name: Liquen de roseta canoso
species.short_description: Grey rosette lichen with a whitish bloom and dark fruiting discs.
species.en_short_description: Grey rosette lichen with a whitish bloom and dark fruiting discs.
species.description: New York, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. The frosted grey surface and black-brown discs are typical. Grows on twigs and bark in open sunny situations.
species.en_description: New York, Washington, Mexico City and Baja. The frosted grey surface and black-brown discs are typical. Grows on twigs and bark in open sunny situations.

species.name: Yellow Cobblestone Lichen
species.short_description: Bright yellow crust broken into small angular blocks on desert rock.
species.en_short_description: Bright yellow crust broken into small angular blocks on desert rock.
species.description: Colorado, California and Mexico City region. Forms vivid yellow mosaics on sun-baked boulders. The cracked cobblestone texture separates it from smooth yellow crusts.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Mexico City region. Forms vivid yellow mosaics on sun-baked boulders. The cracked cobblestone texture separates it from smooth yellow crusts.

species.name: Desert Firedot Lichen
species.short_description: Small orange lichen with narrow lobes and abundant orange discs, on arid rock and bark.
species.en_short_description: Small orange lichen with narrow lobes and abundant orange discs, on arid rock and bark.
species.description: Colorado and California. Bright orange throughout, forming small patches in dry exposed sites. Turns purple-red when a drop of alkali is applied.
species.en_description: Colorado and California. Bright orange throughout, forming small patches in dry exposed sites. Turns purple-red when a drop of alkali is applied.

species.name: Liquen Parietino
species.short_description: Bright orange-yellow foliose lichen with broad ruffled lobes and orange discs.
species.en_short_description: Bright orange-yellow foliose lichen with broad ruffled lobes and orange discs.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Thrives on nitrogen-enriched bark and stone, so it flourishes near farms and roads. One of the most conspicuous lichens.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. Thrives on nitrogen-enriched bark and stone, so it flourishes near farms and roads. One of the most conspicuous lichens.

species.name: Liquen tripa de roca
species.short_description: Large smooth brown leathery lichen attached to rock at a single central point.
species.en_short_description: Large smooth brown leathery lichen attached to rock at a single central point.
species.description: New York. Can exceed 10 cm across. The upper surface is smooth rather than blistered, and the underside is black and matte. Grows on shaded cliff faces.
species.en_description: New York. Can exceed 10 cm across. The upper surface is smooth rather than blistered, and the underside is black and matte. Grows on shaded cliff faces.

species.name: Varied Rag Lichen
species.short_description: Pale grey ruffled foliose lichen with wrinkled lobes and powdery margins.
species.en_short_description: Pale grey ruffled foliose lichen with wrinkled lobes and powdery margins.
species.description: California, New York and Washington. Hangs loosely from conifer branches with a distinctly rag-like torn appearance. Very common in humid forest.
species.en_description: California, New York and Washington. Hangs loosely from conifer branches with a distinctly rag-like torn appearance. Very common in humid forest.

species.name: Emery Rocktripe Lichen
species.short_description: Dark brown rock tripe with a rough sandpapery upper surface.
species.en_short_description: Dark brown rock tripe with a rough sandpapery upper surface.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Smaller than the frosted rock tripe with a gritty emery-like texture. Attached centrally to exposed boulders.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and Baja. Smaller than the frosted rock tripe with a gritty emery-like texture. Attached centrally to exposed boulders.

species.name: Fluffy Dust Lichen
species.short_description: Soft pale blue-green powdery crust with no defined structure.
species.en_short_description: Soft pale blue-green powdery crust with no defined structure.
species.description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Looks like a dusting of coloured flour on sheltered bark and rock. Entirely granular, with no lobes or discs.
species.en_description: California, New York, Washington and Mexico City. Looks like a dusting of coloured flour on sheltered bark and rock. Entirely granular, with no lobes or discs.

species.name: White Fringe
species.short_description: Grey-white foliose lichen with narrow lobes fringed in dark hairs.
species.en_short_description: Grey-white foliose lichen with narrow lobes fringed in dark hairs.
species.description: Mexico City region. The fine black rhizines projecting beyond the pale lobe edges give a fringed look. Grows on bark and mossy rock in the highlands.
species.en_description: Mexico City region. The fine black rhizines projecting beyond the pale lobe edges give a fringed look. Grows on bark and mossy rock in the highlands.

species.name: Smokey-eyed Boulder Lichen
species.short_description: Pale grey crust on rock studded with black discs surrounded by a bluish bloom.
species.en_short_description: Pale grey crust on rock studded with black discs surrounded by a bluish bloom.
species.description: New York. The blue-grey pruinose ring around each black disc gives the smoky-eyed name. Grows tightly bonded to siliceous boulders and outcrops.
species.en_description: New York. The blue-grey pruinose ring around each black disc gives the smoky-eyed name. Grows tightly bonded to siliceous boulders and outcrops.

species.name: membranous pelt lichen
species.short_description: Large thin grey-brown lobed lichen with conspicuous veins on the underside.
species.en_short_description: Large thin grey-brown lobed lichen with conspicuous veins on the underside.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. The pale raised veins and root-like tufts beneath are diagnostic. Grows on mossy soil, rock and logs in damp forest. Fixes nitrogen.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. The pale raised veins and root-like tufts beneath are diagnostic. Grows on mossy soil, rock and logs in damp forest. Fixes nitrogen.

species.name: Pseudevernia intensa
species.short_description: Grey-green shrubby lichen with flattened forking branches, on highland conifers.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green shrubby lichen with flattened forking branches, on highland conifers.
species.description: Colorado, Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A western and Mexican antler lichen of montane conifer bark, with strap-like white-backed branches.
species.en_description: Colorado, Mexico City region and Baja California Sur. A western and Mexican antler lichen of montane conifer bark, with strap-like white-backed branches.

species.name: Golden Moonglow Lichen
species.short_description: Yellow-green crust forming rosettes with a dark centre and radiating lobes on rock.
species.en_short_description: Yellow-green crust forming rosettes with a dark centre and radiating lobes on rock.
species.description: Colorado, California and New York. Forms distinct circular patches with a pale radiating margin and a darkened middle. Common on exposed siliceous rock.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and New York. Forms distinct circular patches with a pale radiating margin and a darkened middle. Common on exposed siliceous rock.

species.name: fan pelt lichen
species.short_description: Small fan-shaped green lichen with veined undersides, on soil and moss.
species.en_short_description: Small fan-shaped green lichen with veined undersides, on soil and moss.
species.description: Colorado, California and Washington. Much smaller than other pelt lichens, forming little green fans on bare damp soil and among mosses. Fixes nitrogen.
species.en_description: Colorado, California and Washington. Much smaller than other pelt lichens, forming little green fans on bare damp soil and among mosses. Fixes nitrogen.

species.name: Golden Hair-lichen
species.short_description: Bright golden-orange tufted lichen with fine branching hairs.
species.en_short_description: Bright golden-orange tufted lichen with fine branching hairs.
species.description: California and Baja California Sur. Forms vivid orange tufts on coastal shrubs and rock in the fog belt. Declining with air pollution in many areas.
species.en_description: California and Baja California Sur. Forms vivid orange tufts on coastal shrubs and rock in the fog belt. Declining with air pollution in many areas.

species.name: Farinose Cartilage Lichen
species.short_description: Pale green strap-like lichen with powdery patches along the branch edges.
species.en_short_description: Pale green strap-like lichen with powdery patches along the branch edges.
species.description: California and Washington. Branches are flattened and slightly channelled, with distinct oval powdery patches on the margins. Tufted on bark and twigs.
species.en_description: California and Washington. Branches are flattened and slightly channelled, with distinct oval powdery patches on the margins. Tufted on bark and twigs.

species.name: Powdery Axil-bristle Lichen
species.short_description: Grey-green foliose lichen with yellow inner tissue and powdery lobe junctions.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green foliose lichen with yellow inner tissue and powdery lobe junctions.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Breaking a lobe reveals a distinctly yellow interior, which is diagnostic. Grows flat on hardwood bark.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Breaking a lobe reveals a distinctly yellow interior, which is diagnostic. Grows flat on hardwood bark.

species.name: rough speckled shield lichen
species.short_description: Grey foliose lichen with white surface speckles and a rough granular surface.
species.en_short_description: Grey foliose lichen with white surface speckles and a rough granular surface.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Broad grey lobes marked with white pores and scattered granules. Common on hardwood trunks in eastern woodland.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Broad grey lobes marked with white pores and scattered granules. Common on hardwood trunks in eastern woodland.

species.name: Trumpet Lichen
species.short_description: Small pale green stalks flaring into neat trumpet-shaped cups.
species.en_short_description: Small pale green stalks flaring into neat trumpet-shaped cups.
species.description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The regular smooth-edged goblets on short stalks are unmistakable. Grows on soil, rotting wood and mossy banks.
species.en_description: Colorado, California, Washington and New York. The regular smooth-edged goblets on short stalks are unmistakable. Grows on soil, rotting wood and mossy banks.

species.name: Liquen limón
species.short_description: Tiny bright egg-yellow granular lichen forming small patches on bark.
species.en_short_description: Tiny bright egg-yellow granular lichen forming small patches on bark.
species.description: New York and Mexico City region. Vivid lemon-yellow and finely divided into small scales. Tolerates urban pollution, so it is common on street trees.
species.en_description: New York and Mexico City region. Vivid lemon-yellow and finely divided into small scales. Tolerates urban pollution, so it is common on street trees.

species.name: Primavera
species.short_description: March to May: snowmelt, first migrants, and the year's fastest change in what is visible.
species.en_short_description: March to May: snowmelt, first migrants, and the year's fastest change in what is visible.
species.description: The season of arrival. Chorus frogs call from meltwater pools, warblers move north, and wildflowers race through the window between snow and summer drought. In the deserts of Baja and southern California the spring bloom follows winter rain, while Colorado's high country is still under snow.
species.en_description: The season of arrival. Chorus frogs call from meltwater pools, warblers move north, and wildflowers race through the window between snow and summer drought. In the deserts of Baja and southern California the spring bloom follows winter rain, while Colorado's high country is still under snow.

species.name: Verano
species.short_description: June to August: peak insect and reptile activity, monsoon storms, alpine wildflowers.
species.en_short_description: June to August: peak insect and reptile activity, monsoon storms, alpine wildflowers.
species.description: The longest days and the widest range of subjects. Lizards and butterflies are at their most active, the North American monsoon brings afternoon storms to Colorado and central Mexico, and the alpine meadows finally flower as the snow retreats above treeline.
species.en_description: The longest days and the widest range of subjects. Lizards and butterflies are at their most active, the North American monsoon brings afternoon storms to Colorado and central Mexico, and the alpine meadows finally flower as the snow retreats above treeline.

species.name: Otoño
species.short_description: September to November: migration, fungi, aspen gold, and the whale calving run beginning.
species.en_short_description: September to November: migration, fungi, aspen gold, and the whale calving run beginning.
species.description: The richest season for fungi, when the first rains bring fruiting bodies up across the Pacific Northwest. Aspens turn in Colorado, raptors and waterfowl stream south, and grey whales begin the journey toward the Baja lagoons.
species.en_description: The richest season for fungi, when the first rains bring fruiting bodies up across the Pacific Northwest. Aspens turn in Colorado, raptors and waterfowl stream south, and grey whales begin the journey toward the Baja lagoons.

species.name: Invierno
species.short_description: December to February: waterfowl concentrations, tracks in snow, whales in Baja lagoons.
species.en_short_description: December to February: waterfowl concentrations, tracks in snow, whales in Baja lagoons.
species.description: The season of concentration rather than absence. Ducks and geese crowd onto open water, snow records the movements of animals that are never seen, grey whales calve in Baja California Sur, and lichens and mosses come into their own on the wet Pacific coast.
species.en_description: The season of concentration rather than absence. Ducks and geese crowd onto open water, snow records the movements of animals that are never seen, grey whales calve in Baja California Sur, and lichens and mosses come into their own on the wet Pacific coast.

species.name: Cielo despejado
species.short_description: Cloudless sky, deepest blue overhead and paler toward the horizon.
species.en_short_description: Cloudless sky, deepest blue overhead and paler toward the horizon.
species.description: The gradient exists because there is more atmosphere to look through near the horizon, scattering the blue away. Deepest at high elevation, where there is less air above — which is why Colorado skies read darker than coastal ones.
species.en_description: The gradient exists because there is more atmosphere to look through near the horizon, scattering the blue away. Deepest at high elevation, where there is less air above — which is why Colorado skies read darker than coastal ones.

species.name: Nubes cúmulus
species.short_description: Detached puffy white clouds with flat bases and cauliflower tops.
species.en_short_description: Detached puffy white clouds with flat bases and cauliflower tops.
species.description: Formed by rising thermals condensing at a uniform height, which is why the bases all sit on one level. Fair-weather cumulus mark a stable day; vertical growth through the afternoon is the first sign of a storm building.
species.en_description: Formed by rising thermals condensing at a uniform height, which is why the bases all sit on one level. Fair-weather cumulus mark a stable day; vertical growth through the afternoon is the first sign of a storm building.

species.name: Cielo cubierto
species.short_description: Featureless grey sheet covering the whole sky, often with drizzle.
species.en_short_description: Featureless grey sheet covering the whole sky, often with drizzle.
species.description: A uniform low layer with no structure and no visible sun disc. The default winter sky of Seattle and the Pacific Northwest. Produces drizzle and mist rather than real rain.
species.en_description: A uniform low layer with no structure and no visible sun disc. The default winter sky of Seattle and the Pacific Northwest. Produces drizzle and mist rather than real rain.

species.name: Nubes cirros
species.short_description: High thin wispy streaks of ice crystals, often hooked at one end.
species.en_short_description: High thin wispy streaks of ice crystals, often hooked at one end.
species.description: Forming above 6,000 metres and made entirely of ice. The hooked shape comes from crystals falling into slower wind below. Thickening cirrus often precedes a warm front by a day.
species.en_description: Forming above 6,000 metres and made entirely of ice. The hooked shape comes from crystals falling into slower wind below. Thickening cirrus often precedes a warm front by a day.

species.name: Altocúmulos
species.short_description: Mid-level sheet broken into regular rounded patches or rolls.
species.en_short_description: Mid-level sheet broken into regular rounded patches or rolls.
species.description: A patterned layer at intermediate height, often described as a mackerel sky. The regular cells indicate instability at that level, and a morning display frequently precedes afternoon thunderstorms.
species.en_description: A patterned layer at intermediate height, often described as a mackerel sky. The regular cells indicate instability at that level, and a morning display frequently precedes afternoon thunderstorms.

species.name: Nubes lenticulares
species.short_description: Smooth lens- or almond-shaped clouds standing still over a mountain range.
species.en_short_description: Smooth lens- or almond-shaped clouds standing still over a mountain range.
species.description: Formed in standing waves downwind of a ridge. They appear stationary while air rushes through them, condensing on the rise and evaporating on the fall. A Colorado Front Range signature, and a sign of severe turbulence aloft.
species.en_description: Formed in standing waves downwind of a ridge. They appear stationary while air rushes through them, condensing on the rise and evaporating on the fall. A Colorado Front Range signature, and a sign of severe turbulence aloft.

species.name: Nubes mammatus
species.short_description: Rows of drooping pouches hanging from the underside of a cloud base.
species.en_short_description: Rows of drooping pouches hanging from the underside of a cloud base.
species.description: Formed by sinking pockets of cool moist air beneath a storm anvil. They usually appear after the worst of a storm has passed rather than before it, and are most striking in low evening light.
species.en_description: Formed by sinking pockets of cool moist air beneath a storm anvil. They usually appear after the worst of a storm has passed rather than before it, and are most striking in low evening light.

species.name: Niebla costera
species.short_description: Low sea fog pushing inland, cutting off abruptly at a hillside or ridge.
species.en_short_description: Low sea fog pushing inland, cutting off abruptly at a hillside or ridge.
species.description: Cool ocean air trapped beneath a warm inversion. The defining summer sky of coastal California and Baja, and the water source that lets coast redwoods grow. Burns back through the morning and returns by evening.
species.en_description: Cool ocean air trapped beneath a warm inversion. The defining summer sky of coastal California and Baja, and the water source that lets coast redwoods grow. Burns back through the morning and returns by evening.

species.name: Niebla de radiación
species.short_description: Shallow ground fog forming overnight in valleys and hollows on still clear nights.
species.en_short_description: Shallow ground fog forming overnight in valleys and hollows on still clear nights.
species.description: The ground radiates heat away under a clear sky, chilling the air just above it past its dew point. Needs calm conditions; any wind mixes it away. Pools in low ground and lifts soon after sunrise.
species.en_description: The ground radiates heat away under a clear sky, chilling the air just above it past its dew point. Needs calm conditions; any wind mixes it away. Pools in low ground and lifts soon after sunrise.

species.name: Amanecer
species.short_description: The sun clearing the horizon, with the longest light path of the day.
species.en_short_description: The sun clearing the horizon, with the longest light path of the day.
species.description: Low-angle light travels through far more atmosphere, scattering out the blue and leaving red and orange. The best hour for mammals and birds, and the reason most field records cluster around it.
species.en_description: Low-angle light travels through far more atmosphere, scattering out the blue and leaving red and orange. The best hour for mammals and birds, and the reason most field records cluster around it.

species.name: Atardecer
species.short_description: The sun dropping below the horizon, often with the strongest colour of the day.
species.en_short_description: The sun dropping below the horizon, often with the strongest colour of the day.
species.description: Colour intensity depends on particles aloft — dust, smoke and haze deepen it. Watch for the green flash at the moment the last edge disappears over an ocean horizon, and for alpenglow on peaks afterward.
species.en_description: Colour intensity depends on particles aloft — dust, smoke and haze deepen it. Watch for the green flash at the moment the last edge disappears over an ocean horizon, and for alpenglow on peaks afterward.

species.name: Arcoíris
