species.short_description: Arc of spectral colour opposite the sun, in falling rain or spray.
species.en_short_description: Arc of spectral colour opposite the sun, in falling rain or spray.
species.description: Sunlight refracts entering a raindrop, reflects off the back and refracts again on exit, always at about 42 degrees from the antisolar point. Look for a fainter secondary bow outside it with the colours reversed.
species.en_description: Sunlight refracts entering a raindrop, reflects off the back and refracts again on exit, always at about 42 degrees from the antisolar point. Look for a fainter secondary bow outside it with the colours reversed.

species.name: Rayos crepusculares
species.short_description: Beams of light and shadow radiating from behind a cloud or ridge.
species.en_short_description: Beams of light and shadow radiating from behind a cloud or ridge.
species.description: Shafts of sunlight made visible by haze and dust, with cloud edges casting the shadows between them. The rays are effectively parallel; the fan shape is perspective. Strongest near sunrise and sunset.
species.en_description: Shafts of sunlight made visible by haze and dust, with cloud edges casting the shadows between them. The rays are effectively parallel; the fan shape is perspective. Strongest near sunrise and sunset.

species.name: Halo solar
species.short_description: A ring 22 degrees around the sun, sometimes with bright spots either side.
species.en_short_description: A ring 22 degrees around the sun, sometimes with bright spots either side.
species.description: Refraction through hexagonal ice crystals in high cirrus. The bright patches level with the sun are sun dogs. Common over Colorado's high country and often a sign of an approaching front.
species.en_description: Refraction through hexagonal ice crystals in high cirrus. The bright patches level with the sun are sun dogs. Common over Colorado's high country and often a sign of an approaching front.

species.name: Tormenta eléctrica
species.short_description: Towering cumulonimbus with lightning, thunder and heavy rain.
species.en_short_description: Towering cumulonimbus with lightning, thunder and heavy rain.
species.description: A single deep convective cell, often anvil-topped where it hits the tropopause. Colorado's Front Range and the Valley of Mexico both get near-daily afternoon storms in the wet season. Count seconds between flash and thunder and divide by three for kilometres.
species.en_description: A single deep convective cell, often anvil-topped where it hits the tropopause. Colorado's Front Range and the Valley of Mexico both get near-daily afternoon storms in the wet season. Count seconds between flash and thunder and divide by three for kilometres.

species.name: Supercelda
species.short_description: Rotating thunderstorm with a persistent updraft and a striated cloud base.
species.en_short_description: Rotating thunderstorm with a persistent updraft and a striated cloud base.
species.description: The most organised and dangerous storm type, with a mesocyclone that can produce large hail and tornadoes. Recognisable by the corkscrew striations on the updraft tower and a lowered rotating wall cloud.
species.en_description: The most organised and dangerous storm type, with a mesocyclone that can produce large hail and tornadoes. Recognisable by the corkscrew striations on the updraft tower and a lowered rotating wall cloud.

species.name: Tormenta monzónica
species.short_description: Afternoon storm from moist air drawn north in mid- to late summer.
species.en_short_description: Afternoon storm from moist air drawn north in mid- to late summer.
species.description: The North American monsoon pulls moisture inland from July through September, bringing the reliable afternoon storms of Colorado, Baja California Sur and central Mexico. Triggers desert amphibian breeding within hours.
species.en_description: The North American monsoon pulls moisture inland from July through September, bringing the reliable afternoon storms of Colorado, Baja California Sur and central Mexico. Triggers desert amphibian breeding within hours.

species.name: Granizada
species.short_description: Storm dropping ice pellets grown in a strong updraft.
species.en_short_description: Storm dropping ice pellets grown in a strong updraft.
species.description: Hail forms as stones cycle repeatedly through a supercooled updraft, adding layers. Colorado's Front Range sits in one of the most hail-prone corridors in North America. Stones show onion-like rings when cut.
species.en_description: Hail forms as stones cycle repeatedly through a supercooled updraft, adding layers. Colorado's Front Range sits in one of the most hail-prone corridors in North America. Stones show onion-like rings when cut.

species.name: Tormenta de nieve
species.short_description: Steady snowfall with light to moderate wind.
species.en_short_description: Steady snowfall with light to moderate wind.
species.description: Snow needs a near-freezing surface and a saturated layer aloft. The heaviest accumulations come with air just at freezing, when crystals grow largest and stick together. Records tracks and activity that would otherwise be invisible.
species.en_description: Snow needs a near-freezing surface and a saturated layer aloft. The heaviest accumulations come with air just at freezing, when crystals grow largest and stick together. Records tracks and activity that would otherwise be invisible.

species.name: Ventisca
species.short_description: Snow driven by sustained strong wind, reducing visibility to near nothing.
species.en_short_description: Snow driven by sustained strong wind, reducing visibility to near nothing.
species.description: Defined by wind and visibility, not by snowfall — ground blizzards occur with no new snow at all. Common on Colorado's eastern plains, where there is nothing to slow the wind.
species.en_description: Defined by wind and visibility, not by snowfall — ground blizzards occur with no new snow at all. Common on Colorado's eastern plains, where there is nothing to slow the wind.

species.name: Río atmosférico
species.short_description: Narrow corridor of concentrated water vapour delivering days of heavy rain.
species.en_short_description: Narrow corridor of concentrated water vapour delivering days of heavy rain.
species.description: A long plume of tropical moisture steered onto the coast, sometimes called a pineapple express. Supplies much of California's and Washington's annual precipitation in a handful of events, and drives both floods and drought relief.
species.en_description: A long plume of tropical moisture steered onto the coast, sometimes called a pineapple express. Supplies much of California's and Washington's annual precipitation in a handful of events, and drives both floods and drought relief.

species.name: Huracán
species.short_description: Rotating tropical cyclone with a defined eye and sustained destructive winds.
species.en_short_description: Rotating tropical cyclone with a defined eye and sustained destructive winds.
species.description: Eastern Pacific hurricanes track up the Baja peninsula between May and November, and their remnants reach as far as Colorado as heavy rain. Called huracán in the eastern Pacific and Atlantic.
species.en_description: Eastern Pacific hurricanes track up the Baja peninsula between May and November, and their remnants reach as far as Colorado as heavy rain. Called huracán in the eastern Pacific and Atlantic.

species.name: Tormenta de polvo
species.short_description: Wall of airborne dust or sand advancing across dry ground.
species.en_short_description: Wall of airborne dust or sand advancing across dry ground.
species.description: Raised by strong winds over bare soil, often on a thunderstorm outflow — a haboob. Occurs on Colorado's plains and in the deserts of Baja and southern California, and can drop visibility to nothing in minutes.
species.en_description: Raised by strong winds over bare soil, often on a thunderstorm outflow — a haboob. Occurs on Colorado's plains and in the deserts of Baja and southern California, and can drop visibility to nothing in minutes.

species.name: Vendaval
species.short_description: Sustained damaging wind without significant precipitation.
species.en_short_description: Sustained damaging wind without significant precipitation.
species.description: Includes the downslope chinook and bora winds that funnel off Colorado's Front Range at hurricane force, and the Santa Ana events that drive California's autumn fire weather. Warm and extremely dry.
species.en_description: Includes the downslope chinook and bora winds that funnel off Colorado's Front Range at hurricane force, and the Santa Ana events that drive California's autumn fire weather. Warm and extremely dry.

species.name: Tormenta de hielo
species.short_description: Freezing rain glazing every surface in clear ice.
species.en_short_description: Freezing rain glazing every surface in clear ice.
species.description: Rain falls through a warm layer and freezes on contact with a below-freezing surface. Produces the heaviest loading of any winter event, snapping branches and power lines. A New York and north-eastern hazard.
species.en_description: Rain falls through a warm layer and freezes on contact with a below-freezing surface. Produces the heaviest loading of any winter event, snapping branches and power lines. A New York and north-eastern hazard.

species.name: Aguanieve granulada
species.short_description: Soft white pellets of rimed snow, bouncing on impact.
species.en_short_description: Soft white pellets of rimed snow, bouncing on impact.
species.description: Snow crystals collect supercooled droplets until they become opaque pellets — neither hail nor snow. Bounces and crumbles rather than shattering. Common in spring convective showers in the mountains.
species.en_description: Snow crystals collect supercooled droplets until they become opaque pellets — neither hail nor snow. Bounces and crumbles rather than shattering. Common in spring convective showers in the mountains.

species.name: Borrego cimarrón
species.short_description: Colorado's state animal: a cliff-dwelling wild sheep whose rams carry curling horns.
species.en_short_description: Colorado's state animal: a cliff-dwelling wild sheep whose rams carry curling horns.
species.description: The Rocky Mountain subspecies is Colorado's state animal and the emblem of its wildlife agency. Rams grow heavy spiralling horns they slam together in autumn rut; ewes carry short spikes. Look for the white rump patch on rock faces and roadcuts rather than in open meadow.
species.en_description: The Rocky Mountain subspecies is Colorado's state animal and the emblem of its wildlife agency. Rams grow heavy spiralling horns they slam together in autumn rut; ewes carry short spikes. Look for the white rump patch on rock faces and roadcuts rather than in open meadow.

species.name: Berrendo
species.short_description: The fastest land animal in North America, and not an antelope despite the name.
species.en_short_description: The fastest land animal in North America, and not an antelope despite the name.
species.description: A shortgrass-prairie runner of Colorado's eastern plains and North Park, capable of holding 55 mph over open ground. The only mammal with branched horns that it sheds each year. Tan and white in sharp bands, with a rump patch it flares as an alarm signal visible a mile off.
species.en_description: A shortgrass-prairie runner of Colorado's eastern plains and North Park, capable of holding 55 mph over open ground. The only mammal with branched horns that it sheds each year. Tan and white in sharp bands, with a rump patch it flares as an alarm signal visible a mile off.

species.name: Cabra de las Rocosas
species.short_description: Shaggy white climber of the highest ridges, with black stiletto horns in both sexes.
species.en_short_description: Shaggy white climber of the highest ridges, with black stiletto horns in both sexes.
species.description: Introduced to Colorado in the 1940s and now firmly established above treeline on Mount Blue Sky, Quandary Peak and the Sawatch. Told from a bighorn ewe by the pure white coat, the beard, and horns that are thin, black and barely curved. Hooves have a soft inner pad for grip on wet rock.
species.en_description: Introduced to Colorado in the 1940s and now firmly established above treeline on Mount Blue Sky, Quandary Peak and the Sawatch. Told from a bighorn ewe by the pure white coat, the beard, and horns that are thin, black and barely curved. Hooves have a soft inner pad for grip on wet rock.

species.name: Bisonte americano
species.short_description: The plains grazer that once numbered in millions, now in managed herds and refuges.
species.en_short_description: The plains grazer that once numbered in millions, now in managed herds and refuges.
species.description: Wild-roaming herds are gone from Colorado, but conservation herds at Rocky Mountain Arsenal, Genesee Park and Soapstone Prairie are genuinely observable and genetically important. Massive shoulder hump, low-slung head, and a habit of dust-wallowing that leaves bare circles in the grass.
species.en_description: Wild-roaming herds are gone from Colorado, but conservation herds at Rocky Mountain Arsenal, Genesee Park and Soapstone Prairie are genuinely observable and genetically important. Massive shoulder hump, low-slung head, and a habit of dust-wallowing that leaves bare circles in the grass.

species.name: Caballo cimarrón
species.short_description: Free-roaming descendants of escaped stock, in four managed herds on the Western Slope.
species.en_short_description: Free-roaming descendants of escaped stock, in four managed herds on the Western Slope.
species.description: Colorado's wild horse herds live in the Sand Wash Basin, Little Book Cliffs, Piceance-East Douglas and Spring Creek Basin. Not a native species and not truly wild, but a self-sustaining population an observer meets on its own terms. Bands are led by a mare; a stallion trails and guards.
species.en_description: Colorado's wild horse herds live in the Sand Wash Basin, Little Book Cliffs, Piceance-East Douglas and Spring Creek Basin. Not a native species and not truly wild, but a self-sustaining population an observer meets on its own terms. Bands are led by a mare; a stallion trails and guards.

species.name: Lince canadiense
species.short_description: Snowshoe-footed cat of the spruce-fir high country, reintroduced to Colorado in 1999.
species.en_short_description: Snowshoe-footed cat of the spruce-fir high country, reintroduced to Colorado in 1999.
species.description: Extirpated from the state by the 1970s and returned by a release programme in the San Juans that is now considered successful. Bigger paws, longer black ear tufts and a wholly black tail tip separate it from a bobcat, whose tail is barred and white underneath.
species.en_description: Extirpated from the state by the 1970s and returned by a release programme in the San Juans that is now considered successful. Bigger paws, longer black ear tufts and a wholly black tail tip separate it from a bobcat, whose tail is barred and white underneath.

species.name: Hurón patinegro
species.short_description: North America's rarest mammal, a prairie dog specialist with a black bandit mask.
species.en_short_description: North America's rarest mammal, a prairie dog specialist with a black bandit mask.
species.description: Declared extinct twice and both times rediscovered; captive-bred animals are released onto Colorado prairie dog colonies at Rocky Mountain Arsenal and in the Grasslands. Entirely nocturnal and entirely dependent on prairie dogs for food and burrows. Spotlight surveys find the green eyeshine.
species.en_description: Declared extinct twice and both times rediscovered; captive-bred animals are released onto Colorado prairie dog colonies at Rocky Mountain Arsenal and in the Grasslands. Entirely nocturnal and entirely dependent on prairie dogs for food and burrows. Spotlight surveys find the green eyeshine.

species.name: Musaraña enana
species.short_description: One of the smallest mammals in North America, at around two grams; a Rocky Mountain endemic.
species.en_short_description: One of the smallest mammals in North America, at around two grams; a Rocky Mountain endemic.
species.description: Described from Colorado and largely confined to the southern Rockies, living in alpine talus, rockslides and dry montane slopes rather than the wet ground most shrews need. Weighs less than a penny. Recorded so rarely that much of its life history is still unknown.
species.en_description: Described from Colorado and largely confined to the southern Rockies, living in alpine talus, rockslides and dry montane slopes rather than the wet ground most shrews need. Weighs less than a penny. Recorded so rarely that much of its life history is still unknown.

species.name: Musaraña cinérea
species.short_description: A thumb-sized insectivore with a pointed snout and a heart rate near a thousand a minute.
species.en_short_description: A thumb-sized insectivore with a pointed snout and a heart rate near a thousand a minute.
species.description: The commonest shrew of Colorado's montane and subalpine damp ground, under logs and in streamside litter. Grey-brown above, paler below, with a bicoloured tail. Must eat close to its own body weight daily; most often found dead on a trail rather than seen alive.
species.en_description: The commonest shrew of Colorado's montane and subalpine damp ground, under logs and in streamside litter. Grey-brown above, paler below, with a bicoloured tail. Must eat close to its own body weight daily; most often found dead on a trail rather than seen alive.

species.name: Musaraña acuática americana
species.short_description: A diving shrew with stiff-haired hind feet that let it run briefly on the water surface.
species.en_short_description: A diving shrew with stiff-haired hind feet that let it run briefly on the water surface.
species.description: Hunts aquatic insects in cold, fast Colorado streams, swimming with a silver film of trapped air on its dark fur. The largest of the state's shrews and the only one likely to be seen entering water. Hunts by touch with its whiskers rather than by sight.
species.en_description: Hunts aquatic insects in cold, fast Colorado streams, swimming with a silver film of trapped air on its dark fur. The largest of the state's shrews and the only one likely to be seen entering water. Hunts by touch with its whiskers rather than by sight.

species.name: Miotis orejudo
species.short_description: A forest bat with ears so long they reach past its nose when laid forward.
species.en_short_description: A forest bat with ears so long they reach past its nose when laid forward.
species.description: Roosts in loose bark, snags and rock crevices through Colorado's ponderosa and mixed conifer country. Gleans beetles and moths straight off foliage rather than hawking them in flight, which makes its echolocation unusually quiet and hard to record.
species.en_description: Roosts in loose bark, snags and rock crevices through Colorado's ponderosa and mixed conifer country. Gleans beetles and moths straight off foliage rather than hawking them in flight, which makes its echolocation unusually quiet and hard to record.

species.name: Miotis franjeado
species.short_description: Named for the stiff fringe of hairs along the trailing edge of its tail membrane.
species.en_short_description: Named for the stiff fringe of hairs along the trailing edge of its tail membrane.
species.description: A bat of pinyon-juniper and ponderosa woodland on Colorado's foothills and Western Slope. The tail-membrane fringe is diagnostic and visible in the hand. Slow, manoeuvrable flight suited to picking beetles from branches and the ground.
species.en_description: A bat of pinyon-juniper and ponderosa woodland on Colorado's foothills and Western Slope. The tail-membrane fringe is diagnostic and visible in the hand. Slow, manoeuvrable flight suited to picking beetles from branches and the ground.

species.name: Murciélago moteado
species.short_description: Enormous pink ears and three white spots on black; its call is audible to human ears.
species.en_short_description: Enormous pink ears and three white spots on black; its call is audible to human ears.
species.description: One of the most striking and least often seen bats in North America, tied to tall cliffs in Colorado's canyon country. Forages high over open ground for moths. Unlike most bats it echolocates at a frequency low enough that a person standing below can hear the clicks.
species.en_description: One of the most striking and least often seen bats in North America, tied to tall cliffs in Colorado's canyon country. Forages high over open ground for moths. Unlike most bats it echolocates at a frequency low enough that a person standing below can hear the clicks.

species.name: Ratón chapulinero norteño
species.short_description: A carnivorous prairie mouse that stands on its hind legs and howls at the moon.
species.en_short_description: A carnivorous prairie mouse that stands on its hind legs and howls at the moon.
species.description: Hunts insects, scorpions and other mice across Colorado's eastern plains and sagebrush, and is immune enough to bark scorpion venom to eat one alive. Defends a territory with a long, thin, genuinely audible howl delivered nose-up. Stockier and shorter-tailed than a deer mouse.
species.en_description: Hunts insects, scorpions and other mice across Colorado's eastern plains and sagebrush, and is immune enough to bark scorpion venom to eat one alive. Defends a territory with a long, thin, genuinely audible howl delivered nose-up. Stockier and shorter-tailed than a deer mouse.

species.name: Rata cambalachera mexicana
species.short_description: A rock-crevice packrat that builds stick middens and trades one found object for another.
species.en_short_description: A rock-crevice packrat that builds stick middens and trades one found object for another.
species.description: Lives on Colorado's foothill cliffs, canyon walls and pinyon-juniper scree. Grey with a white belly and a furred, bicoloured tail — never the naked tail of an introduced rat. Middens accumulate for centuries and are used by paleoecologists to reconstruct past vegetation.
species.en_description: Lives on Colorado's foothill cliffs, canyon walls and pinyon-juniper scree. Grey with a white belly and a furred, bicoloured tail — never the naked tail of an introduced rat. Middens accumulate for centuries and are used by paleoecologists to reconstruct past vegetation.

species.name: Topillo montano
species.short_description: A short-tailed grassland vole whose runways stay visible in the grass after snowmelt.
species.en_short_description: A short-tailed grassland vole whose runways stay visible in the grass after snowmelt.
species.description: Abundant in Colorado's mountain parks and irrigated meadows, and the staple prey of every hawk, weasel and coyote around them. Blunt-faced with small ears buried in fur and a tail under a third of body length. Active day and night, year round, under the snow in winter.
species.en_description: Abundant in Colorado's mountain parks and irrigated meadows, and the staple prey of every hawk, weasel and coyote around them. Blunt-faced with small ears buried in fur and a tail under a third of body length. Active day and night, year round, under the snow in winter.

species.name: Topillo colilargo
species.short_description: A vole of streamside willow and forest edge, with a tail nearly half its body length.
species.en_short_description: A vole of streamside willow and forest edge, with a tail nearly half its body length.
species.description: Widespread through Colorado's montane and subalpine zone, in wetter and brushier ground than the montane vole prefers. Does not build obvious surface runways, so it turns up in odd places — under deadfall, in talus, along ditch banks.
species.en_description: Widespread through Colorado's montane and subalpine zone, in wetter and brushier ground than the montane vole prefers. Does not build obvious surface runways, so it turns up in odd places — under deadfall, in talus, along ditch banks.

species.name: Topillo de artemisa
species.short_description: Pale, silvery and very short-tailed; the only vole that thrives in dry sagebrush.
species.en_short_description: Pale, silvery and very short-tailed; the only vole that thrives in dry sagebrush.
species.description: Lives in loose colonies in northwestern Colorado's sagebrush steppe, cutting green stems and stacking them at burrow mouths to dry. Much paler than any other Colorado vole, an ash-grey that matches the soil. Needs no free water, taking all of it from plants.
species.en_description: Lives in loose colonies in northwestern Colorado's sagebrush steppe, cutting green stems and stacking them at burrow mouths to dry. Much paler than any other Colorado vole, an ash-grey that matches the soil. Needs no free water, taking all of it from plants.

species.name: Ratón saltador occidental
species.short_description: Long hind feet and an enormous tail; leaps a yard at a time through streamside grass.
species.en_short_description: Long hind feet and an enormous tail; leaps a yard at a time through streamside grass.
species.description: A hibernator of Colorado's wet mountain meadows and willow carrs, asleep for eight or nine months of the year. Rich orange-brown flanks with a dark dorsal stripe and a tail longer than head and body combined. Its Front Range cousin, Preble's meadow jumping mouse, is federally threatened.
species.en_description: A hibernator of Colorado's wet mountain meadows and willow carrs, asleep for eight or nine months of the year. Rich orange-brown flanks with a dark dorsal stripe and a tail longer than head and body combined. Its Front Range cousin, Preble's meadow jumping mouse, is federally threatened.

species.name: Tuza de las llanuras
species.short_description: A plains burrower known by its fan-shaped soil mounds and grooved orange incisors.
species.en_short_description: A plains burrower known by its fan-shaped soil mounds and grooved orange incisors.
species.description: Works Colorado's eastern sandy soils entirely underground, pushing spoil out in mounds with a plugged lateral hole off to one side. Fur-lined external cheek pouches carry food, not soil. Larger than the northern pocket gopher of the mountains, with two grooves down each upper incisor.
species.en_description: Works Colorado's eastern sandy soils entirely underground, pushing spoil out in mounds with a plugged lateral hole off to one side. Fur-lined external cheek pouches carry food, not soil. Larger than the northern pocket gopher of the mountains, with two grooves down each upper incisor.

species.name: Chara azul
species.short_description: Loud blue crest and a black necklace; an eastern bird now settled on the Front Range.
species.en_short_description: Loud blue crest and a black necklace; an eastern bird now settled on the Front Range.
species.description: Spread west along the plains cottonwoods and reached Colorado's cities in the twentieth century, where it now nests in town alongside the Steller's Jay of the foothills. Bright blue above with white wing bars and black barring; the pale grey underparts separate it from every western jay.
species.en_description: Spread west along the plains cottonwoods and reached Colorado's cities in the twentieth century, where it now nests in town alongside the Steller's Jay of the foothills. Bright blue above with white wing bars and black barring; the pale grey underparts separate it from every western jay.

species.name: Chara de Woodhouse
species.short_description: A crestless grey-blue jay of pinyon-juniper, split from the California bird in 2016.
species.en_short_description: A crestless grey-blue jay of pinyon-juniper, split from the California bird in 2016.
species.description: The scrub-jay of Colorado's foothills, mesas and Western Slope juniper. Duller and greyer than its coastal counterpart, with a faint necklace and no crest at all. Caches acorns and pinyon nuts by the thousand and remembers where a surprising number of them are.
species.en_description: The scrub-jay of Colorado's foothills, mesas and Western Slope juniper. Duller and greyer than its coastal counterpart, with a faint necklace and no crest at all. Caches acorns and pinyon nuts by the thousand and remembers where a surprising number of them are.

species.name: Chara gris
species.short_description: Soft grey "camp robber" of the spruce-fir; fearless, silent in flight, nests in March snow.
species.en_short_description: Soft grey "camp robber" of the spruce-fir; fearless, silent in flight, nests in March snow.
species.description: A subalpine resident that will land on a hand held out at a Colorado trailhead. Fluffy grey with a white face and dark nape, and no crest. Glues food to bark with sticky saliva to store it, which is what lets it raise young while the snowpack is still deep.
species.en_description: A subalpine resident that will land on a hand held out at a Colorado trailhead. Fluffy grey with a white face and dark nape, and no crest. Glues food to bark with sticky saliva to store it, which is what lets it raise young while the snowpack is still deep.

species.name: Cascanueces americano
species.short_description: Grey crow-cousin with flashing black-and-white wings and a long dagger of a bill.
species.en_short_description: Grey crow-cousin with flashing black-and-white wings and a long dagger of a bill.
species.description: The planter of Colorado's limber and bristlecone pines: it buries tens of thousands of seeds each autumn and relocates most of them months later under snow. A harsh, grating call carries across timberline basins. Watch for the white trailing edge and white outer tail in flight.
species.en_description: The planter of Colorado's limber and bristlecone pines: it buries tens of thousands of seeds each autumn and relocates most of them months later under snow. A harsh, grating call carries across timberline basins. Watch for the white trailing edge and white outer tail in flight.

species.name: Chara piñonera
species.short_description: Dusty blue, short-tailed and crow-billed; travels in noisy nomadic flocks of hundreds.
species.en_short_description: Dusty blue, short-tailed and crow-billed; travels in noisy nomadic flocks of hundreds.
species.description: Tied to pinyon pine on Colorado's Western Slope and southern foothills, and declining sharply as those woodlands are lost. Uniform dull blue with no white anywhere and a bill that looks too long for the head. A flock is heard as a rolling mew long before it is seen.
species.en_description: Tied to pinyon pine on Colorado's Western Slope and southern foothills, and declining sharply as those woodlands are lost. Uniform dull blue with no white anywhere and a bill that looks too long for the head. A flock is heard as a rolling mew long before it is seen.

species.name: Carbonero montañés
species.short_description: The conifer chickadee, told at a glance by a white eyebrow through the black cap.
species.en_short_description: The conifer chickadee, told at a glance by a white eyebrow through the black cap.
species.description: Replaces the Black-capped Chickadee upslope through Colorado's ponderosa, lodgepole and spruce, and drops into Front Range yards in hard winters. The white supercilium is diagnostic. Its whistle is a hoarse three-note descent rather than the black-capped bird's clean two.
species.en_description: Replaces the Black-capped Chickadee upslope through Colorado's ponderosa, lodgepole and spruce, and drops into Front Range yards in hard winters. The white supercilium is diagnostic. Its whistle is a hoarse three-note descent rather than the black-capped bird's clean two.

species.name: Carbonero sencillo
species.short_description: A plain grey bird with a pointed crest and no field marks whatsoever — that is the mark.
species.en_short_description: A plain grey bird with a pointed crest and no field marks whatsoever — that is the mark.
species.description: Resident in Colorado's pinyon-juniper woodland on the Western Slope and southern foothills. Featureless soft grey from bill to tail, which rules out everything else its size and shape. The song is a rapid dry trill delivered from a juniper top.
species.en_description: Resident in Colorado's pinyon-juniper woodland on the Western Slope and southern foothills. Featureless soft grey from bill to tail, which rules out everything else its size and shape. The song is a rapid dry trill delivered from a juniper top.

species.name: Sita pechiblanca
species.short_description: Walks head-down on trunks; clean white face and underparts with a black cap.
species.en_short_description: Walks head-down on trunks; clean white face and underparts with a black cap.
species.description: The nuthatch of Colorado's deciduous and ponderosa trees, in town parks as readily as canyon oaks. Wedges a seed into bark and hammers it open, which is what the name records. Its nasal, repeated yank carries a long way through open woodland.
species.en_description: The nuthatch of Colorado's deciduous and ponderosa trees, in town parks as readily as canyon oaks. Wedges a seed into bark and hammers it open, which is what the name records. Its nasal, repeated yank carries a long way through open woodland.

species.name: Sita canadiense
species.short_description: Small conifer nuthatch with a black eye-line and rusty underparts; sounds like a toy horn.
species.en_short_description: Small conifer nuthatch with a black eye-line and rusty underparts; sounds like a toy horn.
species.description: Common through Colorado's spruce-fir and lodgepole, and irruptive downslope in poor cone years. Smears pitch around its nest hole, apparently to deter predators and insects, and dives cleanly through the sticky ring on arrival.
species.en_description: Common through Colorado's spruce-fir and lodgepole, and irruptive downslope in poor cone years. Smears pitch around its nest hole, apparently to deter predators and insects, and dives cleanly through the sticky ring on arrival.

species.name: Sita enana
species.short_description: A tiny ponderosa specialist that roosts communally, dozens crammed into one cavity.
species.en_short_description: A tiny ponderosa specialist that roosts communally, dozens crammed into one cavity.
species.description: Almost never found away from ponderosa pine, which makes it a good indicator of that forest across Colorado's foothills. Grey-brown cap, whitish nape spot, buff underparts. Feeds in constant peeping flocks high in the needles, often alongside chickadees and creepers.
species.en_description: Almost never found away from ponderosa pine, which makes it a good indicator of that forest across Colorado's foothills. Grey-brown cap, whitish nape spot, buff underparts. Feeds in constant peeping flocks high in the needles, often alongside chickadees and creepers.

species.name: Trepador americano
species.short_description: Bark-patterned and near-invisible; spirals up a trunk, then drops to the base of the next.
species.en_short_description: Bark-patterned and near-invisible; spirals up a trunk, then drops to the base of the next.
species.description: Works Colorado's mature conifers with a decurved bill and a stiff propping tail. Builds a hammock nest behind a loose slab of bark. The thin, high, wiry song is often the only evidence it is present, and is easily lost to older ears.
species.en_description: Works Colorado's mature conifers with a decurved bill and a stiff propping tail. Builds a hammock nest behind a loose slab of bark. The thin, high, wiry song is often the only evidence it is present, and is easily lost to older ears.

species.name: Mirlo acuático norteamericano
species.short_description: A slate-grey songbird that walks underwater on the bottom of cold mountain streams.
species.en_short_description: A slate-grey songbird that walks underwater on the bottom of cold mountain streams.
species.description: North America's only aquatic passerine, resident on Colorado's fast creeks year-round including through ice. Bobs constantly on midstream boulders, then plunges in to grub caddisfly larvae off the gravel. Nests behind waterfalls and under bridges in a domed ball of moss.
species.en_description: North America's only aquatic passerine, resident on Colorado's fast creeks year-round including through ice. Bobs constantly on midstream boulders, then plunges in to grub caddisfly larvae off the gravel. Nests behind waterfalls and under bridges in a domed ball of moss.

species.name: Azulejo pálido
species.short_description: The male is sky-blue all over with no rust at all; hovers over open ground to hunt.
species.en_short_description: The male is sky-blue all over with no rust at all; hovers over open ground to hunt.
species.description: A bird of Colorado's high meadows, sagebrush and burned forest, nesting readily in boxes along mountain fencelines. The female is grey-brown with blue in wings and tail. Unlike the Western Bluebird it hunts by hovering, dropping onto grasshoppers from a few feet up.
species.en_description: A bird of Colorado's high meadows, sagebrush and burned forest, nesting readily in boxes along mountain fencelines. The female is grey-brown with blue in wings and tail. Unlike the Western Bluebird it hunts by hovering, dropping onto grasshoppers from a few feet up.

species.name: Clarín norteño
species.short_description: Slim grey thrush with a white eyering and buff wing patches; defends a juniper all winter.
species.en_short_description: Slim grey thrush with a white eyering and buff wing patches; defends a juniper all winter.
species.description: Sits bolt upright at the top of a Colorado foothills juniper and sings a long rich warble in December, holding a territory whose value is entirely the berry crop on that one tree. In summer it nests on cut banks and road cuts in the high country.
species.en_description: Sits bolt upright at the top of a Colorado foothills juniper and sings a long rich warble in December, holding a territory whose value is entirely the berry crop on that one tree. In summer it nests on cut banks and road cuts in the high country.

species.name: Maullador gris
species.short_description: Slate grey with a black cap and a chestnut vent; its call is a flat, unmistakable mew.
species.en_short_description: Slate grey with a black cap and a chestnut vent; its call is a flat, unmistakable mew.
species.description: Skulks in dense riparian willow and shrubby thickets along Colorado's plains rivers and Front Range greenways. Rarely shows itself, but sings a long rambling improvisation from cover and answers a squeak with a catlike complaint.
species.en_description: Skulks in dense riparian willow and shrubby thickets along Colorado's plains rivers and Front Range greenways. Rarely shows itself, but sings a long rambling improvisation from cover and answers a squeak with a catlike complaint.

species.name: Cuitlacoche de artemisa
species.short_description: The smallest thrasher: heavily streaked below, yellow-eyed, and welded to big sagebrush.
species.en_short_description: The smallest thrasher: heavily streaked below, yellow-eyed, and welded to big sagebrush.
species.description: Breeds in northwestern Colorado's sagebrush steppe and North Park, where it sings a long unbroken warble from the tallest bush available. Shorter-billed than other thrashers, with white tail corners visible as it drops back into the sage.
species.en_description: Breeds in northwestern Colorado's sagebrush steppe and North Park, where it sings a long unbroken warble from the tallest bush available. Shorter-billed than other thrashers, with white tail corners visible as it drops back into the sage.

species.name: Ampelis europeo
species.short_description: A winter irruptive: greyer than a Cedar Waxwing, with rusty undertail and white wing marks.
species.en_short_description: A winter irruptive: greyer than a Cedar Waxwing, with rusty undertail and white wing marks.
species.description: Arrives in Colorado in some winters and not others, stripping crabapples and mountain-ash in flocks of hundreds before vanishing. Larger and greyer than the Cedar Waxwing it often travels with; the cinnamon undertail coverts settle the identification.
species.en_description: Arrives in Colorado in some winters and not others, stripping crabapples and mountain-ash in flocks of hundreds before vanishing. Larger and greyer than the Cedar Waxwing it often travels with; the cinnamon undertail coverts settle the identification.

species.name: Verdugo americano
species.short_description: A songbird that hunts like a raptor and impales its prey on barbed wire and thorns.
species.en_short_description: A songbird that hunts like a raptor and impales its prey on barbed wire and thorns.
species.description: Perches on fences across Colorado's eastern plains and shrubland, watching for lizards, large insects and small birds. Grey above, black mask, white wing patches that flash in flight. The larder of skewered prey is both storage and a display of fitness.
species.en_description: Perches on fences across Colorado's eastern plains and shrubland, watching for lizards, large insects and small birds. Grey above, black mask, white wing patches that flash in flight. The larder of skewered prey is both storage and a display of fitness.

species.name: Zumbador coliancho
species.short_description: The mountain hummingbird whose male makes a loud metallic trill with his wings.
species.en_short_description: The mountain hummingbird whose male makes a loud metallic trill with his wings.
species.description: Colorado's common breeding hummingbird, from foothills to timberline wherever there are penstemon and paintbrush. The male's wing trill announces him well before he is visible; his gorget is a solid rose-red. Enters torpor on cold nights to survive at altitude.
species.en_description: Colorado's common breeding hummingbird, from foothills to timberline wherever there are penstemon and paintbrush. The male's wing trill announces him well before he is visible; his gorget is a solid rose-red. Enters torpor on cold nights to survive at altitude.

species.name: Colibrí barbanegra
species.short_description: A lowland hummingbird whose black chin shows a violet band only in the right light.
species.en_short_description: A lowland hummingbird whose black chin shows a violet band only in the right light.
species.description: Breeds along Colorado's canyon streams and lower foothills, and visits Front Range feeders. The male pumps his tail constantly while hovering, a useful habit when the gorget is turned away and looks plain black.
species.en_description: Breeds along Colorado's canyon streams and lower foothills, and visits Front Range feeders. The male pumps his tail constantly while hovering, a useful habit when the gorget is turned away and looks plain black.

species.name: Zumbador rufo
species.short_description: Orange, tiny and pugnacious; passes through Colorado in July on its way south.
species.en_short_description: Orange, tiny and pugnacious; passes through Colorado in July on its way south.
species.description: Does not breed in the state — adult males appear in early July, having finished nesting in the Pacific Northwest, and drive every other hummingbird off a feeder for six weeks. The male's back is solid copper, unlike the green-backed Broad-tailed.
species.en_description: Does not breed in the state — adult males appear in early July, having finished nesting in the Pacific Northwest, and drive every other hummingbird off a feeder for six weeks. The male's back is solid copper, unlike the green-backed Broad-tailed.

species.name: Vencejo pechiblanco
species.short_description: Black-and-white cigar on scythe wings, screaming past cliff faces at enormous speed.
species.en_short_description: Black-and-white cigar on scythe wings, screaming past cliff faces at enormous speed.
species.description: Nests in crevices on Colorado's canyon walls, from the Black Canyon to Front Range hogbacks, and feeds entirely on the wing. Pairs sometimes clasp and tumble hundreds of feet together. The white throat, breast and flank patches make a broken white stripe underneath.
species.en_description: Nests in crevices on Colorado's canyon walls, from the Black Canyon to Front Range hogbacks, and feeds entirely on the wing. Pairs sometimes clasp and tumble hundreds of feet together. The white throat, breast and flank patches make a broken white stripe underneath.

species.name: Chotacabras zumbón
species.short_description: Erratic dusk flier with a white wing-bar; the male dives and the air booms through his wings.
species.en_short_description: Erratic dusk flier with a white wing-bar; the male dives and the air booms through his wings.
species.description: Hunts insects over Colorado towns, plains and gravel rooftops on summer evenings, calling a nasal peent. Not a hawk and not strictly nocturnal. The courtship dive ends in a hollow whoomph made by air rushing through the primaries.
species.en_description: Hunts insects over Colorado towns, plains and gravel rooftops on summer evenings, calling a nasal peent. Not a hawk and not strictly nocturnal. The courtship dive ends in a hollow whoomph made by air rushing through the primaries.

species.name: Carpintero velloso mayor
species.short_description: A Downy Woodpecker scaled up, with a bill as long as its head instead of half of it.
species.en_short_description: A Downy Woodpecker scaled up, with a bill as long as its head instead of half of it.
species.description: Widespread in Colorado's conifer and riparian woodland. Bill length is the reliable mark: the Downy's is a stub, the Hairy's is a chisel. Its call is a sharp single peek rather than the Downy's descending whinny.
species.en_description: Widespread in Colorado's conifer and riparian woodland. Bill length is the reliable mark: the Downy's is a stub, the Hairy's is a chisel. Its call is a sharp single peek rather than the Downy's descending whinny.

species.name: Chupasavia nuquirroja
species.short_description: Drills orderly rows of wells in aspen and willow and returns to drink the sap.
species.en_short_description: Drills orderly rows of wells in aspen and willow and returns to drink the sap.
species.description: The common breeding sapsucker of Colorado's montane aspen. Red crown and throat with a red nape spot and a long white wing stripe. Its sap wells feed hummingbirds, warblers and squirrels — a whole small economy that depends on the woodpecker keeping them open.
species.en_description: The common breeding sapsucker of Colorado's montane aspen. Red crown and throat with a red nape spot and a long white wing stripe. Its sap wells feed hummingbirds, warblers and squirrels — a whole small economy that depends on the woodpecker keeping them open.

species.name: Chupasavia oscura
species.short_description: The sexes look so different they were described as two separate species.
species.en_short_description: The sexes look so different they were described as two separate species.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's mature ponderosa and mixed conifer. The male is glossy black with white face stripes, a red throat and a lemon belly; the female is barred brown with a tan head and no white wing patch. Both drill sap wells like their red-naped cousin.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's mature ponderosa and mixed conifer. The male is glossy black with white face stripes, a red throat and a lemon belly; the female is barred brown with a tan head and no white wing patch. Both drill sap wells like their red-naped cousin.

species.name: Carpintero de Lewis
species.short_description: A dark green-black woodpecker with a pink belly that catches insects in mid-air like a crow.
species.en_short_description: A dark green-black woodpecker with a pink belly that catches insects in mid-air like a crow.
species.description: Named for Meriwether Lewis and found in Colorado's open burned pine, cottonwood bottoms and orchards. Flies with steady crow-like flapping rather than the usual woodpecker bounding, and hawks flying insects instead of excavating for them.
species.en_description: Named for Meriwether Lewis and found in Colorado's open burned pine, cottonwood bottoms and orchards. Flies with steady crow-like flapping rather than the usual woodpecker bounding, and hawks flying insects instead of excavating for them.

species.name: Carpintero tridáctilo
species.short_description: A beetle-kill specialist with a yellow crown patch and, as billed, three toes.
species.en_short_description: A beetle-kill specialist with a yellow crown patch and, as billed, three toes.
species.description: Follows bark beetle outbreaks and burns through Colorado's spruce-fir, quietly flaking bark off dead trunks rather than hammering. The male's yellow cap and the barred flanks are the marks. Numbers rise for a few years after a fire, then fall away.
species.en_description: Follows bark beetle outbreaks and burns through Colorado's spruce-fir, quietly flaking bark off dead trunks rather than hammering. The male's yellow cap and the barred flanks are the marks. Numbers rise for a few years after a fire, then fall away.

species.name: Papamoscas llanero
species.short_description: Pale grey-brown flycatcher with a cinnamon belly and a black tail; pumps it while perched.
species.en_short_description: Pale grey-brown flycatcher with a cinnamon belly and a black tail; pumps it while perched.
species.description: One of the first spring migrants back to Colorado's plains and canyons, often in March. Nests under bridges, on rock ledges and in outbuildings. Hovers over short grass to take insects, which no other flycatcher here does routinely.
species.en_description: One of the first spring migrants back to Colorado's plains and canyons, often in March. Nests under bridges, on rock ledges and in outbuildings. Hovers over short grass to take insects, which no other flycatcher here does routinely.

species.name: Tirano pálido
species.short_description: Grey head, yellow belly, and white edges to a black tail; owns every roadside fence in summer.
species.en_short_description: Grey head, yellow belly, and white edges to a black tail; owns every roadside fence in summer.
species.description: A conspicuous summer bird of Colorado's plains, farmland and town edges, nesting on power poles and in cottonwoods. Aggressively mobs crows, hawks and anything else that comes near the nest, chattering all the way.
species.en_description: A conspicuous summer bird of Colorado's plains, farmland and town edges, nesting on power poles and in cottonwoods. Aggressively mobs crows, hawks and anything else that comes near the nest, chattering all the way.

species.name: Pibí occidental
species.short_description: A drab grey flycatcher best identified by its burry, descending peeer.
species.en_short_description: A drab grey flycatcher best identified by its burry, descending peeer.
species.description: Sits upright on a bare branch in Colorado's open montane forest and riparian cottonwood, sallying out and returning to the same perch. Wing bars are dull, there is no eyering, and the voice is the only quick way to be sure of it.
species.en_description: Sits upright on a bare branch in Colorado's open montane forest and riparian cottonwood, sallying out and returning to the same perch. Wing bars are dull, there is no eyering, and the voice is the only quick way to be sure of it.

species.name: Vireo plomizo
species.short_description: Grey with bold white spectacles and wing bars; sings a slow, deliberate question-and-answer.
species.en_short_description: Grey with bold white spectacles and wing bars; sings a slow, deliberate question-and-answer.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's ponderosa, oak scrub and pinyon-juniper. Heavier-billed and slower-moving than a warbler, working methodically along branches. The white eyering joined to a white loral stripe forms the spectacles that name it.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's ponderosa, oak scrub and pinyon-juniper. Heavier-billed and slower-moving than a warbler, working methodically along branches. The white eyering joined to a white loral stripe forms the spectacles that name it.

species.name: Vireo gorjeador
species.short_description: Plain olive-grey with a pale eyebrow, and a long tumbling warble from high in a cottonwood.
species.en_short_description: Plain olive-grey with a pale eyebrow, and a long tumbling warble from high in a cottonwood.
species.description: Abundant in Colorado's riparian cottonwood and aspen but far more often heard than seen. Has no wing bars and no strong face pattern at all; the run-on song, ending on an upward note, is the identification.
species.en_description: Abundant in Colorado's riparian cottonwood and aspen but far more often heard than seen. Has no wing bars and no strong face pattern at all; the run-on song, ending on an upward note, is the identification.

species.name: Reyezuelo de rojo
species.short_description: A restless scrap of a bird with a bold white eyering that flicks its wings constantly.
species.en_short_description: A restless scrap of a bird with a bold white eyering that flicks its wings constantly.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's spruce-fir and floods the lowlands on migration. The male's red crown patch stays hidden unless he is excited. The wing-flicking is near-continuous and identifies it at a distance where the eyering cannot be seen.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's spruce-fir and floods the lowlands on migration. The male's red crown patch stays hidden unless he is excited. The wing-flicking is near-continuous and identifies it at a distance where the eyering cannot be seen.

species.name: Perlita grisilla
species.short_description: Tiny, long-tailed and blue-grey, flicking a white-edged tail from side to side.
species.en_short_description: Tiny, long-tailed and blue-grey, flicking a white-edged tail from side to side.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's pinyon-juniper, oak scrub and canyon woodland. Builds a lichen-covered cup saddled on a branch, like a hummingbird's but larger. Gives a thin wheezy call almost continuously as it forages.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's pinyon-juniper, oak scrub and canyon woodland. Builds a lichen-covered cup saddled on a branch, like a hummingbird's but larger. Gives a thin wheezy call almost continuously as it forages.

species.name: Golondrina verdemar
species.short_description: Green-and-violet above, with white that wraps up around the eye and onto the rump.
species.en_short_description: Green-and-violet above, with white that wraps up around the eye and onto the rump.
species.description: Nests in cliff crevices, aspen cavities and building eaves across Colorado's foothills and mountains. The white flank patches nearly meeting over the rump separate it in flight from the Tree Swallow, whose white stops at the belly.
species.en_description: Nests in cliff crevices, aspen cavities and building eaves across Colorado's foothills and mountains. The white flank patches nearly meeting over the rump separate it in flight from the Tree Swallow, whose white stops at the belly.

species.name: Golondrina bicolor
species.short_description: Iridescent steel-blue above, clean white below, with a shallow notch in the tail.
species.en_short_description: Iridescent steel-blue above, clean white below, with a shallow notch in the tail.
species.description: Takes over woodpecker holes and nest boxes around Colorado's beaver ponds, reservoirs and mountain meadows. Feeds low over water in cold weather when insects stay down. The white does not reach above the eye, unlike the Violet-green.
species.en_description: Takes over woodpecker holes and nest boxes around Colorado's beaver ponds, reservoirs and mountain meadows. Feeds low over water in cold weather when insects stay down. The white does not reach above the eye, unlike the Violet-green.

species.name: Golondrina risquera
species.short_description: Square tail, buff rump and a pale forehead; builds gourd-shaped mud nests in dense colonies.
species.en_short_description: Square tail, buff rump and a pale forehead; builds gourd-shaped mud nests in dense colonies.
species.description: Colonies of hundreds plaster Colorado's bridges, dam faces and highway culverts. Each nest is a closed mud jug with a side entrance, built pellet by pellet from a puddle nearby. The square tail distinguishes it instantly from the forked Barn Swallow.
species.en_description: Colonies of hundreds plaster Colorado's bridges, dam faces and highway culverts. Each nest is a closed mud jug with a side entrance, built pellet by pellet from a puddle nearby. The square tail distinguishes it instantly from the forked Barn Swallow.

species.name: Pradero occidental
species.short_description: Yellow breast crossed by a black V, and a flutey song that carries across open prairie.
species.en_short_description: Yellow breast crossed by a black V, and a flutey song that carries across open prairie.
species.description: The defining sound of Colorado's eastern plains and mountain parks from March onward, sung from a fencepost or a yucca stalk. Cryptic brown from above and startling from the front. Walks rather than hops, and flashes white outer tail feathers when flushed.
species.en_description: The defining sound of Colorado's eastern plains and mountain parks from March onward, sung from a fencepost or a yucca stalk. Cryptic brown from above and startling from the front. Walks rather than hops, and flashes white outer tail feathers when flushed.

species.name: Tordo cabeza amarilla
species.short_description: A black bird with a blazing yellow head and a song like a rusty gate being forced.
species.en_short_description: A black bird with a blazing yellow head and a song like a rusty gate being forced.
species.description: Nests in deep cattail marsh across Colorado, taking the wettest zone and pushing Red-winged Blackbirds to the edges. The male's display song is one of the least musical sounds in North American birding, and entirely deliberate.
species.en_description: Nests in deep cattail marsh across Colorado, taking the wettest zone and pushing Red-winged Blackbirds to the edges. The male's display song is one of the least musical sounds in North American birding, and entirely deliberate.

species.name: Tordo ojo amarillo
species.short_description: Glossy purple-and-green black male with a pale staring eye; the female is plain brown.
species.en_short_description: Glossy purple-and-green black male with a pale staring eye; the female is plain brown.
species.description: Walks parking lots, feedlots and picnic grounds throughout Colorado. Smaller and shorter-tailed than a Common Grackle, and the yellow-white iris on the male is the quickest mark. Females are dark-eyed and easily passed over as cowbirds.
species.en_description: Walks parking lots, feedlots and picnic grounds throughout Colorado. Smaller and shorter-tailed than a Common Grackle, and the yellow-white iris on the male is the quickest mark. Females are dark-eyed and easily passed over as cowbirds.

species.name: Zanate norteño
species.short_description: Long keel-shaped tail and an oil-slick iridescent head; a plains-town bird in Colorado.
species.en_short_description: Long keel-shaped tail and an oil-slick iridescent head; a plains-town bird in Colorado.
species.description: Nests in conifers in Front Range and eastern plains towns, and gathers in large noisy roosts in late summer. Smaller than the Great-tailed Grackle of the southeast corner, with a bronzy back rather than uniform violet-black.
species.en_description: Nests in conifers in Front Range and eastern plains towns, and gathers in large noisy roosts in late summer. Smaller than the Great-tailed Grackle of the southeast corner, with a bronzy back rather than uniform violet-black.

species.name: Tordo cabecicafé
species.short_description: A brood parasite: lays in other birds' nests and leaves the rearing to them entirely.
species.en_short_description: A brood parasite: lays in other birds' nests and leaves the rearing to them entirely.
species.description: Followed bison herds across Colorado's plains and now follows cattle and mowed lawns into the mountains. The male is black with a chocolate head; the female is featureless grey-brown. A single female may lay three dozen eggs a season in other species' nests.
species.en_description: Followed bison herds across Colorado's plains and now follows cattle and mowed lawns into the mountains. The male is black with a chocolate head; the female is featureless grey-brown. A single female may lay three dozen eggs a season in other species' nests.

species.name: Bolsero calandria
species.short_description: Flame-orange with a black eyeline and a big white wing patch; weaves a hanging pouch nest.
species.en_short_description: Flame-orange with a black eyeline and a big white wing patch; weaves a hanging pouch nest.
species.description: Nests in Colorado's plains and canyon cottonwoods, the pendulous woven bag swinging from a branch tip well out of reach. The male's orange face with a narrow black line through the eye separates it from the Baltimore Oriole's fully black hood.
species.en_description: Nests in Colorado's plains and canyon cottonwoods, the pendulous woven bag swinging from a branch tip well out of reach. The male's orange face with a narrow black line through the eye separates it from the Baltimore Oriole's fully black hood.

species.name: Piranga capucha roja
species.short_description: A yellow bird with black wings and a red face, improbably bright for a conifer canopy.
species.en_short_description: A yellow bird with black wings and a red face, improbably bright for a conifer canopy.
species.description: Breeds through Colorado's montane forest and turns up in Front Range yards on migration in May. The red pigment comes from insects in the diet, not from the bird itself. Song is a hoarse, robin-like phrase; the call a dry pit-er-ick.
species.en_description: Breeds through Colorado's montane forest and turns up in Front Range yards on migration in May. The red pigment comes from insects in the diet, not from the bird itself. Song is a hoarse, robin-like phrase; the call a dry pit-er-ick.

species.name: Picogordo tigrillo
species.short_description: Burnt-orange body, black hood and an outsized pale bill built for cracking seeds.
species.en_short_description: Burnt-orange body, black hood and an outsized pale bill built for cracking seeds.
species.description: Common in Colorado's riparian and foothill woodland in summer, and a reliable feeder visitor. Both sexes sing, which is unusual, and the female sometimes sings from the nest. One of the few birds that eats monarch butterflies despite the toxins.
species.en_description: Common in Colorado's riparian and foothill woodland in summer, and a reliable feeder visitor. Both sexes sing, which is unusual, and the female sometimes sings from the nest. One of the few birds that eats monarch butterflies despite the toxins.

species.name: Colorín lazulita
species.short_description: Turquoise head, cinnamon breast and white wing bars; sings from the top of a shrub.
species.en_short_description: Turquoise head, cinnamon breast and white wing bars; sings from the top of a shrub.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's brushy foothill draws, oak scrub and burned slopes. Young males learn a song by improvising on fragments from neighbours, so local groups end up sharing dialects. Females are warm brown and easily overlooked.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's brushy foothill draws, oak scrub and burned slopes. Young males learn a song by improvising on fragments from neighbours, so local groups end up sharing dialects. Females are warm brown and easily overlooked.

species.name: Jilguero pinero
species.short_description: A streaky brown finch with yellow wing flashes and a rising, unfinished zzzreeee call.
species.en_short_description: A streaky brown finch with yellow wing flashes and a rising, unfinished zzzreeee call.
species.description: Irruptive and unpredictable in Colorado — absent one winter, swarming feeders the next, depending on the conifer seed crop. The notched tail and yellow at the base of the flight feathers separate it from any sparrow.
species.en_description: Irruptive and unpredictable in Colorado — absent one winter, swarming feeders the next, depending on the conifer seed crop. The notched tail and yellow at the base of the flight feathers separate it from any sparrow.

species.name: Pinzón de Cassin
species.short_description: A mountain finch; the male has a bright red crown cap sharply set off from a brown nape.
species.en_short_description: A mountain finch; the male has a bright red crown cap sharply set off from a brown nape.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's high conifer forest and drops lower in winter. Told from a House Finch by the peaked red crown, the crisp brown streaking, and a straight-edged culmen rather than a curved one. Mimics other species within its warbling song.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's high conifer forest and drops lower in winter. Told from a House Finch by the peaked red crown, the crisp brown streaking, and a straight-edged culmen rather than a curved one. Mimics other species within its warbling song.

species.name: Picogrueso vespertino
species.short_description: A heavy yellow-and-black finch with a huge pale green bill and white wing panels.
species.en_short_description: A heavy yellow-and-black finch with a huge pale green bill and white wing panels.
species.description: Roams Colorado's montane forest in flocks, descending on box-elder seeds and sunflower feeders and stripping both. Numbers have fallen steeply across the continent. Loud ringing call notes usually announce the flock before it arrives.
species.en_description: Roams Colorado's montane forest in flocks, descending on box-elder seeds and sunflower feeders and stripping both. Numbers have fallen steeply across the continent. Loud ringing call notes usually announce the flock before it arrives.

species.name: Pinzón montano coronicafé
species.short_description: A near-endemic alpine finch: pink-washed brown, breeding almost only in Colorado.
species.en_short_description: A near-endemic alpine finch: pink-washed brown, breeding almost only in Colorado.
species.description: Nests in cliffs and talus above treeline, feeding on insects blown onto snowfields, and winters in flocks at high mountain-town feeders. Colorado holds the great majority of the world population. Unlike the Gray-crowned it has no grey on the head, only a plain brown cap.
species.en_description: Nests in cliffs and talus above treeline, feeding on insects blown onto snowfields, and winters in flocks at high mountain-town feeders. Colorado holds the great majority of the world population. Unlike the Gray-crowned it has no grey on the head, only a plain brown cap.

species.name: Gorrión alipálido
species.short_description: Colorado's state bird: the breeding male is jet black with one bold white wing patch.
species.en_short_description: Colorado's state bird: the breeding male is jet black with one bold white wing patch.
species.description: Adopted as the state bird in 1931 and found on the eastern plains from May to August, where males flutter up and parachute down singing. Out of breeding plumage the male becomes streaky brown like the female, keeping only the white wing patch.
species.en_description: Adopted as the state bird in 1931 and found on the eastern plains from May to August, where males flutter up and parachute down singing. Out of breeding plumage the male becomes streaky brown like the female, keeping only the white wing patch.

species.name: Gorrión arlequín
species.short_description: A harlequin face of chestnut, black and white, with a black breast spot and white tail corners.
species.en_short_description: A harlequin face of chestnut, black and white, with a black breast spot and white tail corners.
species.description: Breeds on Colorado's open plains, sandhills and mesa grassland with scattered shrubs. The boldest facial pattern of any North American sparrow, and unmistakable once seen. Fans a rounded tail with white corners as it flies up from a road edge.
species.en_description: Breeds on Colorado's open plains, sandhills and mesa grassland with scattered shrubs. The boldest facial pattern of any North American sparrow, and unmistakable once seen. Fans a rounded tail with white corners as it flies up from a road edge.

species.name: Gorrión coliblanco
species.short_description: A plain streaked sparrow with a thin white eyering, chestnut shoulder and white outer tail.
species.en_short_description: A plain streaked sparrow with a thin white eyering, chestnut shoulder and white outer tail.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's sagebrush, dry meadow and shortgrass. Named for a habit of singing late into the evening. The flash of white on either side of the tail as it flushes is the fastest field mark.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's sagebrush, dry meadow and shortgrass. Named for a habit of singing late into the evening. The flash of white on either side of the tail as it flushes is the fastest field mark.

species.name: Gorrión cejiblanco
species.short_description: Rusty cap, black eyeline and clean grey underparts; sings a long dry mechanical trill.
species.en_short_description: Rusty cap, black eyeline and clean grey underparts; sings a long dry mechanical trill.
species.description: Nests in Colorado's open conifer forest, campgrounds and town conifers, and feeds in loose flocks on lawns and roadsides. Small, slim and long-tailed for a sparrow. Winter birds lose the bright cap and become a dull streaky brown.
species.en_description: Nests in Colorado's open conifer forest, campgrounds and town conifers, and feeds in loose flocks on lawns and roadsides. Small, slim and long-tailed for a sparrow. Winter birds lose the bright cap and become a dull streaky brown.

species.name: Gorrión arbóreo
species.short_description: A winter-only sparrow with a rusty cap, a bicoloured bill and one dark central breast spot.
species.en_short_description: A winter-only sparrow with a rusty cap, a bicoloured bill and one dark central breast spot.
species.description: Breeds on the arctic tundra and winters on Colorado's plains, weedy fields and brushy creek bottoms from November to March. The yellow lower mandible against a dark upper is a reliable mark, as is the single stickpin spot on a plain grey breast.
species.en_description: Breeds on the arctic tundra and winters on Colorado's plains, weedy fields and brushy creek bottoms from November to March. The yellow lower mandible against a dark upper is a reliable mark, as is the single stickpin spot on a plain grey breast.

species.name: Gorrión sabanero
species.short_description: Finely streaked grassland sparrow, usually with a yellow wash before the eye.
species.en_short_description: Finely streaked grassland sparrow, usually with a yellow wash before the eye.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's wet mountain meadows and irrigated hayfields and passes through the plains in numbers on migration. Short notched tail, crisp streaking, and an insect-like buzzy song. Runs mouse-like through grass rather than flying when disturbed.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's wet mountain meadows and irrigated hayfields and passes through the plains in numbers on migration. Short notched tail, crisp streaking, and an insect-like buzzy song. Runs mouse-like through grass rather than flying when disturbed.

species.name: Toquí colicafé
species.short_description: Grey below with an olive-green tail, a rufous cap and a white throat stripe.
species.en_short_description: Grey below with an olive-green tail, a rufous cap and a white throat stripe.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's mountain shrubland, sagebrush and recovering burns. Scratches in leaf litter with both feet at once like its spotted cousin, and runs off through cover with the crown raised. The mewing call is often mistaken for a cat.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's mountain shrubland, sagebrush and recovering burns. Scratches in leaf litter with both feet at once like its spotted cousin, and runs off through cover with the crown raised. The mewing call is often mistaken for a cat.

species.name: Grulla gris
species.short_description: Tall grey crane with a red crown; its bugling carries for miles and it dances in spring.
species.en_short_description: Tall grey crane with a red crown; its bugling carries for miles and it dances in spring.
species.description: Tens of thousands stage in Colorado's San Luis Valley each March and October, feeding in stubble by day and roosting in shallow water at night. Flies with the neck outstretched, unlike a heron. Pairs leap, bow and toss vegetation in a courtship dance that lasts for life.
species.en_description: Tens of thousands stage in Colorado's San Luis Valley each March and October, feeding in stubble by day and roosting in shallow water at night. Flies with the neck outstretched, unlike a heron. Pairs leap, bow and toss vegetation in a courtship dance that lasts for life.

species.name: Avoceta americana
species.short_description: Long blue legs, a sharply upturned bill and a rusty head in breeding plumage.
species.en_short_description: Long blue legs, a sharply upturned bill and a rusty head in breeding plumage.
species.description: Breeds on Colorado's alkaline flats, reservoir shallows and the San Luis Valley wetlands. Feeds by sweeping the scythe-shaped bill sideways through shallow water. Adults perform a broken-wing distraction display and dive-bomb intruders near the nest.
species.en_description: Breeds on Colorado's alkaline flats, reservoir shallows and the San Luis Valley wetlands. Feeds by sweeping the scythe-shaped bill sideways through shallow water. Adults perform a broken-wing distraction display and dive-bomb intruders near the nest.

species.name: Candelero americano
species.short_description: Black above and white below on absurdly long, thin, coral-pink legs.
species.en_short_description: Black above and white below on absurdly long, thin, coral-pink legs.
species.description: Nests on the margins of Colorado's shallow wetlands and playa lakes, often alongside avocets. Proportionally the second-longest legs of any bird relative to body size. Yaps continuously and persistently at anything that approaches the nest scrape.
species.en_description: Nests on the margins of Colorado's shallow wetlands and playa lakes, often alongside avocets. Proportionally the second-longest legs of any bird relative to body size. Yaps continuously and persistently at anything that approaches the nest scrape.

species.name: Agachona norteamericana
species.short_description: A cryptic long-billed marsh bird whose display is a hollow winnowing made by its tail.
species.en_short_description: A cryptic long-billed marsh bird whose display is a hollow winnowing made by its tail.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's wet mountain meadows and willow bogs. Flushes underfoot in a zigzag with a rasping call. In spring the male circles high at dusk and dives, air through the stiff outer tail feathers producing a pulsing woo-woo-woo that sounds like an owl.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's wet mountain meadows and willow bogs. Flushes underfoot in a zigzag with a rasping call. In spring the male circles high at dusk and dives, air through the stiff outer tail feathers producing a pulsing woo-woo-woo that sounds like an owl.

species.name: Playero alzacolita
species.short_description: Teeters constantly on stream edges; spotted below in summer, plain in winter.
species.en_short_description: Teeters constantly on stream edges; spotted below in summer, plain in winter.
species.description: The default shorebird of Colorado's mountain creeks, reservoirs and gravel bars. Flies low over water on stiff, shallow, fluttering wingbeats. Females hold territories and may mate with several males, each of whom incubates his own clutch.
species.en_description: The default shorebird of Colorado's mountain creeks, reservoirs and gravel bars. Flies low over water on stiff, shallow, fluttering wingbeats. Females hold territories and may mate with several males, each of whom incubates his own clutch.

species.name: Zarapito ganga
species.short_description: North America's largest shorebird, cinnamon-buff with a bill longer than its head and neck.
species.en_short_description: North America's largest shorebird, cinnamon-buff with a bill longer than its head and neck.
species.description: Breeds on Colorado's shortgrass prairie and grazed rangeland, far from water. The extraordinary decurved bill probes for earthworms and pulls burrowing shrimp from tidal mud in winter. Gives a rising, clear cur-lee that names it.
species.en_description: Breeds on Colorado's shortgrass prairie and grazed rangeland, far from water. The extraordinary decurved bill probes for earthworms and pulls burrowing shrimp from tidal mud in winter. Gives a rising, clear cur-lee that names it.

species.name: Chorlo llanero
species.short_description: A plain sandy plover of bare shortgrass and prairie dog towns — nowhere near mountains.
species.en_short_description: A plain sandy plover of bare shortgrass and prairie dog towns — nowhere near mountains.
species.description: A Colorado breeding speciality and a species of concern, nesting on the eastern plains in ground so bare it looks unused. No breast band at all, unlike other plovers. Relies on stillness for camouflage, which is why it is so often missed.
species.en_description: A Colorado breeding speciality and a species of concern, nesting on the eastern plains in ground so bare it looks unused. No breast band at all, unlike other plovers. Relies on stillness for camouflage, which is why it is so often missed.

species.name: Achichilique pico amarillo
species.short_description: Long-necked black-and-white grebe; pairs rush upright across the water side by side.
species.en_short_description: Long-necked black-and-white grebe; pairs rush upright across the water side by side.
species.description: Breeds on Colorado's larger reservoirs and marshes in floating colonies. The courtship rush, both birds sprinting on the surface with necks arched, is one of the great sights of a Colorado spring. The black cap enclosing the eye separates it from Clark's Grebe.
species.en_description: Breeds on Colorado's larger reservoirs and marshes in floating colonies. The courtship rush, both birds sprinting on the surface with necks arched, is one of the great sights of a Colorado spring. The black cap enclosing the eye separates it from Clark's Grebe.

species.name: Zambullidor orejudo
species.short_description: A small grebe with a red eye and golden ear plumes fanned back over a black head.
species.en_short_description: A small grebe with a red eye and golden ear plumes fanned back over a black head.
species.description: The most abundant grebe in the world and a common Colorado breeder on alkaline lakes and marshes. Between migrations its flight muscles atrophy and its digestive organs swell — for months of the year it physically cannot fly.
