species.en_description: The most abundant grebe in the world and a common Colorado breeder on alkaline lakes and marshes. Between migrations its flight muscles atrophy and its digestive organs swell — for months of the year it physically cannot fly.

species.name: Ibis cara blanca
species.short_description: A dark wader that looks black until sunlight turns it bronze, green and purple.
species.en_short_description: A dark wader that looks black until sunlight turns it bronze, green and purple.
species.description: Feeds in flooded fields and marsh edges across Colorado, probing mud with a long decurved bill. Breeding adults show a narrow white border around a red face and red legs. Flies in lines and Vs with the neck extended and quick shallow wingbeats.
species.en_description: Feeds in flooded fields and marsh edges across Colorado, probing mud with a long decurved bill. Breeding adults show a narrow white border around a red face and red legs. Flies in lines and Vs with the neck extended and quick shallow wingbeats.

species.name: Polluela sora
species.short_description: A chicken-shaped marsh bird with a stubby yellow bill and a descending whinny call.
species.en_short_description: A chicken-shaped marsh bird with a stubby yellow bill and a descending whinny call.
species.description: Common but hard to see in Colorado cattail marsh, walking on long toes over floating vegetation. Far more often detected by its rising ker-wee or its horse-like whinny than by sight. Flushes weakly with legs dangling and drops straight back into cover.
species.en_description: Common but hard to see in Colorado cattail marsh, walking on long toes over floating vegetation. Far more often detected by its rising ker-wee or its horse-like whinny than by sight. Flushes weakly with legs dangling and drops straight back into cover.

species.name: Rascón limícola
species.short_description: A narrow-bodied rusty marsh bird with a long slightly curved bill and grey cheeks.
species.en_short_description: A narrow-bodied rusty marsh bird with a long slightly curved bill and grey cheeks.
species.description: Shares Colorado's cattail marshes with the Sora and is even more secretive. Its body is laterally compressed to slip between stems — the origin of "thin as a rail". Announces itself with a metallic kid-ick series at dawn and dusk.
species.en_description: Shares Colorado's cattail marshes with the Sora and is even more secretive. Its body is laterally compressed to slip between stems — the origin of "thin as a rail". Announces itself with a metallic kid-ick series at dawn and dusk.

species.name: Lagópodo coliblanco
species.short_description: A grouse that lives above treeline year-round and turns completely white for winter.
species.en_short_description: A grouse that lives above treeline year-round and turns completely white for winter.
species.description: The only bird resident on Colorado's alpine tundra through the winter, roosting in snow burrows on feathered feet. Mottled grey-brown in summer and pure white in winter, with a white tail in every plumage. Sits tight and is usually walked past rather than seen.
species.en_description: The only bird resident on Colorado's alpine tundra through the winter, roosting in snow burrows on feathered feet. Mottled grey-brown in summer and pure white in winter, with a white tail in every plumage. Sits tight and is usually walked past rather than seen.

species.name: Gallo oscuro
species.short_description: Large dark forest grouse; the displaying male inflates purple-red neck sacs on a bare patch.
species.en_short_description: Large dark forest grouse; the displaying male inflates purple-red neck sacs on a bare patch.
species.description: Found in Colorado's montane conifer and aspen edge, and unusual in moving upslope for winter to feed on conifer needles. The male's deep hooting is so low-pitched it is felt more than heard, and is easily mistaken for distant machinery.
species.en_description: Found in Colorado's montane conifer and aspen edge, and unusual in moving upslope for winter to feed on conifer needles. The male's deep hooting is so low-pitched it is felt more than heard, and is easily mistaken for distant machinery.

species.name: Gallo de las artemisas
species.short_description: A big sagebrush grouse whose males gather on leks and pop inflated chest sacs at dawn.
species.en_short_description: A big sagebrush grouse whose males gather on leks and pop inflated chest sacs at dawn.
species.description: Depends entirely on big sagebrush in northwestern Colorado and North Park, eating its leaves all winter. Males return to the same traditional lek for generations, fanning spiky tails and producing a liquid bloop from yellow air sacs. Populations are in long decline.
species.en_description: Depends entirely on big sagebrush in northwestern Colorado and North Park, eating its leaves all winter. Males return to the same traditional lek for generations, fanning spiky tails and producing a liquid bloop from yellow air sacs. Populations are in long decline.

species.name: Gallo de las praderas
species.short_description: A barred plains grouse; booming males raise neck feathers into horns and inflate orange sacs.
species.en_short_description: A barred plains grouse; booming males raise neck feathers into horns and inflate orange sacs.
species.description: Restricted in Colorado to the sandsage and native prairie of the far northeastern counties. The booming call, produced from inflated orange throat sacs, carries more than a mile across flat ground on a still April morning.
species.en_description: Restricted in Colorado to the sandsage and native prairie of the far northeastern counties. The booming call, produced from inflated orange throat sacs, carries more than a mile across flat ground on a still April morning.

species.name: Faisán de collar
species.short_description: An introduced Asian gamebird; the male is iridescent with a white collar and a very long tail.
species.en_short_description: An introduced Asian gamebird; the male is iridescent with a white collar and a very long tail.
species.description: Established in Colorado's eastern farmland and irrigated corridors since introductions began in the 1890s. Explodes from cover with a clattering cackle. The hen is mottled buff-brown with a long pointed tail and no collar.
species.en_description: Established in Colorado's eastern farmland and irrigated corridors since introductions began in the 1890s. Explodes from cover with a clattering cackle. The hen is mottled buff-brown with a long pointed tail and no collar.

species.name: Codorniz escamosa
species.short_description: Grey quail with scalloped feathering and a white-tipped crest — the "cottontop".
species.en_short_description: Grey quail with scalloped feathering and a white-tipped crest — the "cottontop".
species.description: Runs in coveys across Colorado's southeastern shortgrass, sandsage and yucca country, preferring to sprint rather than fly. The scaled breast pattern and cotton-white crest tuft are unmistakable. Coveys break up in spring and re-form by late summer.
species.en_description: Runs in coveys across Colorado's southeastern shortgrass, sandsage and yucca country, preferring to sprint rather than fly. The scaled breast pattern and cotton-white crest tuft are unmistakable. Coveys break up in spring and re-form by late summer.

species.name: Paloma doméstica
species.short_description: The city pigeon: a cliff bird from the Old World that took to buildings and bridges.
species.en_short_description: The city pigeon: a cliff bird from the Old World that took to buildings and bridges.
species.description: Ubiquitous in Colorado towns and on canyon cliffs and grain elevators, in every colour from blue-grey with two black wing bars to white, rust and pied. Worth logging honestly — it is a wild-nesting bird here and a major food source for urban Peregrine Falcons.
species.en_description: Ubiquitous in Colorado towns and on canyon cliffs and grain elevators, in every colour from blue-grey with two black wing bars to white, rust and pied. Worth logging honestly — it is a wild-nesting bird here and a major food source for urban Peregrine Falcons.

species.name: Tórtola turca
species.short_description: Pale sandy dove with a narrow black half-collar and a square white-cornered tail.
species.en_short_description: Pale sandy dove with a narrow black half-collar and a square white-cornered tail.
species.description: Reached Colorado around 2000 after spreading across the continent from a Bahamas release, and is now in nearly every town. Larger and paler than a Mourning Dove, with a three-note coo instead of a mournful five. Flight is direct with a stiff-winged glide.
species.en_description: Reached Colorado around 2000 after spreading across the continent from a Bahamas release, and is now in nearly every town. Larger and paler than a Mourning Dove, with a three-note coo instead of a mournful five. Flight is direct with a stiff-winged glide.

species.name: Alondra cornuda
species.short_description: A bare-ground lark with a black mask, yellow face and two small feather horns.
species.en_short_description: A bare-ground lark with a black mask, yellow face and two small feather horns.
species.description: Breeds from Colorado's eastern plains to the alpine tundra — one of very few birds spanning that whole range. Walks rather than hops. Winter flocks on ploughed fields and roadsides can run into the thousands and blow up like leaves as a car passes.
species.en_description: Breeds from Colorado's eastern plains to the alpine tundra — one of very few birds spanning that whole range. Walks rather than hops. Winter flocks on ploughed fields and roadsides can run into the thousands and blow up like leaves as a car passes.

species.name: Bisbita norteamericana
species.short_description: A slender grey-brown ground bird that walks steadily and bobs its tail as it goes.
species.en_short_description: A slender grey-brown ground bird that walks steadily and bobs its tail as it goes.
species.description: Nests on Colorado's alpine tundra and moves onto plains fields, shorelines and parking lots in migration. Thin bill and white outer tail feathers set it apart from any sparrow. The tail-pumping is constant and is the quickest identification at distance.
species.en_description: Nests on Colorado's alpine tundra and moves onto plains fields, shorelines and parking lots in migration. Thin bill and white outer tail feathers set it apart from any sparrow. The tail-pumping is constant and is the quickest identification at distance.

species.name: Saltapared continental
species.short_description: A small brown wren with a cocked tail and an outsized bubbling song.
species.en_short_description: A small brown wren with a cocked tail and an outsized bubbling song.
species.description: Nests in cavities and boxes throughout Colorado's foothills, riparian woods and town gardens. Fills every available hole in its territory with sticks, including ones it will not use. Fiercely aggressive to other cavity nesters despite weighing less than half an ounce.
species.en_description: Nests in cavities and boxes throughout Colorado's foothills, riparian woods and town gardens. Fills every available hole in its territory with sticks, including ones it will not use. Fiercely aggressive to other cavity nesters despite weighing less than half an ounce.

species.name: Saltapared roquero
species.short_description: A pale grey wren of talus and rimrock that bobs on its legs and paves its own doorstep.
species.en_short_description: A pale grey wren of talus and rimrock that bobs on its legs and paves its own doorstep.
species.description: Lives on Colorado's scree slopes, hogbacks and canyon rubble from the plains to the alpine. Lays a walkway of small flat stones at the nest crevice entrance, for reasons still not settled. Has a large and endlessly varied repertoire of harsh trills.
species.en_description: Lives on Colorado's scree slopes, hogbacks and canyon rubble from the plains to the alpine. Lays a walkway of small flat stones at the nest crevice entrance, for reasons still not settled. Has a large and endlessly varied repertoire of harsh trills.

species.name: Saltapared barranqueño
species.short_description: Rusty body, white throat, and a cascading song that spills down the rock and slows at the end.
species.en_short_description: Rusty body, white throat, and a cascading song that spills down the rock and slows at the end.
species.description: Lives on Colorado's sheer canyon walls and cliff faces, creeping into cracks with a flattened skull and a long fine bill. The falling series of clear whistles is among the most recognisable sounds in western canyon country.
species.en_description: Lives on Colorado's sheer canyon walls and cliff faces, creeping into cracks with a flattened skull and a long fine bill. The falling series of clear whistles is among the most recognisable sounds in western canyon country.

species.name: Saltapared pantanero
species.short_description: A cattail wren with a white eyebrow and black-and-white streaking down the back.
species.en_short_description: A cattail wren with a white eyebrow and black-and-white streaking down the back.
species.description: Sings a rattling, sewing-machine chatter day and night from Colorado marshes. Each male builds several dummy nests within his territory and the female selects and lines one. Punctures the eggs of neighbouring marsh birds, including other Marsh Wrens.
species.en_description: Sings a rattling, sewing-machine chatter day and night from Colorado marshes. Each male builds several dummy nests within his territory and the female selects and lines one. Punctures the eggs of neighbouring marsh birds, including other Marsh Wrens.

species.name: Chipe amarillo
species.short_description: Entirely yellow, with chestnut breast streaks on the male and a large dark eye.
species.en_short_description: Entirely yellow, with chestnut breast streaks on the male and a large dark eye.
species.description: The commonest breeding warbler in Colorado's willow and cottonwood riparian, singing a bright sweet-sweet-sweet-I'm-so-sweet. Responds to cowbird parasitism by building a new nest floor over the foreign egg, sometimes stacking six storeys.
species.en_description: The commonest breeding warbler in Colorado's willow and cottonwood riparian, singing a bright sweet-sweet-sweet-I'm-so-sweet. Responds to cowbird parasitism by building a new nest floor over the foreign egg, sometimes stacking six storeys.

species.name: Chipe corona negra
species.short_description: A small round yellow warbler; the male wears a neat black skullcap.
species.en_short_description: A small round yellow warbler; the male wears a neat black skullcap.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's subalpine willow thickets and floods every migration corridor in May and August. Constantly active, flicking its tail and hovering to snatch insects from leaf undersides. Females may show only a shadow of the cap or none.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's subalpine willow thickets and floods every migration corridor in May and August. Constantly active, flicking its tail and hovering to snatch insects from leaf undersides. Females may show only a shadow of the cap or none.

species.name: Chipe de Tolmie
species.short_description: Grey hood and broken white eye-arcs above a yellow belly; skulks low in dense brush.
species.en_short_description: Grey hood and broken white eye-arcs above a yellow belly; skulks low in dense brush.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's brushy montane understorey, burns and streamside tangles. The bold white crescents above and below the eye, unjoined at front and back, are the mark. Sings a burry two-part song from deep inside a thicket.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's brushy montane understorey, burns and streamside tangles. The bold white crescents above and below the eye, unjoined at front and back, are the mark. Sings a burry two-part song from deep inside a thicket.

species.name: Mascarita común
species.short_description: The male wears a broad black bandit mask; sings a rolling witchety-witchety-witchety.
species.en_short_description: The male wears a broad black bandit mask; sings a rolling witchety-witchety-witchety.
species.description: Nests in Colorado's cattail marsh, wet meadow and willow edge. Females and young lack the mask entirely and are plain olive with a yellow throat. Stays low, working stems near water rather than up in the canopy like most warblers.
species.en_description: Nests in Colorado's cattail marsh, wet meadow and willow edge. Females and young lack the mask entirely and are plain olive with a yellow throat. Stays low, working stems near water rather than up in the canopy like most warblers.

species.name: Búho lapón boreal
species.short_description: A small spruce-fir owl with a white-framed face and a rapid, hollow winnowing song.
species.en_short_description: A small spruce-fir owl with a white-framed face and a rapid, hollow winnowing song.
species.description: Breeds in Colorado's high subalpine forest, near the southern edge of a circumpolar range. Larger than a Saw-whet, with a pale bill and black borders down the sides of the facial disc. Sings only briefly in late winter, which is why it is so rarely found.
species.en_description: Breeds in Colorado's high subalpine forest, near the southern edge of a circumpolar range. Larger than a Saw-whet, with a pale bill and black borders down the sides of the facial disc. Sings only briefly in late winter, which is why it is so rarely found.

species.name: Tortuga de caja ornamentada
species.short_description: A land turtle of the shortgrass plains with a hinged shell it can close completely.
species.en_short_description: A land turtle of the shortgrass plains with a hinged shell it can close completely.
species.description: Colorado's only true box turtle, found in the sandsage and prairie of the eastern counties. Yellow radiating lines on a dark domed carapace; the plastron hinge seals the animal in like a box. Long-lived and slow to mature, which makes road mortality costly.
species.en_description: Colorado's only true box turtle, found in the sandsage and prairie of the eastern counties. Yellow radiating lines on a dark domed carapace; the plastron hinge seals the animal in like a box. Long-lived and slow to mature, which makes road mortality costly.

species.name: Tortuga de concha blanda espinosa
species.short_description: A flat, leathery, pancake-shaped turtle with a snorkel snout and no hard scutes.
species.en_short_description: A flat, leathery, pancake-shaped turtle with a snorkel snout and no hard scutes.
species.description: Lives in Colorado's plains rivers and reservoirs, burying itself in sand with only the head exposed. The shell is flexible cartilage covered in skin, with small spines along the leading edge. Fast in water and surprisingly quick on land, and it bites.
species.en_description: Lives in Colorado's plains rivers and reservoirs, burying itself in sand with only the head exposed. The shell is flexible cartilage covered in skin, with small spines along the leading edge. Fast in water and surprisingly quick on land, and it bites.

species.name: Culebra corredora
species.short_description: A fast, slender, smooth-scaled snake; adults are plain olive-blue, juveniles heavily blotched.
species.en_short_description: A fast, slender, smooth-scaled snake; adults are plain olive-blue, juveniles heavily blotched.
species.description: Hunts by sight across Colorado's grasslands and open foothills, often with the head raised above the vegetation. Despite the scientific name it does not constrict, simply pinning prey and swallowing it. Juveniles look like an entirely different, patterned species.
species.en_description: Hunts by sight across Colorado's grasslands and open foothills, often with the head raised above the vegetation. Despite the scientific name it does not constrict, simply pinning prey and swallowing it. Juveniles look like an entirely different, patterned species.

species.name: Culebra nariz de cerdo occidental
species.short_description: An upturned shovel snout for digging, and a spectacular bluff-and-play-dead routine.
species.en_short_description: An upturned shovel snout for digging, and a spectacular bluff-and-play-dead routine.
species.description: A toad specialist of Colorado's sandy eastern plains. When cornered it flattens its neck, hisses and strikes with a closed mouth; if that fails it writhes, voids and rolls belly-up with its tongue out. Rear-fanged and mildly venomous, but of no danger to people.
species.en_description: A toad specialist of Colorado's sandy eastern plains. When cornered it flattens its neck, hisses and strikes with a closed mouth; if that fails it writhes, voids and rolls belly-up with its tongue out. Rear-fanged and mildly venomous, but of no danger to people.

species.name: Cascabel masasauga occidental
species.short_description: A small grey rattlesnake of the southeastern plains with nine large scales on its crown.
species.en_short_description: A small grey rattlesnake of the southeastern plains with nine large scales on its crown.
species.description: Colorado's least-known venomous snake, restricted to the sandhills and prairie of the far southeast. Much smaller than a Prairie Rattlesnake, with a thin buzzing rattle. The enlarged head plates, rather than tiny scales, are the reliable distinction.
species.en_description: Colorado's least-known venomous snake, restricted to the sandhills and prairie of the far southeast. Much smaller than a Prairie Rattlesnake, with a thin buzzing rattle. The enlarged head plates, rather than tiny scales, are the reliable distinction.

species.name: Cascabel occidental
species.short_description: The Western Slope rattlesnake, including the pale midget faded form of the canyon country.
species.en_short_description: The Western Slope rattlesnake, including the pale midget faded form of the canyon country.
species.description: Replaces the Prairie Rattlesnake west of the Continental Divide in Colorado. The midget faded rattlesnake of the Colorado and Gunnison canyons is a small, washed-out subspecies with unusually potent venom. Dens communally in rock fissures through the winter.
species.en_description: Replaces the Prairie Rattlesnake west of the Continental Divide in Colorado. The midget faded rattlesnake of the Colorado and Gunnison canyons is a small, washed-out subspecies with unusually potent venom. Dens communally in rock fissures through the winter.

species.name: Culebra verde lisa
species.short_description: A slim, harmless, grass-green snake that hunts insects and turns blue after death.
species.en_short_description: A slim, harmless, grass-green snake that hunts insects and turns blue after death.
species.description: Lives in Colorado's moist mountain meadows and foothill grasslands, where the green back and white belly make it near-invisible until it moves. Eats spiders, caterpillars and crickets. The green pigment breaks down quickly, so museum specimens are blue.
species.en_description: Lives in Colorado's moist mountain meadows and foothill grasslands, where the green back and white belly make it near-invisible until it moves. Eats spiders, caterpillars and crickets. The green pigment breaks down quickly, so museum specimens are blue.

species.name: Culebra nocturna del desierto
species.short_description: A small pale nocturnal snake with dark neck blotches and vertical cat-like pupils.
species.en_short_description: A small pale nocturnal snake with dark neck blotches and vertical cat-like pupils.
species.description: Found under rocks in Colorado's western canyons and semi-desert shrubland. Rear-fanged, with a mild venom used on lizards and entirely harmless to people. The vertical pupil is unusual among Colorado snakes and separates it at a glance from young racers.
species.en_description: Found under rocks in Colorado's western canyons and semi-desert shrubland. Rear-fanged, with a mild venom used on lizards and entirely harmless to people. The vertical pupil is unusual among Colorado snakes and separates it at a glance from young racers.

species.name: Eslizón multilineado
species.short_description: A glossy, small-legged lizard with fine dark stripes and, when young, a bright blue tail.
species.en_short_description: A glossy, small-legged lizard with fine dark stripes and, when young, a bright blue tail.
species.description: Slips through leaf litter and under rocks on Colorado's plains, foothills and canyon slopes. The polished, wet-looking scales separate every skink from the state's rough-scaled lizards. The blue tail detaches readily and keeps twitching to buy the animal time.
species.en_description: Slips through leaf litter and under rocks on Colorado's plains, foothills and canyon slopes. The polished, wet-looking scales separate every skink from the state's rough-scaled lizards. The blue tail detaches readily and keeps twitching to buy the animal time.

species.name: Eslizón de las llanuras
species.short_description: The largest skink in the region; adults are grey with dark scale edges in a net pattern.
species.en_short_description: The largest skink in the region; adults are grey with dark scale edges in a net pattern.
species.description: Found in Colorado's southeastern canyons and rocky grassland. Hatchlings are jet black with a blue tail and orange head spots, looking nothing like the adult. The female stays with the eggs, turning them and defending the nest — rare behaviour in a lizard.
species.en_description: Found in Colorado's southeastern canyons and rocky grassland. Hatchlings are jet black with a blue tail and orange head spots, looking nothing like the adult. The female stays with the eggs, turning them and defending the nest — rare behaviour in a lizard.

species.name: Huico de seis líneas
species.short_description: A striped whiptail built for speed, sprinting between shrubs at 15 mph in full sun.
species.en_short_description: A striped whiptail built for speed, sprinting between shrubs at 15 mph in full sun.
species.description: Hunts on Colorado's sandy eastern plains during the hottest part of the day, when most other lizards have retreated. Six pale stripes on a dark back, with a long whip tail. Digs a shallow burrow at night and stays underground for two-thirds of the year.
species.en_description: Hunts on Colorado's sandy eastern plains during the hottest part of the day, when most other lizards have retreated. Six pale stripes on a dark back, with a long whip tail. Digs a shallow burrow at night and stays underground for two-thirds of the year.

species.name: Camaleón cornudo de Texas
species.short_description: A flat, spiny ant-eater with two long central head spines; can squirt blood from its eyes.
species.en_short_description: A flat, spiny ant-eater with two long central head spines; can squirt blood from its eyes.
species.description: Lives on Colorado's southeastern sandy plains and eats harvester ants almost exclusively, which is why it declines wherever those ants are poisoned. Two head horns are much longer than the rest. The blood squirt is a genuine defence aimed at canids.
species.en_description: Lives on Colorado's southeastern sandy plains and eats harvester ants almost exclusively, which is why it declines wherever those ants are poisoned. Two head horns are much longer than the rest. The blood squirt is a genuine defence aimed at canids.

species.name: Sapo de espuelas de las llanuras
species.short_description: A round-bodied burrower with a hard black spade on each hind foot and a raised forehead boss.
species.en_short_description: A round-bodied burrower with a hard black spade on each hind foot and a raised forehead boss.
species.description: Spends most of the year a foot underground on Colorado's eastern plains, emerging only after heavy summer rain to breed in temporary pools. Tadpoles can complete metamorphosis in under two weeks before the water goes. The call is a short low bleat.
species.en_description: Spends most of the year a foot underground on Colorado's eastern plains, emerging only after heavy summer rain to breed in temporary pools. Tadpoles can complete metamorphosis in under two weeks before the water goes. The call is a short low bleat.

species.name: Sapo de las llanuras
species.short_description: Large paired dark blotches with pale edges, and a deafening, machine-like breeding trill.
species.en_short_description: Large paired dark blotches with pale edges, and a deafening, machine-like breeding trill.
species.description: Breeds in flooded fields and rain pools across Colorado's eastern plains. The male inflates a sausage-shaped throat sac as long as his body and produces a continuous metallic rattle that can be heard a mile away and is painful up close.
species.en_description: Breeds in flooded fields and rain pools across Colorado's eastern plains. The male inflates a sausage-shaped throat sac as long as his body and produces a continuous metallic rattle that can be heard a mile away and is painful up close.

species.name: Sapo verde
species.short_description: A small, flat, bright yellow-green toad netted with black, calling with a buzzy trill.
species.en_short_description: A small, flat, bright yellow-green toad netted with black, calling with a buzzy trill.
species.description: A southeastern Colorado species of grassland playas and rocky canyon drainages, active only during summer monsoon rain. Flatter-bodied than any other Colorado toad and far more brightly coloured, which makes it unmistakable when found.
species.en_description: A southeastern Colorado species of grassland playas and rocky canyon drainages, active only during summer monsoon rain. Flatter-bodied than any other Colorado toad and far more brightly coloured, which makes it unmistakable when found.

species.name: Rana leopardo de las llanuras
species.short_description: Spotted brown frog with a broken dorsolateral ridge that jogs inward near the hip.
species.en_short_description: Spotted brown frog with a broken dorsolateral ridge that jogs inward near the hip.
species.description: Lives in Colorado's eastern plains streams, ponds and irrigation ditches. Told from the Northern Leopard Frog by the interrupted ridge along the back and a pale spot in the centre of the eardrum. Its call is a series of low chuckling clucks.
species.en_description: Lives in Colorado's eastern plains streams, ponds and irrigation ditches. Told from the Northern Leopard Frog by the interrupted ridge along the back and a pale spot in the centre of the eardrum. Its call is a series of low chuckling clucks.

species.name: Trucha degollada de espalda verde
species.short_description: Colorado's state fish: large-spotted, crimson-slashed, and back from presumed extinction.
species.en_short_description: Colorado's state fish: large-spotted, crimson-slashed, and back from presumed extinction.
species.description: Declared extinct twice, and reduced by 2012 genetic work to a single wild population in one creek south of Colorado Springs. Reintroduction into South Platte headwaters is ongoing. Told by very large round spots crowded toward the tail and a bright red throat slash.
species.en_description: Declared extinct twice, and reduced by 2012 genetic work to a single wild population in one creek south of Colorado Springs. Reintroduction into South Platte headwaters is ongoing. Told by very large round spots crowded toward the tail and a bright red throat slash.

species.name: Trucha degollada del río Colorado
species.short_description: The Western Slope native cutthroat: crimson-bellied in spawning colour, spots toward the rear.
species.en_short_description: The Western Slope native cutthroat: crimson-bellied in spawning colour, spots toward the rear.
species.description: Occupies headwater streams west of the Continental Divide, now in a fraction of its historic range after a century of stocking with non-native trout. Spawning males turn deep orange-red along the belly. Hybridises readily with rainbow trout, which is its main threat.
species.en_description: Occupies headwater streams west of the Continental Divide, now in a fraction of its historic range after a century of stocking with non-native trout. Spawning males turn deep orange-red along the belly. Hybridises readily with rainbow trout, which is its main threat.

species.name: Corégono de montaña
species.short_description: A native cylindrical silver fish with a small underslung mouth and a trout's adipose fin.
species.en_short_description: A native cylindrical silver fish with a small underslung mouth and a trout's adipose fin.
species.description: Common in Colorado's larger cold rivers on the Western Slope, feeding on the bottom for insect larvae. Often mistaken for a sucker, but the adipose fin marks it as a salmonid. Spawns over gravel in late autumn with no nest built at all.
species.en_description: Common in Colorado's larger cold rivers on the Western Slope, feeding on the bottom for insect larvae. Often mistaken for a sucker, but the adipose fin marks it as a salmonid. Spawns over gravel in late autumn with no nest built at all.

species.name: Trucha lacustre
species.short_description: A deep-water char with cream spots on dark green and a deeply forked tail.
species.en_short_description: A deep-water char with cream spots on dark green and a deeply forked tail.
species.description: Stocked into Colorado's big cold reservoirs, where it grows very large and lives for decades. A char, like the brook trout, not a true trout. In some waters it has decimated the kokanee and cutthroat populations it was introduced alongside.
species.en_description: Stocked into Colorado's big cold reservoirs, where it grows very large and lives for decades. A char, like the brook trout, not a true trout. In some waters it has decimated the kokanee and cutthroat populations it was introduced alongside.

species.name: Salmón kokanee
species.short_description: A landlocked sockeye that turns brilliant red and hook-jawed to spawn, then dies.
species.en_short_description: A landlocked sockeye that turns brilliant red and hook-jawed to spawn, then dies.
species.description: Stocked in Colorado reservoirs and running up their inlet streams each autumn in one of the state's most visible wildlife spectacles. Silver and troutlike for three or four years, then crimson-bodied with a green head for a few weeks at the end of life.
species.en_description: Stocked in Colorado reservoirs and running up their inlet streams each autumn in one of the state's most visible wildlife spectacles. Silver and troutlike for three or four years, then crimson-bodied with a green head for a few weeks at the end of life.

species.name: Lucio del norte
species.short_description: A long green ambush predator with a duck-billed snout and rows of backward-curving teeth.
species.en_short_description: A long green ambush predator with a duck-billed snout and rows of backward-curving teeth.
species.description: Introduced to Colorado waters and now unwanted in many of them, since it preys heavily on native and stocked fish alike. Lies motionless in weed beds and strikes at short range. Pale bean-shaped spots on a dark green flank distinguish it from a tiger muskie.
species.en_description: Introduced to Colorado waters and now unwanted in many of them, since it preys heavily on native and stocked fish alike. Lies motionless in weed beds and strikes at short range. Pale bean-shaped spots on a dark green flank distinguish it from a tiger muskie.

species.name: Lucioperca americana
species.short_description: Olive-gold perch relative with a glassy reflective eye built for hunting in low light.
species.en_short_description: Olive-gold perch relative with a glassy reflective eye built for hunting in low light.
species.description: Stocked in Colorado's larger warmwater reservoirs and most active at dusk and after dark. The reflective tapetum that gives the fish its name and its night vision also makes it shy of bright sun. A white tip on the lower tail lobe is a good field mark.
species.en_description: Stocked in Colorado's larger warmwater reservoirs and most active at dusk and after dark. The reflective tapetum that gives the fish its name and its night vision also makes it shy of bright sun. A white tip on the lower tail lobe is a good field mark.

species.name: Bagre de canal
species.short_description: Deeply forked tail, scattered dark spots and eight barbels around a broad mouth.
species.en_short_description: Deeply forked tail, scattered dark spots and eight barbels around a broad mouth.
species.description: The common catfish of Colorado's plains rivers and warmwater reservoirs. Tastes with chemoreceptors spread over its whole body, not just the barbels, which is how it feeds in muddy water. The pectoral and dorsal spines can inflict a painful wound.
species.en_description: The common catfish of Colorado's plains rivers and warmwater reservoirs. Tastes with chemoreceptors spread over its whole body, not just the barbels, which is how it feeds in muddy water. The pectoral and dorsal spines can inflict a painful wound.

species.name: Charalito del Colorado
species.short_description: North America's largest minnow, historically to six feet; now federally endangered.
species.en_short_description: North America's largest minnow, historically to six feet; now federally endangered.
species.description: A long-lived predator endemic to the Colorado River basin, once caught and sold as "white salmon". Dams, diversions and introduced predators cut it to a fraction of its range. Surviving adults in the Yampa and Green migrate hundreds of miles to spawn.
species.en_description: A long-lived predator endemic to the Colorado River basin, once caught and sold as "white salmon". Dams, diversions and introduced predators cut it to a fraction of its range. Surviving adults in the Yampa and Green migrate hundreds of miles to spawn.

species.name: Carpa jorobada
species.short_description: A streamlined native minnow with a pronounced fleshy hump behind the head.
species.en_short_description: A streamlined native minnow with a pronounced fleshy hump behind the head.
species.description: Endemic to the swift canyon reaches of the Colorado River basin, including Colorado's Black Rocks and Westwater. The hump and small eyes are thought to be adaptations to fast, turbid, sediment-heavy flow. Listed as threatened after decades as endangered.
species.en_description: Endemic to the swift canyon reaches of the Colorado River basin, including Colorado's Black Rocks and Westwater. The hump and small eyes are thought to be adaptations to fast, turbid, sediment-heavy flow. Listed as threatened after decades as endangered.

species.name: Matalote jorobado
species.short_description: A large native sucker with a sharp bony keel rising along its back.
species.en_short_description: A large native sucker with a sharp bony keel rising along its back.
species.description: Once abundant throughout the Colorado River basin and now maintained largely by stocking. The keel appears to stabilise the fish in strong current. Individuals over forty years old have been recorded, but natural recruitment in the wild remains very rare.
species.en_description: Once abundant throughout the Colorado River basin and now maintained largely by stocking. The keel appears to stabilise the fish in strong current. Individuals over forty years old have been recorded, but natural recruitment in the wild remains very rare.

species.name: Carpa colirrala
species.short_description: The rarest big-river native of the Colorado basin: a pencil-thin tail stalk and huge fins.
species.en_short_description: The rarest big-river native of the Colorado basin: a pencil-thin tail stalk and huge fins.
species.description: Effectively extinct in the wild and surviving as stocked hatchery fish in Colorado's Western Slope rivers. The extremely narrow caudal peduncle and large falcate fins mark an animal built for holding position in torrential flow.
species.en_description: Effectively extinct in the wild and surviving as stocked hatchery fish in Colorado's Western Slope rivers. The extremely narrow caudal peduncle and large falcate fins mark an animal built for holding position in torrential flow.

species.name: Matalote narizón
species.short_description: A native bottom-feeder with a long fleshy snout overhanging a downward-facing sucker mouth.
species.en_short_description: A native bottom-feeder with a long fleshy snout overhanging a downward-facing sucker mouth.
species.description: Widespread in Colorado's cold mountain streams and lakes, vacuuming invertebrates and algae from gravel. Spawning males develop a bright red lateral stripe and tubercled heads. Often the largest fish visible in a mountain creek, and routinely ignored.
species.en_description: Widespread in Colorado's cold mountain streams and lakes, vacuuming invertebrates and algae from gravel. Spawning males develop a bright red lateral stripe and tubercled heads. Often the largest fish visible in a mountain creek, and routinely ignored.

species.name: Carpita narizona
species.short_description: A small, torpedo-shaped native minnow that lives on the bottom of fast riffles.
species.en_short_description: A small, torpedo-shaped native minnow that lives on the bottom of fast riffles.
species.description: One of the most widespread native fish in Colorado, hugging the streambed between cobbles where the current is strongest. The snout projects well past the mouth. Rarely seen without turning rocks, but a key food for trout and kingfishers.
species.en_description: One of the most widespread native fish in Colorado, hugging the streambed between cobbles where the current is strongest. The snout projects well past the mouth. Rarely seen without turning rocks, but a key food for trout and kingfishers.

species.name: Carpita cabezona
species.short_description: A stubby, hardy baitfish; breeding males turn black with a spongy pad on the head.
species.en_short_description: A stubby, hardy baitfish; breeding males turn black with a spongy pad on the head.
species.description: Native to Colorado's plains streams and ponds and spread everywhere else as bait. The male guards eggs glued to the underside of a rock or log and cleans them with the fleshy dorsal pad. Tolerates warm, low-oxygen water that kills most other fish.
species.en_description: Native to Colorado's plains streams and ponds and spread everywhere else as bait. The male guards eggs glued to the underside of a rock or log and cleans them with the fleshy dorsal pad. Tolerates warm, low-oxygen water that kills most other fish.

species.name: Perca dardo del Arkansas
species.short_description: A two-inch spring-fed-stream fish; breeding males glow orange along the belly.
species.en_short_description: A two-inch spring-fed-stream fish; breeding males glow orange along the belly.
species.description: Restricted in Colorado to spring seeps and sandy creeks in the Arkansas River basin, and a species of concern as groundwater withdrawal dries them. Darters have no swim bladder and rest on the bottom in short hops. Easily missed and easily lost.
species.en_description: Restricted in Colorado to spring seeps and sandy creeks in the Arkansas River basin, and a species of concern as groundwater withdrawal dries them. Darters have no swim bladder and rest on the bottom in short hops. Easily missed and easily lost.

species.name: Colorado Hairstreak
species.short_description: Colorado's state insect: deep purple wings edged in black with orange spots at the tails.
species.en_short_description: Colorado's state insect: deep purple wings edged in black with orange spots at the tails.
species.description: Named the state insect in 1996 after a campaign by a fourth-grade class. Lives its whole life around Gambel oak in the foothills and canyons, where the caterpillars feed on the leaves. Adults are most active at dusk and drink oak sap and aphid honeydew rather than nectar.
species.en_description: Named the state insect in 1996 after a campaign by a fourth-grade class. Lives its whole life around Gambel oak in the foothills and canyons, where the caterpillars feed on the leaves. Adults are most active at dusk and drink oak sap and aphid honeydew rather than nectar.

species.name: Escarabajo de la papa
species.short_description: Ten black stripes on a yellow dome; it left native buffalo-bur for potatoes and went global.
species.en_short_description: Ten black stripes on a yellow dome; it left native buffalo-bur for potatoes and went global.
species.description: Native to Colorado and the southwest, where it fed on buffalo-bur until settlers planted potatoes across its path in the 1850s. It has since spread through Europe and Asia and evolved resistance to more than fifty insecticides. Larvae are humped, orange and voracious.
species.en_description: Native to Colorado and the southwest, where it fed on buffalo-bur until settlers planted potatoes across its path in the 1850s. It has since spread through Europe and Asia and evolved resistance to more than fifty insecticides. Larvae are humped, orange and voracious.

species.name: Palomilla miller
species.short_description: The "miller moth" that floods Colorado houses each spring on its way to the alpine.
species.en_short_description: The "miller moth" that floods Colorado houses each spring on its way to the alpine.
species.description: Larvae feed in eastern-plains crop fields; the adults migrate west to the high country in May and June, blundering into every lit doorway on the Front Range en route. Once above treeline they feed on alpine flowers and become a major pre-hibernation food for black bears.
species.en_description: Larvae feed in eastern-plains crop fields; the adults migrate west to the high country in May and June, blundering into every lit doorway on the Front Range en route. Once above treeline they feed on alpine flowers and become a major pre-hibernation food for black bears.

species.name: Escarabajo del pino de montaña
species.short_description: A rice-grain bark beetle that killed millions of acres of Colorado lodgepole and ponderosa.
species.en_short_description: A rice-grain bark beetle that killed millions of acres of Colorado lodgepole and ponderosa.
species.description: Bores through bark to breed in the living phloem, carrying a blue-stain fungus that blocks the tree's water transport. The epidemic that peaked in the 2000s reshaped whole watersheds. Look for popcorn-like pitch tubes on the trunk and J-shaped galleries under loose bark.
species.en_description: Bores through bark to breed in the living phloem, carrying a blue-stain fungus that blocks the tree's water transport. The epidemic that peaked in the 2000s reshaped whole watersheds. Look for popcorn-like pitch tubes on the trunk and J-shaped galleries under loose bark.

species.name: Apolo de las Rocosas
species.short_description: A translucent white alpine swallowtail with red-and-black eyespots and no tails.
species.en_short_description: A translucent white alpine swallowtail with red-and-black eyespots and no tails.
species.description: Flies slowly over Colorado's high meadows and tundra from July, where the caterpillars eat stonecrop. Mated females carry a waxy plug left by the male that prevents further mating. The papery, half-transparent wings are unlike any other butterfly here.
species.en_description: Flies slowly over Colorado's high meadows and tundra from July, where the caterpillars eat stonecrop. Mated females carry a waxy plug left by the male that prevents further mating. The papery, half-transparent wings are unlike any other butterfly here.

species.name: Almirante de Weidemeyer
species.short_description: Black wings crossed by a broad white band; glides between aspen and willow on flat wings.
species.en_short_description: Black wings crossed by a broad white band; glides between aspen and willow on flat wings.
species.description: A characteristic butterfly of Colorado's montane riparian and aspen edge. Caterpillars overwinter half-grown inside a rolled leaf shelter tied to a twig with silk, and look convincingly like bird droppings at every stage.
species.en_description: A characteristic butterfly of Colorado's montane riparian and aspen edge. Caterpillars overwinter half-grown inside a rolled leaf shelter tied to a twig with silk, and look convincingly like bird droppings at every stage.

species.name: Tortuga de Milbert
species.short_description: Dark chocolate wings with a wide orange-and-yellow band along the outer margin.
species.en_short_description: Dark chocolate wings with a wide orange-and-yellow band along the outer margin.
species.description: Overwinters as an adult in Colorado, so it is often the first butterfly seen on a warm February day. Caterpillars feed communally in a silk nest on nettles. Wings closed, it is bark-coloured and near-invisible; open, it is one of the brightest insects in the state.
species.en_description: Overwinters as an adult in Colorado, so it is often the first butterfly seen on a warm February day. Caterpillars feed communally in a silk nest on nettles. Wings closed, it is bark-coloured and near-invisible; open, it is one of the brightest insects in the state.

species.name: Fritilaria Afrodita
species.short_description: Orange above and silver-spotted below; a large fritillary of mountain meadows.
species.en_short_description: Orange above and silver-spotted below; a large fritillary of mountain meadows.
species.description: Females lay eggs near violets in late summer; the caterpillars hatch, eat nothing, and overwinter, waiting for the plants to reappear in spring. Common in Colorado's montane and subalpine meadows through July and August.
species.en_description: Females lay eggs near violets in late summer; the caterpillars hatch, eat nothing, and overwinter, waiting for the plants to reappear in spring. Common in Colorado's montane and subalpine meadows through July and August.

species.name: Azul de Melissa
species.short_description: A thumbnail-sized blue butterfly with an orange band inside the hindwing margin.
species.en_short_description: A thumbnail-sized blue butterfly with an orange band inside the hindwing margin.
species.description: Common on Colorado's plains, roadsides and foothill meadows wherever there is lupine, alfalfa or locoweed. The caterpillars secrete sugars that attract ants, which in turn defend them. The male is violet-blue above, the female mostly brown.
species.en_description: Common on Colorado's plains, roadsides and foothill meadows wherever there is lupine, alfalfa or locoweed. The caterpillars secrete sugars that attract ants, which in turn defend them. The male is violet-blue above, the female mostly brown.

species.name: Mariposa de la alfalfa
species.short_description: Lemon-yellow with a solid dark border; never settles with its wings open.
species.en_short_description: Lemon-yellow with a solid dark border; never settles with its wings open.
species.description: One of the most abundant butterflies in Colorado, patrolling alfalfa fields, ditches and lawns from spring to hard frost. Hybridises freely with the Orange Sulphur, which makes intermediate individuals common and identification genuinely uncertain.
species.en_description: One of the most abundant butterflies in Colorado, patrolling alfalfa fields, ditches and lawns from spring to hard frost. Hybridises freely with the Orange Sulphur, which makes intermediate individuals common and identification genuinely uncertain.

species.name: Libélula verde común
species.short_description: A big green-and-blue dragonfly with a bullseye on the forehead; one of the few that migrate.
species.en_short_description: A big green-and-blue dragonfly with a bullseye on the forehead; one of the few that migrate.
species.description: Hawks over Colorado ponds and fields all summer. Part of the population migrates south in autumn and a different generation returns north in spring, a relay that takes three generations to complete a round trip. Can raise its body temperature by whirring its wings.
species.en_description: Hawks over Colorado ponds and fields all summer. Part of the population migrates south in autumn and a different generation returns north in spring, a relay that takes three generations to complete a round trip. Can raise its body temperature by whirring its wings.

species.name: Libélula de doce manchas
species.short_description: Three dark blotches on each wing; mature males add white patches between them.
species.en_short_description: Three dark blotches on each wing; mature males add white patches between them.
species.description: Patrols Colorado's ponds, marsh edges and slow ditches, perching on tall stems between sorties. Males defend a stretch of shoreline against all comers. The alternating black and white wing patches flicker distinctively in flight.
species.en_description: Patrols Colorado's ponds, marsh edges and slow ditches, perching on tall stems between sorties. Males defend a stretch of shoreline against all comers. The alternating black and white wing patches flicker distinctively in flight.

species.name: Chinche del negundo
species.short_description: Black with three red lines on the thorax; masses on sunlit walls in autumn.
species.en_short_description: Black with three red lines on the thorax; masses on sunlit walls in autumn.
species.description: Feeds on boxelder and maple seeds all summer, then aggregates by the hundred on the south side of Colorado houses in September looking for a place to overwinter. Harmless — it neither bites nor breeds indoors — but persistent.
species.en_description: Feeds on boxelder and maple seeds all summer, then aggregates by the hundred on the south side of Colorado houses in September looking for a place to overwinter. Harmless — it neither bites nor breeds indoors — but persistent.

species.name: Grillo mormón
species.short_description: A flightless, armoured katydid that marches across rangeland in bands of millions.
species.en_short_description: A flightless, armoured katydid that marches across rangeland in bands of millions.
species.description: Not a cricket and does not fly. Outbreaks in northwestern Colorado and the Great Basin move on foot in a rolling front, driven forward partly by cannibalism from behind. Females carry a long curved ovipositor often mistaken for a stinger.
species.en_description: Not a cricket and does not fly. Outbreaks in northwestern Colorado and the Great Basin move on foot in a rolling front, driven forward partly by cannibalism from behind. Females carry a long curved ovipositor often mistaken for a stinger.

species.name: Chapulín de Carolina
species.short_description: Flushes from a dirt road on black butterfly-like wings edged in pale yellow.
species.en_short_description: Flushes from a dirt road on black butterfly-like wings edged in pale yellow.
species.description: The large grasshopper that startles walkers off Colorado's bare trails and gravel roads, then lands and vanishes against the dust. Males hover and crackle in a display flight. The black hindwings are visible only when it is airborne.
species.en_description: The large grasshopper that startles walkers off Colorado's bare trails and gravel roads, then lands and vanishes against the dust. Males hover and crackle in a display flight. The black hindwings are visible only when it is airborne.

species.name: Esfinge colibrí
species.short_description: A day-flying moth with clear wings and a bumblebee body that hovers at flowers like a hummingbird.
species.en_short_description: A day-flying moth with clear wings and a bumblebee body that hovers at flowers like a hummingbird.
species.description: Visits Colorado gardens and montane meadows in daylight, hovering at penstemon and bee balm with an audible hum. Regularly reported as a very small hummingbird. Caterpillars feed on snowberry and honeysuckle, both common in the foothills.
species.en_description: Visits Colorado gardens and montane meadows in daylight, hovering at penstemon and bee balm with an audible hum. Regularly reported as a very small hummingbird. Caterpillars feed on snowberry and honeysuckle, both common in the foothills.

species.name: Palomilla de la yuca
species.short_description: A small white moth that deliberately pollinates yucca and lays its eggs in the flower.
species.en_short_description: A small white moth that deliberately pollinates yucca and lays its eggs in the flower.
species.description: Neither the yucca nor the moth can reproduce without the other. The female gathers pollen into a ball with specialised mouthparts, lays eggs in the ovary and then packs the pollen onto the stigma. Some larvae eat the resulting seeds; enough survive for both species.
species.en_description: Neither the yucca nor the moth can reproduce without the other. The female gathers pollen into a ball with specialised mouthparts, lays eggs in the ovary and then packs the pollen onto the stigma. Some larvae eat the resulting seeds; enough survive for both species.

species.name: Escarabajo de junio rayado
species.short_description: A large striped scarab; males have fanned antennae and hiss loudly when picked up.
species.en_short_description: A large striped scarab; males have fanned antennae and hiss loudly when picked up.
species.description: Comes to porch lights across Colorado in midsummer with a heavy clattering flight. The white stripes on brown are chalky scales that rub off. Larvae spend two or three years underground chewing roots before emerging as adults.
species.en_description: Comes to porch lights across Colorado in midsummer with a heavy clattering flight. The white stripes on brown are chalky scales that rub off. Larvae spend two or three years underground chewing roots before emerging as adults.

species.name: Abejorro occidental
species.short_description: A once-common black bumblebee with a white rear end, now sharply declined across the West.
species.en_short_description: A once-common black bumblebee with a white rear end, now sharply declined across the West.
species.description: Formerly one of the most abundant bumblebees in Colorado and now scarce at lower elevations, though it persists in the high country. Suspected causes include a pathogen spread from commercial colonies. Robs nectar by biting holes in the base of long flowers.
species.en_description: Formerly one of the most abundant bumblebees in Colorado and now scarce at lower elevations, though it persists in the high country. Suspected causes include a pathogen spread from commercial colonies. Robs nectar by biting holes in the base of long flowers.

species.name: Tarántula café de Texas
species.short_description: Colorado's tarantula; mature males cross southeastern roads each September looking for mates.
species.en_short_description: Colorado's tarantula; mature males cross southeastern roads each September looking for mates.
species.description: Lives in silk-lined burrows on the shortgrass prairie around La Junta and Comanche National Grassland. The autumn "migration" is males walking, sometimes for miles, at the end of a life that took ten years to reach. Females can live thirty years. The bite is trivial.
species.en_description: Lives in silk-lined burrows on the shortgrass prairie around La Junta and Comanche National Grassland. The autumn "migration" is males walking, sometimes for miles, at the end of a life that took ten years to reach. Females can live thirty years. The bite is trivial.

species.name: Garrapata de las Rocosas
species.short_description: A brown tick with a pale shield, questing on brush at trail height from March to July.
species.en_short_description: A brown tick with a pale shield, questing on brush at trail height from March to July.
species.description: The main vector in Colorado of Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Colorado tick fever and tularemia, and the cause of tick paralysis. Waits on grass tips with front legs extended. Peaks in spring and early summer and largely disappears by August.
species.en_description: The main vector in Colorado of Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Colorado tick fever and tularemia, and the cause of tick paralysis. Waits on grass tips with front legs extended. Peaks in spring and early summer and largely disappears by August.

species.name: Araña cara de gato
species.short_description: A bulbous orbweaver with two horn-like humps that make a cat's face on the abdomen.
species.en_short_description: A bulbous orbweaver with two horn-like humps that make a cat's face on the abdomen.
species.description: Builds a large orb under Colorado porch eaves and window frames from late summer, rebuilding it most nights. Colour ranges from cream to deep brown on the same street. Harmless, and one of the most effective mosquito controls a house can have.
species.en_description: Builds a large orb under Colorado porch eaves and window frames from late summer, rebuilding it most nights. Colour ranges from cream to deep brown on the same street. Harmless, and one of the most effective mosquito controls a house can have.

species.name: Araña lobo de Carolina
species.short_description: The largest wolf spider in North America; the female carries her young on her back.
species.en_short_description: The largest wolf spider in North America; the female carries her young on her back.
species.description: Hunts on foot at night across Colorado's plains and open ground, its eyes returning a green shine to a headlamp. Does not build a web. Carries the egg sac attached to the spinnerets and then ferries dozens of spiderlings on the abdomen for a week or more.
species.en_description: Hunts on foot at night across Colorado's plains and open ground, its eyes returning a green shine to a headlamp. Does not build a web. Carries the egg sac attached to the spinnerets and then ferries dozens of spiderlings on the abdomen for a week or more.

species.name: Araña de embudo
species.short_description: Builds the flat sheet webs with a funnel retreat that dew makes visible across a lawn.
species.en_short_description: Builds the flat sheet webs with a funnel retreat that dew makes visible across a lawn.
species.description: Extremely common in Colorado grass, shrubs and window wells. The web is not sticky; the spider sprints out over the sheet and grabs prey that stumbles onto it. Long spinnerets projecting behind the abdomen are the quickest identification.
species.en_description: Extremely common in Colorado grass, shrubs and window wells. The web is not sticky; the spider sprints out over the sheet and grabs prey that stumbles onto it. Long spinnerets projecting behind the abdomen are the quickest identification.

species.name: Alacrán del norte
species.short_description: A small pale scorpion of dry western valleys, and the northernmost in North America.
species.en_short_description: A small pale scorpion of dry western valleys, and the northernmost in North America.
species.description: Found under rocks in Colorado's semi-desert shrubland and canyon country on the Western Slope. Glows blue-green under ultraviolet light, like all scorpions. The sting is comparable to a bee's and has no serious effect on people.
species.en_description: Found under rocks in Colorado's semi-desert shrubland and canyon country on the Western Slope. Glows blue-green under ultraviolet light, like all scorpions. The sting is comparable to a bee's and has no serious effect on people.

species.name: Solífugo gigante
species.short_description: Neither spider nor scorpion: a fast tan hunter with enormous jaws and no venom at all.
species.en_short_description: Neither spider nor scorpion: a fast tan hunter with enormous jaws and no venom at all.
species.description: Runs down insects at speed across Colorado's plains and dry foothills, mostly at night, and turns up in tents and garages. The front pair of leg-like pedipalps are sensory, not legs. Powerful chelicerae, no venom gland, and an entirely undeserved reputation.
species.en_description: Runs down insects at speed across Colorado's plains and dry foothills, mostly at night, and turns up in tents and garages. The front pair of leg-like pedipalps are sensory, not legs. Powerful chelicerae, no venom gland, and an entirely undeserved reputation.

species.name: Pícea azul
species.short_description: Colorado's state tree: stiff, sharply pointed needles in a silver-blue that varies by tree.
species.en_short_description: Colorado's state tree: stiff, sharply pointed needles in a silver-blue that varies by tree.
species.description: Named the state tree in 1939 by a vote of schoolchildren. Native to streamsides and moist montane slopes between roughly 6,000 and 9,000 feet, though far more people meet it as a planted ornamental. Needles are square in cross-section and genuinely painful to grasp.
species.en_description: Named the state tree in 1939 by a vote of schoolchildren. Native to streamsides and moist montane slopes between roughly 6,000 and 9,000 feet, though far more people meet it as a planted ornamental. Needles are square in cross-section and genuinely painful to grasp.

species.name: Pícea de Engelmann
species.short_description: The spire-shaped spruce of the subalpine, forming dense dark forest with subalpine fir.
species.en_short_description: The spire-shaped spruce of the subalpine, forming dense dark forest with subalpine fir.
species.description: Dominates Colorado between about 9,000 feet and treeline, where wind shears it into krummholz. Needles are softer and bluer-green than blue spruce and smell faintly sour when crushed. Cones hang down and are papery; a fir's stand upright and disintegrate on the branch.
species.en_description: Dominates Colorado between about 9,000 feet and treeline, where wind shears it into krummholz. Needles are softer and bluer-green than blue spruce and smell faintly sour when crushed. Cones hang down and are papery; a fir's stand upright and disintegrate on the branch.

species.name: Pino erizo de las Rocosas
species.short_description: Twisted timberline pine with resin-flecked needles in fives; individuals live for millennia.
species.en_short_description: Twisted timberline pine with resin-flecked needles in fives; individuals live for millennia.
species.description: Grows on exposed high ridges in central and southern Colorado — Mount Goliath, Windy Ridge, the Sangre de Cristos. Needles are held for twenty years or more and are speckled with white resin dots that look like disease and are not. Dead wood on a living tree can stand for centuries.
species.en_description: Grows on exposed high ridges in central and southern Colorado — Mount Goliath, Windy Ridge, the Sangre de Cristos. Needles are held for twenty years or more and are speckled with white resin dots that look like disease and are not. Dead wood on a living tree can stand for centuries.

species.name: Pino flexible
species.short_description: A five-needle pine of windswept ridges whose young branches can be tied in a knot.
species.en_short_description: A five-needle pine of windswept ridges whose young branches can be tied in a knot.
species.description: Grows on dry rocky exposures at both the lower and upper edges of Colorado's forest, often on ground no other conifer will take. Its heavy wingless seeds are planted by Clark's Nutcracker, so the tree's distribution follows the bird's caching habits.
species.en_description: Grows on dry rocky exposures at both the lower and upper edges of Colorado's forest, often on ground no other conifer will take. Its heavy wingless seeds are planted by Clark's Nutcracker, so the tree's distribution follows the bird's caching habits.

species.name: Abeto blanco
species.short_description: Flat blue-green needles that curve upward off the twig, on a straight-trunked mountain fir.
species.en_short_description: Flat blue-green needles that curve upward off the twig, on a straight-trunked mountain fir.
species.description: Grows in Colorado's southern and western mixed-conifer forest. Needles are soft, flattened and easy to roll between the fingers, unlike a spruce's square ones. Cones sit upright on high branches and shatter in place, so an intact fir cone is rarely found on the ground.
species.en_description: Grows in Colorado's southern and western mixed-conifer forest. Needles are soft, flattened and easy to roll between the fingers, unlike a spruce's square ones. Cones sit upright on high branches and shatter in place, so an intact fir cone is rarely found on the ground.

species.name: Sabina de Utah
species.short_description: A shrubby, many-stemmed juniper of the Western Slope, often paired with pinyon pine.
species.en_short_description: A shrubby, many-stemmed juniper of the Western Slope, often paired with pinyon pine.
species.description: The dominant juniper of Colorado's canyon and mesa country, usually branching from near the ground into a broad rounded crown. Scale leaves and reddish-brown berry cones. Slow-growing and long-lived; a small tree can be several hundred years old.
species.en_description: The dominant juniper of Colorado's canyon and mesa country, usually branching from near the ground into a broad rounded crown. Scale leaves and reddish-brown berry cones. Slow-growing and long-lived; a small tree can be several hundred years old.

species.name: Sabina de una semilla
species.short_description: A southern juniper that branches at ground level into several trunks, each cone with one seed.
species.en_short_description: A southern juniper that branches at ground level into several trunks, each cone with one seed.
species.description: Found in southeastern and south-central Colorado on dry mesas and canyon rims. Distinguished from Rocky Mountain juniper by its multi-stemmed base and from Utah juniper by the single seed in each blue-brown cone. Roots go extremely deep for water.
species.en_description: Found in southeastern and south-central Colorado on dry mesas and canyon rims. Distinguished from Rocky Mountain juniper by its multi-stemmed base and from Utah juniper by the single seed in each blue-brown cone. Roots go extremely deep for water.

species.name: Álamo de hoja angosta
species.short_description: A mountain cottonwood with willow-like leaves, lining streams up to 8,000 feet.
species.en_short_description: A mountain cottonwood with willow-like leaves, lining streams up to 8,000 feet.
species.description: Follows Colorado's montane creeks and rivers, forming pale-barked corridors of shade. The narrow lance-shaped leaves look nothing like a plains cottonwood's triangles, but the drifting cotton in June is the same. Hybridises with plains cottonwood where their ranges meet.
species.en_description: Follows Colorado's montane creeks and rivers, forming pale-barked corridors of shade. The narrow lance-shaped leaves look nothing like a plains cottonwood's triangles, but the drifting cotton in June is the same. Hybridises with plains cottonwood where their ranges meet.

species.name: Sauce hoja de durazno
species.short_description: The largest native willow of the plains, tree-sized, with drooping peach-shaped leaves.
species.en_short_description: The largest native willow of the plains, tree-sized, with drooping peach-shaped leaves.
species.description: Grows along Colorado's eastern rivers, ditches and reservoir margins, often the only native tree for miles. Leaves are pale and whitish underneath and flutter conspicuously. Frequently multi-trunked and leaning out over water.
species.en_description: Grows along Colorado's eastern rivers, ditches and reservoir margins, often the only native tree for miles. Leaves are pale and whitish underneath and flutter conspicuously. Frequently multi-trunked and leaning out over water.

species.name: Abedul de agua
species.short_description: A thicket-forming streamside birch with shiny dark copper bark that does not peel.
species.en_short_description: A thicket-forming streamside birch with shiny dark copper bark that does not peel.
species.description: Lines Colorado's foothill and montane creeks in dense clumps of slender trunks. The bark is bronze to nearly black with pale horizontal lenticels and, unlike a paper birch, stays tight to the tree. Turns clear yellow in autumn along the length of a drainage.
species.en_description: Lines Colorado's foothill and montane creeks in dense clumps of slender trunks. The bark is bronze to nearly black with pale horizontal lenticels and, unlike a paper birch, stays tight to the tree. Turns clear yellow in autumn along the length of a drainage.

species.name: Aliso de hoja delgada
species.short_description: Streamside shrub-tree with doubly toothed leaves and small woody cones that persist all winter.
species.en_short_description: Streamside shrub-tree with doubly toothed leaves and small woody cones that persist all winter.
species.description: Holds the banks of Colorado's mountain streams and fixes nitrogen in root nodules, enriching the soil around it. Old female catkins harden into little cones that stay on the twigs through winter and are a reliable identification when the leaves are gone.
species.en_description: Holds the banks of Colorado's mountain streams and fixes nitrogen in root nodules, enriching the soil around it. Old female catkins harden into little cones that stay on the twigs through winter and are a reliable identification when the leaves are gone.

species.name: Fresno verde
species.short_description: Compound opposite leaves and paddle-shaped winged seeds; the standard Front Range street tree.
species.en_short_description: Compound opposite leaves and paddle-shaped winged seeds; the standard Front Range street tree.
species.description: Planted extensively across Colorado's towns and shelterbelts and naturalised along plains rivers. Opposite branching narrows the possibilities immediately. The emerald ash borer, confirmed in Boulder County in 2013, threatens a large share of the state's urban canopy.
species.en_description: Planted extensively across Colorado's towns and shelterbelts and naturalised along plains rivers. Opposite branching narrows the possibilities immediately. The emerald ash borer, confirmed in Boulder County in 2013, threatens a large share of the state's urban canopy.

species.name: Olmo siberiano
species.short_description: A tough, brittle, fast-growing introduction that seeds into every alley and ditch bank.
species.en_short_description: A tough, brittle, fast-growing introduction that seeds into every alley and ditch bank.
species.description: Planted across Colorado after the Dust Bowl for shelterbelts and now thoroughly invasive along plains waterways and urban margins. Small asymmetrical leaves and papery round seeds produced in enormous quantity in April. Breaks apart in wind and heavy snow.
species.en_description: Planted across Colorado after the Dust Bowl for shelterbelts and now thoroughly invasive along plains waterways and urban margins. Small asymmetrical leaves and papery round seeds produced in enormous quantity in April. Breaks apart in wind and heavy snow.

species.name: Olivo ruso
species.short_description: Silver willow-like leaves, thorny twigs, and intensely fragrant small yellow flowers in June.
species.en_short_description: Silver willow-like leaves, thorny twigs, and intensely fragrant small yellow flowers in June.
species.description: A List B noxious weed in Colorado, planted as a windbreak and now dominating riparian corridors on the plains and Western Slope, where it crowds out cottonwood and willow. Fixes nitrogen, which changes the soil chemistry against native species.
species.en_description: A List B noxious weed in Colorado, planted as a windbreak and now dominating riparian corridors on the plains and Western Slope, where it crowds out cottonwood and willow. Fixes nitrogen, which changes the soil chemistry against native species.

species.name: Roble bur
species.short_description: A massive plains oak with deeply lobed leaves and acorns in a shaggy fringed cup.
species.en_short_description: A massive plains oak with deeply lobed leaves and acorns in a shaggy fringed cup.
species.description: Native to Colorado's far northeastern corner and planted widely in Front Range towns for its drought and cold tolerance. Thick corky bark makes it unusually fire-resistant. The fringed acorn cap is unmistakable and the acorns are the largest of any North American oak.
species.en_description: Native to Colorado's far northeastern corner and planted widely in Front Range towns for its drought and cold tolerance. Thick corky bark makes it unusually fire-resistant. The fringed acorn cap is unmistakable and the acorns are the largest of any North American oak.

species.name: Pincel indio escarlata
species.short_description: The red is not petals but bracts; the actual flowers are thin green tubes hidden inside.
species.en_short_description: The red is not petals but bracts; the actual flowers are thin green tubes hidden inside.
species.description: Common in Colorado's montane and subalpine meadows. Partly parasitic — it taps the roots of neighbouring grasses and sagebrush for water and nutrients, which is why it resists transplanting. Broad-tailed Hummingbirds are its main pollinators.
species.en_description: Common in Colorado's montane and subalpine meadows. Partly parasitic — it taps the roots of neighbouring grasses and sagebrush for water and nutrients, which is why it resists transplanting. Broad-tailed Hummingbirds are its main pollinators.

species.name: Musgo florido
species.short_description: A tight green alpine cushion studded with tiny pink flowers, growing a millimetre a year.
species.en_short_description: A tight green alpine cushion studded with tiny pink flowers, growing a millimetre a year.
species.description: Forms dense mounds on Colorado's tundra that may be a century old at the size of a dinner plate. The cushion traps heat and soil and shelters other plants that colonise its centre. Flowers on the sunniest side of the mound first.
species.en_description: Forms dense mounds on Colorado's tundra that may be a century old at the size of a dinner plate. The cushion traps heat and soil and shelters other plants that colonise its centre. Flowers on the sunniest side of the mound first.

species.name: Pedicularia cabeza de elefante
species.short_description: Every pink flower on the spike is a miniature elephant's head, trunk raised.
species.en_short_description: Every pink flower on the spike is a miniature elephant's head, trunk raised.
species.description: Grows in wet Colorado subalpine meadows and along snowmelt channels, often in dense colonies. The resemblance is exact once seen — ears, forehead and a long curved trunk. Bumblebees vibrate the flowers to shake pollen loose.
species.en_description: Grows in wet Colorado subalpine meadows and along snowmelt channels, often in dense colonies. The resemblance is exact once seen — ears, forehead and a long curved trunk. Bumblebees vibrate the flowers to shake pollen loose.

species.name: Nomeolvides alpina
species.short_description: An intense sky-blue with a yellow eye, on a grey cushion barely an inch tall.
species.en_short_description: An intense sky-blue with a yellow eye, on a grey cushion barely an inch tall.
species.description: One of the most sought-after plants of Colorado's tundra, flowering for a few weeks in June and July on wind-scoured ridges. The whole plant hugs the ground below the killing wind. Colour is deeper than any other blue at that altitude.
