species.en_description: One of the most sought-after plants of Colorado's tundra, flowering for a few weeks in June and July on wind-scoured ridges. The whole plant hugs the ground below the killing wind. Colour is deeper than any other blue at that altitude.

species.name: Girasol alpino
species.short_description: A big shaggy yellow sunflower on a short woolly stem, always facing east.
species.en_short_description: A big shaggy yellow sunflower on a short woolly stem, always facing east.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's exposed alpine gravel, spending years storing energy in a taproot before flowering once and dying. The head is enormous relative to the plant. It orients east to catch the morning sun and warm its pollinators.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's exposed alpine gravel, spending years storing energy in a taproot before flowering once and dying. The head is enormous relative to the plant. It orients east to catch the morning sun and warm its pollinators.

species.name: Polemonio alpino
species.short_description: Clusters of violet-blue trumpets on sticky ladder-like leaves that smell strongly of skunk.
species.en_short_description: Clusters of violet-blue trumpets on sticky ladder-like leaves that smell strongly of skunk.
species.description: A high alpine plant of Colorado's talus and ridgelines. The skunky resin deters ants that would rob nectar without pollinating. Crush a leaf to confirm the identification; the smell is unmistakable and lingers on the fingers.
species.en_description: A high alpine plant of Colorado's talus and ridgelines. The skunky resin deters ants that would rob nectar without pollinating. Crush a leaf to confirm the identification; the smell is unmistakable and lingers on the fingers.

species.name: Zapatilla de hada
species.short_description: A single pink orchid slipper on a stem two inches high, in deep mossy conifer shade.
species.en_short_description: A single pink orchid slipper on a stem two inches high, in deep mossy conifer shade.
species.description: Flowers in Colorado's damp spruce and fir understorey in late May and June. It offers no nectar at all — the flower deceives naive bumblebees into visiting. Depends on a soil fungus and dies if transplanted or if its litter layer is disturbed.
species.en_description: Flowers in Colorado's damp spruce and fir understorey in late May and June. It offers no nectar at all — the flower deceives naive bumblebees into visiting. Depends on a soil fungus and dies if transplanted or if its litter layer is disturbed.

species.name: Bergamota silvestre
species.short_description: A ragged lavender pompom on a square stem; the crushed leaves smell of oregano.
species.en_short_description: A ragged lavender pompom on a square stem; the crushed leaves smell of oregano.
species.description: Grows in Colorado's foothill meadows, roadsides and open woodland. Square stems and opposite leaves place it in the mint family immediately. Heavily visited by hummingbirds, sphinx moths and long-tongued bees, and traditionally used as a medicinal tea.
species.en_description: Grows in Colorado's foothill meadows, roadsides and open woodland. Square stems and opposite leaves place it in the mint family immediately. Heavily visited by hummingbirds, sphinx moths and long-tongued bees, and traditionally used as a medicinal tea.

species.name: Gaillardia
species.short_description: Red-centred yellow daisy with three-toothed ray tips, flowering all summer on dry ground.
species.en_short_description: Red-centred yellow daisy with three-toothed ray tips, flowering all summer on dry ground.
species.description: Common on Colorado's foothill grasslands, roadsides and mesas from June through September. Drought-hardy and long-blooming, which is why it has become a staple of xeric planting across the Front Range. The dark centre dries to a bristly globe.
species.en_description: Common on Colorado's foothill grasslands, roadsides and mesas from June through September. Drought-hardy and long-blooming, which is why it has become a staple of xeric planting across the Front Range. The dark centre dries to a bristly globe.

species.name: Sombrero mexicano
species.short_description: Drooping yellow or mahogany rays under a tall thimble-shaped brown cone.
species.en_short_description: Drooping yellow or mahogany rays under a tall thimble-shaped brown cone.
species.description: Abundant on Colorado's eastern plains, roadsides and disturbed grassland. Also called Mexican Hat for the shape. Some populations are almost entirely red-brown and others pure yellow, sometimes within the same stand.
species.en_description: Abundant on Colorado's eastern plains, roadsides and disturbed grassland. Also called Mexican Hat for the shape. Some populations are almost entirely red-brown and others pure yellow, sometimes within the same stand.

species.name: Guaco
species.short_description: Tall pink flower heads with long protruding stamens, above three-part leaves.
species.en_short_description: Tall pink flower heads with long protruding stamens, above three-part leaves.
species.description: Colonises Colorado's disturbed ground, roadsides and old fields, often in solid pink stands. A major nectar source late in the season. Ancestral Puebloan potters boiled it down to make the black paint used on their ceramics.
species.en_description: Colonises Colorado's disturbed ground, roadsides and old fields, often in solid pink stands. A major nectar source late in the season. Ancestral Puebloan potters boiled it down to make the black paint used on their ceramics.

species.name: Lirio de las Rocosas
species.short_description: Pale blue-violet iris that carpets wet mountain meadows in June, usually where cattle graze.
species.en_short_description: Pale blue-violet iris that carpets wet mountain meadows in June, usually where cattle graze.
species.description: Grows in Colorado's moist montane parks and irrigated pastures. Toxic to livestock, so heavy grazing leaves it behind and it spreads — a dense iris meadow is often a sign of a hard-used pasture. Reproduces mostly by spreading rhizomes.
species.en_description: Grows in Colorado's moist montane parks and irrigated pastures. Toxic to livestock, so heavy grazing leaves it behind and it spreads — a dense iris meadow is often a sign of a hard-used pasture. Reproduces mostly by spreading rhizomes.

species.name: Lupino plateado
species.short_description: Spikes of blue pea flowers over silky palmate leaves that hold beads of rain.
species.en_short_description: Spikes of blue pea flowers over silky palmate leaves that hold beads of rain.
species.description: Widespread through Colorado's foothills and montane openings. Fixes nitrogen and is often first into disturbed ground and burns. Seeds are toxic to livestock. The leaflets radiate from a single point like fingers, which separates lupine from every clover.
species.en_description: Widespread through Colorado's foothills and montane openings. Fixes nitrogen and is often first into disturbed ground and burns. Seeds are toxic to livestock. The leaflets radiate from a single point like fingers, which separates lupine from every clover.

species.name: Acónito
species.short_description: Deep blue-purple flowers hooded like a cowl, on tall stems in wet shade — and highly toxic.
species.en_short_description: Deep blue-purple flowers hooded like a cowl, on tall stems in wet shade — and highly toxic.
species.description: Grows along Colorado's subalpine streams and in wet meadows, often mixed with larkspur. The upper sepal forms a helmet over the rest of the flower, which only long-tongued bumblebees can enter. Every part contains aconitine and is dangerously poisonous.
species.en_description: Grows along Colorado's subalpine streams and in wet meadows, often mixed with larkspur. The upper sepal forms a helmet over the rest of the flower, which only long-tongued bumblebees can enter. Every part contains aconitine and is dangerously poisonous.

species.name: Caléndula de pantano
species.short_description: White cups with a yellow centre, pushing up through the edge of the melting snowpack.
species.en_short_description: White cups with a yellow centre, pushing up through the edge of the melting snowpack.
species.description: One of the first plants to flower in Colorado's subalpine, sometimes blooming through a thin crust of snow along seeps and wet meadows. What look like petals are sepals. Frequently grows alongside globeflower, which has cream-coloured blooms and divided leaves.
species.en_description: One of the first plants to flower in Colorado's subalpine, sometimes blooming through a thin crust of snow along seeps and wet meadows. What look like petals are sepals. Frequently grows alongside globeflower, which has cream-coloured blooms and divided leaves.

species.name: Campanillas de montaña
species.short_description: Nodding clusters of blue bells that open pink, along mountain streams and seeps.
species.en_short_description: Nodding clusters of blue bells that open pink, along mountain streams and seeps.
species.description: Forms lush blue-green stands beside Colorado's subalpine creeks, sometimes waist-high. Buds are pink and turn blue as they open, so a single cluster shows both colours. A favourite of bumblebees and a food plant of black bears in early summer.
species.en_description: Forms lush blue-green stands beside Colorado's subalpine creeks, sometimes waist-high. Buds are pink and turn blue as they open, so a single cluster shows both colours. A favourite of bumblebees and a food plant of black bears in early summer.

species.name: Lino azul silvestre
species.short_description: Sky-blue five-petalled flowers on wiry stems; each bloom lasts a single morning.
species.en_short_description: Sky-blue five-petalled flowers on wiry stems; each bloom lasts a single morning.
species.description: Common on Colorado's dry foothill slopes, roadsides and mesas from May onward. Petals drop by afternoon and are replaced the next day, so a plant flowers for weeks while never holding a bloom for long. Collected by the Lewis and Clark expedition.
species.en_description: Common on Colorado's dry foothill slopes, roadsides and mesas from May onward. Petals drop by afternoon and are replaced the next day, so a plant flowers for weeks while never holding a bloom for long. Collected by the Lewis and Clark expedition.

species.name: Geum alpino
species.short_description: Yellow five-petalled flowers over fern-like leaves that turn the tundra red in autumn.
species.en_short_description: Yellow five-petalled flowers over fern-like leaves that turn the tundra red in autumn.
species.description: One of the most abundant plants on Colorado's alpine tundra, often the dominant cover on gentler slopes. The finely divided foliage colours deep maroon in late August and is what gives the high country its autumn tone from a distance.
species.en_description: One of the most abundant plants on Colorado's alpine tundra, often the dominant cover on gentler slopes. The finely divided foliage colours deep maroon in late August and is what gives the high country its autumn tone from a distance.

species.name: Estrella fugaz
species.short_description: Magenta petals swept back from a pointed dark beak, like a shuttlecock in flight.
species.en_short_description: Magenta petals swept back from a pointed dark beak, like a shuttlecock in flight.
species.description: Grows in Colorado's wet mountain meadows and along streams in early summer. Bumblebees must grip the flower and buzz at a specific frequency to shake the pollen loose — honeybees cannot do it and the plant ignores them entirely.
species.en_description: Grows in Colorado's wet mountain meadows and along streams in early summer. Bumblebees must grip the flower and buzz at a specific frequency to shake the pollen loose — honeybees cannot do it and the plant ignores them entirely.

species.name: Girasol común
species.short_description: The wild ancestor of the crop: many-branched, many-headed, and all over the plains in August.
species.en_short_description: The wild ancestor of the crop: many-branched, many-headed, and all over the plains in August.
species.description: Lines Colorado's eastern roads, ditches and fallow fields in late summer, quite unlike the single-headed cultivated form. Young buds track the sun through the day; mature heads settle facing east. A major seed source for finches, doves and buntings into winter.
species.en_description: Lines Colorado's eastern roads, ditches and fallow fields in late summer, quite unlike the single-headed cultivated form. Young buds track the sun through the day; mature heads settle facing east. A major seed source for finches, doves and buntings into winter.

species.name: Azucena de arena
species.short_description: Fragrant white star flowers sitting flat on the ground with no visible stem at all.
species.en_short_description: Fragrant white star flowers sitting flat on the ground with no visible stem at all.
species.description: Flowers on Colorado's dry foothill and plains grassland in April and May, one of the earliest blooms of the year. The flower tube runs underground to the ovary, so the plant appears stemless. Grass-like leaves fade away by midsummer.
species.en_description: Flowers on Colorado's dry foothill and plains grassland in April and May, one of the earliest blooms of the year. The flower tube runs underground to the ovary, so the plant appears stemless. Grass-like leaves fade away by midsummer.

species.name: Artemisa grande
species.short_description: The defining shrub of the interior West; silver three-toothed leaves and a resinous smell.
species.en_short_description: The defining shrub of the interior West; silver three-toothed leaves and a resinous smell.
species.description: Covers northwestern Colorado, North Park and the Gunnison basin, and supports an entire community from sage-grouse to pygmy rabbits. Evergreen and aromatic, with tiny wind-pollinated flowers in late summer. The smell after rain is the signature scent of the sagebrush steppe.
species.en_description: Covers northwestern Colorado, North Park and the Gunnison basin, and supports an entire community from sage-grouse to pygmy rabbits. Evergreen and aromatic, with tiny wind-pollinated flowers in late summer. The smell after rain is the signature scent of the sagebrush steppe.

species.name: Bitterbrush
species.short_description: Three-lobed leaves like sagebrush but green, with small cream flowers and no smell.
species.en_short_description: Three-lobed leaves like sagebrush but green, with small cream flowers and no smell.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's dry foothill and mountain slopes, often mixed with sagebrush. Critical winter browse for mule deer and elk. Fixes nitrogen through root associations, and its seeds are cached and planted by rodents.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's dry foothill and mountain slopes, often mixed with sagebrush. Critical winter browse for mule deer and elk. Fixes nitrogen through root associations, and its seeds are cached and planted by rodents.

species.name: Zumaque aromático
species.short_description: Three-part leaves and sticky red berries; smells sharp when crushed, and turns scarlet in fall.
species.en_short_description: Three-part leaves and sticky red berries; smells sharp when crushed, and turns scarlet in fall.
species.description: Common on Colorado's hogbacks, canyon slopes and plains draws. Looks alarmingly like poison ivy — the reliable difference is that the terminal leaflet has no stalk of its own. Berries are edible and sour, and were used to make a lemonade-like drink.
species.en_description: Common on Colorado's hogbacks, canyon slopes and plains draws. Looks alarmingly like poison ivy — the reliable difference is that the terminal leaflet has no stalk of its own. Berries are edible and sour, and were used to make a lemonade-like drink.

species.name: Rosa de Woods
species.short_description: The common native wild rose: five pink petals, straight thorns, and red hips into winter.
species.en_short_description: The common native wild rose: five pink petals, straight thorns, and red hips into winter.
species.description: Thickets along Colorado's streams, fencelines and foothill draws. Hips stay on the canes all winter and are a major food for birds and bears. Spreads by suckers into dense stands that provide some of the best small-bird nesting cover in the state.
species.en_description: Thickets along Colorado's streams, fencelines and foothill draws. Hips stay on the canes all winter and are a major food for birds and bears. Spreads by suckers into dense stands that provide some of the best small-bird nesting cover in the state.

species.name: Guillomo
species.short_description: White five-petalled flowers before the leaves, then sweet purple berries in midsummer.
species.en_short_description: White five-petalled flowers before the leaves, then sweet purple berries in midsummer.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's foothill and montane slopes and in canyon bottoms. One of the earliest shrubs to bloom, a haze of white on brown hillsides in April. The berries are genuinely good and are stripped quickly by bears, robins and waxwings.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's foothill and montane slopes and in canyon bottoms. One of the earliest shrubs to bloom, a haze of white on brown hillsides in April. The berries are genuinely good and are stripped quickly by bears, robins and waxwings.

species.name: Chamiso
species.short_description: Grey-green desert shrub whose seeds are enclosed in four papery wings.
species.en_short_description: Grey-green desert shrub whose seeds are enclosed in four papery wings.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's alkaline plains and Western Slope badlands, tolerating salt that excludes almost everything else. Excretes excess salt onto the leaf surface, which is what gives the foliage its dusty grey cast. Important winter browse on hard range.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's alkaline plains and Western Slope badlands, tolerating salt that excludes almost everything else. Excretes excess salt onto the leaf surface, which is what gives the foliage its dusty grey cast. Important winter browse on hard range.

species.name: Chamizo
species.short_description: Spiny white-barked shrub with fleshy succulent leaves, on the saltiest ground there is.
species.en_short_description: Spiny white-barked shrub with fleshy succulent leaves, on the saltiest ground there is.
species.description: Indicates shallow saline groundwater across Colorado's alkali flats and Western Slope basins. Leaves are high in oxalates and toxic to sheep in quantity. Its presence reliably tells you the water table is close and the soil is bad.
species.en_description: Indicates shallow saline groundwater across Colorado's alkali flats and Western Slope basins. Leaves are high in oxalates and toxic to sheep in quantity. Its presence reliably tells you the water table is close and the soil is bad.

species.name: Borrego
species.short_description: Low grey shrub that turns woolly white in autumn as the seed hairs develop.
species.en_short_description: Low grey shrub that turns woolly white in autumn as the seed hairs develop.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's dry plains and semi-desert flats. Named for its value as winter forage — it holds high protein through the cold months when nothing else does. Late-season stands glow silver-white in low sun.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's dry plains and semi-desert flats. Named for its value as winter forage — it holds high protein through the cold months when nothing else does. Late-season stands glow silver-white in low sun.

species.name: Búfalo plateado
species.short_description: Thorny shrub with silvery opposite leaves and translucent red berries on female plants only.
species.en_short_description: Thorny shrub with silvery opposite leaves and translucent red berries on female plants only.
species.description: Grows along Colorado's plains streams and foothill draws. Male and female flowers are on separate plants, so only some shrubs fruit. The berries are tart and were mixed with bison meat in pemmican. Fixes nitrogen like Russian-olive, but is native.
species.en_description: Grows along Colorado's plains streams and foothill draws. Male and female flowers are on separate plants, so only some shrubs fruit. The berries are tart and were mixed with bison meat in pemmican. Fixes nitrogen like Russian-olive, but is native.

species.name: Ciruelo americano
species.short_description: Thicket-forming small tree, white with blossom in April, with edible red plums by August.
species.en_short_description: Thicket-forming small tree, white with blossom in April, with edible red plums by August.
species.description: Forms dense suckering stands in Colorado's plains draws, fencelines and foothill canyons. The spring bloom is heavily scented and draws every early insect around. Fruit is tart-skinned and sweet inside, and heavily used by bears, coyotes and foxes.
species.en_description: Forms dense suckering stands in Colorado's plains draws, fencelines and foothill canyons. The spring bloom is heavily scented and draws every early insect around. Fruit is tart-skinned and sweet inside, and heavily used by bears, coyotes and foxes.

species.name: Frambuesa de Boulder
species.short_description: Large white rose-like flowers on a thornless raspberry of the Front Range foothills.
species.en_short_description: Large white rose-like flowers on a thornless raspberry of the Front Range foothills.
species.description: Almost a Colorado speciality, common on rocky foothill slopes from Boulder south. The flowers are showy and the shrub is thornless, both unusual for a Rubus. The species name is a well-known misnomer — the dry fruit is close to inedible.
species.en_description: Almost a Colorado speciality, common on rocky foothill slopes from Boulder south. The flowers are showy and the shrub is thornless, both unusual for a Rubus. The species name is a well-known misnomer — the dry fruit is close to inedible.

species.name: Flor de cera
species.short_description: Clusters of thick waxy white flowers on a cliff shrub with veined, felty leaves.
species.en_short_description: Clusters of thick waxy white flowers on a cliff shrub with veined, felty leaves.
species.description: Grows out of rock crevices and boulder fields in Colorado's foothill canyons. Leaves are deeply veined above and white-hairy beneath, and turn rose-red in autumn. Named for Edwin James, who made the first recorded ascent of Pikes Peak.
species.en_description: Grows out of rock crevices and boulder fields in Colorado's foothill canyons. Leaves are deeply veined above and white-hairy beneath, and turn rose-red in autumn. Named for Edwin James, who made the first recorded ascent of Pikes Peak.

species.name: Perlilla de montaña
species.short_description: Small pink tubular flowers and waxy white berries that persist long after the leaves drop.
species.en_short_description: Small pink tubular flowers and waxy white berries that persist long after the leaves drop.
species.description: Common in Colorado's montane forest understorey and mountain shrubland. The white berries are conspicuous into winter and are eaten by grouse and robins, though mildly toxic to people. Longer-flowered than the common snowberry of lower ground.
species.en_description: Common in Colorado's montane forest understorey and mountain shrubland. The white berries are conspicuous into winter and are eaten by grouse and robins, though mildly toxic to people. Longer-flowered than the common snowberry of lower ground.

species.name: Pino salado
species.short_description: Feathery grey-green foliage and pink flower plumes on a riverbank invader.
species.en_short_description: Feathery grey-green foliage and pink flower plumes on a riverbank invader.
species.description: A List B noxious weed choking Colorado's Western Slope and Arkansas River corridors. Draws enormous quantities of groundwater and deposits salt on the soil surface from its leaves, which suppresses native seedlings. Resprouts vigorously from cut stumps.
species.en_description: A List B noxious weed choking Colorado's Western Slope and Arkansas River corridors. Draws enormous quantities of groundwater and deposits salt on the soil surface from its leaves, which suppresses native seedlings. Resprouts vigorously from cut stumps.

species.name: Sauce coyote
species.short_description: Very narrow silvery leaves on slender stems, forming dense clonal thickets along water.
species.en_short_description: Very narrow silvery leaves on slender stems, forming dense clonal thickets along water.
species.description: Colonises Colorado's sandbars, ditch banks and river margins by suckering, so a stand is often one plant. Key nesting cover for Yellow Warblers and willow flycatchers, and the beaver's preferred building and feeding material on the plains.
species.en_description: Colonises Colorado's sandbars, ditch banks and river margins by suckering, so a stand is often one plant. Key nesting cover for Yellow Warblers and willow flycatchers, and the beaver's preferred building and feeding material on the plains.

species.name: Zacate búfalo
species.short_description: A low sod-forming shortgrass that spreads by runners and needs almost no water.
species.en_short_description: A low sod-forming shortgrass that spreads by runners and needs almost no water.
species.description: With blue grama, the backbone of Colorado's shortgrass prairie, and increasingly used as a low-water lawn on the Front Range. Male and female flowers are on separate plants and look entirely different. Grows four to six inches tall and stops.
species.en_description: With blue grama, the backbone of Colorado's shortgrass prairie, and increasingly used as a low-water lawn on the Front Range. Male and female flowers are on separate plants and look entirely different. Grows four to six inches tall and stops.

species.name: Trigo occidental
species.short_description: Stiff blue-grey blades with prominent ribs, in an upright wheat-like seed spike.
species.en_short_description: Stiff blue-grey blades with prominent ribs, in an upright wheat-like seed spike.
species.description: A dominant native of Colorado's northern plains and mountain parks, spreading by rhizomes to form durable sod. Stays palatable when cured, which makes it valuable winter forage. The strongly ridged, waxy blue leaves are distinctive at any season.
species.en_description: A dominant native of Colorado's northern plains and mountain parks, spreading by rhizomes to form durable sod. Stays palatable when cured, which makes it valuable winter forage. The strongly ridged, waxy blue leaves are distinctive at any season.

species.name: Aguja e hilo
species.short_description: Seeds with a sharp point and a four-inch twisting awn that drills them into the soil.
species.en_short_description: Seeds with a sharp point and a four-inch twisting awn that drills them into the soil.
species.description: Common on Colorado's sandy plains and foothills. The awn coils and uncoils with changing humidity, screwing the seed into the ground. Those same seeds work into socks, dog ears and sheep fleece, which is how the grass gets moved around.
species.en_description: Common on Colorado's sandy plains and foothills. The awn coils and uncoils with changing humidity, screwing the seed into the ground. Those same seeds work into socks, dog ears and sheep fleece, which is how the grass gets moved around.

species.name: Zacate popotillo arenoso
species.short_description: A tall blue-waxy sandhills grass with a whitish, densely hairy turkeyfoot seed head.
species.en_short_description: A tall blue-waxy sandhills grass with a whitish, densely hairy turkeyfoot seed head.
species.description: Anchors the blowouts and dunes of Colorado's eastern sandhills, spreading by heavy rhizomes through loose sand. Closely related to big bluestem and hybridising with it where they meet, but paler, waxier and much more hairy in the seed head.
species.en_description: Anchors the blowouts and dunes of Colorado's eastern sandhills, spreading by heavy rhizomes through loose sand. Closely related to big bluestem and hybridising with it where they meet, but paler, waxier and much more hairy in the seed head.

species.name: Zacate colorado
species.short_description: Blue-green in summer and mahogany-orange all winter, with fluffy silver seed tufts.
species.en_short_description: Blue-green in summer and mahogany-orange all winter, with fluffy silver seed tufts.
species.description: A midgrass of Colorado's eastern plains, sandhills and foothill grasslands, and the plant that gives the winter prairie its rust colour. Bunching rather than sod-forming. Its seed heads catch low light and glow white along a whole hillside.
species.en_description: A midgrass of Colorado's eastern plains, sandhills and foothill grasslands, and the plant that gives the winter prairie its rust colour. Bunching rather than sod-forming. Its seed heads catch low light and glow white along a whole hillside.

species.name: Barba de indio
species.short_description: Tallgrass to six feet, with a three-parted seed head like a turkey's foot.
species.en_short_description: Tallgrass to six feet, with a three-parted seed head like a turkey's foot.
species.description: Reaches its western limit in Colorado's eastern sandhills and moist plains draws, a remnant of the tallgrass prairie. Roots go down two metres or more. The split seed head is the origin of its other name, turkeyfoot.
species.en_description: Reaches its western limit in Colorado's eastern sandhills and moist plains draws, a remnant of the tallgrass prairie. Roots go down two metres or more. The split seed head is the origin of its other name, turkeyfoot.

species.name: Pasto varilla
species.short_description: Tall warm-season bunchgrass with an open, airy, pink-tinged seed panicle.
species.en_short_description: Tall warm-season bunchgrass with an open, airy, pink-tinged seed panicle.
species.description: Grows in Colorado's eastern sandhills, wet meadows and river bottoms. Deep-rooted and long-lived, and much studied as a biofuel crop. The panicle is diffuse and cloudlike, unlike the compact heads of most prairie grasses.
species.en_description: Grows in Colorado's eastern sandhills, wet meadows and river bottoms. Deep-rooted and long-lived, and much studied as a biofuel crop. The panicle is diffuse and cloudlike, unlike the compact heads of most prairie grasses.

species.name: Zacate arenoso
species.short_description: Seed head partly wrapped in the top leaf sheath, as if it never quite emerged.
species.en_short_description: Seed head partly wrapped in the top leaf sheath, as if it never quite emerged.
species.description: A pioneer of Colorado's sandy and disturbed ground across the plains. The name records the seeds falling free of their hulls when ripe. The half-hidden panicle inside a swollen sheath is the fastest way to recognise it.
species.en_description: A pioneer of Colorado's sandy and disturbed ground across the plains. The name records the seeds falling free of their hulls when ripe. The half-hidden panicle inside a swollen sheath is the fastest way to recognise it.

species.name: Zacate de junio
species.short_description: A neat, compact, shining seed spike on a short cool-season bunchgrass, ripe by June.
species.en_short_description: A neat, compact, shining seed spike on a short cool-season bunchgrass, ripe by June.
species.description: Widespread from Colorado's plains to the subalpine, and one of the first native grasses to set seed each year. The dense silvery-green panicle contracts after flowering into a tight spike. Small, tidy and easily overlooked among taller grasses.
species.en_description: Widespread from Colorado's plains to the subalpine, and one of the first native grasses to set seed each year. The dense silvery-green panicle contracts after flowering into a tight spike. Small, tidy and easily overlooked among taller grasses.

species.name: Zacate de penacho
species.short_description: Dense basal tussock under a shimmering open panicle; the grass of wet mountain meadows.
species.en_short_description: Dense basal tussock under a shimmering open panicle; the grass of wet mountain meadows.
species.description: Dominant in Colorado's subalpine wet meadows and along tundra seeps, forming hummocks that are centuries old. The flowering panicle catches light and gives whole meadows a golden haze in July. Highly palatable and a mainstay of high-country grazing.
species.en_description: Dominant in Colorado's subalpine wet meadows and along tundra seeps, forming hummocks that are centuries old. The flowering panicle catches light and gives whole meadows a golden haze in July. Highly palatable and a mainstay of high-country grazing.

species.name: Zacatón alcalino
species.short_description: A large grey-green bunchgrass with a wide airy panicle, on salty bottomland.
species.en_short_description: A large grey-green bunchgrass with a wide airy panicle, on salty bottomland.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's alkaline flats, playa margins and San Luis Valley bottoms where salt excludes most grasses. Forms conspicuous rounded clumps a metre across. The open, pinkish seed head breaks off and tumbles, spreading seed as it goes.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's alkaline flats, playa margins and San Luis Valley bottoms where salt excludes most grasses. Forms conspicuous rounded clumps a metre across. The open, pinkish seed head breaks off and tumbles, spreading seed as it goes.

species.name: Pasto azul de Kentucky
species.short_description: The standard lawn grass; boat-shaped leaf tips and a pair of tramlines down each blade.
species.en_short_description: The standard lawn grass; boat-shaped leaf tips and a pair of tramlines down each blade.
species.description: Introduced from Europe and now the most widespread grass in Colorado's towns, irrigated pasture and disturbed montane meadow, where it displaces natives. The prow-shaped leaf tip and the two light lines flanking the midrib identify it in any lawn.
species.en_description: Introduced from Europe and now the most widespread grass in Colorado's towns, irrigated pasture and disturbed montane meadow, where it displaces natives. The prow-shaped leaf tip and the two light lines flanking the midrib identify it in any lawn.

species.name: Woodsia de las Rocosas
species.short_description: A small glandular cliff fern growing straight out of shaded rock cracks.
species.en_short_description: A small glandular cliff fern growing straight out of shaded rock cracks.
species.description: Tucked into north-facing crevices and boulder fields through Colorado's foothills and montane zone. Fronds are twice-divided, slightly sticky to the touch, and die back to a tuft of persistent old stipe bases at the crown.
species.en_description: Tucked into north-facing crevices and boulder fields through Colorado's foothills and montane zone. Fronds are twice-divided, slightly sticky to the touch, and die back to a tuft of persistent old stipe bases at the crown.

species.name: Helecho de roble occidental
species.short_description: A bright green triangular frond held flat, like three separate leaflets on one thin stalk.
species.en_short_description: A bright green triangular frond held flat, like three separate leaflets on one thin stalk.
species.description: Carpets damp shaded ground in Colorado's spruce-fir forest, along seeps and under deadfall. The blade is horizontal rather than upright, and the lowest pair of divisions is nearly as large as the rest of the frond, giving the three-part look.
species.en_description: Carpets damp shaded ground in Colorado's spruce-fir forest, along seeps and under deadfall. The blade is horizontal rather than upright, and the lowest pair of divisions is nearly as large as the rest of the frond, giving the three-part look.

species.name: Helecho vejiga de montaña
species.short_description: A delicate lacy fern of cold wet limestone ledges, rare and local in the high country.
species.en_short_description: A delicate lacy fern of cold wet limestone ledges, rare and local in the high country.
species.description: Grows on moist shaded calcareous rock in Colorado's subalpine, at the southern edge of a mostly boreal range. Fronds are finely three-times divided and thin-textured, arising singly from a creeping rhizome rather than in a clump.
species.en_description: Grows on moist shaded calcareous rock in Colorado's subalpine, at the southern edge of a mostly boreal range. Fronds are finely three-times divided and thin-textured, arising singly from a creeping rhizome rather than in a clump.

species.name: Cacto copa de vino
species.short_description: Mounds of ribbed stems topped in May by waxy scarlet cups that stay open for days.
species.en_short_description: Mounds of ribbed stems topped in May by waxy scarlet cups that stay open for days.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's southern and Western Slope rock outcrops, sometimes in clumps of hundreds of stems. The flowers are among the very few red ones in the state pollinated by hummingbirds rather than bees. Fruit is edible and mildly sweet.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's southern and Western Slope rock outcrops, sometimes in clumps of hundreds of stems. The flowers are among the very few red ones in the state pollinated by hummingbirds rather than bees. Fruit is edible and mildly sweet.

species.name: Cacto erizo de flor verde
species.short_description: A single small ribbed barrel with unexpected yellow-green flowers that smell of lemon.
species.en_short_description: A single small ribbed barrel with unexpected yellow-green flowers that smell of lemon.
species.description: Widespread but easily missed on Colorado's shortgrass plains and foothill gravel, often only two inches tall. One of the most cold-hardy cacti in North America. The green flowers are unlike anything else on the prairie.
species.en_description: Widespread but easily missed on Colorado's shortgrass plains and foothill gravel, often only two inches tall. One of the most cold-hardy cacti in North America. The green flowers are unlike anything else on the prairie.

species.name: Cacto cola de zorro
species.short_description: A low nipple cactus with straw-coloured flowers and bright red fruit that persists all winter.
species.en_short_description: A low nipple cactus with straw-coloured flowers and bright red fruit that persists all winter.
species.description: Buried nearly flush with the soil on Colorado's plains and mesas, and often found only when the scarlet fruits appear. Tubercles rather than ribs, each tipped with a spine cluster. Shrinks into the ground in drought and reinflates after rain.
species.en_description: Buried nearly flush with the soil on Colorado's plains and mesas, and often found only when the scarlet fruits appear. Tubercles rather than ribs, each tipped with a spine cluster. Shrinks into the ground in drought and reinflates after rain.

species.name: Cacto sin gancho de Colorado
species.short_description: A federally threatened barrel cactus found only in three river valleys in western Colorado.
species.en_short_description: A federally threatened barrel cactus found only in three river valleys in western Colorado.
species.description: Endemic to the Colorado, Gunnison and Delores river basins on adobe and gravel benches. Pink to magenta flowers in April. Named for lacking the hooked central spine of its relatives. Threatened primarily by illegal collection and energy development.
species.en_description: Endemic to the Colorado, Gunnison and Delores river basins on adobe and gravel benches. Pink to magenta flowers in April. Named for lacking the hooked central spine of its relatives. Threatened primarily by illegal collection and energy development.

species.name: Rebozuelo de las Rocosas
species.short_description: Egg-yolk orange with blunt forking ridges running down the stalk, and an apricot smell.
species.en_short_description: Egg-yolk orange with blunt forking ridges running down the stalk, and an apricot smell.
species.description: The chanterelle of Colorado's spruce-fir forest, fruiting through the late-summer monsoon. False gills are blunt ridges, not blades, and cannot be peeled away. The toxic false chanterelle has true thin gills and a duller orange-brown cap.
species.en_description: The chanterelle of Colorado's spruce-fir forest, fruiting through the late-summer monsoon. False gills are blunt ridges, not blades, and cannot be peeled away. The toxic false chanterelle has true thin gills and a duller orange-brown cap.

species.name: Hongo del álamo
species.short_description: Orange cap, pores beneath, and a white stalk covered in small dark scabers.
species.en_short_description: Orange cap, pores beneath, and a white stalk covered in small dark scabers.
species.description: Grows only with aspen, so a Colorado aspen grove after August rain is where to look. The flesh bruises grey then nearly black when cut. Widely eaten but occasionally causes gastric upset, and should always be cooked thoroughly.
species.en_description: Grows only with aspen, so a Colorado aspen grove after August rain is where to look. The flesh bruises grey then nearly black when cut. Widely eaten but occasionally causes gastric upset, and should always be cooked thoroughly.

species.name: Colmenilla de incendio
species.short_description: A grey, fuzzy-stemmed morel that fruits in enormous numbers the year after a forest fire.
species.en_short_description: A grey, fuzzy-stemmed morel that fruits in enormous numbers the year after a forest fire.
species.description: Appears in Colorado's conifer burn scars the first or second spring after a wildfire, sometimes by the thousand, then vanishes as the site recovers. Cap is deeply pitted and hollow from tip to base — a solid interior means a poisonous false morel.
species.en_description: Appears in Colorado's conifer burn scars the first or second spring after a wildfire, sometimes by the thousand, then vanishes as the site recovers. Cap is deeply pitted and hollow from tip to base — a solid interior means a poisonous false morel.

species.name: Hongo ala de halcón
species.short_description: A large brown cap covered in coarse upturned scales, with soft teeth instead of gills.
species.en_short_description: A large brown cap covered in coarse upturned scales, with soft teeth instead of gills.
species.description: Fruits under Colorado spruce in late summer and is a reliable beginner's find because nothing dangerous resembles it. The underside is a mass of downward-pointing spines. Older specimens turn bitter, so only young caps are worth taking.
species.en_description: Fruits under Colorado spruce in late summer and is a reliable beginner's find because nothing dangerous resembles it. The underside is a mass of downward-pointing spines. Older specimens turn bitter, so only young caps are worth taking.

species.name: Boleto viscoso
species.short_description: A dark brown cap with a slimy skin over yellow pores, on a short stout stalk.
species.en_short_description: A dark brown cap with a slimy skin over yellow pores, on a short stout stalk.
species.description: Abundant under Colorado's lodgepole and ponderosa pine after rain. The glutinous cap surface is diagnostic and is usually peeled before cooking, since it upsets some people. Almost always found in troops rather than singly.
species.en_description: Abundant under Colorado's lodgepole and ponderosa pine after rain. The glutinous cap surface is diagnostic and is usually peeled before cooking, since it upsets some people. Almost always found in troops rather than singly.

species.name: Hongo del anillo de hadas
species.short_description: Tan caps with a low central bump and widely spaced gills, in arcs across a lawn.
species.en_short_description: Tan caps with a low central bump and widely spaced gills, in arcs across a lawn.
species.description: Grows in expanding rings on Colorado's grassland and irrigated lawns, the ring marking the outward growth of the underground mycelium. Dries out and revives with rain rather than rotting. Deadly lawn species grow in the same places, so care is warranted.
species.en_description: Grows in expanding rings on Colorado's grassland and irrigated lawns, the ring marking the outward growth of the underground mycelium. Dries out and revives with rain rather than rotting. Deadly lawn species grow in the same places, so care is warranted.

species.name: Champiñón de campo
species.short_description: The wild button mushroom: white cap, pink gills turning chocolate, and a ring on the stalk.
species.en_short_description: The wild button mushroom: white cap, pink gills turning chocolate, and a ring on the stalk.
species.description: Fruits in Colorado's pastures, mountain meadows and lawns after summer rain. Gills are pink when young and never white — a white-gilled lookalike with a cup at the stem base is a deadly Amanita. Spore print is dark brown.
species.en_description: Fruits in Colorado's pastures, mountain meadows and lawns after summer rain. Gills are pink when young and never white — a white-gilled lookalike with a cup at the stem base is a deadly Amanita. Spore print is dark brown.

species.name: Bejín gigante
species.short_description: A white ball the size of a football, pure white inside when it is worth eating.
species.en_short_description: A white ball the size of a football, pure white inside when it is worth eating.
species.description: Appears in Colorado meadows, pastures and river bottoms in late summer. Edible only while the interior is uniformly white and firm; any yellowing or an outline of a mushroom inside means it should be left. A mature one releases trillions of spores.
species.en_description: Appears in Colorado meadows, pastures and river bottoms in late summer. Edible only while the interior is uniformly white and firm; any yellowing or an outline of a mushroom inside means it should be left. A mature one releases trillions of spores.

species.name: Parasol lanudo
species.short_description: Tall stalk, a movable ring, and a white cap breaking into coarse brown scales.
species.en_short_description: Tall stalk, a movable ring, and a white cap breaking into coarse brown scales.
species.description: Common in Colorado's gardens, compost and disturbed montane soil. Flesh reddens when cut. Closely resembles the poisonous green-spored parasol, which is separated only by taking a spore print — white here, pale green there.
species.en_description: Common in Colorado's gardens, compost and disturbed montane soil. Flesh reddens when cut. Closely resembles the poisonous green-spored parasol, which is separated only by taking a spore print — white here, pale green there.

species.name: Galerina mortal
species.short_description: A small brown wood-rotting mushroom carrying the same toxins as the death cap.
species.en_short_description: A small brown wood-rotting mushroom carrying the same toxins as the death cap.
species.description: Fruits in clusters on rotting Colorado conifer wood, often alongside edible honey mushrooms and mistaken for them. Rusty-brown spore print and a ring on the stalk. Contains amatoxins; a small quantity can destroy the liver.
species.en_description: Fruits in clusters on rotting Colorado conifer wood, often alongside edible honey mushrooms and mistaken for them. Rusty-brown spore print and a ring on the stalk. Contains amatoxins; a small quantity can destroy the liver.

species.name: Sombrero de bruja
species.short_description: A sharply conical orange-red waxcap that blackens entirely wherever it is touched.
species.en_short_description: A sharply conical orange-red waxcap that blackens entirely wherever it is touched.
species.description: Grows in Colorado's mossy montane meadows and forest edges. Gills feel waxy between the fingers. The whole fruiting body turns coal-black with age or handling, which makes the identification certain and gives it its other name, blackening waxcap.
species.en_description: Grows in Colorado's mossy montane meadows and forest edges. Gills feel waxy between the fingers. The whole fruiting body turns coal-black with age or handling, which makes the identification certain and gives it its other name, blackening waxcap.

species.name: Hongo cáscara de naranja
species.short_description: Brilliant orange cups sprawling on bare soil, looking exactly like discarded peel.
species.en_short_description: Brilliant orange cups sprawling on bare soil, looking exactly like discarded peel.
species.description: Fruits on compacted ground, road cuts and trail edges through Colorado's montane forest in late summer. A cup fungus, so spores are fired from the upper surface — a puff of smoke sometimes rises from a colony when it is disturbed.
species.en_description: Fruits on compacted ground, road cuts and trail edges through Colorado's montane forest in late summer. A cup fungus, so spores are fired from the upper surface — a puff of smoke sometimes rises from a colony when it is disturbed.

species.name: Melena de oso
species.short_description: A white cascade of branching stems hung with rows of soft icicle-like spines.
species.en_short_description: A white cascade of branching stems hung with rows of soft icicle-like spines.
species.description: Grows from wounds and dead wood on Colorado's aspen and cottonwood. There is nothing poisonous that resembles it. Fruits in the same spot on the same log for several years running, so a found specimen is worth remembering.
species.en_description: Grows from wounds and dead wood on Colorado's aspen and cottonwood. There is nothing poisonous that resembles it. Fruits in the same spot on the same log for several years running, so a found specimen is worth remembering.

species.name: Rúsula emética
species.short_description: A glossy scarlet cap on a chalk-white brittle stalk that snaps like a stick of chalk.
species.en_short_description: A glossy scarlet cap on a chalk-white brittle stalk that snaps like a stick of chalk.
species.description: Common under Colorado conifers in damp summers. Russulas break cleanly rather than tearing, which places the genus quickly. This one is intensely acrid and causes violent vomiting, hence the name — a useful marker species rather than a food.
species.en_description: Common under Colorado conifers in damp summers. Russulas break cleanly rather than tearing, which places the genus quickly. This one is intensely acrid and causes violent vomiting, hence the name — a useful marker species rather than a food.

species.name: Yesquero del álamo
species.short_description: A hard grey hoof on an aspen trunk, always just under a dead branch stub.
species.en_short_description: A hard grey hoof on an aspen trunk, always just under a dead branch stub.
species.description: The single most important decay fungus of Colorado's aspen forest, hollowing living trunks and in doing so creating the cavities that sapsuckers, bluebirds and flying squirrels nest in. A conk on a stem means extensive rot inside.
species.en_description: The single most important decay fungus of Colorado's aspen forest, hollowing living trunks and in doing so creating the cavities that sapsuckers, bluebirds and flying squirrels nest in. A conk on a stem means extensive rot inside.

species.name: Yesquero de la quinina
species.short_description: A chalky white hoof-shaped conk on old conifers, and one of the bitterest substances known.
species.en_short_description: A chalky white hoof-shaped conk on old conifers, and one of the bitterest substances known.
species.description: Grows on ancient Douglas-fir and larch in Colorado's high forest and is increasingly rare as old trees are lost. Used medicinally for two thousand years, which the species name records. Individual conks can grow for decades and reach considerable size.
species.en_description: Grows on ancient Douglas-fir and larch in Colorado's high forest and is increasingly rare as old trees are lost. Used medicinally for two thousand years, which the species name records. Individual conks can grow for decades and reach considerable size.

species.name: Yesquero del sauce
species.short_description: A black cracked hoof on willow and aspen, growing a new layer of pores each year.
species.en_short_description: A black cracked hoof on willow and aspen, growing a new layer of pores each year.
species.description: Perennial on Colorado's riparian willow and birch, and hard enough to blunt a knife. The upper surface cracks into a rough black crust while the pore layer underneath stays brown. Ash from the burnt conk has long been mixed with chewing tobacco in the north.
species.en_description: Perennial on Colorado's riparian willow and birch, and hard enough to blunt a knife. The upper surface cracks into a rough black crust while the pore layer underneath stays brown. Ash from the burnt conk has long been mixed with chewing tobacco in the north.

species.name: Políporo del tintorero
species.short_description: A soft yellow-and-rust rosette at the base of a conifer, hardening to dark brown.
species.en_short_description: A soft yellow-and-rust rosette at the base of a conifer, hardening to dark brown.
species.description: Causes butt and root rot in Colorado's Douglas-fir, spruce and pine, so a fruiting body means the tree is compromised at the base. Fresh growth is velvety with a sulphur-yellow margin. Yields strong yellow, gold and green dyes for wool, which names it.
species.en_description: Causes butt and root rot in Colorado's Douglas-fir, spruce and pine, so a fruiting body means the tree is compromised at the base. Fresh growth is velvety with a sulphur-yellow margin. Yields strong yellow, gold and green dyes for wool, which names it.

species.name: Liquen rodante
species.short_description: A loose yellow-green lichen that lives unattached on the prairie and blows about.
species.en_short_description: A loose yellow-green lichen that lives unattached on the prairie and blows about.
species.description: Lies free on the soil of Colorado's shortgrass plains and sagebrush, anchored to nothing, and collects in drifts against fences and shrubs. Poisonous to elk and sheep in quantity, and implicated in periodic die-offs in Wyoming and Colorado.
species.en_description: Lies free on the soil of Colorado's shortgrass plains and sagebrush, anchored to nothing, and collects in drifts against fences and shrubs. Poisonous to elk and sheep in quantity, and implicated in periodic die-offs in Wyoming and Colorado.

species.name: Liquen de nieve
species.short_description: Crinkled pale yellow upright lobes forming loose mats on exposed alpine ground.
species.en_short_description: Crinkled pale yellow upright lobes forming loose mats on exposed alpine ground.
species.description: Grows on Colorado's tundra ridges and fellfields, where snow blows clear. The wavy, almost translucent lobes stand up from the soil rather than lying flat. Slow enough growing that a mat may represent a century of accumulation.
species.en_description: Grows on Colorado's tundra ridges and fellfields, where snow blows clear. The wavy, almost translucent lobes stand up from the soil rather than lying flat. Slow enough growing that a mat may represent a century of accumulation.

species.name: Liquen gusano blanco
species.short_description: Hollow chalk-white tubes lying loose among tundra plants, like scattered worms.
species.en_short_description: Hollow chalk-white tubes lying loose among tundra plants, like scattered worms.
species.description: Found on Colorado's alpine turf and among moss on high ridges. Never produces spores anywhere in the world and reproduces only by fragmentation, so the entire global population is a set of clones. Bright white and quite unmistakable.
species.en_description: Found on Colorado's alpine turf and among moss on high ridges. Never produces spores anywhere in the world and reproduces only by fragmentation, so the entire global population is a set of clones. Bright white and quite unmistakable.
